entries.q: What is Qortal?
entries.a: Qortal is a fully decentralized blockchain and peer-to-peer data network: infrastructure for a parallel internet. People run their own nodes, earn QORT by minting, and publish websites, Q-Apps, files and media on QDN, the Qortal Data Network. Q-Chat, Q-Mail and Torq carry messages and social posts. There was no ICO and no company owns the network. For a guided start, open the Welcome to Qortal Q-App.

entries.q: Is Qortal a video game?
aliases: is Qortal like a Discord game
entries.a: No. Qortal is a fully decentralized blockchain and peer-to-peer data network. People run nodes, mint QORT by contributing, and publish on QDN. Levels are on-chain minting contribution levels.

entries.q: What is the native coin of Qortal?
entries.a: The native coin is QORT. It pays transaction fees (about 0.01 QORT each) and the one-time name registration fee, it is earned by minting (helping secure the network), and it can be traded peer-to-peer in Q-Trade for LTC, BTC, DOGE, RVN, DGB and ARRR. New QORT is created only by minting: there was no ICO and no pre-mine for early investors.

entries.q: When was Qortal Genesis?
entries.a: Qortal mainnet Genesis — the first block — was minted on June 29, 2020. That is the network's birthday. Qortal was written from scratch after earlier work on QORA; Genesis started with nothing pre-mined for a privileged sale.

entries.q: What is minting on Qortal?
entries.a: On Qortal, minting replaces mining. Accounts with minting rights run a full node that stays online, and every online minter shares in each block's reward. Your share grows with your level, which rises with time spent minting. Expensive hardware gives no advantage: a modest always-on machine, even a Raspberry Pi-class board, is enough. The rule is one minting account per person.

entries.q: How do I become a minter?
aliases: how do i get minting rights
how do I get a minting nomination
how do I get nominated for minting
how to get nominated for minting
entries.a:
1. Register a Qortal name and keep a little QORT for fees.
2. Run a full node in Qortal Hub that stays synced and online.
3. Use Qortal visibly for a while: publish on QDN, use Q-Mail and Q-Chat, help others.
4. A Level 5+ minter who knows your work nominates you in Q-Mintership (you cannot nominate yourself).
5. Minter Admins vote. At about 40% yes, an admin creates your MINTER group invite, which needs signatures from about 40% of the admins to become active.
6. Accept it with JOIN_GROUP, then open Minting in Qortal Hub (the sprout icon) and start minting: Hub sets up the minting key for you.
The Q-Minter guide has the full walkthrough. Sponsorship keys are no longer used.

entries.q: What are Qortal levels?
entries.a: Levels are on-chain account levels from 0 to 10 that come from minting, not game scores. Level 0 is the waiting room, with no reward share. Level 1 (Initiation) comes after about 7,200 online blocks. Level 5, a little over a year of steady minting, lets you nominate new minters. Level 10 (Maturity) takes about eight years. Higher levels earn a larger share of each block reward and more voting weight.

entries.q: What is sponsorship or nomination?
entries.a: A nomination is how someone gets minting rights on Qortal today. Sponsorship was the old way: a Level 5+ sponsor gave a newcomer a reward-share key. It has been retired. Now a Level 5+ minter publishes a nomination card for you on the Minter Board in Q-Mintership. Minter Admins vote (about 40% yes unlocks the next step), and about 40% of them must sign your MINTER group invite. You accept it with JOIN_GROUP, start minting from Qortal Hub's Minting settings, and keep a synced full node online. You cannot nominate yourself.

entries.q: Why is my seedphrase so important?
aliases: why is my seed phrase important
what is a seed phrase in qortal
entries.a: Your Qortal account is a key pair made from your seed phrase; your address starts with "Q". No server holds the account, so there is no recovery service, support desk or reset button. To restore it you need the seed phrase, or your backup file plus its password. Lose all of them and the account, its names and its funds are gone for good. Write the seed phrase on paper, keep the backup file offline, never screenshot either into cloud photos, and never share them.

entries.q: Can someone recover my account if I lose my seedphrase?
aliases: can qortal support recover my wallet
how do I recover my qortal wallet
how to recover my qortal account
entries.a: No. Nobody can recover it for you: not founders, admins, Hub, GO, Core or any support channel. Accounts are keys, not server records. Without the seed phrase you can still restore the account with your backup file and its password; with neither, the account is gone. If you can still sign in, make a fresh backup now (Backup wallet) and store it offline.

entries.q: What is a Qortal name?
aliases: do i need a qortal name
entries.a: A registered name is your public identity on Qortal and the anchor for everything you publish on QDN (websites, apps, files, avatars). Names are unique, owned by your account and can be sold. You need one before you can publish on QDN. Registering costs a one-time 1.25 QORT, with no yearly renewal. Your first name becomes your primary name, and you can add more to the same account.

entries.q: What is QDN?
aliases: what is the Qortal Data Network
what is qdn from a developer perspective
entries.a: QDN (Qortal Data Network) is Qortal's decentralized data layer. Every resource is identified by a registered name, a service type (e.g. WEBSITE, APP, DOCUMENT, FILE), and an optional identifier; a new publish with the same three replaces the old one. Nodes that follow a name store and serve that name's data. Large payloads are stored off-chain and verified by an on-chain SHA-256 hash; tiny payloads under 240 bytes can live fully on-chain.

entries.q: What is Q-Chat?
aliases: what is private messaging on qortal
entries.a: Q-Chat is the chat built into Qortal Hub and Qortal GO: groups with channels, direct messages (DMs), mentions, replies, attachments and voice calls. It now runs over Reticulum, a peer-to-peer network, while your Qortal account and group memberships stay at the centre. Sending messages costs no QORT and needs no minimum balance. If you turn Reticulum off, Q-Chat falls back to legacy chat, which needs at least 4 QORT in your balance and has no calls.

entries.q: What are Q-Apps?
entries.a: Q-Apps are static web apps (HTML/JS/CSS) published on QDN, usually as a zip with index.html at the root, service type APP (max about 50 MB). They run inside Qortal Hub or Qortal GO with the qortalRequest bridge for wallet, publish, and payments — no private corporate backend required. Identity is your wallet address plus optional registered name.

entries.q: What is the Trade Portal?
entries.a: The Trade Portal is Qortal's built-in cross-chain trading, which you use through the Q-Trade app in Hub and GO. QORT trades directly for LTC, BTC, DOGE, RVN, DGB and ARRR using AT (Automated Transaction) contracts on the Qortal chain, with no exchange company holding your coins. Prices come from open offers between users.

entries.q: Do I need to run a node?
aliases: should I run a qortal node
do I need my own qortal node
must I run a qortal node
can i use qortal without a node
entries.a: Not to start. Hub and GO can use a public node for Q-Apps, Q-Mail, Q-Chat and most everyday things. Your own node (Qortal Core) is needed to mint, and it makes you independent: it checks the chain itself, hosts QDN data for the names you follow and keeps working if public nodes go down. A few features only work on your own node, such as minting and publishing on QDN from GO. For a node, plan on at least 4 GB of RAM (8 GB is comfortable), an SSD and an always-on connection.

entries.q: How do fees work on Qortal?
aliases: how much does publishing on qdn cost
entries.a: Most on-chain actions, such as a payment or a QDN publish, cost a small flat fee of about 0.01 QORT. Registering a name costs 1.25 QORT once. No company takes the fees: they go into each block's reward for the minters who secure the network, and they deter spam. Q-Chat messages cost nothing: Reticulum chat uses no transactions, and legacy chat messages never go into blocks. You need a little QORT before you can register a name or publish.

entries.q: What is Qortal GO?
entries.a: Qortal GO (GO 3.0) is the Android app for Qortal, built from the same code as Qortal Hub. It holds your wallet and opens Q-Apps and QDN websites, with a Torq feed on Home, Q-Chat with groups, DMs and voice calls, a widgets screen, and Qortino, the offline AI helper. It connects to a public node or to your own node. Get it as an APK from the GO 3.0 name on Q-Share (it is not on Google Play): the older official GO build does not support the new Q-Chat.

entries.q: What is Qortal Hub?
entries.a: Qortal Hub (Hub 3.0) is the desktop app for Qortal on Windows, macOS and Linux. It holds your wallet, opens Q-Apps and QDN websites, registers names, has Q-Chat with channels, DMs and voice calls over Reticulum, and includes minting tools and node control. It can run your own node (Qortal Core) or connect to a public node. Q-Apps can use your wallet only through approval prompts.

entries.q: Is there an ICO or pre-mine?
aliases: did qortal have a token sale
can I buy qort on binance
entries.a: No. Qortal had no ICO and no pre-mine: it launched in 2020 with zero coins for insiders, and new QORT only comes from minting. Influence cannot be bought with a big wallet; it is earned with time spent minting. Hub and GO are free, open-source software, and on-chain actions cost small QORT fees. Big exchanges are not the usual route to QORT: qortal.dev suggests buying LTC anywhere, sending it to the Litecoin wallet in your Qortal account and swapping it for QORT in Q-Trade.

entries.q: Can I buy minting power with better hardware?
aliases: does a faster pc mint more qort
entries.a: No. Unlike proof-of-work mining races, Qortal minting does not reward faster or more expensive machines. You cannot buy your way to minting more QORT with ASIC farms. A modest always-on computer is enough; rewards are about contribution time and level, shared within tiers among online minters.

entries.q: What is Proof of Contribution?
aliases: proof of contribution vs proof of work
how Qortal differs from Bitcoin mining
entries.a: Proof of Contribution (minting) means you earn by keeping a minting account online and synchronized, helping secure the chain over time. It is light enough for ordinary hardware. Combined with nomination (Organic Proof of Humanity) and one minting account per person, it resists corporate farm capture that proof-of-work or pay-to-stake systems invite.

entries.q: What are groups on Qortal?
aliases: how do I join a group on qortal
entries.a: Groups are on-chain memberships, each with its own Q-Chat space. A group is open (anyone can join) or closed (invite or approval), and in the new Q-Chat it can hold many channels and categories, so one community no longer needs a separate group for every topic. Private groups can share group-encrypted data that only members can read. Network roles use groups too, such as the MINTER group for minters. To find one to join, use Find Groups in Q-Chat.

entries.q: How do I follow a name and why?
aliases: what does following a qortal name do
entries.a: Following a name tells your node to host and serve that name's QDN data. Persistence is social: content stays alive because people who value it follow its publisher, and popular content gains copies on many nodes. Follow your own name on your node so your publishes stay local. Follows live on the node, so they need your own node: a public node does not take changes to its lists.

entries.q: How do I publish data on QDN?
aliases: how do I publish a website on qdn
how to publish a website on qortal
how do I make a q-app
entries.a:
1. Own a registered name: publishing without one fails.
2. Pick a service type such as WEBSITE, APP, DOCUMENT, FILE or IMAGE.
3. Optionally set an identifier (case-sensitive, so keep one scheme).
4. Publish, in Hub under Publish / Websites / Q-Apps or from a Q-App, and pay the small fee (about 0.01 QORT).
Publishing again with the same name, service and identifier replaces the old version, and only the name's current owner can do that. Hub currently allows one App and one Website per name.

entries.q: What happens if I sell my name?
aliases: what happens to my qdn content if i sell my name
entries.a: Update rights move with the name. Only the current owner of a name can publish or overwrite resources under it, so if you sell or transfer the name, the buyer controls every future update, and the content already published under it goes with the name. Plan publishes and transfers carefully.

entries.q: Addresses start with what letter?
aliases: what does a Qortal address look like
entries.a: Qortal account addresses start with the letter "Q". The account itself is a keypair derived from your seedphrase. The address is how payments and on-chain actions identify you; a registered name is the human-readable identity layered on top for QDN and public presence.

entries.q: Who controls Qortal?
entries.a: No company owns Qortal. The community running nodes is the infrastructure. Even founders cannot shut it down — it keeps running while peers secure it. Governance uses on-chain votes with weight from minting level/time. Dev Admins steward core software updates by shared approval; Minter Admins handle minting nominations — elected roles, not thrones.

entries.q: What is Organic Proof of Humanity?
aliases: how does qortal stop bots minting
entries.a: It is the human nomination layer: a Level 5+ minter must vouch for you, Minter Admins approve, and the hard rule is one minting account per person. That stops corporations from spinning up hundreds of minting bots. You may hold multiple non-minting accounts, but only one minting account per human.

entries.q: How often is a new block minted?
aliases: how long is a qortal block
entries.a: A new block is minted about once every 60 seconds. Each block carries freshly minted QORT plus that block's transaction fees, shared among online minters by level tiers. Rewards are often tallied in batches (roughly every 1,000 blocks), so your balance may jump in steps rather than every minute.

entries.q: Do founders still get special rewards?
entries.a: No. Since Qortal Core 4.7.0 (from block 2,012,800) there is no founder reward share: the founder concept was removed from rewards. What founders used to receive, plus the share of the still-inactive top tier (Levels 9 and 10), now goes to the Minter Admins and Dev Admins, split 50/50.

entries.q: Who is Crowetic?
entries.a: Crowetic is Jason Crowe, the original Qortal founder and a Q-App developer. The Team page on qortal.dev lists him among the Dev Admins, working on Q-App development, hardware and partnerships. He also runs Crowetic Hardware Development, home of the original QORTector node device, and NuQloud, a private-cloud and decentralized-data service. Qortal itself is community-run, with no company owner.

entries.q: Is Qortal the same as Playing Qortal the book?
entries.a: No. Qortal is the decentralized blockchain and QDN network. Playing Qortal (by Simon James) is a philosophy book about the Revolution of Values — voluntary cooperation and sovereignty. Keep the network definition separate from the book.

entries.q: What hardware do I need for a node?
aliases: what computer do I need for qortal
entries.a: Qortal Core is Java software for Linux, Windows and macOS. Minimum: a dual-core CPU, 4 GB of RAM and an SSD with comfortable free space. Recommended: quad-core, 8 GB or more, a larger SSD, a wired connection with port forwarding, and a UPS. A desktop, a QORTector, a VPS or a Raspberry Pi-class board with an SSD (not an SD card) all work. A 24/7 node can use well over 1 TB of internet data a month, so an unlimited plan helps.

entries.q: What if my node goes offline?
entries.a: Minting pauses while your node is offline: you get no credit for the blocks that pass while it is down. When it comes back, it resyncs from peers; the chain itself is the backup. To avoid gaps you may run your one minting account on more than one node at the same time. For QDN, others who follow the same names may still host the data, but following your own name keeps your publishes safe locally.

entries.q: How do I keep my account secure?
aliases: how to keep my qortal wallet safe
how do i protect my account
entries.a:
1. Back up both ways: write the seed phrase on paper, and keep the backup file offline with its password stored separately, safe from fire, theft and cloud sync.
2. Never share the seed phrase, backup file or password, or paste them into random apps or sites.
3. Download Hub and GO only from official sources.
4. Read every approval prompt, and treat unexpected payment or publish requests as suspicious.
5. Prefer your own node, and keep Core, Hub and GO updated.

entries.q: Can I mint on multiple accounts?
aliases: can i mint on two nodes
same minting account on several nodes
entries.a: No. The rule is one minting account per person. You may keep any number of non-minting accounts, and you may run your one minting account on several nodes at once for redundancy. If several minting accounts are traced to one person, all of them are removed from the MINTER group. That protects Organic Proof of Humanity.

entries.q: What are Minter Admins?
entries.a: Minter Admins are community-elected minters who review nomination cards and approve or remove minting rights through shared on-chain GROUP_APPROVAL transactions; about 40% of them must agree. It is a paid role funded from block rewards, and to draw that share an admin must be actively minting. Being an admin adds no extra voting weight. There is no minimum level: any existing minter can be proposed for the role on the Minter Admin Management board in Q-Mintership.

entries.q: What are Dev Admins?
entries.a: Dev Admins steward Qortal Core development. A Core update is only applied once enough of them, about 40%, approve it on-chain with GROUP_APPROVAL transactions. Because they contribute through development rather than uptime, the role has no minting requirement, and a Dev Admin who stops contributing can be removed. They are a separate group from the Minter Admins; qortal.dev's Team page lists them.

entries.q: How does voting work?
entries.a: Qortal uses decentralized on-chain ballots. Higher minting level means more voting weight because you have contributed longer. Ideas can be brought to the community and put to a vote — influence is earned with time, not bought with a large QORT balance.

entries.q: What is an AT trade?
aliases: what is an AT on qortal
entries.a: AT means Automated Transaction: a smart contract on the Qortal chain that Q-Trade (the Trade Portal) uses for cross-chain swaps. Your trade runs peer-to-peer by the contract's rules, not through a company holding your coins. Check the offer terms and keep enough balance for fees before you commit.

entries.q: Do I need internet for Qortal forever?
entries.a: Peers need some path to reach each other to sync and trade. Running your own node keeps your access independent of corporate gateways. In censored or degraded conditions, locally synced chain data and followed QDN content remain usable, and nodes can sync from any reachable peer — including community mesh paths where set up.

entries.q: What is Qortal Core?
entries.a: Qortal Core is the node software: it validates the blockchain, stores and serves QDN data for followed names, exposes a local API/UI, and participates in P2P peering. Hub and Qortal GO are user interfaces that talk to Core. Updates can ship through the network's auto-update mechanism — keep disk space healthy and Core current.

entries.q: Why do I need QORT before I can mint?
aliases: why do i need qort first
how much qort do I need to start
entries.a: Becoming a minter starts with a registered name (1.25 QORT) and a visible track record, and most lasting on-chain actions cost a small fee of about 0.01 QORT. You cannot earn by minting until you have minting rights, so newcomers need a little starter QORT first. Hub's Getting Started lists three ways to get your first 2 QORT: the onboarding steps on qortal.dev, the Nextcloud support chat, or Q-Trade. Chatting needs no QORT in Reticulum Q-Chat.

entries.q: What is the difference between WEBSITE and APP on QDN?
aliases: which qdn service type for my site
what is the difference between website and app services
entries.a: Both are multi-file QDN publishes. WEBSITE is for visitor-facing sites where missing paths 404. APP is for interactive apps and SPAs — missing paths fall through to index.html. APP max size is about 50 MB. Rule of thumb: client-side router and app behaviour → APP; mostly static pages with real 404s → WEBSITE.

entries.q: What is a default QDN resource?
aliases: what does default mean on QDN
entries.a: A resource published without an identifier is the default for that name + service — for example a user's main website is the default WEBSITE for their name. Apps can address it by omitting the identifier or using the keyword "default". Shared identifiers (like qortal_avatar) are the opposite idea: the same identifier across many names.

entries.q: How do avatars work?
aliases: how do i set my qortal avatar
entries.a: Avatars use a shared identifier convention: service THUMBNAIL with identifier "qortal_avatar" under a user's registered name. Any app can fetch any user's avatar knowing only their name. THUMBNAIL is limited to about 500 KB, so keep avatar images small.

entries.q: Are private QDN resources possible?
aliases: can i publish private data on qdn
entries.a: Yes. Private service variants (e.g. MAIL_PRIVATE, IMAGE_PRIVATE, DOCUMENT_PRIVATE) store data encrypted so only the intended recipient's private key can decrypt. Group-encrypted data is readable by group members. Public services are visible to anyone whose node can fetch them.

entries.q: What size limits should I know for QDN?
aliases: how big a file can I publish on qdn
entries.a: Common documented limits: JSON about 25 KB; THUMBNAIL about 500 KB; IMAGE about 10 MB; APP about 50 MB; MAIL about 1 MB; CHAIN_COMMENT 239 bytes fully on-chain. Resources under 240 bytes can live fully on-chain; larger payloads are off-chain with an on-chain hash. Hub and GO accept files up to 2 GB each when you publish through your own node, and up to 500 MB through a public node. Large files suit the FILE service rather than DOCUMENT.

entries.q: What coins can I trade for QORT?
entries.a: In Q-Trade (the Trade Portal) you can trade QORT directly for LTC, BTC, DOGE, RVN, DGB and ARRR (Pirate Chain), peer-to-peer with no custodial exchange. Your Qortal account comes with wallets for these coins, made from the same keys, and LTC is the main QORT market. Always check the offer details before you commit.

entries.q: Does Qortal use huge amounts of electricity?
aliases: how much power does a qortal node use
entries.a: No. Minting is light work for a small always-on computer or Raspberry Pi-class board, not a proof-of-work race between warehouses of mining machines. What counts is uptime and a stable connection, not computing power.

entries.q: What is QORA and how does it relate?
entries.a: QORA was a 2014 blockchain with early ideas like on-chain data hosting, but it used Proof of Stake and was abandoned by its founding team. A development group rebuilt it from scratch as Qortal (work began in 2016), without Proof of Stake, and Qortal's Genesis was in 2020. QORA holders who burned their coins are repaid in QORT at 250 QORA to 1 QORT, from a small share of every block: 20% at first, 1% since a 2022 community vote.

entries.q: How long to reach Level 5?
entries.a: Level 5 needs 618,400 online blocks in total. At about one block a minute that is roughly 430 days, a little over a year, of minting without breaks, and downtime adds to it. Level 5 is when you may nominate new minters; community language calls it Baptism. Hub's Minting panel shows how many days your next level needs.

entries.q: How long to reach Level 10?
aliases: how long to reach level 10 qortal
entries.a: Level 10 (Maturity) is the top level and needs 4,074,400 online blocks in total. At about one block a minute that is roughly 2,830 days, close to eight years of continuous minting, and any downtime adds to it. Hub's Minting panel shows how many blocks and days your next level needs.

entries.q: Why is my QORT balance jumping in steps?
aliases: qort balance not updating every minute
why does my qort balance jump
entries.a: Minting rewards are often tallied in batches, roughly every 1,000 blocks, rather than credited on every single ~60-second block. That is normal — do not assume minting is broken just because the balance is quiet between batch payouts. Also confirm your minting key is active and blocks-minted is increasing.

entries.q: What is a minting key?
aliases: how do i get a minting key
entries.a: A minting key (reward-share key) ties your account to a node so that node can mint for you. After you join the MINTER group, open Minting in Qortal Hub (the sprout icon) and start minting: Hub creates and assigns the key for you. The Q-Node app is a more manual alternative. Never share the key publicly. If you move to a new node, you can add the key again there.

entries.q: Can money buy voting power?
entries.a: No. Buying a large pile of QORT on the market does not buy extra votes, faster minting, or control. Voting weight comes from minting level/time. A wealthy newcomer still needs nomination, one minting account, and years of contribution — money is designed not to capture governance.

entries.q: What should I do on day one?
aliases: how do I get started on qortal
what do I need to use qortal
what do I need for qortal
entries.a:
1. Install Qortal Hub (desktop) or Qortal GO (Android) from official sources and create an account.
2. Back up right away: save the encrypted backup file and its password, and write down the seed phrase, all offline.
3. Get a little QORT (Hub's Getting Started lists ways) and register a name for 1.25 QORT.
4. Join the Welcome to Qortal group in Q-Chat and say hello.
5. Open the Welcome to Qortal Q-App and try a few apps, such as Q-Mail, Torq or Q-Share.

entries.q: Is Qortal censorship resistant?
entries.a: Qortal is built so identity, data, and apps live on peer-run infrastructure rather than a company server that can flip a switch. Anyone can run a node, follow names, and host data. Persistence still depends on peers following and serving content — so follow what matters, run your own node when you can, and publish under your own name.

entries.q: What is qortalRequest?
entries.a: qortalRequest is the JavaScript bridge Hub and Qortal GO inject into embedded Q-Apps. Apps call it for wallet identity, payments, publishing, encryption, and navigation — always with user approval for sensitive actions. Use try/catch; call identity actions from a user gesture (button), not automatically on first paint.

entries.q: Do Q-Chat messages stay forever?
aliases: how long are q-chat messages kept
entries.a: Not by default. In Q-Chat you pick an expiry before you send: 1 day up to 1 month, within what the channel allows, and some channels keep messages with no expiry. Direct messages expire after 1 month by default. Messages are not stored on the blockchain: your devices keep them and share recent history with other members peer to peer. Legacy Q-Chat messages are never put into blocks and drop off after about 24 hours. For lasting messages, use Q-Mail.

entries.q: What ports does a node use?
entries.a: Qortal Core talks to peers on port 12392, and current versions use port 12394 for QDN data. Its API, which Hub and Q-Apps use, is on port 12391. Forwarding the peer ports on your router (or letting UPnP do it) helps your node reach more peers, but it is not required. Never open the API port to the internet.

entries.q: How do I verify minting is working?
entries.a: Open Minting in Qortal Hub (the sprout icon). It shows whether your account is minting on this node, your level and tier, blocks to the next level and an estimated reward. Your blocks-minted count should keep rising while the node is online and synced, but credits arrive in batches of about 1,000 blocks. Minting only works on your own node; on a public node Hub says so. Also watch disk space and keep Core updated.

entries.q: Will anyone ask for my seedphrase?
aliases: qortal support asked for my seed
someone asked for my seed phrase
should i share my qortal backup file
entries.a: No legitimate helper ever needs your seed phrase, backup file or password. There is no official Qortal support desk that asks for them, and anyone who does is trying to steal your account. Mentors can guide your clicks and explain ideas; they never need your keys. End the conversation at once.

entries.q: What remains usable if the wider internet degrades?
aliases: what works in qortal when the internet is down
entries.a: Your node's synced copy of the blockchain, the QDN content it already hosts, and Hub or GO running against that node. Qortino in GO works with no internet at all, but Q-Chat needs a connection to Qortal's Reticulum hubs, which normally runs over the internet. Plan your setup assuming gateways and corporate clouds may vanish.

entries.q: What is Q-Mail?
aliases: how do i email on qortal
entries.a: Q-Mail is encrypted mail between Qortal names. Each mail is published on QDN encrypted for its recipient, so only they can read it, and unlike chat it does not expire. It suits messages that should last, such as writing to a Minter Admin. Open it from Apps or with qortal://APP/Q-Mail.

entries.q: What is Q-Tube?
entries.a: Q-Tube is the Q-App for publishing and watching videos on QDN. Videos live under their publishers' names and are served by the nodes that host them, not by a corporate video site. New users can start with the explainer videos on the On Qortal channel.

entries.q: What is Q-Share?
aliases: how do i share a file on qortal
entries.a: Q-Share is for sharing files and documents on QDN under your registered name. You publish a file, pay the small fee, and anyone can fetch it from the nodes that host it. GO 3.0 releases, for example, are shared on Q-Share under the GO 3.0 name.

entries.q: What is Q-Mintership?
entries.a: Q-Mintership is the Q-App where minting rights are decided. Level 5+ minters publish nomination cards on its Minter Board, the community and Minter Admins vote, and admins approve MINTER group invites. It also has the encrypted Admin Board and the MAM / AR Board for adding or removing Minter Admins. Open qortal://APP/Q-Mintership; the Q-Minter guide explains the whole flow.

entries.q: What is Subwire?
entries.a: Subwire (SubWire) is a Q-App for publishing on QDN: articles, episodes with audio or video, author profiles and private content for subscribers. Readers follow creators to get their updates. Everything lives under the author's registered name on QDN, not on a company's blog host.

entries.q: What is the Qortal Web Builder?
entries.a: Qortal Web Builder is a no-code, drag-and-drop website builder, published on QDN as the Q-App QWB (qortal://APP/QWB). You design a site and publish it to QDN under your name without writing code. The result is a normal QDN website that other nodes can host, and the Qortal Web Q-App lists sites made with it.

entries.q: What is a QORTector?
entries.a: A QORTector is a plug-and-play Qortal node device built for 24/7 uptime, so a node (and minting) keeps running without tying up your main computer. The original QORTector comes from Crowetic Hardware Development, and 3D-print files and guides are on the Qortal wiki. The same rules apply as for any node: back up your account offline and keep the device powered and synced.

entries.q: How do identifiers work on QDN?
entries.a: The optional identifier string distinguishes multiple resources for the same name + service. Identifiers are case-sensitive — "MyApp_config" and "myapp_config" are different. Apps should prefix identifiers with their app name (e.g. myapp_ + suffix) and later search with that prefix. Always validate fetched data; QDN is permissionless.

entries.q: Can I update a published resource?
aliases: how do i update my qortal website
entries.a: Yes. Publish again with the same name + service + identifier and the new version overwrites for fetchers. Only the current owner of the name can update. There is no separate "edit password" — control of the name is control of updates.

entries.q: What is CHAIN_COMMENT?
entries.a: CHAIN_COMMENT is a tiny fully on-chain payload service capped at 239 bytes. Use it for small permanent comments anchored in the chain itself. Larger discussion or content belongs in off-chain QDN services with on-chain hashes.

entries.q: What happens to data if nobody follows a name?
entries.a: QDN persistence is follow-based. If no node follows a name, that name's hosted payloads can become hard to fetch. Popular content gains redundancy; obscure content needs friends, mirrors, or your own always-on node following your name. Social hosting is a feature, not a bug — value what you want to keep alive.

entries.q: How do I register a name step by step?
aliases: how do I register a name on qortal
how to register a qortal name
entries.a:
1. Create an account and back it up (backup file plus password, and the seed phrase).
2. Get at least 1.25 QORT for the one-time fee, plus a little for other fees.
3. In Hub or GO, use Register your name in Home's Getting Started, or open the Names Q-App, and pick a name nobody has taken.
4. Confirm the transaction.
5. Once it confirms, the name is yours and you can publish on QDN under it. Your first name becomes your primary name.

entries.q: Are names renewed every year?
entries.a: No. There is no yearly renewal: you pay a one-time 1.25 QORT fee, and the name stays with your account until you sell or transfer it. Protect your backups, because losing the account loses the name with it.

entries.q: What is Level 0?
entries.a: Level 0 is where you start once you join the MINTER group: the waiting room, with no share of block rewards. After about 7,200 online blocks you reach Level 1 (Initiation) and start earning in your tier. Because credits are batched, Level 1 often shows after 8,000 to 9,000 blocks, about six days of steady minting.

entries.q: What is Level 1 Initiation?
entries.a: Level 1, called Initiation in community language, is the first earning level. It needs about 7,200 online minted blocks, but credits are batched about every 1,000 blocks, so it often appears after 8,000 to 9,000 online blocks. Trust the level shown in Hub, not the raw block counter.

entries.q: Can corporations farm QORT?
entries.a: The design pushes back hard: nomination is a human handshake, one minting account per person, and multi-account farms get removed. Paying workers to beg nominations for phantom accounts is brittle compared to those workers simply minting for themselves. Money alone cannot buy minting rights or vote weight.

entries.q: How is the block reward shared?
entries.a: Each block's reward (new QORT plus that block's fees) is split by level tier: Levels 1-2 get 6%, 3-4 get 13%, 5-6 get 19%, 7-8 get 26% and 9-10 get 32%. Every online minter in a tier gets an equal part of that tier's slice. 1% goes to old QORA holders, and the Minter Admins and Dev Admins get 1.5% each; while Levels 9-10 are inactive, their 32% goes to the admins too (17.5% for each group). Rewards are credited in batches of about 1,000 blocks.

entries.q: Does the block reward change over time?
aliases: will the qortal block reward go down
entries.a: Yes. Qortal Core's schedule started at 5 QORT per block at Genesis (29 June 2020) and drops by 0.25 QORT every 259,200 blocks, roughly every six months, down to 2 QORT per block. New QORT is created only by minting. The Q-Minter guide shows today's reward per block.

entries.q: Is there a maximum QORT supply?
aliases: how many qort will there be
entries.a: There is no hard cap like Bitcoin's 21 million: every block creates new QORT for online minters. The reward per block steps down by 0.25 QORT every 259,200 blocks, from 5 QORT at Genesis to 2 QORT, so new supply slows over time but does not stop.

entries.q: What is the 1% QORA repayment share?
entries.a: A small share of every block, 1% since a 2022 community vote (it was 20% at first), repays people who burned QORA for the move to Qortal, at 250 QORA to 1 QORT. The holders do not need to run a node or mint to receive it.

entries.q: Do I need port forwarding to mint?
aliases: do i need to open ports to mint
entries.a: Port forwarding improves peer connectivity but is not strictly required to use the network or begin participating. Prioritize a stable machine, synced Core, active minting key, and offline seedphrase backup. Improve networking if you see poor peer counts.

entries.q: How much storage does a node need?
aliases: how big is the qortal blockchain
entries.a: There is no fixed figure: the chain keeps growing, and the QDN data your node hosts for the names it follows adds more. Use an SSD with plenty of free space and room to grow, and check the Qortal wiki for current needs before you buy hardware. Watch the free space: a full disk stops a node faster than almost anything else.

entries.q: Should I use a UPS with minting?
entries.a: Yes if you can. Minting rewards consistent uptime; power blips mean downtime and slower level progress. An uninterruptible power supply for a Pi or small PC is a practical pairing with an always-on node.

entries.q: How do Core updates work?
entries.a: Qortal Core updates itself by default: a new version is applied once enough Dev Admins, about 40%, approve it on-chain. Keep enough free disk space and check that the node restarts cleanly afterwards, since running old Core brings sync and compatibility trouble. Hub checks for its own updates in the app, and GO has a GO 3.0 Updates screen in the account menu that installs newer versions over the old one, keeping your accounts and chats.

entries.q: What is the local trust model?
aliases: why run my own qortal node for apps
qortal public node vs own node
is a public qortal node safe
entries.a: Hub, GO and every Q-App work through the node they are connected to. On your own node your data stays local and you decide what it stores and blocks. A public node is someone else's node made public: convenient, but its operator decides what is blocked, and some actions are refused there or come with warnings, such as minting, follow lists and trades that need another coin's private key. For important actions, prefer a node you control.

entries.q: Can I use Qortal without registering a name?
aliases: publish on qdn without a name
do i need a name to use qortal
entries.a: You can hold an account and receive QORT with just an address, but a registered name is required to publish QDN resources and is the practical public identity for apps, sites, and being known in the community. Most newcomers register a name early.

entries.q: What are shared identifiers?
entries.a: Shared identifiers are deterministic locations used across many names — for example every avatar uses THUMBNAIL + "qortal_avatar". Apps agree on the identifier string so they can find the same kind of resource for any name without a central profile server.

entries.q: How should apps name their QDN identifiers?
entries.a: Prefix with the app slug, e.g. myapp_config_v1 or myapp_post_<id>. Later search with SEARCH_QDN_RESOURCES using the prefix option. Because QDN is permissionless, validate the schema of everything you fetch — an identifier match is not proof your app wrote it.

entries.q: What is the APP 50 MB limit?
aliases: how big can a q-app be
entries.a: Q-Apps published as service APP are multi-file zips with a typical maximum around 50 MB. Stay under the limit, ship assets inside the zip (avoid CDN dependencies), and use relative paths with a flat dist layout so Hub/GO can serve the app offline-friendly.

entries.q: Why did my Q-App show a grey screen?
entries.a: Common causes: zip layout wrong (index.html not at root), bundler base path not "./" so assets 404, Hub opening /render/APP/Name without a trailing slash so relative assets resolve badly, or relying on external CDNs blocked offline. Rebuild, flatten dist, re-zip, and republish.

entries.q: WEBSITE missing file returns what?
entries.a: On QDN WEBSITE service, a missing file path returns 404. On APP service, missing paths fall through to index.html for SPA routing. Choosing the wrong service type is a frequent publishing mistake.

entries.q: What is FILE vs DOCUMENT on QDN?
aliases: which qdn service for large files
entries.a: Use FILE/FILES for large binary or general file payloads. DOCUMENT is for document-style payloads; do not force huge binaries into the wrong service. JSON is for small structured metadata (~25 KB). Pick the service that matches validation rules and size expectations.

entries.q: Can resources live fully on-chain?
entries.a: Yes if they are under about 240 bytes (CHAIN_COMMENT max 239 bytes is the clear example). Larger payloads are stored off-chain on QDN and verified by an on-chain SHA-256 hash. That keeps the chain lean while data remains integrity-checked.

entries.q: How do private groups help?
aliases: what is a closed qortal group for
entries.a: Closed groups use invite/approval membership. They enable private group chat and group-encrypted QDN data readable only by members — useful for teams, families, or communities who want shared private publishing without a company chat server.

entries.q: Open vs closed groups?
aliases: difference between open and closed qortal groups
entries.a: Open groups allow broader joining; closed groups require invite or approval. Both are on-chain membership structures with chat and permission features. Pick closed when membership itself is part of the security boundary.

entries.q: How do I pay with a QR code or a qortal://pay link?
entries.a: In GO's Send QORT, tap Scan QR code, or open a qortal://pay link such as qortal://pay?recipient=NAME&amount=5. Send QORT opens with the recipient and amount filled in, and nothing is sent until you check them and confirm. On Android, GO also opens these links and scanned codes from other apps. To get paid, show your own code under Receive QORT. A sent payment cannot be undone.

entries.q: What are qortal:// links?
entries.a: qortal:// links open QDN resources and apps inside Hub or GO, in the form qortal://SERVICE/name/identifier/path, for example qortal://APP/Q-Mail or qortal://WEBSITE/Q-Minter. A group link (qortal://use-group/action-join/groupid-NUMBER) offers to join that group, and in GO a payment link (qortal://pay?recipient=NAME&amount=5) opens Send QORT filled in for you to confirm; Hub 3.0.3 doesn't open payment links. Inside a Q-App, OPEN_NEW_TAB or LINK_TO_QDN_RESOURCE opens a link. On Android, GO opens these links, scanned codes and Qortal gateway web links directly.

entries.q: Is Trade Portal custodial?
entries.a: Not when you trade through your own node: Q-Trade (the Trade Portal) uses AT contracts peer-to-peer, and no exchange company holds your coins. On a public node it is different: to finish a trade, your other coin's private key is encrypted and sent to the Qortal trade proxy account, so whoever controls that account could spend that coin, and you are asked to confirm this first. Non-custodial does not mean risk-free: check offers and protect your backups.

entries.q: Can I trade without KYC on a company exchange?
aliases: p2p qort trade without exchange account
entries.a: Yes. Q-Trade (the Trade Portal) trades are peer-to-peer on Qortal, with no exchange account and no KYC. You still need the other coin in your Qortal wallet (for example LTC) and a little QORT for fees. Follow the laws that apply where you live.

entries.q: What foreign wallets are involved in trading?
aliases: which wallets does my qortal account have
entries.a: Cross-chain trades need the other chain's coin. Hub and GO give your Qortal account its own wallets for LTC, BTC, DOGE, DGB, RVN and ARRR, made from the same keys, so your Qortal backup restores them too. Litecoin is the usual way in: fund the LTC wallet, then swap in Q-Trade. To trade or send these coins, their private key must go to the node doing the work, so use your own node when you can.

entries.q: What is Reticulum in relation to Qortal?
aliases: how do hub and go use reticulum
entries.a: Reticulum is an encrypted networking stack built to work over almost any kind of link. Qortal Hub and Qortal GO use it for Q-Chat (groups, channels and DMs), online presence, file transfers in chat, voice calls and syncing settings between your devices, while your account and group memberships stay on the Qortal blockchain. It reaches other users through Qortal's Reticulum hubs on the internet.

entries.q: Who is Simon James in Playing Qortal?
entries.a: Simon James is a long-time Qortal community member, supporter and promoter, known for his contributions to various Q-Apps and websites as well as Qortal GO, the Android app. He is also the author of Playing Qortal, about the Revolution of Values philosophy, which is separate from the technical definition of Qortal as a blockchain and QDN network.

entries.q: Why does nomination require Level 5?
aliases: why must a nominator be level 5
entries.a: Level 5 takes a little over a year of steady minting (618,400 online blocks), so a nominator has a long record on the network and a reputation to stake. That is the point: Level 5+ minters vouching for real people they know adds a web of trust. It replaced self-made cards, which some people abused with low-quality AI-written posts. Only Level 5+ minters can publish a nomination card in Q-Mintership.

entries.q: What does MINTER group invite mean?
aliases: what is a minter group invite
entries.a: Once enough Minter Admins vote yes on your nomination (about 40%), an admin creates a pending invite to the MINTER group, the on-chain group whose members may mint. About 40% of the Minter Admins must sign it (GROUP_APPROVAL) before it becomes active. Then you accept it with a JOIN_GROUP transaction in Hub and start minting from Minting (the sprout icon).

entries.q: Can I nominate myself?
aliases: can i apply for minting myself
can i make my own minter card
entries.a: No. Someone else must vouch for you: a Level 5+ minter who knows you or your work publishes your nomination card in Q-Mintership. Self-made cards were the earlier Mintership way and were dropped because some people abused them. Build a visible track record, such as publishing on QDN, using Q-Mail and Q-Chat and helping others, so a nominator has something real to point to.

entries.q: What if nomination is rejected?
aliases: what if minter admins say no
entries.a: If Minter Admin yes votes do not reach about 40%, the admin actions on the card never unlock, so no MINTER group invite is made. Your account is not affected: you can still hold QORT, register names, publish and chat. Admins look for a real, visible track record, so keep taking part (publish on QDN, use Q-Mail and Q-Chat, help others); a specific, honest nomination from a Level 5+ minter who knows you also matters.

entries.q: Can minting rights be removed?
aliases: can i be removed from the minter group
entries.a: Yes. Minter Admins can remove minting rights with the same quorum-based group approval, for example for suspected multiple minting accounts, or when someone was active only to get approved and then stopped looking like a unique, contributing user. If a removal was a mistake, the account can be invited again. Minting is a responsibility the community grants, not a purchase.

entries.q: Do admins get extra vote power?
aliases: do minter admins have more votes
entries.a: Admin roles are paid responsibilities for specific jobs (nominations or software stewardship), not general thrones. Genuine influence on Qortal still comes from minting over time. Minter Admins must actively mint to draw their admin reward share.

entries.q: What percentage do admins currently receive?
aliases: how much do minter admins earn
entries.a: Admins get a base 3% of each block reward: 1.5% for the Minter Admins and 1.5% for the Dev Admins. While Tier 5 (Levels 9-10) is inactive, its 32% is split between the two groups as well, so each group gets about 17.5%, 35% in all, shared evenly among its members. This replaced the old founder share in Core 4.7.0. Once Tier 5 has 30 or more active minters, its 32% goes to them and the admins keep their 3%.

entries.q: Why is Levels 9–10 empty important?
entries.a: Tier 5 (Levels 9 and 10) is set to share 32% of every block reward. Qortal Core pays a top tier on its own only when it has 30 or more online minters; with fewer, its minters and its share join the tier below, and only while a tier has nobody online does its share go to the Minter Admins and Dev Admins. As more minters reach the top levels, the tier pays its own share, so this is a young-network arrangement, not a permanent tax.

entries.q: How do I back up correctly?
aliases: how to back up my qortal wallet
entries.a: Make two kinds of backup. Write the full seed phrase on paper and check every word, and save the encrypted backup file (Backup wallet in Hub or GO) to a USB drive or other offline storage, with its password kept separately. Keep copies in separate safe places, and never put them in email, cloud notes or chat. Losing all of them loses the account.

entries.q: Should I screenshot my seedphrase?
aliases: can i photograph my seed phrase
entries.a: Avoid it. Phone screenshots often sync to cloud photo backups — exactly the failure mode that loses sovereignty. Prefer handwritten offline copies. If a screen display is unavoidable temporarily, do not leave it in gallery sync; move to offline storage and delete synced copies.

entries.q: Can Hub custodially hold my coins?
aliases: can qortal hub reset my password
entries.a: No. Hub, GO and Core do not hold accounts as server logins: your keys stay on your device, encrypted with your password. If you lose both your seed phrase and your backup file (or its password), no button in Hub can bring the account back. That is the price of holding your own keys.

entries.q: What does a Qortal account contain?
aliases: what is in my qortal wallet
how do I create a qortal wallet
how do I make a qortal account
entries.a: A key pair made from your seed phrase. It gives you an address (starting with Q), and it can hold registered names, QORT and wallets for other coins (LTC, BTC and more), minting status if approved, and group memberships. There is no company database that could bring it back. Create one in Hub or GO, then save the backup file and its password, and write down the seed phrase, all offline.

entries.q: How do I restore an account on a new phone?
aliases: move qortal account to new phone
import backup file into qortal go
entries.a: Install Qortal GO 3.0 from the GO 3.0 name on Q-Share (or Hub on a computer), then add your account in one of two ways: import your backup file and enter its password, or enter your seed phrase. Check that the address is the one you expect before you move any funds. Never type your seed phrase into an app from an unknown source. Then choose your node again in the connection settings.

entries.q: What is gateway mode?
aliases: what is a public qortal node
entries.a: A public node (also called a gateway) is a Qortal node someone else runs and opens to everyone. Hub and GO can use one instead of your own node: quick to start, but with limits. You cannot mint through it, its operator controls follow lists and blocking, some actions are refused, and trades that need another coin's private key send it to a trade proxy. For full independence, run your own node and connect to it.

entries.q: Why follow my own name on my node?
aliases: why follow my own name on qdn
should my qortal node follow my name
entries.a: So your published apps, sites, and documents are always held locally on hardware you control. Even if other followers drop away temporarily, your node still has your data. Encourage friends to follow names that matter to them for social redundancy.

entries.q: What is data hosting socially?
entries.a: QDN storage is follow-based: nodes host data for names they follow. Content survives because communities care enough to host it. That is different from paying a cloud bill to one company — persistence is earned by relevance and relationships.

entries.q: Can I host data for friends?
aliases: host data for friends on qortal
entries.a: Yes — follow their registered names on your node. You help keep their QDN resources available to the network. This is one of the most practical ways to support creators you value without a platform middleman.

entries.q: What media services exist on QDN?
entries.a: Common ones include IMAGE (~10 MB), THUMBNAIL (~500 KB), VIDEO, AUDIO, FILE/FILES, plus app/site packages WEBSITE and APP. Private variants encrypt for a recipient. Choose the service that matches the content type and size.

entries.q: What is LIST service on QDN?
entries.a: LIST is a QDN service type used for list-structured resources in the ecosystem. Like other services, it is addressed by name + service + optional identifier and hosted by followers of that name. Validate formats in apps that consume lists.

entries.q: What is NFT on QDN?
entries.a: NFT appears as a QDN service type for non-fungible style resources published under names. As always, ownership/update rights follow the registered name's owner, and data availability depends on followers hosting the payload.

entries.q: What is CODE service?
entries.a: CODE is a QDN service type for publishing code artifacts under a name. Use clear identifiers and remember that republishing the same coordinates overwrites. Consumers should still verify what they run — permissionless publish means caveat emptor.

entries.q: What is GAME service on QDN?
entries.a: GAME is a QDN service type for game-related resources some apps publish — one content category on the data network, like IMAGE or DOCUMENT. It does not change what the Qortal network itself is: a blockchain and peer-to-peer data network.

entries.q: What is MESSAGE vs CHAIN_COMMENT?
entries.a: MESSAGE is a QDN-oriented message resource type; CHAIN_COMMENT is a tiny fully on-chain 239-byte comment. Use CHAIN_COMMENT for microscopic permanent anchors; use broader message/mail/document services when you need more space or encryption features.

entries.q: How do JSON resources differ?
entries.a: JSON service is for small structured metadata with a tight limit (~25 KB). Ideal for manifests, configs, and indexes. Larger documents should use DOCUMENT or FILE. Apps often publish a JSON manifest then point to bigger assets.

entries.q: How do I publish a JSON document from a Q-App?
entries.a: Own a name, then call qortalRequest with action PUBLISH_QDN_RESOURCE, setting name, service "DOCUMENT" or "JSON" as appropriate, a clear identifier, and data64 (UTF-8-safe base64 of your payload). Handle errors if the name is missing or the fee balance is too low.

entries.q: Why validate anything fetched from QDN?
entries.a: QDN is permissionless — anyone can publish under their own name, and identifiers can be mimicked across names. An app must validate format and trust the publisher name it intends, not assume an identifier string alone means "safe" or "official."

entries.q: What is SEARCH_QDN_RESOURCES?
entries.a: It is the search action/API pattern Q-Apps use to find resources, often filtering by service and identifier prefix. Use app-prefixed identifiers so your search returns your app's data cluster, then validate each result.

entries.q: Can I publish a multi-file website from inside a Q-App?
entries.a: Yes, in current Hub and GO: call PUBLISH_QDN_RESOURCE with service APP or WEBSITE, the zip as the file, and isMultiFileZip set to true, and the node unpacks it into a multi-file resource. Without that flag the zip is stored as one file. Older Hub builds may not support it, so check the version you target. To read a multi-file resource back, FETCH_QDN_RESOURCE needs a filepath.

entries.q: What is window._qdnTheme?
aliases: what host variables does hub inject
entries.a: Q-Apps can read built-in variables: window._qdnTheme is 'light' or 'dark' to match the current theme, and window._qdnContext is 'gateway' when the app is opened through a gateway node. Apps can theme themselves to match without calling any cloud service. Feature-detect qortalRequest before assuming wallet actions exist.

entries.q: Should Q-Apps call GET_USER_ACCOUNT on page load?
aliases: why shouldn't I call GET_USER_ACCOUNT on page load
when should q-apps ask for the account
entries.a: No. Identity actions are gesture-gated — call them from a button click so the user consciously approves. Auto-prompting on first paint creates bad UX and looks like phishing. Detect the bridge, show UI, then request account on demand.

entries.q: What offline rule should Q-Apps follow?
entries.a: Ship assets inside the zip; use relative paths; avoid CDN scripts that vanish offline. Qortal users and Qortino itself may be offline or mesh-only. An app that requires the corporate web is fighting the platform's purpose.

entries.q: Hub vs Qortal GO — what's the difference?
aliases: what is the difference between hub and go
difference between hub and qortal go
should i use hub or go
entries.a: Qortal Hub is the desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux, and it can run its own node or use a public one. Qortal GO is the Android app, built from the same code; it connects to a public node or to a node you run. Both use the same account, QORT, names, Q-Apps and Q-Chat, so you can sign in to both with one account. GO adds phone features such as Qortino (the offline AI helper), widgets and call notifications.

entries.q: Can I mint from my phone alone?
entries.a: No. Minting runs on a full node (Qortal Core) that stays online and synced, and GO is not a node: it connects to one. Run Core on an always-on computer, Raspberry Pi-class board, VPS or QORTector, and use GO on your phone for daily use, chat and apps. On a public node, minting is not available at all.

entries.q: What is exqlorer?
entries.a: Exqlorer (exqlorer.com) is a community-run block explorer website for Qortal, showing blocks, accounts and network figures such as the reward split. It is not part of Qortal itself and needs the internet. Inside Qortal, the Q-Minter guide and Hub's Minting panel show live figures from your node.

entries.q: How do I read the current block reward offline?
aliases: how much qort per block now
entries.a: Work it out from the schedule built into Qortal Core: 5 QORT per block at Genesis, minus 0.25 QORT for every 259,200 blocks, down to 2 QORT. So you only need the current block height, which your node shows. When your node is reachable, the Q-Minter guide's home page shows the current reward per block directly.

entries.q: What is #QQQ?
aliases: what does qqq mean in playing qortal
entries.a: #QQQ comes from the book Playing Qortal, not from the network itself. It is the book's "real currency" of kind words and acts given without a bill, such as thank you, I'm sorry or how are you. It is not a token or a second coin; QORT remains the network's coin.

entries.q: What are the Golden Rules about?
entries.a: Community golden rules emphasize staying synchronized and minting when you can, and helping people you love join so they can mint their own sovereignty too. Teach installation of Core, Hub, or GO when someone is stuck. The spirit is mutual aid, not extractive farming.

entries.q: Is "the most interactive game" literal?
entries.a: No. It is a metaphor from community writing, mainly the book Playing Qortal, for taking part in the network and its values. Qortal itself is real software: a blockchain, the QDN data network, Q-Apps and the QORT coin, not a video game. Account levels come from time spent minting, not from playing.

entries.q: What was wrong with early sponsorship keys?
entries.a: Sponsorship (about 2020 to 2024) let one Level 5+ sponsor give a newcomer a reward-share key. There was no community-wide oversight of who was brought in, it leaned on personal connections, and it could become a bottleneck. It was retired for Mintership and then Nominations: a Level 5+ minter vouches for you in Q-Mintership, Minter Admins approve on-chain, and you join the MINTER group and mint from your own node.

entries.q: How many Minter Admins are there?
aliases: how many votes does a nomination need
entries.a: The number changes as admins are added or removed through the MAM / AR Board, so there is no fixed count. The live list is in Q-Mintership: they are the admins of the MINTER group. The Q-Minter guide shows the current count and how many votes about 40% means right now. What stays the same is shared on-chain approval, never one person's switch.

entries.q: What is Initiation, Baptism, Maturity?
entries.a: Community names for milestones: Initiation ≈ Level 1; Baptism ≈ the long path to Level 5 (may nominate); Maturity ≈ Level 10. They describe contribution age in the community, not video-game achievements.

entries.q: Why do early minters hold more QORT?
aliases: why do early qortal minters have more
is qortal fair to late joiners
entries.a: Someone always goes first; earlier continuous minters simply spent more time earning. That is not a permanent throne — everyone can climb toward Level 10 equality of standing, and even early people stop earning if they go offline. The design pays time, not a privileged sale.

entries.q: Can founders shut Qortal down?
aliases: can qortal founders stop the chain
can the qortal team turn it off
entries.a: No. No company or person owns Qortal: it runs on nodes that ordinary people operate around the world, and it keeps running while they do. Founders have no special switch. Core updates only apply when about 40% of the Dev Admins approve them on-chain, and anyone can read, run and check the open-source code.

entries.q: How does community writing contrast Qortal with Bitcoin?
aliases: how is qortal different from bitcoin
entries.a: The contrast drawn is that proof-of-work coins tend to concentrate in those who can afford industrial mining, while Qortal lets ordinary people mint on modest hardware with human nomination — ownership of issuance tied to participation time, not capital expenditure.

entries.q: Do I pay monthly to host a website on Qortal?
aliases: no monthly web bill on qortal
entries.a: There is no monthly hosting bill. You pay a small fee each time you publish or update (about 0.01 QORT), and your site stays available as long as nodes host it, including your own if it follows your name. Popular sites gain many hosts; your own node is your best insurance.

entries.q: What is Qortal Web?
entries.a: Qortal Web means the decentralized web on QDN: websites and Q-Apps published under registered names and served by peers, not by a company's servers. Hub and GO open any of them straight from its name, such as qortal://WEBSITE/Q-Minter. There is also a Qortal Web Q-App (qortal://APP/Qortal Web) that searches and lists sites made with Qortal Web Builder (QWB).

entries.q: How do voice calls work in the ecosystem?
aliases: how do i call someone in q-chat
entries.a: Q-Chat in Qortal Hub and Qortal GO has 1:1 and group voice calls; group calls take up to 15 people. For a 1:1 call you must be DM friends first. 1:1 calls try a direct connection first and switch to Reticulum if that fails; in GO, choosing Private (Reticulum only) in the Calls setting under Settings → System keeps every call on Reticulum so your IP address stays hidden. Calls need Reticulum turned on.

entries.q: What should I publish in my first week?
aliases: what should i post on qortal first
what to publish for a nomination
entries.a: Something lasting under your name: a small website made with Qortal Web Builder, a file on Q-Share, a video on Q-Tube, a Torq post or a short document. Publishes stay on QDN, so nominators and Minter Admins can see them later, unlike chat. Also join groups in Q-Chat so people get to know you.

entries.q: How do I ask for starter QORT safely?
aliases: how do I get my first qort
where do I get qort as a beginner
entries.a: Ask real people who already use Qortal, for example in the Welcome to Qortal group in Q-Chat. Hub's Getting Started also lists three ways to get your first 2 QORT: the onboarding steps on qortal.dev, asking in the Nextcloud support chat, or buying with Q-Trade. Prefer trusted people over strangers who message you first. Nobody legitimate will ask for your seed phrase or backup file.

entries.q: What is a nomination card?
aliases: what goes in a nomination card
entries.a: A nomination card is the post a Level 5+ minter publishes on the Minter Board in Q-Mintership to put a candidate forward for minting rights. It names the candidate, says how the nominator knows them, and lists their contributions with links to their work on QDN. A poll is attached, and the community and Minter Admins vote on it, with admin votes counted separately.

entries.q: What does "blocks-minted increasing" mean?
aliases: my blocks minted is not going up
is my blocks minted count rising
entries.a: It is a practical health check: your minting account's count of blocks participated in should rise while you are online and approved. If it stalls for a long synced period, re-check minting key status, group membership, and Core health.

entries.q: Why monitor disk space on a node?
aliases: what happens if my qortal node disk is full
why watch disk space on a qortal node
entries.a: A full disk can halt Core, break sync, stop serving QDN, and interrupt minting. Chain + followed content grows. Leave headroom, prefer SSD, and expand storage before you hit zero bytes free.

entries.q: Linux, Windows, or macOS for Core?
aliases: run qortal on linux or mac
entries.a: Qortal Core runs on Linux, Windows, and macOS. Many dedicated minters prefer Linux on a Pi or small PC for 24/7 uptime. Choose what you can keep updated and powered; the network does not require a data-center OS.

entries.q: What is the address letter Q for?
aliases: why do qortal addresses start with q
what does the q in a qortal address mean
entries.a: It is simply the visible prefix of Qortal addresses — a quick sanity check you are copying a Qortal address and not another chain's format. Always verify the full string, not only the first character.

entries.q: Can names be traded?
aliases: buy a qortal name from someone
entries.a: Yes. Names are unique and can be sold and bought on-chain, for example in the Names Q-App. A sale moves the name, and control of everything published under it, to the buyer. You cannot sell your primary name while you hold other names. Check the exact name before you buy.

entries.q: Where do fees go?
aliases: where do qortal transaction fees go
do qortal fees go to a company
entries.a: Into the block reward. Each block's new QORT plus its transaction fees is shared out by the reward split: mostly to online minters by level tier, plus the Minter Admin, Dev Admin and QORA-holder shares. No company takes a cut, so usage pays the people who run the network.

entries.q: Why hold about 4 QORT for chat?
aliases: do i need 4 qort to chat
why cant i send q-chat messages
entries.a: Only legacy Q-Chat needs it. With Reticulum turned off, Hub and GO ask for at least 4 QORT in your balance before you can send, as a guard against spam from empty accounts, and the coins stay yours. Reticulum Q-Chat, which is on by default, needs no balance at all.

entries.q: About how much QORT to register a name?
aliases: how much does a qortal name cost
entries.a: Registering a name costs a one-time 1.25 QORT, and most other transactions about 0.01 QORT, so 2 QORT covers a name with room for a few fees. That is why Hub's Getting Started asks you to get your first 2 QORT. Hub shows the exact fee before you confirm.

entries.q: What does "paid in time, for time" mean?
aliases: paid in time for time meaning
entries.a: A community phrase meaning QORT issuance pays people for the time they keep the network secured, not for capital spent on mining rigs. Your standing grows with synchronized contribution, not with buying hashpower.

entries.q: Does Level 0 earn rewards?
entries.a: No. Level 0 earns nothing from the block reward share — it is the waiting room until you reach Level 1 after roughly 7,200 online blocks.

entries.q: What is a peer in Qortal?
aliases: how many peers does my qortal node need
entries.a: A peer is another node on the P2P network you sync chain data and QDN content with. More healthy peers generally mean better sync and fetch reliability. Port forwarding can help others reach you.

entries.q: Can I sync from any reachable peer?
aliases: where does my qortal node sync from
can my node sync from any qortal peer
entries.a: Mostly. Your node syncs the chain from the peers it is connected to, but it skips peers that misbehaved recently, run too old a Core version or have a weaker chain, and it waits until it has enough peers. Once synced, your own copy of the chain keeps you independent of any one peer.

entries.q: Is Qortino part of Qortal?
entries.a: Yes. Qortino is the offline AI helper inside Qortal GO, the Android app. It runs one model, Qwen3 4B Instruct 2507, fully on your phone, so it works with no internet and nothing leaves the phone. You download it once from QDN (about 2.3 GB); your own node is highly recommended for that. It helps with first aid, survival, gardening, cooking, Qortal and more, but it can be confidently wrong, so double-check anything important.

entries.q: How does Qortino answer Qortal questions?
aliases: how does qortino know about qortal
where do qortino answers come from
entries.a: For Qortal questions, Qortino first looks for a close match in its curated answers, which are written from Qortal's own guides and code, and shows that answer as written. Otherwise its offline model answers, using the closest curated answers as hints. It cannot see live data such as prices, balances or block heights, so check Hub, Q-Trade or the Welcome to Qortal Q-App for those.

entries.q: What does "no yearly renewal" mean for names?
aliases: do i pay yearly for my qortal name
entries.a: There is no registrar charging you every year to keep the name, as with web domains. You pay 1.25 QORT once, and the name is recorded on-chain as yours until you sell or transfer it. The real risk is losing access to your account, so keep your seed phrase and backup file safe.

entries.q: Can I have multiple registered names?
aliases: what is a qortal primary name
entries.a: Yes. The first name you register is your primary name, your main identity; you can register or buy as many more (secondary names) as you like on the same account, each with its own fee. Each name is its own QDN publishing root, and people can pay you using any of them. One backup controls them all, so keep it safe.

entries.q: What is GET_ACCOUNT_NAMES for?
aliases: get names of an address in a q-app
entries.a: In Q-Apps, GET_ACCOUNT_NAMES retrieves the registered names for an address via qortalRequest. Useful after GET_USER_ACCOUNT when an app needs to know which name to publish under.

entries.q: Why chunk large files?
entries.a: Huge payloads are awkward for some services and UX. Prefer FILE service and sensible chunking/packaging rather than stuffing oversized data into DOCUMENT. Users on modest nodes will thank you.

entries.q: What is BLOG_COMMENT?
entries.a: BLOG_COMMENT is a QDN service used by blogging apps for comments threaded to posts. Comments are still resources under names/services/identifiers — validate them in apps like any other permissionless data.

entries.q: What does "latest publish wins" mean?
entries.a: For a given name + service + identifier triple, the newest successful publish is what fetchers retrieve. There is not a forever version museum unless an app deliberately versions identifiers (v1, v2).

entries.q: How do I version QDN data without losing history?
entries.a: Use new identifiers for immutable versions (myapp_post_2026_01_a) and optionally a mutable pointer identifier for "latest". Overwriting the same identifier replaces history at that coordinate.

entries.q: What is DECRYPT_DATA used for?
entries.a: Q-Apps use decryption actions (such as DECRYPT_DATA or group variants) via qortalRequest so the wallet can decrypt private QDN payloads for the logged-in user. Private services are useless without the recipient key.

entries.q: Why feature-detect qortalRequest?
entries.a: Pages may open outside Hub/GO (previews, browsers) where the bridge is missing. Resolve window.qortalRequest or parent/top, and show a clear message to open inside Hub/GO instead of crashing.

entries.q: Why set Vite base to ./ ?
entries.a: Relative base paths make asset URLs work when Hub serves the app from a nested render path. Absolute roots often 404 inside QDN rendering. Rebuild after changing base.

entries.q: What is the trailing slash SPA issue?
entries.a: If Hub opens /render/APP/YourName without a trailing slash, relative ./assets/file.js may resolve against /render/APP/ and 404. Fixes include ensuring a trailing slash, a correct base href, or paths that match how Hub serves you.

entries.q: Can I rely on npm CDNs in a Q-App?
aliases: can a q-app load from a cdn
entries.a: Avoid them. Offline users, CSP, and sovereignty goals break when apps call corporate CDNs. Vendor libraries into the zip instead.

entries.q: What is IMAGE_PRIVATE?
entries.a: A private image service variant encrypted for a recipient. Only their key decrypts it. Use when a public IMAGE would leak the photo to anyone who fetches the coordinates.

entries.q: What is MAIL_PRIVATE?
entries.a: MAIL_PRIVATE is encrypted mail-style QDN data for one recipient, up to 5 MB; Q-Mail uses it. It is the private counterpart to MAIL publishing: confidentiality depends on encryption and key custody, not on hiding an identifier.

entries.q: How do thumbs differ from images?
entries.a: THUMBNAIL (~500 KB) is for small previews/avatars; IMAGE (~10 MB) is for fuller pictures. Using IMAGE for avatars wastes bandwidth; using THUMBNAIL for large photos will fail limits.

entries.q: Can ARRR be traded on the Trade Portal?
aliases: can i trade pirate chain for qort
entries.a: Yes. Pirate Chain (ARRR) is one of the coins you can trade for QORT in Q-Trade (the Trade Portal), alongside LTC, BTC, DOGE, RVN and DGB. Whether a trade is possible depends on open offers from other users.

entries.q: Can DOGE be traded for QORT?
aliases: can i buy qort with doge
entries.a: Yes. DOGE is one of Q-Trade's cross-chain coins, and your Qortal account includes a DOGE wallet. You need some DOGE in it and an open offer from another user; no exchange company holds your coins.

entries.q: Can RVN be traded?
aliases: can i trade ravencoin for qort
entries.a: Yes. Ravencoin (RVN) is one of Q-Trade's cross-chain coins for trades with QORT. Offers from other users set the price; check the amounts and fees before you commit.

entries.q: Can DGB be traded?
aliases: can i trade digibyte for qort
entries.a: Yes. DigiByte (DGB) is in Q-Trade's coin list for trades with QORT. As with every pair, a trade depends on open offers and on having enough balance for fees on both sides.

entries.q: Why create LTC with the account?
aliases: why does qortal have an ltc wallet
do i need to back up my ltc wallet
why does my qortal account have litecoin
entries.a: Litecoin is the main way into QORT: you fund the LTC wallet in your Qortal account from any exchange, then swap LTC for QORT in Q-Trade. Hub and GO make that wallet, and the wallets for BTC, DOGE, DGB, RVN and ARRR, from your Qortal account's keys, so your Qortal backup restores them too and there is no separate seed to keep.

entries.q: What is an unconfirmed chat message?
aliases: what is a chat transaction qortal
entries.a: In legacy Q-Chat, each message is a CHAT transaction that never goes into a block: nodes pass it around as unconfirmed, and it drops off after about 24 hours. It pays no fee; instead the sender's device does a small proof-of-work, which is quicker with at least 4 QORT in the balance. Reticulum Q-Chat, the default now, does not use chain transactions at all.

entries.q: Raspberry Pi node tips?
aliases: qortal pi ssd not sd card
entries.a: Use a Raspberry Pi-class board with at least 4 GB of RAM (8 GB is more comfortable) and run it from a quality SSD, not an SD card. Give it steady power (a UPS helps) and a wired connection, follow your own name, and keep Core updated. Minting needs uptime, not raw power, so a lean always-on board works for many minters.

entries.q: Can I run a node on a laptop?
aliases: can i run qortal core on my laptop
entries.a: Yes, but laptops sleep and travel — uptime suffers for minting. Fine for learning and light use; for serious minting, a small always-on box is happier.

entries.q: What is node hygiene?
aliases: how to look after my qortal node
entries.a: Keep Core updated, back up seeds offline, monitor disk, confirm minting activity if you mint, and maintain sane peer connectivity. A neglected node eventually fails at the worst time — usually during sync catch-up after a long sleep.

entries.q: Can non-minters use Qortal fully?
aliases: do i have to mint to use qortal
entries.a: Yes. Minting is optional. Non-minters can hold QORT, register names, publish QDN content, chat, trade, and run apps. Minting is how you earn issuance and deepen governance weight — not a ticket required for basic use.

entries.q: What is the Welcome to Qortal Q-App?
entries.a: Welcome to Qortal is a Q-App that orients newcomers to the network — first steps, concepts, and where to go next. Open it as APP “Welcome to Qortal” (qortal://APP/Welcome to Qortal).

entries.q: What is the Q-Minter Guide?
entries.a: Q-Minter Guide is the WEBSITE published as Q-Minter on QDN — a precise minting handbook. Open qortal://WEBSITE/Q-Minter. For nominations and admin voting use the Q-Mintership Q-App.

entries.q: How does the new nomination system work?
entries.a:
Nomination is how minting rights are granted today; it replaced sponsorship.
1. A Level 5+ minter publishes your nomination card on the Minter Board in Q-Mintership.
2. A poll opens; community and Minter Admin votes are counted separately.
3. About 40% Minter Admin yes votes unlock the admin actions.
4. An admin creates a MINTER group invite, which needs signatures from about 40% of the Minter Admins to become active.
5. You accept with JOIN_GROUP, start minting from Minting in Qortal Hub (the sprout icon), and keep a synced full node online.
You cannot nominate yourself. The Q-Minter guide covers every step.

entries.q: Who is on the Qortal team?
entries.a: qortal.dev's Team page lists the Dev Admins: Jason Crowe (original Qortal founder and Q-App developer), Ice (founder and core developer), Siddi (core network and Reticulum developer), Phillip Lang (user interface developer), Justin Ferrari (marketer and developer), Kenny Cudworth (core development consultant), Qortal Seth (Q-App developer and tester), Gisele (community administrator and tester) and Nicola (interface developer). The list can change, so check that page for the current team.

entries.q: What can I do on Qortal?
aliases: what can you do on Qortal
what is there to do on Qortal
what can I use Qortal for
