entries.a: On Qortal you can hold and send QORT and trade it for LTC, BTC, DOGE, RVN, DGB or ARRR in Q-Trade. You can chat in Q-Chat groups, channels and DMs, with voice calls; send encrypted Q-Mail; post on Torq; register names; and publish files (Q-Share), videos (Q-Tube), websites (Qortal Web Builder) and your own Q-Apps on QDN. You can also run a node and, with minting rights, mint QORT. Minting is optional. The Welcome to Qortal Q-App is a good first stop.

entries.q: What is a Qortal node?
aliases: what does a qortal node do
how do I sync my qortal node
what is a node in qortal
entries.a: A Qortal node (Qortal Core) is software that checks the blockchain, talks to peers and can host QDN data. Hub and Qortal GO are the apps that talk to a node, your own or a public one. Syncing means downloading and checking blocks until your node has caught up with the network; the first sync can take several hours, and a bootstrap download can speed it up. Your own node is optional for browsing but needed for full independence and minting.

entries.q: Can I mint without a nomination?
aliases: do I need nomination to mint
is a nomination required to mint
entries.a: No. Minting rights come through nomination: a Level 5+ minter publishes your card in Q-Mintership, Minter Admins vote, and you accept the MINTER group invite. Then you start minting from Minting in Qortal Hub and keep your node online. You cannot switch minting on by yourself. Until then you can still hold QORT, chat, register a name and publish on QDN.

entries.q: How do I send QORT to someone?
entries.a: In Hub or GO, open Send QORT, enter the recipient's Qortal address (it starts with Q) or registered name, set the amount, check the fee and confirm. In GO you can also scan a QR code. Double-check the recipient: a sent payment cannot be undone. Keep a little extra QORT for fees. Nobody legitimate will ask for your seed phrase to "test" a payment.

entries.q: Can I use Qortal without a computer?
aliases: do I need a computer for qortal
entries.a: Yes, for everyday use. Qortal GO on Android holds your account and wallet, opens Q-Apps and websites, runs Q-Chat with DMs and calls, and connects to a public node, so you do not need a computer. Minting is different: it needs your own always-on node (Qortal Core) on a computer, a Raspberry Pi-class board, a VPS or a QORTector. Many people use GO on the go and keep a node at home.

entries.q: What is the price of QORT?
entries.a: There is no single official QORT price: peer offers set the rate, and LTC is the main QORT market. Qortino runs offline, so it cannot see live offers and will never invent USD or BTC figures. For a live rate, open Q-Trade, Qortal's trade portal, or ask in Q-Chat.

entries.q: What are QDN coordinates?
aliases: how to address a qdn resource
entries.a: Every QDN object is addressed by name (publisher's registered name controlling update rights), service (IMAGE, JSON, APP, WEBSITE, etc.), and optional identifier (distinguishes multiple resources per name+service). Omit identifier or use "default" for the main website/app for a name.

entries.q: Do I need a registered name to publish from a Q-App?
entries.a: Yes. Publishing from a Q-App requires the user to own a registered name; name ownership gates update rights for that name's resources. Call GET_USER_ACCOUNT then GET_ACCOUNT_NAMES, and if there is no name, explain that publish cannot proceed until they register one.

entries.q: How do I detect if qortalRequest is available?
entries.a: Resolve the bridge with window.qortalRequest ?? window.parent?.qortalRequest (and top if nested). If typeof req !== "function", the page is not inside Hub—show preview mode and refuse wallet/payment fakes. Example: async function qr(p){ const r=window.qortalRequest??window.parent?.qortalRequest; if(typeof r!=="function") throw new Error("Open inside Qortal Hub"); return r(p); }

entries.q: When should I use qortalRequest vs fetch?
aliases: when to use REST in q-app
entries.a: Use qortalRequest for wallet identity, signing, publish, encrypt, payments, and anything personalized. Use relative fetch("/names/foo") inside Hub for anonymous public Core REST reads. fetch cannot see the logged-in wallet; never hardcode the local node address (127.0.0.1:12391) in shipped apps.

entries.q: What is the authority order for Q-App API docs?
entries.a: When sources conflict: (1) the user's running Qortal Core + Hub version, (2) Q-Apps.md in Core, (3) qortal.dev/docs/q-apps, (4) community guides for patterns only. Do not invent parameters; verify action names in qortal.dev or Core q-apps.js.

entries.q: What are typical Q-App constraints?
entries.a: No private backend holding secrets; identity is wallet address plus optional name; ship fonts/JS/assets in the zip (offline and CSP-safe); no required CDN. Prefer single-file HTML for small tools and Vite with a flat zip for production SPAs.

entries.q: How should I package a Q-App zip?
entries.a: Zip the contents of dist/, not a wrapper folder: index.html must sit at the zip root, with assets/ and manifest.json beside it. Use relative paths (./assets/...), Vite base: "./", case-sensitive [a-z0-9._-] names, and ship fonts/JS in-bundle with no required CDN. Rebuild and re-zip after any HTML or bundler config change.

entries.q: What goes in manifest.json for a Q-App?
entries.a: Include at least "main": "index.html" plus title, version, and category metadata. The manifest sits at the zip root next to index.html so Hub knows the entry point. Keep paths relative and consistent with the built assets.

entries.q: How do I publish a new Q-App?
entries.a: Build (npm run build), create a flat zip from dist/, load it in Hub and Preview, then publish under an owned name with service APP. Open via qortal://APP/<Name>. Multi-file APP/WEBSITE publish from inside a Q-App is limited or unavailable in many Hub builds—use Hub UI and verify your version.

entries.q: How do I publish a WEBSITE resource in code?
entries.a: Build a static site with relative paths, then publish via Hub under an owned registered name with service WEBSITE. Link with qortal://WEBSITE/<Name>/... . If you need SPA routing and heavy qortalRequest throughout, prefer APP instead of WEBSITE.

entries.q: Why is my Q-App a grey screen or stuck on Loading?
entries.a: Usually assets/index-*.js 404s: Hub opened without trailing slash so ./assets resolves wrong, or you zipped a dist/ wrapper, used absolute /assets/ paths, or shipped a stale hashed build. Fix with flat zip, base: "./", relative ./assets/, full rebuild, and trailing slash or careful <base href>. Some builds also fail on crossorigin script tags—remove if needed.

entries.q: What Vite base should I use for Q-Apps?
entries.a: Set Vite base: "./" so built asset URLs are relative. Absolute /assets/... paths break under Hub render URLs like /render/APP/YourName without a trailing slash. After changing base, rebuild and create a fresh flat zip.

entries.q: Should I use <base href> in a Q-App?
entries.a: Avoid <base href> unless you deliberately fix APP path resolution when Hub serves without a trailing slash. Prefer relative ./assets/ paths and ensuring the app URL has a trailing slash. Mis-set base can break deep links and asset loading.

entries.q: What is the publish workflow after building?
entries.a: 1) npm run build → dist/ 2) (cd dist && zip -r ../MyApp.zip .) 3) Hub → load zip → Preview 4) Publish service APP (or WEBSITE via Hub) 5) Open qortal://APP/<Name> or qortal://WEBSITE/<Name>/. Always Preview before QDN publish.

entries.q: What is the JSON service used for?
entries.a: JSON holds small structured metadata on QDN, typically capped around 25 KB. Publish with PUBLISH_QDN_RESOURCE using UTF-8-safe data64. For larger structured data use DOCUMENT or FILE. Always validate schema on fetch—never trust identifier alone.

entries.q: What is the DOCUMENT service?
entries.a: DOCUMENT stores larger text/JSON documents with a much higher size allowance than JSON (request caps can reach hundreds of MB depending on Core). Use DOCUMENT when metadata outgrows the ~25 KB JSON limit. DOCUMENT_PRIVATE (801) is the encrypted variant for recipients.

entries.q: What are IMAGE and THUMBNAIL services?
entries.a: IMAGE and THUMBNAIL store media on QDN (typical documented limits ~10 MB for IMAGE and ~500 KB for THUMBNAIL). Fetch via FETCH_QDN_RESOURCE or GET_QDN_RESOURCE_URL for . Shared convention: THUMBNAIL + identifier qortal_avatar for user avatars.

entries.q: What are FILE, VIDEO, and AUDIO services?
entries.a: FILE, VIDEO, and AUDIO hold binary payloads on QDN for downloads and media apps (e.g. Q-Share/Q-Tube patterns). Publish as single-file/data64 resources; fetch with FETCH_QDN_RESOURCE or resource URLs. Prefer SAVE_FILE on mobile instead of relying on blob anchor downloads.

entries.q: What is the APP service size limit?
entries.a: APP multi-file zips are commonly limited around 50 MB (check your Core docs). Keep bundles lean: no CDN, tree-shake, and avoid shipping unused assets. WEBSITE is also multi-file; both need filepath when fetching individual files.

entries.q: When is a resource single-file vs multi-file?
entries.a: JSON, IMAGE, FILE, VIDEO, AUDIO and similar services carry one payload (data64 or file). WEBSITE, APP, and GIF_REPOSITORY are multi-file; FETCH_QDN_RESOURCE requires filepath to load a specific file. Choose single-file services for records; use APP/WEBSITE for UI bundles.

entries.q: What are BLOG_POST, MAIL, and MESSAGE services?
entries.a: These are ecosystem-oriented QDN services used by apps like Q-Blog and Q-Mail (MAIL/MAIL_PRIVATE, MESSAGE, BLOG_POST). Follow each app's identifier conventions and validate payloads. Size and schema vary by app—study reference repos before publishing into those namespaces.

entries.q: What services do reference apps use?
entries.a: Q-Mail uses MAIL/MAIL_PRIVATE; Q-Share uses FILE/DOCUMENT; Q-Tube uses VIDEO/BLOG_POST; Q-Shop uses STORE/PRODUCT plus payments. Study their GitHub zips for packaging and qortalRequest patterns before inventing parallel conventions.

entries.q: How should I name QDN identifiers?
entries.a: Prefix identifiers with your app slug, e.g. myapp_config_v1 or myapp_post_<id>. QDN is permissionless—validate payload schema and never trust identifier alone. Use versioned schema strings in JSON (myapp-index-v1) and document the scheme in your README.

entries.q: What is the default identifier?
entries.a: For a name's main website or app, omit identifier or use "default". In qortal:// paths you can include default when you need explicit no-identifier semantics. Shared cross-app locations use well-known identifiers like qortal_avatar.

entries.q: What is the qortal_avatar convention?
entries.a: User avatars commonly use service THUMBNAIL with identifier qortal_avatar under the user's registered name. Fetch with FETCH_QDN_RESOURCE or GET_QDN_RESOURCE_URL for display. Always handle missing avatars gracefully.

entries.q: How do I get names for a wallet address?
entries.a: After GET_USER_ACCOUNT, call GET_ACCOUNT_NAMES with the address (and limit/offset). Use the primary name for publishing. Example: await qr({ action: "GET_ACCOUNT_NAMES", address: acc.address, limit: 10, offset: 0 }).

entries.q: What does GET_NAME_DATA return?
entries.a: GET_NAME_DATA returns name owner and metadata for a registered name. Use it to verify ownership or show profile info before trusting a publisher name. Combine with payload schema validation—name alone does not prove content quality.

entries.q: How do latest publishes work for the same resource?
entries.a: For a given name + service + identifier triple, the latest publish wins. Updates overwrite prior payload for that coordinate. Design identifiers so each logical object has a stable key, or version identifiers when you need immutable history.

entries.q: How do I search resources by identifier prefix?
entries.a: Use SEARCH_QDN_RESOURCES with prefix: true and a minimal payload (service + identifier prefix). Keep optional fields stripped if search returns empty mysteriously. Normalize the response to an array—cores may wrap results in resources/results/entries/hits/data.

entries.q: Why do unprefixed identifiers cause problems?
entries.a: Global QDN namespaces collide easily. Unprefixed ids make discovery and ownership intent unclear and invite cross-app confusion. Always use appslug_type_id style identifiers and validate every fetched JSON schema.

entries.q: How should multi-app ecosystems structure resources?
entries.a: Publish a WEBSITE for visitors, separate APP tools, and small JSON/DOCUMENT indexes for discovery. Use stable identifier prefixes, versioned schema strings, SEARCH_QDN_RESOURCES with prefix: true, and open partners via qortal:// or LINK_TO_QDN_RESOURCE. Never assume identifier proves origin.

entries.q: What FILE identifier pattern do blog/mail apps use?
entries.a: File attachments in blog/mail-style apps often use FILE with identifiers like qfile_…. Follow the host app's documented prefix so other clients can find attachments. Validate mime/size from GET_QDN_RESOURCE_PROPERTIES before rendering.

entries.q: How do I authenticate the user in a Q-App?
entries.a: Call GET_USER_ACCOUNT from an explicit Connect/Authenticate button after a user gesture—never on first paint. It returns address and publicKey and shows an approval popup. Opening built index.html in a normal browser cannot complete wallet auth.

entries.q: What if my Q-App runs in a nested iframe and auth fails?
entries.a: Resolve qortalRequest from window → parent → top. Parent pages may need a message relay that forwards qortalRequest to Hub. If parent === top and only a stub exists, or inner auth still fails, open the target in a new Hub tab.

entries.q: Which qortalRequest actions require user approval?
entries.a: Approval-gated examples include GET_USER_ACCOUNT, wallet info/balance variants, PUBLISH_QDN_RESOURCE, PUBLISH_MULTIPLE_QDN_RESOURCES, SEND_COIN, JOIN_GROUP, DEPLOY_AT, CREATE_POLL/VOTE_ON_POLL, SAVE_FILE, list item mutations, and friends/profile writes. Batch reads; keep approval calls behind clear user actions.

entries.q: Which qortalRequest actions are read-only without approval?
entries.a: Examples: GET_ACCOUNT_DATA, GET_ACCOUNT_NAMES, GET_NAME_DATA, GET_BALANCE, FETCH_QDN_RESOURCE, LIST_QDN_RESOURCES, SEARCH_QDN_RESOURCES, GET_QDN_RESOURCE_STATUS/METADATA/PROPERTIES/URL, SEARCH_NAMES, SEARCH_TRANSACTIONS, FETCH_BLOCK, group/AT list reads, GET_PRICE. Prefer these for background refresh.

entries.q: How do I implement preview mode?
entries.a: If qortalRequest is missing on window and parent, show "Preview mode" and allow mock reads only. Never fake successful payments or publishes. Prompt the user to open the app inside Qortal Hub for live APIs.

entries.q: Can fetch tell me who is logged in?
entries.a: No. Relative fetch hits the node REST API anonymously and cannot identify the logged-in wallet. Use qortalRequest GET_USER_ACCOUNT (and related wallet actions) for anything personalized or signing-related.

entries.q: How do I fetch a QDN resource?
entries.a: Use FETCH_QDN_RESOURCE with name, service, and optional identifier; add filepath for multi-file APP/WEBSITE; set encoding: "base64" when you need binary-safe data. Example: await qr({ action: "FETCH_QDN_RESOURCE", name, service: "JSON", identifier: id }).

entries.q: How do I publish a JSON resource?
entries.a: Own a name, UTF-8-encode JSON to data64 (never raw btoa on Unicode), then PUBLISH_QDN_RESOURCE. Example: await qr({ action: "PUBLISH_QDN_RESOURCE", name, service: "JSON", identifier: id, data64: b64Utf8(obj) }). Await user approval and handle cancel vs errors.

entries.q: How do I safely base64-encode UTF-8 JSON for publish?
entries.a: Never btoa(JSON.stringify(obj)) on Unicode. Use TextEncoder: const bytes=new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify(obj)); let bin=""; for(const b of bytes) bin+=String.fromCharCode(b); return btoa(bin);. Decode symmetrically when reading base64 text.

entries.q: How do I search QDN resources?
entries.a: Call SEARCH_QDN_RESOURCES with a minimal payload (service, optional name/identifier, prefix: true for prefixes). Normalize array-or-wrapper responses. If results are mysteriously empty, strip unknown optional keys—extra fields can yield [].

entries.q: How do I list QDN resources for a name?
entries.a: LIST_QDN_RESOURCES lists by name/service with richer filters than search in some builds. Example: await qr({ action: "LIST_QDN_RESOURCES", name: "Qortino", service: "FILE", limit: 20 }). Prefer listing when you know the publisher name.

entries.q: What is GET_QDN_RESOURCE_URL for?
entries.a: GET_QDN_RESOURCE_URL returns a URL suitable for or fetch (often /arbitrary/...). Use it for media display without manually building paths. On mobile, append ?attachment=true when you need native download handling.

entries.q: What is GET_QDN_RESOURCE_STATUS?
entries.a: GET_QDN_RESOURCE_STATUS reports build/load status such as READY and percent loaded. Probe status without downloading the full payload—useful before playing VIDEO/AUDIO or large FILE resources.

entries.q: What is GET_QDN_RESOURCE_METADATA?
entries.a: GET_QDN_RESOURCE_METADATA returns title, tags, category and similar metadata without fetching the full payload. Use it for cards, search UIs, and galleries. Pair with PROPERTIES for filename/mimeType/size.

entries.q: What is GET_QDN_RESOURCE_PROPERTIES?
entries.a: GET_QDN_RESOURCE_PROPERTIES returns filename, mimeType, and size for a resource. Use before download/preview to show size and choose renderers. Validate mime types from untrusted publishers.

entries.q: What is PUBLISH_MULTIPLE_QDN_RESOURCES?
entries.a: PUBLISH_MULTIPLE_QDN_RESOURCES batch-publishes several resources to reduce approval rounds. Feature-detect availability for the user's Hub version. Prefer batches for related metadata+thumbnail publishes behind one clear user action.

entries.q: How do I normalize SEARCH_QDN_RESOURCES results?
entries.a: Cores may return a bare array or an object with resources, results, entries, hits, or data arrays. Coerce: const arr = Array.isArray(r) ? r : (r?.resources ?? r?.results ?? r?.entries ?? r?.hits ?? r?.data ?? []);. Always Array.isArray-check before map.

entries.q: How do I open another QDN resource from my app?
entries.a: Prefer LINK_TO_QDN_RESOURCE or OPEN_NEW_TAB with a qortal:// URL. For Hub tab switches, postMessage SET_TAB with { action: 'SET_TAB', requestedHandler: 'UI', payload: { service, name, identifier?, path? } }. Avoid raw window.open to localhost.

entries.q: What is QDN_RESOURCE_DISPLAYED?
entries.a: Call QDN_RESOURCE_DISPLAYED so Hub's address bar/copy-link matches the sub-path the user sees: { action, service, name, path? }. Useful for multi-page WEBSITE SPAs. Optionally keep <link rel="canonical"> with matching qortal://WEBSITE/<name>/<slug>.

entries.q: How should SPA routing work inside Hub?
entries.a: Published apps often run under /render/WEBSITE/<name>/ or /render/APP/<name>/. Use pathname segments with history.pushState/popstate for in-app navigation without leaving Hub. Preserve intentional hash fragments when cleaning pathnames with replaceState.

entries.q: How do hash deep links work in Q-Apps?
entries.a: SPAs may use location.hash for anchors (e.g. #section-id). If you use multiple prefixes like #folder- and #folderdir-, parse longest match first—naive startsWith('folder-') breaks on substrings. Preserve hashes across history.replaceState cleanup.

entries.q: What is NAVIGATION_HISTORY for?
entries.a: NAVIGATION_HISTORY integrates back/forward with Hub (availability is Hub-dependent). Use it when your SPA should participate in Hub navigation chrome. Always feature-detect and provide in-app back affordances as fallback.

entries.q: How do I encrypt data with qortalRequest?
entries.a: Use ENCRYPT_DATA with file or base64 payload; pass optional publicKeys for group encryption. Store ciphertext under separate identifier namespaces from public metadata. Explain the encrypt action to the user before calling.

entries.q: How do I decrypt data with qortalRequest?
entries.a: Use DECRYPT_DATA with ciphertext base64 and the counterparty publicKey. Group variants ENCRYPT_QORTAL_GROUP_DATA / DECRYPT_QORTAL_GROUP_DATA handle group-scoped encryption. Handle user cancel and wrong-key errors distinctly.

entries.q: Should encrypted and public data share identifiers?
entries.a: No. Use separate identifier namespaces for encrypted blobs versus public JSON indexes. That prevents accidental public fetch of private coordinates and clarifies schema. Still validate decrypted payloads before use.

entries.q: How do QORT amounts work in APIs?
entries.a: SEND_COIN takes the amount as plain QORT, for example 1.5, not multiplied by 1e8; Hub or GO shows it in the approval window. QORT has up to 8 decimal places. For other APIs, check how each response field is written before converting it.

entries.q: How do I send coins from a Q-App?
entries.a: Use SEND_COIN / SEND_PAYMENT / TRANSFER_ASSET only after explaining amounts and recipients; these require user approval. Confirm parameters against the target Hub version. Treat payment success and any follow-up notification as separate steps—payment can succeed while notify fails.

entries.q: How do I sign and broadcast a transaction?
entries.a: Use SIGN_TRANSACTION for a Hub-signed transaction, then broadcast via REST /transactions/process. Keep signing behind an explicit user action and never handle seed phrases. Verify the exact payload shape for your Core version.

entries.q: How do I create a poll?
entries.a: CREATE_POLL requires pollOptions as an array (e.g. objects with optionName), not a string, and pollName must be unique. VOTE_ON_POLL casts a vote with user approval. Validate options client-side before calling.

entries.q: How do group actions work?
entries.a: LIST_GROUPS, JOIN_GROUP, and GET_GROUPS_WITH_MEMBER manage membership. JOIN_GROUP requires approval. Use groups with ENCRYPT_QORTAL_GROUP_DATA when sharing private payloads among members. Feature-detect and handle cancel.

entries.q: Why is SEARCH_TRANSACTIONS message often missing?
entries.a: Payment matching via SEARCH_TRANSACTIONS often lacks a reliable message field. Match by reference, type, amounts (1e8 scale), and parties instead of free-text memo. Design payment protocols that do not depend on message alone.

entries.q: How do I save files on Qortal Go / mobile?
entries.a: Mobile WebViews often ignore anchor/blob downloads. Use SAVE_FILE with blob + filename, or /arbitrary/…?attachment=true on builds with a native download listener. Detect mobile via user-agent when choosing download strategy.

entries.q: How should I handle data larger than the JSON 25 KB limit?
entries.a: Do not stuff oversized objects into JSON. Split: small JSON metadata (index, titles, pointers) plus FILE/DOCUMENT/IMAGE/VIDEO payloads under related identifiers. For very large content, chunk into multiple FILE parts with a versioned index JSON describing order and hashes.

entries.q: What is a good chunking pattern for large files?
entries.a: Publish a JSON index (myapp_file_<id>_meta_v1) with part count, sizes, and SHA-256 hashes, then publish parts as FILE identifiers myapp_file_<id>_part_0001…. Fetch status before each part; reassemble client-side; verify hashes. Bound concurrency—avoid Promise.all on hundreds of fetches.

entries.q: Why avoid Promise.all on hundreds of QDN fetches?
entries.a: Unbounded concurrency overwhelms Core/Hub, triggers timeouts, and freezes UI. Use a small worker pool (e.g. 3–6) with retries and backoff. Prefer GET_QDN_RESOURCE_STATUS before heavy FETCH on large media.

entries.q: How should I handle qortalRequest timeouts?
entries.a: Timeouts are per-action in Core q-apps.js. Fix payload size and batching rather than wrapping everything in huge timeouts. Prefer Core-managed timeouts; qortalRequestWithTimeout exists but letting Core manage limits is more futureproof. Use longer helpers only for publish/payment UX.

entries.q: How should I test a new Q-App?
entries.a: Test root URL, deep links, no-name wallet (publish gated), Connect gesture, publish then fetch after propagation delay, search normalization, and grey-screen asset loads. Use Hub Preview before QDN publish; when Core supports it, local preview is the node's /render/APP/<Name>?preview=true path on port 12391.

entries.q: What should I test for packaging?
entries.a: After zip: open in Hub Preview, confirm Network shows assets/index-*.js as 200, navigate SPA routes, hard-refresh, and re-open via qortal://APP/<Name>. Catch absolute /assets/ paths and stale hashed filenames before publishing.

entries.q: How do I test auth edge cases?
entries.a: Cover: user cancels GET_USER_ACCOUNT; wallet with zero names; nested iframe without relay; opening index.html outside Hub (preview mode). Ensure publish buttons stay disabled without a name and errors are human-readable.

entries.q: What security rules apply to Q-Apps?
entries.a: Never collect seed phrases or private keys. Treat all QDN JSON as untrusted—validate schema and sizes. Explain publishes, payments, and decrypt before calling qortalRequest. Sanitize any HTML from QDN to prevent XSS. Rate-limit retries; distinguish user cancel vs technical errors.

entries.q: Why sanitize HTML from QDN?
entries.a: Anyone can publish under their own name; fetched HTML/Markdown can contain scripts. Escape or sanitize before innerHTML. Prefer text content or a vetted sanitizer. Never eval remote JS from QDN.

entries.q: How do relative fetch calls work inside Hub?
entries.a: Inside Hub, fetch("/names/foo") hits the user's node API—good for public reads (blocks, names, arbitrary endpoints). Do not hardcode 127.0.0.1:12391. For personalized or signing flows use qortalRequest instead.

entries.q: What is the difference between QDN search mode ALL and LATEST?
entries.a: REST QDN search modes mode=ALL vs mode=LATEST change whether you see historical publishes or only latest per coordinate. Wrong mode causes duplicates or wrong counts. Prefer LATEST for current app state unless you need history.

entries.q: Where is the REST API documentation?
entries.a: Use the API documentation on api.qortal.org for node REST fields. Cross-check field names when debugging bridge vs REST mismatches. For qortalRequest actions, prefer the Q-Apps docs on qortal.dev and Core's Q-Apps.md.

entries.q: Where are official Q-App docs?
entries.a: Authoritative qortalRequest reference: the Q-Apps docs on qortal.dev. Protocol: Q-Apps.md in the Qortal/qortal repository. Core implementation and timeouts: q-apps.js in Qortal/qortal. REST: api.qortal.org. Community code: gitea.qortal.link and the Qortal organisation on GitHub.

entries.q: What GitHub repos should Q-App developers study?
entries.a: Qortal/qortal (Core, Q-Apps.md, q-apps.js), Qortal/Qortal-Hub, optional Qortal/qapp-core helpers, and reference apps q-mail, q-share, q-tube, q-shop. Community projects also live on gitea.qortal.link.

entries.q: What is qapp-core?
entries.a: Qortal/qapp-core is an optional npm helper library for Q-App development. It can wrap common bridge patterns, but you should still understand raw qortalRequest and verify actions against your Hub/Core version.

entries.q: How do I publish a thumbnail with metadata?
entries.a: Publish IMAGE or THUMBNAIL for the media and a small JSON record with title, tags, category, and pointer identifiers. Or set metadata fields supported by your publish action and read them later via GET_QDN_RESOURCE_METADATA. Keep JSON ≤25 KB; put heavy media in IMAGE/VIDEO/FILE.

entries.q: How do I show a resource thumbnail in the UI?
entries.a: Resolve a URL with GET_QDN_RESOURCE_URL for the THUMBNAIL/IMAGE coordinate, or fetch base64 and build a blob URL. Check GET_QDN_RESOURCE_STATUS before display for large media. Provide a placeholder when missing.

entries.q: How do I read title and tags without downloading the file?
entries.a: Call GET_QDN_RESOURCE_METADATA for title, tags, and category without the full payload. Use GET_QDN_RESOURCE_PROPERTIES for filename, mimeType, and size. Ideal for galleries and search result rows.

entries.q: What is the recommended new Q-App workflow?
entries.a: Choose single HTML vs Vite/React; scaffold index.html + manifest with relative paths; centralize qortalRequest; Connect → GET_USER_ACCOUNT → GET_ACCOUNT_NAMES → gate publish; design identifier/schema; read with FETCH/SEARCH (+normalize); write with UTF-8 data64; test edge cases; flat zip → Hub Preview → publish APP.

entries.q: How should I structure a central bridge module?
entries.a: Export one qr(payload) that resolves window/parent/top qortalRequest, wraps try/catch, and optionally short vs long timeout helpers for publish/payments. All features call this module so iframe/mobile differences stay in one place.

entries.q: What is a minimal Connect then publish pattern?
entries.a: On Connect: account = GET_USER_ACCOUNT; names = GET_ACCOUNT_NAMES; pick primary name. On publish: PUBLISH_QDN_RESOURCE with owned name, service, identifier, data64. Then FETCH_QDN_RESOURCE to verify. Disable publish when no name exists.

entries.q: How do I wait for publish propagation?
entries.a: After PUBLISH_QDN_RESOURCE, fetches/search may lag briefly. Retry FETCH or STATUS with backoff, or poll GET_QDN_RESOURCE_STATUS until READY. Do not assume instant global visibility; design UI for "publishing…" states.

entries.q: How do I feature-detect optional publish batching?
entries.a: Try PUBLISH_MULTIPLE_QDN_RESOURCES inside try/catch; on failure fall back to sequential PUBLISH_QDN_RESOURCE with clear progress. Do not invent parameters—check qortal.dev for the user's version.

entries.q: What causes SEARCH_QDN_RESOURCES to return empty unexpectedly?
entries.a: Unknown or extra JSON keys on the search payload can yield empty results on some cores. Use a minimal payload, enable prefix: true only when intended, and normalize wrapped responses. Also confirm service/name/identifier spelling and case.

entries.q: What is the SPA asset trap under /render/APP?
entries.a: Hub may open /render/APP/YourName without a trailing slash, so ./assets/index.js resolves against /render/APP/ and 404s. Fix with trailing slash, careful <base href>, or paths matching how Hub serves the resource. Rebuild after HTML changes.

entries.q: Why shouldn't Q-Apps depend on external CDNs?
entries.a: Hub CSP, offline use, and gateway contexts often block or break CDN scripts/fonts. Bundle JS/CSS/fonts inside the zip with relative paths so the app works offline and consistently across desktop and mobile Hub.

entries.q: What if payment succeeded but notification failed?
entries.a: Treat payment and notification as separate steps. Persist local state that payment confirmed (tx signature/reference) even if a follow-up QDN publish or chat notify fails, then retry notify without charging again.

entries.q: Why are case-sensitive paths important in zips?
entries.a: QDN/Hub serving is case-sensitive. Mismatched Asset vs asset paths work on some desktop FS previews and fail in Hub. Prefer lowercase [a-z0-9._-] filenames and matching import paths from the bundler.

entries.q: What does a minimal qortalRequest helper look like?
entries.a: async function qr(payload){ const req=window.qortalRequest??window.parent?.qortalRequest; if(typeof req!=="function") throw new Error("Open inside Qortal Hub"); return req(payload); } Always try/catch at call sites. Extend resolution to top for nested iframes.

entries.q: How do I load demo JSON after connect in a skeleton app?
entries.a: After Connect obtains a primary name, PUBLISH_QDN_RESOURCE a small JSON with identifier myapp_demo_<timestamp> and data64 from b64Utf8, then FETCH_QDN_RESOURCE the same coordinates and display the result. Disable the load/publish button until a name exists.

entries.q: How do Hub themes affect my Q-App UI?
entries.a: Read window._qdnTheme ("light"|"dark") and style accordingly so the app matches Hub chrome. Re-check on visibility changes if Hub can toggle theme while open. Avoid assuming dark mode defaults.

entries.q: How do I keep Hub copy-link accurate for WEBSITE subpages?
entries.a: On each route change, call QDN_RESOURCE_DISPLAYED with service WEBSITE, name, and path. Optionally update canonical qortal://WEBSITE/<name>/<slug>. Without this, copy-link may point only at the site root.

entries.q: Should Connect buttons meet mobile touch targets?
entries.a: Yes. Use adequate tap targets (e.g. min-height ~44px) for Connect, Publish, and payment buttons. Mobile Hub and Qortal Go are primary surfaces—avoid hover-only UX and tiny icon-only critical actions.

entries.q: What is GIF_REPOSITORY?
entries.a: GIF_REPOSITORY is a multi-file QDN service type (like APP/WEBSITE) requiring filepath on fetch. Use it for gif packs rather than APP UI. Confirm size limits and publish path via Hub for your Core version.

entries.q: Can I use STORE or PRODUCT services?
entries.a: Q-Shop-style apps use STORE/PRODUCT services plus payment actions. Follow Q-Shop conventions for identifiers and JSON schemas rather than inventing incompatible shapes if you want ecosystem interoperability. Always validate foreign product JSON.

entries.q: How do I publish an IMAGE?
entries.a: Use PUBLISH_QDN_RESOURCE with service IMAGE, owned name, identifier, and file or data64 payload within size limits (~10 MB typical). Pair with JSON metadata for title/alt. Fetch via GET_QDN_RESOURCE_URL for display.

entries.q: How do I publish a VIDEO or AUDIO resource?
entries.a: Publish service VIDEO or AUDIO with file/data64 under a namespaced identifier, keep a small JSON index for title/thumbnail pointers, and probe GET_QDN_RESOURCE_STATUS before playback. Use SAVE_FILE or attachment URLs for downloads on mobile.

entries.q: How do I publish a FILE for download?
entries.a: PUBLISH_QDN_RESOURCE with service FILE, owned name, identifier (e.g. myapp_file_<id>), and payload. Expose downloads via GET_QDN_RESOURCE_URL; on mobile prefer SAVE_FILE. Store filename/mime in metadata or rely on PROPERTIES.

entries.q: What is GET_ACCOUNT_DATA?
entries.a: GET_ACCOUNT_DATA returns the account record for an address (read-only, typically no approval). Use it for public account fields after you know an address from GET_USER_ACCOUNT or a name lookup.

entries.q: What is GET_BALANCE used for?
entries.a: GET_BALANCE reads a balance for an address without implying the logged-in wallet session. For the user's wallet-specific balance UI, also consider approval-gated wallet balance actions on your Hub version. Remember 1e8 scaling for QORT display.

entries.q: What chain helpers exist via qortalRequest?
entries.a: Common helpers include FETCH_BLOCK, FETCH_BLOCK_RANGE, GET_BLOCK_HEIGHT, GET_PRICE, DEPLOY_AT, GET_AT, GET_AT_DATA, LIST_ATS, and day summary reads. Verify names/params for your Core; wrap in try/catch and prefer relative REST fetch for simple public chain reads.

entries.q: How do I avoid approval-popup fatigue?
entries.a: Batch read-only calls freely; group approval-needing calls behind one explicit user action (Connect, Publish, Pay). Prefer PUBLISH_MULTIPLE_QDN_RESOURCES when available. Never spam GET_USER_ACCOUNT on timers or route changes.

entries.q: What happens if I open index.html in Chrome outside Hub?
entries.a: qortalRequest is missing, so wallet auth, publish, and encrypt cannot work. Show preview mode with mock reads only. Instruct users to open via Hub/Qortal Go. Do not silently fake payments.

entries.q: How do I link to a WEBSITE sub-page?
entries.a: Use qortal://WEBSITE/MySite/gallery (service/name/path). Ensure the WEBSITE zip actually contains that path or APP-style SPA fallback will not apply—WEBSITE 404s missing files. Sync Hub chrome with QDN_RESOURCE_DISPLAYED.

entries.q: How do I link to an APP?
entries.a: Use qortal://APP/MyQApp or OPEN_NEW_TAB / LINK_TO_QDN_RESOURCE with service APP and name. For in-app routes, combine Hub render paths with pushState and optional hash fragments. Prefer Hub navigation APIs over external browsers.

entries.q: What UTF-8 publish bug should I always avoid?
entries.a: Raw btoa(JSON.stringify(obj)) throws or corrupts on Unicode characters. Always TextEncoder → binary string → btoa for data64 JSON publishes. This is a top production pitfall for international text.

entries.q: How do I validate fetched QDN JSON?
entries.a: Check typeof/object shape, required fields, schema version string, and size bounds before use. Reject unknown versions safely. Remember permissionless names: malicious publishers can reuse your identifier patterns under their own name.

entries.q: What is the difference between LIST_QDN_RESOURCES and SEARCH_QDN_RESOURCES?
entries.a: LIST is suited to enumerating resources for a known name/service with richer filters in some builds. SEARCH discovers across the network with prefix options but needs minimal payloads and result normalization. Use LIST when you know the publisher; SEARCH for discovery.

entries.q: How do identifiers work with MAIL or BLOG_POST?
entries.a: Follow each ecosystem app's documented identifier schemes (Q-Mail, Q-Blog) so other clients interoperate. Prefix your own extensions carefully and never overwrite foreign coordinates. Validate payload schemas from those apps' repos.

entries.q: What should I put in a JSON index resource?
entries.a: Keep a versioned schema (v or schema field), lists of child identifiers, titles, timestamps, and content hashes—stay under ~25 KB. Point to FILE/IMAGE/VIDEO for heavy bytes. Publish index updates when parts change.

entries.q: How do private services relate to encryption actions?
entries.a: Private services (*_PRIVATE, 801, etc.) store encrypted payloads for recipients. Use ENCRYPT_DATA / DECRYPT_DATA or group encrypt/decrypt variants with the right public keys. Keep UX copy clear that decryption requires wallet approval.

entries.q: Can I hardcode the Core API port 12391?
entries.a: No—not in shipped apps. Use relative fetch so Hub routes to the user's node, and qortalRequest for wallet flows. Hardcoded localhost breaks remote gateways, mobile, and non-default ports.

entries.q: What is local preview URL for an APP?
entries.a: When Core supports it: the node's /render/APP/<Name>?preview=true path on port 12391 (varies by version). Still prefer Hub Preview for realistic bridge behavior. Confirm assets load under the render path.

entries.q: How do I use GET_QDN_RESOURCE_STATUS before playing video?
entries.a: Poll or await GET_QDN_RESOURCE_STATUS until READY (and acceptable percent loaded) before setting video src or fetching large blobs. Show progress UI; cancel cleanly on navigation away.

entries.q: What parameters does PUBLISH_QDN_RESOURCE need?
entries.a: At minimum: action PUBLISH_QDN_RESOURCE, owned name, service, and payload via data64 or file; identifier recommended for non-default resources. User approval required. Confirm optional metadata fields against qortal.dev for your Hub version—do not invent keys.

entries.q: How do I get a URL for an arbitrary resource path?
entries.a: Prefer GET_QDN_RESOURCE_URL over string-concatenating /arbitrary/... yourself. For multi-file resources include the filepath Hub expects. Append ?attachment=true on mobile when triggering native download listeners.

entries.q: What is OPEN_NEW_TAB used for?
entries.a: OPEN_NEW_TAB opens a new Hub tab with a URL or qortal:// link. Use it for cross-app navigation while staying inside Hub. Prefer it over external browser windows for QDN targets.

entries.q: How does SET_TAB postMessage work?
entries.a: Post a message like { action: 'SET_TAB', requestedHandler: 'UI', payload: { service, name, identifier?, path? } } to switch Hub tabs to a QDN resource. Feature-detect Hub support and fall back to LINK_TO_QDN_RESOURCE or OPEN_NEW_TAB.

entries.q: What friends/profile list actions exist?
entries.a: Hub builds may expose GET_FRIENDS_LIST, SET_PROFILE_DATA, and list item APIs—often approval-gated. Verify against your version's q-apps docs before relying on them. Store cross-user public profile data on QDN when other apps must read it.

entries.q: How do I handle user cancel on approval popups?
entries.a: Catch errors from qortalRequest and branch UX: user cancel should be quiet/non-alarming; technical failures can show retry. Do not loop automatic retries on cancel. Keep buttons re-enabled after cancel.

entries.q: What is SEND_CHAT_MESSAGE used for?
entries.a: SEND_CHAT_MESSAGE (group) sends chat with user approval on supported Hubs. Do not use it as a reliable payment receipt channel. Confirm group context and permissions; handle cancel and rate limits.

entries.q: How should category and tags be used on resources?
entries.a: Set category/tags in publish metadata when supported, and read them via GET_QDN_RESOURCE_METADATA for filtering UIs. Keep tags short and consistent within your app. Do not trust tags for security decisions—validate payload bodies.

entries.q: What is the APP vs WEBSITE choice for a portfolio site?
entries.a: A mostly static portfolio with real 404s for bad URLs should use WEBSITE. If it is an interactive builder/marketplace with client routing, use APP. Confusing the two causes most routing bugs—read that distinction before architecture.

entries.q: How do I fetch a file inside a published APP zip?
entries.a: FETCH_QDN_RESOURCE with service APP, name, optional identifier, and filepath set to the in-zip path (e.g. assets/config.json). Multi-file services require filepath; omitting it will not return a single nested file correctly.

entries.q: What does latest publish wins mean for identifiers?
entries.a: Updating the same name+service+identifier overwrites prior content for readers fetching latest. To keep history, use new identifiers or version suffixes and point the index at the current id. Design for immutability when audits matter.

entries.q: How do I use prefix:true correctly?
entries.a: Pass prefix: true on SEARCH_QDN_RESOURCES when the identifier field is a prefix (e.g. myapp_post_). Without it, many cores expect exact identifier match. Combine with service filter and minimal payload for reliable discovery.

entries.q: What notifications permission actions exist?
entries.a: Some Hub versions expose notifications permission actions alongside SET_TAB_NOTIFICATIONS. Feature-detect, request only from a gesture, and degrade silently if unavailable. Never depend on notifications for critical payment state.

entries.q: How do I debug bridge vs REST field mismatches?
entries.a: Compare qortalRequest responses with the same data from relative fetch against api.qortal.org field names. Log raw payloads in Preview. Prefer bridge for wallet-bound ops and REST/fetch for anonymous public reads.

entries.q: What should an LLM remember before generating Q-App code?
entries.a: Do not confuse WEBSITE and APP; use qortalRequest for wallet/publish/encrypt and relative fetch for public reads; verify actions against Hub/Core; flat zip with base "./"; Connect-button auth; UTF-8 safe base64; prefix identifiers; normalize search arrays; JSON ≤25 KB; try/catch; never handle seeds.

entries.q: How do I register publish rights conceptually?
entries.a: Only the account that owns the registered name can publish/update resources under that name. GET_ACCOUNT_NAMES shows names you control; publishing under someone else's name fails. Plan multi-admin flows via shared wallets/groups carefully.

entries.q: What is GET_USER_WALLET vs GET_USER_ACCOUNT?
entries.a: GET_USER_ACCOUNT returns address/publicKey for identity. GET_USER_WALLET / GET_USER_WALLET_INFO are approval-gated wallet details on some Hubs—use only when needed and verify fields for your version. Prefer the least-privileged action.

entries.q: How do I display QORT prices?
entries.a: Call GET_PRICE (read-only) and divide integer amounts by 1e8 for human QORT. Cache briefly to avoid spamming; handle missing market data. Confirm units before using prices in SEND_COIN UX copy.

entries.q: What is SEARCH_NAMES for?
entries.a: SEARCH_NAMES finds registered names (read-only). Use it for typeahead when linking to publishers. After picking a name, fetch resources with LIST/SEARCH QDN APIs and validate payloads.

entries.q: How should error messages be written for users?
entries.a: Map bridge errors to short actions: open in Hub, connect wallet, register a name, approve the popup, reduce payload size, or retry after publish delay. Avoid dumping raw stacks. Distinguish cancel from failure.

entries.q: How do I keep Q-App builds deterministic for republish?
entries.a: Pin dependency versions, rebuild clean dist/, zip contents only, and bump manifest version. After publish, verify GET_QDN_RESOURCE_PROPERTIES size/hash expectations. Stale hashed assets in an old zip cause eternal Loading.

entries.q: What is the role of Qortal Core vs Hub for Q-Apps?
entries.a: Core validates chain data, stores QDN, and exposes REST. Hub/Mobile/Extension embed the Q-App UI and inject qortalRequest for privileged actions. Your static app talks to both: fetch for public REST, qortalRequest for wallet-scoped operations.

entries.q: How do I open Q-Mail or other apps for a user?
entries.a: Navigate with qortal:// or LINK_TO_QDN_RESOURCE / OPEN_NEW_TAB to the target APP name used by that product. Do not scrape their private coordinates; use documented public identifiers and services. Fail soft if the app is unpublished on that node.

entries.q: What packaging mistake causes /assets 404 specifically?
entries.a: Using absolute /assets/... in the bundler output or HTML, or zipping a parent folder so paths disagree. Set base "./" , verify built index references ./assets/..., and zip dist contents. Check Network tab inside Hub Preview.

entries.q: How do I use encoding base64 on fetch?
entries.a: Pass encoding: "base64" on FETCH_QDN_RESOURCE when you need binary-safe content for files/images. Decode to Uint8Array/Blob in the app. For JSON text, you may get string/object depending on Hub—normalize before parse.

entries.q: What is a safe pattern for Connect button code?
entries.a: btn.onclick = async () => { try { const acc = await qr({ action: "GET_USER_ACCOUNT" }); const names = await qr({ action: "GET_ACCOUNT_NAMES", address: acc.address, limit: 10, offset: 0 }); /* enable publish if names[0] */ } catch (e) { /* show e.message */ } }; Never invoke that on DOMContentLoaded.

entries.q: How do I gate publish UI without a name?
entries.a: After fetching names, disable Publish and show "Register a Qortal name to publish". Do not call PUBLISH_QDN_RESOURCE hoping for a helpful error. Re-check names when the user returns from Hub name registration.

entries.q: What crossorigin script issue can grey-screen an app?
entries.a: Some Hub builds fail loading scripts marked crossorigin, leaving a blank/Loading UI even when files exist. If assets 200 but JS never runs, try removing crossorigin from script tags, rebuild, and re-zip.

entries.q: How do I design identifier namespaces for encrypted mail-like apps?
entries.a: Use public JSON indexes under myapp_pub_* and ciphertext under myapp_priv_* (or private services). ENCRYPT_DATA with recipient publicKeys; DECRYPT_DATA with counterparty publicKey. Never put secrets in public JSON.

entries.q: What is GET_GROUPS_WITH_MEMBER?
entries.a: GET_GROUPS_WITH_MEMBER lists groups that include a member address (read-oriented; confirm approval needs for your version). Use it to personalize group UIs after Connect. Pair with LIST_GROUPS for broader discovery.

entries.q: How do I use polls safely in a Q-App?
entries.a: Ensure pollName uniqueness, pass pollOptions as an array of option objects, confirm copy before CREATE_POLL/VOTE_ON_POLL approvals, and handle cancel. Do not encode critical funds movement only in poll text—use SEND_COIN for payments.

entries.q: What offline-safe rules apply to Q-App assets?
entries.a: Ship all critical JS/CSS/fonts/images in the zip; use relative URLs; avoid CDN and runtime code downloads. QDN itself may still need network to fetch remote resources, but the app shell should render offline once cached by Hub.

entries.q: How do I report resource display to Hub for APP routes?
entries.a: Use QDN_RESOURCE_DISPLAYED with service APP, name, and path when your in-app route should appear in Hub chrome/copy-link. Keep path aligned with what you would put in a qortal:// link.

entries.q: What is the teaching-default artifact for small tools?
entries.a: Default to a single-file HTML Q-App for small tools, and Vite + flat zip for production SPAs. Single-file simplifies packaging (still may zip one html); SPAs need careful relative asset paths and SPA service APP.

entries.q: How do I verify action names before shipping?
entries.a: Check the Q-Apps docs on qortal.dev and Core's q-apps.js for the user's Hub/Core version. Feature-detect optional actions. Do not invent parameters from memory—wrong keys can fail publishes or empty searches.

entries.q: What is TRANSFER_ASSET used for?
entries.a: TRANSFER_ASSET moves assets with user approval (confirm params on target Hub). Explain asset name/amount in UI first. Like SEND_COIN, treat confirmation and any later notify/publish as separate steps.

entries.q: What METADATA fields are commonly useful in galleries?
entries.a: Title, tags, category from GET_QDN_RESOURCE_METADATA plus filename/mimeType/size from PROPERTIES and a THUMBNAIL URL. Lazy-load full FETCH only on open. Validate strings before rendering into HTML.

entries.q: How do I avoid XSS when rendering Markdown from DOCUMENT?
entries.a: Fetch DOCUMENT as text, run a sanitizer or render to text-only, never inject raw HTML. Combine with CSP-friendly in-zip scripts only. Treat every publisher as untrusted even if the name looks familiar.

entries.q: What is the difference between gateway context and full Hub?
entries.a: window._qdnContext may be "gateway" vs fuller Hub environments. Some privileged behaviors differ; always feature-detect qortalRequest and degrade. Theme still via _qdnTheme. Test both if you support public gateways.

entries.q: How do I publish multiple related resources with fewer popups?
entries.a: Feature-detect PUBLISH_MULTIPLE_QDN_RESOURCES to batch JSON metadata + THUMBNAIL + FILE in one approval when supported. Otherwise sequence publishes with a progress UI after one user click. Explain what will be published before starting.

entries.q: What FILE size strategy should apps use?
entries.a: Prefer one FILE when under comfortable Hub timeouts; for larger binaries, chunk into parts with a JSON index and bounded parallel fetches. Probe STATUS before heavy FETCH. Show clear size warnings before user-approved publish.

entries.q: How do I integrate Hub back buttons with my SPA?
entries.a: Listen to popstate for in-app routes and integrate NAVIGATION_HISTORY when available. Ensure each pushState has a matching UI state. Do not break Hub-level back by replacing history incorrectly.

entries.q: What should be in a Q-App README for other developers?
entries.a: Document identifier prefixes, JSON schema versions, services used, publish rights (name ownership), Hub version tested, and example qortal:// links. Point to qortal.dev for actions. Clear conventions beat clever undocumented namespaces.

entries.q: How do I fetch account names with pagination?
entries.a: Pass limit and offset to GET_ACCOUNT_NAMES and loop until a short page returns. Most users have few names—still code defensively. Cache after Connect for the session unless the user refreshes names.

entries.q: What is a good identifier for per-user app config?
entries.a: Use a stable id like myapp_config_v1 under the user's name and service JSON. Latest publish wins for updates. Bump _v2 only for breaking schema changes and migrate readers carefully.

entries.q: How do I open an avatar in the UI?
entries.a: Request GET_QDN_RESOURCE_URL for service THUMBNAIL, name = user name, identifier qortal_avatar, and set img.src. On failure show a placeholder. Do not block Connect UX on avatar load.

entries.q: Why must pollOptions be an array?
entries.a: CREATE_POLL rejects or mis-handles pollOptions when passed as a string. Pass an array of option objects (e.g. { optionName }). Validate non-empty unique labels client-side before the approval popup.

entries.q: How do relative asset paths interact with deep links?
entries.a: Deep links into /render/APP/Name/some/route still need assets resolved from the app root, not the deep path. Relative ./assets from a nested route can break—use root-correct relative URLs from the bundler base or Hub trailing-slash strategies.

entries.q: What is the recommended concurrency for chunk fetches?
entries.a: Use a small pool (about 3–6 concurrent FETCH_QDN_RESOURCE calls), retry transient failures with backoff, and update progress from STATUS. Hundreds in Promise.all cause timeouts and UI jank.

entries.q: How do I use DOCUMENT vs FILE for text?
entries.a: DOCUMENT suits larger text/JSON documents; FILE is generic binary/download oriented. If clients should edit structured text in-app, DOCUMENT (or JSON when tiny) is clearer; if users download opaque blobs, FILE fits. Either way validate size and mime.

entries.q: What Hub UI actions help multi-page sites?
entries.a: QDN_RESOURCE_DISPLAYED keeps copy-link aligned; OPEN_NEW_TAB/LINK_TO_QDN_RESOURCE opens peers; SET_TAB switches tabs; SET_TAB_NOTIFICATIONS badges unread. Combine with real WEBSITE file paths or APP SPA fallback appropriately.

entries.q: How do I safely mock data in preview mode?
entries.a: When the bridge is missing, serve local fixture JSON for reads and disable Publish/Pay buttons. Label the UI Preview. Never mark a mock payment as success. The same code paths should call qr() in Hub.

entries.q: What causes stale hashed files after rebuild?
entries.a: Zipping an old dist/ or mixing previous index-*.js hashes with a new index.html yields Loading forever. Always clean build, zip fresh contents, and Preview once before publish. Clear Hub cache if it pins old assets during testing.

entries.q: How do I read GET_USER_ACCOUNT fields?
entries.a: Typical shape: { address, publicKey }. Use address for GET_ACCOUNT_NAMES and publicKey for encryption counterparties when appropriate. Do not log sensitive wallet details verbosely in production UIs.

entries.q: What is SEARCH_CHAT_MESSAGES?
entries.a: SEARCH_CHAT_MESSAGES searches chat on supported Hubs and may be approval-gated depending on version. Confirm parameters in qortal.dev. Do not treat chat search as a transactional ledger.

entries.q: What is the end-to-end path for a WEBSITE visitor link?
entries.a: Publisher builds static files → Hub publishes service WEBSITE under owned name → visitors open qortal://WEBSITE/<Name>/path. Missing files 404. For interactive wallet features on every page, consider APP instead.

entries.q: How do I combine JSON metadata with VIDEO content?
entries.a: Publish VIDEO under myapp_video_<id>, THUMBNAIL under myapp_video_<id>_thumb, and JSON myapp_video_<id>_meta with title/tags/pointers. Search prefix myapp_video_ for discovery; fetch metadata first, then STATUS, then play.

entries.q: What REST mode mistake causes duplicate resources in UI?
entries.a: Using mode=ALL when you meant LATEST lists historical publishes as separate rows. Prefer LATEST for current catalogs, or dedupe by name+service+identifier yourself if you need ALL for history UIs.

entries.q: How do I implement bounded concurrency in JS?
entries.a: Keep a queue of identifiers and N workers: while queue length, worker shifts an id, await FETCH_QDN_RESOURCE, push result, repeat. Avoid awaiting Promise.all on the entire list. Surface partial errors per id.

entries.q: What should happen when parent.qortalRequest is only a stub?
entries.a: If parent === top and the stub cannot reach Hub, wallet calls fail—tell the user to open the app from Hub or a real Hub tab. Implement a message relay only when you control the parent embedder.

entries.q: How do I use SAVE_FILE correctly?
entries.a: Call SAVE_FILE with blob and filename from a user gesture on mobile when anchor download fails. Ensure blob type/filename are set. Feature-detect and fall back to GET_QDN_RESOURCE_URL with attachment=true when appropriate.

entries.q: What is the relationship between registered names and resources?
entries.a: Resources publish under a name you own; that name is part of the public coordinate others use to fetch. Changing ownership/name registration affects who can update. Design UX around primary name selection when users have several names.

entries.q: How do I avoid inventing qortalRequest parameters?
entries.a: Copy parameter names from qortal.dev/docs/q-apps or Core sources for the installed version. When unsure, feature-detect and keep payloads minimal—especially for SEARCH_*. Extra unknown keys can break searches.

entries.q: What packaging checklist prevents grey screens?
entries.a: index.html at zip root; flat zip of dist contents; base "./"; relative ./assets; no required CDN; rebuild after config changes; Preview Network 200s; consider trailing slash; remove problematic crossorigin; case-sensitive paths.

entries.q: How do inter-app SEARCH prefixes enable ecosystems?
entries.a: Agree on myapp_ prefixes and schema versions; publish discovery JSON; partners SEARCH_QDN_RESOURCES with prefix: true; open hits via LINK_TO_QDN_RESOURCE. Validate every foreign payload—prefixes are not authentication.

entries.q: How do I handle ENCRYPT_DATA for groups?
entries.a: Pass a publicKeys array to ENCRYPT_DATA for group encryption, or use ENCRYPT_QORTAL_GROUP_DATA / DECRYPT_QORTAL_GROUP_DATA for group-scoped flows. Explain recipients before approval. Store ciphertext under private namespaces.

entries.q: What UI pattern fits Hub-embedded Q-Apps?
entries.a: One primary Connect CTA, clear publish/pay confirmations, theme via _qdnTheme, large tap targets, and progressive loading with STATUS for media. Avoid assuming desktop hover. Keep critical actions gesture-gated.

entries.q: How do I test publish then search discovery?
entries.a: Publish JSON with prefixed identifier, wait/retry, SEARCH_QDN_RESOURCES with prefix: true and minimal payload, normalize to array, and assert your item appears. If empty, strip optional fields and confirm service spelling.

entries.q: How much water should I store per person per day?
entries.a: Plan at least 4 litres per person per day: about 2 for drinking and 2 for cooking and basic hygiene. In heat, hard work, illness, or pregnancy, drinking alone can need 4–6 litres. Two weeks per person is a solid household baseline — a family of four needs roughly 112 litres for one week.

entries.q: How do I store water safely at home?
entries.a: Use food-grade containers only (HDPE #2 jugs, 200 L drums, or factory-sealed bottled water). Store cool and dark, off concrete on wood slats. Never reuse milk jugs. Tap water from a treated municipal supply can store as-is; rotate yearly. For well water, add 2 drops of unscented 5–6% bleach per litre when filling.

entries.q: How do I purify water by boiling?
aliases: how do I make water safe to drink
entries.a:
1. Bring water to a rolling boil.
2. Keep it boiling 1 minute (3 minutes above about 2,000 m elevation).
3. Let it cool covered before drinking.
Boiling kills bacteria, protozoa, and viruses — the gold standard when you have fuel.
Do NOT skip the full boil time at altitude, where water boils cooler.

entries.q: How do I treat water with household bleach?
aliases: how do I purify water with bleach
entries.a:
1. Use unscented 5–6% household bleach only.
2. Add 2 drops per litre of clear water, or 4 drops per litre if cloudy (after settling/pre-filtering).
3. Mix and wait 30–60 minutes before drinking.
Bleach helps against bacteria and viruses but is only partial against Cryptosporidium.
Do NOT use scented, colour-safe, or cleaning blends — only plain bleach.

entries.q: Do hollow-fiber water filters remove viruses?
aliases: does a water filter kill viruses
how do I filter river water
what if I have no fire to boil water
entries.a: A good hollow-fiber filter (about 0.1 micron) removes bacteria and protozoa (Giardia/Crypto) but typically does NOT remove viruses. Pair it with boiling or a chemical that covers viruses (chlorine dioxide or bleach for many viruses), or use a true purifier bottle. Protect hollow-fiber filters from freezing — cracked fibres can pass microbes with no visible damage. With no fire: filter first, then use chemical treatment or a purifier — do not rely on clear looks alone.

entries.q: What is the best layered water treatment kit?
entries.a: Cover three layers: a gravity or squeeze hollow-fiber filter for volume, chlorine dioxide tablets as compact backup (best chemical option; wait up to 4 hours for Crypto), and the knowledge plus fuel to boil. Mark dedicated dirty and clean buckets permanently to avoid cross-contamination.

entries.q: How do I make muddy river water drinkable?
entries.a:
1. Pre-filter through cloth, a coffee filter, or a Millbank bag, or let sediment settle and decant.
2. Then boil, filter with a hollow-fiber unit, and/or use chlorine dioxide.
3. Prefer moving water, collected from the surface upstream of trails and livestock.
Sediment shelters microbes and clogs filters.
Do NOT drink untreated surface water no matter how clear — Giardia is invisible.

entries.q: Can I drink rainwater from my roof?
entries.a: Rain catchment is useful: roughly 1 litre per square metre per millimetre of rain (a 20 m² roof in a 10 mm shower ≈ 200 L). First-flush the initial runoff that carries roof grime and bird droppings, then still treat before drinking (boil, filter, or chemical). Use clean tarp or metal roof sections into food-grade barrels.

entries.q: Is urine or salt water drinkable in survival?
entries.a: Salt water and urine are never drinkable as-is — both dehydrate you further. Distillation is the only practical way to reclaim usable water from them. Focus on finding fresh sources, melting snow properly, rain catchment, or treating surface water instead.

entries.q: How do I get water from snow or ice?
entries.a: Melt snow with a little starter liquid in the pot so it does not scorch. Ice yields more water per volume than snow. In cold conditions, never eat snow directly — it lowers core temperature. Once melted, treat as needed (boil is most reliable). Keep hollow-fiber filters warm against your body so they do not freeze.

entries.q: Should I ration water in the heat?
entries.a: Ration sweat, not water: rest in shade through midday, work at dawn and dusk, and drink what you have. People have died of dehydration with water still in their canteens. Shade, pacing, and treating every available source beat sipping tiny amounts while still sweating hard.

entries.q: How do I capture emergency water if the taps may fail?
entries.a: The moment trouble is announced, fill bathtubs (a tub liner can hold ~350 L), sinks, pots, and washing machines. Your hot-water tank holds 100–300 L of drinkable water — turn off power/gas, let it cool, drain from the bottom valve. Toilet tanks (not bowls) hold a few litres of tap water if no chemical pucks were used.

entries.q: How long does stored bleach stay useful for water treatment?
entries.a: Household bleach loses potency roughly a year after opening. Rotate unscented 5–6% bleach yearly for water treatment. Chlorine dioxide tablets have a longer shelf life and are the better compact chemical backup, especially because they can cover Cryptosporidium with a long enough wait.

entries.q: What is SODIS water treatment?
entries.a: SODIS uses a clear PET bottle filled with clear water left in full sun for about 6 hours (UV kills many microbes). UV pens work similarly but need batteries. Only use clear water — cloudy water blocks UV. Boiling or a good filter-plus-chemical stack is more reliable when fuel or tablets are available.

entries.q: Why not reuse milk jugs for water storage?
entries.a: Milk jugs leave protein residue that breeds bacteria, and the plastic degrades. Old soda bottles washed with a bleach rinse are acceptable short-term. Prefer purpose-made food-grade HDPE (#2) jugs or drums for serious storage.

entries.q: How do chlorine dioxide tablets compare to bleach?
entries.a: Chlorine dioxide tablets are the best chemical option for field use: they cover bacteria, viruses, and Cryptosporidium (often needing up to about 4 hours for Crypto). Bleach is cheap and common but only partial against Crypto. Keep tablets as compact backup even if you mainly boil or filter.

entries.q: What water sources should I prefer in the wild?
entries.a: Prefer moving water over stagnant. Collect from the surface, not a stirred-up bottom, and upstream of trails, livestock, and settlements. Always treat before drinking. Avoid salt water and anything you cannot distill. Clarity means nothing — treat every wild source.

entries.q: How much rain can a roof collect?
entries.a: About 1 litre per square metre of catchment per millimetre of rain. Example: a 20 m² clean roof section in a 10 mm shower yields roughly 200 litres before losses. First-flush dirty runoff, store in food-grade barrels, and treat before drinking.

entries.q: How do I protect a water filter in winter?
entries.a: Freezing destroys hollow-fiber filters — cracked fibres can pass microbes with no visible damage. Sleep with the filter in your jacket, keep it against your body when hiking, or switch to boiling and chemicals in hard freezes. Never assume a thawed filter is still safe if it froze solid.

entries.q: Can I drink water from the toilet tank?
entries.a: Toilet tanks (cisterns) often hold a few litres of tap water usable in an emergency if no chemical blue pucks or cleaners were used. Never drink from the bowl. Still prefer stored jugs and treated sources; use tank water as a last clean-looking reserve and boil if unsure.

entries.q: How do I mark dirty and clean water buckets?
entries.a: Permanently mark one dirty and one clean bucket and never swap roles. Use the dirty bucket only for source water going into a filter or pre-settle stage; the clean bucket only for treated water. Cross-contamination undoes careful boiling and filtering.

entries.q: What elevation changes boiling time for water?
entries.a: At low elevation, a rolling boil for 1 minute is the usual standard. Above about 2,000 m, boil 3 minutes because water boils at a lower temperature. When fuel is scarce, a quality filter plus chemical backup can save fuel, but boiling remains the most foolproof microbial kill.

entries.q: Can UV pens purify cloudy water?
entries.a: UV pens and SODIS need clear water — turbidity blocks ultraviolet light and hides microbes. Pre-filter or settle first, then UV, or choose boiling/chemicals. Always confirm battery state for pens before relying on them in the kit.

entries.q: How do I use a hot-water tank as an emergency supply?
entries.a: A household tank often holds 100–300 L of originally potable water. Turn off power or gas to the heater, let it cool, and drain from the bottom valve into clean containers. Treat if the tank is old or uncertain.

entries.q: What is first-flush in rain catchment?
entries.a: The first runoff after dry weather carries bird droppings, dust, and roof grime. Divert or discard that first flush, then collect into clean barrels — and still treat before drinking. Clean catchment surfaces collect safer water than filthy ones.

entries.q: What is the survival rule of threes?
entries.a: Rough priorities: about 3 minutes without air, 3 hours without shelter in harsh exposure, 3 days without water, and 3 weeks without food. In cold, wet climates, shelter and fire often outrank everything else — hypothermia kills far faster than hunger.

entries.q: What are the 5 C's of survivability?
entries.a: A common bushcraft framework: (1) Cutting tool — fixed-blade knife; (2) Combustion — ferro rod, lighter, tinder; (3) Cover — tarp/blanket/rain gear; (4) Container — metal bottle or pot you can boil in; (5) Cordage — paracord or bankline. These are hard to improvise well in the field.

entries.q: How do I build a reliable fire in the wild?
aliases: how do I start a fire without matches
entries.a:
1. Gather tinder, pencil-thin twigs, then finger- and wrist-thick fuel before striking.
2. Build on dry ground or a stick platform; shield from wind.
3. Light the tinder, then feed gradually up in size.
Carry two ignition sources; a ferro rod still works when wet/cold lighters fail.
Do NOT light first and scramble for fuel — that is how fires die.

entries.q: What is the next-fire mentality?
entries.a: Never consume your last means of making fire, and prepare the next fire while you still have this one. Dry tomorrow’s tinder beside tonight’s fire, keep char cloth or charred punk in a tin, carry a dry tinder pouch on your body, and treat the lighter as convenience and the ferro rod as reserve — not the other way around.

entries.q: How do I make fire in winter snow?
entries.a: Clear snow to ground or build a raft of green logs so the fire does not melt into a pit. Use standing dead wood (ground wood is soaked), split to dry cores, and process 3–4× more fuel than feels necessary before lighting. Feather sticks and fatwood light when everything else is wet. Warm the ferro rod and your hands first.

entries.q: How should I site and build an emergency shelter?
aliases: how do I build a shelter outside
how to make a shelter outdoors
entries.a:
1. Pick a site out of wind, off low ground, away from dead standing trees.
2. Rig a tarp A-frame or lean-to fast.
3. Insulate underneath you — ground conduction steals more heat than air.
A quality emergency blanket or wool layer under/over you matters as much as the roof.
Do NOT soak your clothes with sweat while overbuilding a debris hut in cold weather.

entries.q: Why is wool better than cotton in the cold?
entries.a: Never wear cotton against skin when cold — it holds moisture and chills you. Wool (and many synthetics) insulates even when wet; down fails when wet. Wool also resists ember burns near fires and odour over multi-day wear. A sturdy wool blanket can serve as coat, sleep system, stretcher pad, or windbreak.

entries.q: What knots should I learn for bushcraft?
entries.a: Learn five knots deeply: bowline (fixed loop), taut-line hitch (adjustable tension), trucker’s hitch (mechanical advantage), clove hitch (quick attach), and square lashing (structures). Tarred bank line handles most camp jobs light and strong. A carved toggle turns a loop into a quick-release connector.

entries.q: How do I signal for help if I am lost?
entries.a:
1. Stop, stay warm, and stay put if safe.
2. Make yourself visible: open ground, bright colours, signal mirror/flashes.
3. Use three of anything — whistle blasts, fires, or light flashes — as a distress pattern.
A whistle carries farther than shouting for far less energy.
Do NOT wander farther looking for a perfect ridge once you are already exhausted and cold.

entries.q: How do I navigate without a GPS?
entries.a: Carry a compass and paper map even if you have GPS. Without a compass: sun rises roughly east and sets roughly west; a stick’s shadow tip marked twice gives an east–west line; the North Star (via the Big Dipper pointers) sits due north. Pace-count distance (calibrate your own paces; many adults are ~65 double-paces per 100 m). Look behind you regularly so the return route is memorised.

entries.q: What should I do if I get lost outdoors?
aliases: lost in woods what to do
entries.a:
1. Stop. Sit, breathe, and prevent panic decisions.
2. Stay warm and dry — shelter and fire before long searches.
3. Mark your location, make yourself visible, and signal (whistle threes).
Tell someone your route and return time before you leave home.
Do NOT keep walking for hours hoping to stumble on a road when night and cold are coming.

entries.q: What tinder works best for fire starting?
entries.a: Reliable tinder includes birch bark, fatwood shavings, dry inner bark, feather sticks, and prepared char cloth. Collect it before you need sparks. Keep a dry tinder pouch on your body. In wet weather, split wood to dry hearts and carve feather sticks rather than hunting soggy ground litter.

entries.q: Why carry a metal bottle for survival?
entries.a: A single-wall metal bottle or pot lets you boil water — the most reliable field treatment — and cook. Plastic bottles cannot go in the fire. Pair the container with a cutting tool, ignition, cover, and cordage so you can make safe water and hot drinks when you are cold.

entries.q: How does ground insulation affect shelter warmth?
entries.a: You lose more heat into the ground than into the air. Always put insulation under you: closed-cell foam, a thick bed of dry debris, packs, or extra clothing. A tarp roof without under-insulation still leaves you cold. Elevate or pad before you add fancy walls.

entries.q: Is fishing a good beginner wild-food skill?
entries.a: Fishing is often the most calorie-positive wild-food skill for beginners: a hand reel, hooks, and line weigh little and can work while you do other tasks. Passive methods beat active hunting on energy budget, but many are regulated or illegal outside genuine emergencies — know the law. For plants and mushrooms, only eat species you can identify with certainty.

entries.q: How do I gather fuel before lighting a fire?
entries.a: Collect the whole ladder first: fluffy or bark tinder, pencil-thin twigs, finger-thick sticks, then wrist-thick fuel. Light only when the pile is ready and weather-protected. Leaving a baby flame to fetch wood is a classic way to lose the fire — especially in winter.

entries.q: What ignition sources should I carry?
entries.a: Carry at least two ignition sources. A butane lighter is convenient; a ferro rod still throws sparks when wet or frozen. Pair both with dry tinder on your body. Bic-style lighters fail in cold until warmed in a pocket.

entries.q: How do I use a tarp as a quick shelter?
entries.a: An A-frame or lean-to tarp is the fastest effective shelter for most people. Rig ridge line with cordage, stake corners, and put thick insulation on the ground under your sleep system. Face the open side away from wind and rain. Practice at home so you can do it in the dark.

entries.q: Why avoid camping under dead trees?
entries.a: Dead standing trees ("widowmakers") drop limbs without warning, especially in wind. Site shelters out of their fall zone, off flood-prone low ground, and out of prevailing wind. Good site selection prevents emergencies better than clever lashings.

entries.q: How do I pace count distance on a hike?
entries.a: Calibrate your own pace: many adults take about 65 double-paces per 100 m — measure yours on a known distance. Use ranger beads or another counter in poor visibility. Combine with map, compass, and frequent back-bearings so the return is not a guess.

entries.q: How do I find north using the stars?
entries.a: Find the Big Dipper; the two pointer stars at the bowl’s end aim at Polaris, the North Star, which sits due north. Polaris’s height above the horizon roughly matches your latitude. Use stars to check compass work, not as an excuse to leave the map at home.

entries.q: What does three whistle blasts mean?
entries.a: Three of anything — whistle blasts, fires, or light flashes — is widely recognised as a distress signal. Carry a loud whistle; it saves voice and energy. Keep signalling on a schedule so rescuers can home in.

entries.q: How should I dress in layers for cold weather?
entries.a: Use a moisture-managing base (wool/synthetic, not cotton), an insulating mid layer, and a wind/rain shell. Vent before you sweat; damp clothing destroys insulation. Cover head and hands. Change into dry sleep clothes before bed in the field.

entries.q: How do I avoid soaking clothes while building shelter?
entries.a: Debris and snow shelters cost sweat. Vent layers, work at a sustainable pace, and stop to rewarm before you are damp. Wet clothing in wind can turn shelter-building into a hypothermia emergency. Sometimes a simple tarp beats an epic debris hut.

entries.q: What should I tell someone before a hike?
entries.a: Share your route, companions, and return time with someone who will notice if you are late. Agree when they should call for help. This single habit saves more lives than exotic gear, because searchers know where to look.

entries.q: What makes a fixed-blade knife the top bushcraft tool?
entries.a: A decent fixed-blade carbon-steel knife processes tinder, builds shelter, prepares food, and does camp crafts when folders fail. It is the cutting tool in the 5 C’s because replacing that capability from scratch in the field is hard. Keep it sharp and sheathed.

entries.q: How do I use cordage in camp craft?
entries.a: Cordage builds shelters, hangs pots, repairs gear, and lashes poles. Prefer learning a few strong knots over collecting fifty you forget. A toggle — a simple carved stick — makes quick-release connectors for ridgelines and loads.

entries.q: What wild plants are safer learning targets?
entries.a: Learn a handful of unmistakable local species from experts — e.g. bilberries/crowberries in some northern regions, and widespread cooked nettles or dandelion greens elsewhere. Harvest away from roads and spray. Never invent tests for unknown plants or mushrooms.

entries.q: Why shouldn't I eat unidentified mushrooms?
entries.a: Assume any wild mushroom is unsafe until an expert confirms the exact species — there is no reliable shortcut test. Never experiment. Learn a handful of unmistakable local plants from experts and leave all uncertain fungi alone. Mistakes can be fatal.

entries.q: Why keep paper maps if I have offline map apps?
entries.a: Phones die, freeze, drown, and fail. A paper map with rally points marked, plus a compass you know how to use, still works. Download offline maps too — redundancy is the point. Tell someone your route before you go.

entries.q: How do I recognize and treat hypothermia?
entries.a:
1. Get them out of wind and wet clothing; add dry insulation.
2. If fully conscious, give warm sweet drinks; warm the torso with skin-to-skin or heat packs (not extremities first).
3. Handle gently and seek emergency services (112 in Europe) if available — severe hypothermia is life-threatening.
Early signs: intense shivering, clumsy hands, slurred speech, apathy.
Do NOT rub extremities hard, give alcohol, or use hot baths on a semi-conscious person.

entries.q: How do I stay warm when home heating fails?
aliases: how do I stay warm without power
keep warm in a power outage
entries.a: Heat the person, then one room, then maybe the house. Wear wool/synthetic base layers, hat and warm socks indoors, use a hot water bottle in a sleeping bag, and gather everyone in the smallest sheltered room with doors closed and blankets over windows. A climate-rated sleeping bag is a heating system that needs no fuel. Safe heat: wood stove, or indoor-rated heaters with ventilation and a working CO alarm.

entries.q: What causes carbon monoxide poisoning in blackouts?
entries.a: Carbon monoxide from combustion kills quietly every winter. Never heat or cook with a barbecue, camp stove, open oven, or generator indoors or in a garage. Generators stay outdoors, 5+ m from windows, exhaust pointed away. Indoor-rated paraffin/propane heaters still need a cracked window and a working CO alarm with fresh batteries.

entries.q: What are the signs of carbon monoxide poisoning?
entries.a:
1. Headache, nausea, dizziness, confusion, or flu-like symptoms with combustion appliances running — get everyone outside to fresh air immediately.
2. Turn off the source if safe; ventilate.
3. Call emergency services if anyone is altered, fainting, or not improving.
CO is odourless.
