entries.a: Anyone can read the code, copy it under its open-source licence and propose changes: the repositories take pull requests, which maintainers review. But a change only reaches the live network as a Core release that about 40% of the Dev Admins approve on-chain; nodes then install it through auto-update. No single person can push an update alone.

entries.q: What happens if no one is minting?
aliases: what if all minters go offline
entries.a: New blocks need online minters, so without any the chain simply pauses: nobody produces new blocks, but nothing already recorded is lost. When minters come back online, block production carries on. Qortal Core even has a recovery mode that lets minters restart a stalled network on top of older blocks.

entries.q: Can I help translate Qortal?
entries.a: Yes. Qortal Hub, and Qortal GO built from it, ship in 12 languages: English, Arabic, German, Spanish, Estonian, Finnish, French, Italian, Japanese, Portuguese, Russian and Chinese. The texts live in the open-source Hub code, and translators are among the contributors qortal.org asks for. Offer help in the Core Development group in Q-Chat or through the Qortal repositories on GitHub.

entries.q: Is Qortal still active?
entries.a: Yes. Qortal Core received a major networking and QDN update, version 6, in 2026; Qortal Hub 3.0 brought Reticulum-based chat, voice calls and file transfers; Qortal GO 3.0 keeps shipping releases; and new community Q-Apps keep appearing. Development is open, so you can follow it on GitHub and in Q-Chat.

entries.q: Do I need permission to build on Qortal?
entries.a: No. Anyone can build on Qortal without asking: all you need to publish a website or Q-App is a registered name and a little QORT for the fee. Nobody reviews apps before they go live; users choose what to open, and Hub or GO asks them to approve any action an app wants to take with their account.

entries.q: Who decides the QORT block reward?
entries.a: The schedule is written into Qortal Core's rules: 5 QORT per block at Genesis, 0.25 less every 259,200 blocks, down to 2 QORT. After that, the qortal.dev wiki says a vote can adjust the reward once a year by 0.25 to 1 QORT, never below 1 or above 5 QORT per block. Any change to the rules reaches nodes as a Core update approved on-chain by the Dev Admins.

entries.q: Will Qortal survive if its founders leave?
aliases: does qortal depend on the founders
what if the qortal developers quit
entries.a: It is designed to. The network runs on nodes that ordinary people operate, not on any founder's hardware or company; the code is open source, so others can keep developing it; and Dev Admin roles can pass to new contributors through on-chain approval. The community wiki says Qortal is intended to outlive its founders.

entries.q: What happens to Qortal if qortal.org or qortal.dev goes offline?
entries.a: The network keeps running: the blockchain and QDN live on users' nodes, not on those websites. The source code and releases are also on GitHub and gitea.qortal.link, the community wiki has a copy on QDN (qortal://WEBSITE/wiki.qortal.org), and Qortal GO publishes its updates on QDN as well. The websites help newcomers find Qortal, but Qortal does not depend on them.

entries.q: How does Qortal Hub run a Q-App?
aliases: how hub runs a q-app frame
entries.a: Hub opens the app in a frame at your node's address /render/APP/<name>, so the node itself serves the files it holds from QDN. Hub adds theme, lang and identifier to that address. The node adds a small script, q-apps.js, which gives the page qortalRequest. Read-only requests are answered by the node; anything that needs the user, such as the account, a publish or a payment, goes up to Hub, which asks for approval. Qortal GO runs Q-Apps the same way inside its Android WebView.

entries.q: What does the node add to my Q-App's index.html?
aliases: base href added by node q-app
entries.a: When the node serves an HTML page of an app or website, it adds at the top of the head: a UTF-8 charset tag, a base href so relative paths resolve inside the app, a script with the _qdn variables, and q-apps.js, which defines qortalRequest. On a gateway it also adds q-apps-gateway.js. You don't ship any of these yourself.

entries.q: What do the _qdn variables in a Q-App hold?
entries.a: The node defines them on every page it renders: _qdnContext (render, or gateway on a gateway), _qdnTheme (light or dark), _qdnLang (the language code), _qdnService, _qdnName and _qdnIdentifier (which resource this is), _qdnPath (the file shown), _qdnBase (the /render/<service>/<name> prefix) and _qdnBaseWithPath. Read these instead of parsing the address yourself.

entries.q: What basename should my Q-App's router use?
entries.a: Use the prefix the node puts in window._qdnBase, for example /render/APP/<name>, exactly as given (just drop a trailing slash). Don't decode it: the router compares it with the page address, where a space stays %20. When you read the app name (_qdnName) or path parts as text, decode them with decodeURIComponent, never URLSearchParams, which turns a + into a space. Then the same routes work in Hub and GO, and deep links open the right page.

entries.q: What query parameters does Hub add to my Q-App's address?
aliases: theme lang identifier in q-app url
why is theme in my app address
entries.a: Hub opens your app with theme (dark or light), lang (the language code) and identifier (empty for a default resource). A refresh or Back can add time and isManualNavigation=false, and GO's widgets screen adds goWidget=1. q-apps.js leaves these keys out when it tells Hub which path is showing, and some apps also remove them from the visible address.

entries.q: What is q-apps.js?
entries.a: q-apps.js is the script the node adds to every Q-App and QDN website page. It defines qortalRequest and qortalRequestWithTimeout, answers read-only actions by calling the node's API, and passes every other action up to Hub or GO. It also turns clicks on qortal:// links into LINK_TO_QDN_RESOURCE, rewrites qortal:// image sources, blocks plain web links, and tells Hub which path is showing for Back and Copy link.

entries.q: Why don't web links work inside my Q-App?
aliases: external links in q-app do nothing
https link not working hub app
entries.a: q-apps.js blocks clicks on ordinary web links (http and https addresses), and Hub and GO keep the frame on the node, so a Q-App can't send people to the outside web. Use qortal:// links for QDN content. For an outside address, show it as text the user can copy, and say why.

entries.q: Can I use a qortal:// link as an image source in a Q-App?
aliases: qortal link in img element code
entries.a: Yes, for images in your page's HTML: write src as qortal://THUMBNAIL/<name>/qortal_avatar or qortal://WEBSITE/<name>/assets/logo.png, and q-apps.js rewrites it to the node's /arbitrary/ address when the page loads. It only handles images that are in the page at load time. For images your code adds later, such as list rows, get the address with GET_QDN_RESOURCE_URL.

entries.q: Do all Q-Apps share the same browser storage?
entries.a: Yes. Every Q-App and website rendered from one node has the same browser origin, so localStorage, sessionStorage and IndexedDB are shared between them. Prefix every key with your app's name, for example myapp.settings, and never keep private keys, seeds or secrets there. Two versions of an app that use the same keys will mix their settings.

entries.q: Can my Q-App call an outside web API?
entries.a: No. Hub and GO give every Q-App frame a content security policy that keeps its requests on the node: fetches, scripts, styles, images, fonts and media may come only from the node, data: and blob:. A call to an outside server is blocked, and it would leak the user's IP address anyway. Put the data on QDN or ship it inside your zip.

entries.q: Can a Q-App use inline scripts, eval or WebAssembly?
entries.a: Yes. The policy Hub and GO put on Q-App pages allows inline scripts and styles, eval and WebAssembly, as long as the code comes from your app's own files on the node. A single-file app with its script inside index.html works, and so do bundles that use WebAssembly.

entries.q: Can my Q-App open a WebSocket?
entries.a: Only to the node the app is served from. Hub and GO allow WebSocket connections to that node, but not to any other host, so a Q-App can't keep a live connection to an outside server.

entries.q: Can a Q-App use a service worker in GO?
entries.a: No. GO refuses to install service workers for Q-Apps. It also blocks prefetches to other sites and links such as intent:, market: and tel:. Keep your app small and its files in the zip instead of relying on a service worker.

entries.q: What is the Loading page that shows before my Q-App opens?
aliases: node loading page before q-app opens
entries.a: When the node doesn't have all of an app's files yet, it shows its own Loading - Qortal Network page while it downloads and builds them from peers, then reloads into your app once the status is READY. The first open after a publish, or on a node that doesn't host your name, can take a while. GO also checks the app's address itself every few seconds and opens it as soon as the node serves it.

entries.q: What happens to wallet requests when my Q-App is opened on a gateway?
entries.a: A gateway shows QDN apps in an ordinary browser, and _qdnContext is then gateway. Read-only requests still work, but GET_USER_ACCOUNT, PUBLISH_QDN_RESOURCE, SEND_COIN, SEND_CHAT_MESSAGE, JOIN_GROUP, DEPLOY_AT, GET_WALLET_BALANCE and the list actions fail with an error saying interactive features aren't supported via a gateway, and the page shows a small read-only notice. Make sure your app still reads well in that mode.

entries.q: Should my APP show its own not-found page?
entries.a: Yes. For an APP the node sends every path that isn't a real file to index.html, so your router has to deal with unknown paths. Qortal's docs recommend showing a not-found page when a path can't be routed, rather than a blank screen.

entries.q: How does qortalRequest pass a request to Hub?
entries.a: Each call posts your request object, with its action, through a MessageChannel and returns a Promise. q-apps.js either answers it from the node or forwards it to Hub or GO, and the reply comes back on that channel as a result or an error. That's why every call needs await and try/catch, and why a call can stay open while the user reads an approval.

entries.q: How many qortalRequest calls can run at once?
entries.a: q-apps.js runs at most 30 requests at the same time and queues the rest until a slot is free. A page that fires hundreds of searches at start just waits in that queue, so load in pages and fetch only what is on screen.

entries.q: How long does qortalRequest wait before it times out?
entries.a: q-apps.js gives each action its own limit: most get 30 seconds; FETCH_QDN_RESOURCE and SEND_CHAT_MESSAGE 60 seconds; SEND_COIN, JOIN_GROUP, polls, trades and DEPLOY_AT 5 minutes; GET_WALLET_BALANCE 2 minutes; publishes, GET_USER_ACCOUNT, SAVE_FILE, SIGN_TRANSACTION and DECRYPT_DATA up to an hour. Hub and GO also stop waiting after 30 seconds for most requests they handle themselves, except publishes. When a limit runs out, the call fails with a timeout error.

entries.q: What if a payment request times out while the approval is still open?
entries.a: Hub and GO stop waiting for an approval request after 30 seconds, although the approval window stays open for about a minute, and if the user accepts later the action still happens. So treat a timeout on SEND_COIN or any other write as unknown, not failed. Check first, for example with SEARCH_TRANSACTIONS for the payment, and only then offer Retry.

entries.q: What shape do qortalRequest errors have?
entries.a: It depends on who answered. Hub and GO usually reject with an object holding error and message, for example User declined request. A q-apps.js timeout rejects with a plain string, and errors from the node's API come as the node's JSON error object. Read e.message, then e.error, then the value itself, and show a short plain sentence to the user.

entries.q: Why is the decline error from Hub in another language?
entries.a: Hub and GO translate their error messages into the user's language, so User declined request can arrive in any of their 12 languages. Don't match the English text alone. Treat a rejection right after an approval as a likely cancel: show nothing alarming and leave the button usable.

entries.q: What happens if my app calls an action Hub doesn't know?
entries.a: Nothing answers it: Hub and GO ignore actions they don't handle, so the call only fails when q-apps.js times out, after 30 seconds for most actions. Check the spelling, and ask SHOW_ACTIONS for the list the user's Hub or GO supports before you rely on a newer action.

entries.q: How can my app list the qortalRequest actions this Hub supports?
aliases: which actions does this hub support q-app
entries.a: Call qortalRequest with the action SHOW_ACTIONS. It returns the list of every action the running Hub or GO handles, without asking the user. Use it to hide features the user's version can't do.

entries.q: Which older qortalRequest actions are missing in Hub 3.0?
aliases: How do I open a peer profile
entries.a: Some actions in older docs came from the old Qortal UI and aren't in Hub 3.0's list: GET_FRIENDS_LIST, GET_PROFILE_DATA, SET_PROFILE_DATA, OPEN_PROFILE, SET_TAB_NOTIFICATIONS, SEND_LOCAL_NOTIFICATION and NOTIFICATIONS_PERMISSION. Calls to them get no answer. Use OPEN_USER_LOOKUP to show a person, and NOTIFICATION_PERMISSION with NOTIFICATION_ADD for notifications.

entries.q: How can my Q-App tell whether it runs in the desktop Hub?
aliases: is my q-app in electron hub
which ui is running q-app code
entries.a: Call WHICH_UI. It answers HUB_ELECTRON in the desktop Hub and HUB_WEB anywhere else, which includes Qortal GO on Android. It needs no approval.

entries.q: How does my app know the user is on a public node?
aliases: own node or public node app code
entries.a: Call IS_USING_PUBLIC_NODE. It returns true when Hub or GO is connected to a public node and false on the user's own node. Use it to explain features a public node can't do, instead of showing an error.

entries.q: Which qortalRequest actions fail on a public node?
aliases: which q-app actions need own node
entries.a: Hub and GO refuse these on a public node: GET_LIST_ITEMS, ADD_LIST_ITEMS and DELETE_LIST_ITEM, GET_HOSTED_DATA and DELETE_HOSTED_DATA, ADMIN_ACTION, the foreign server and foreign fee settings, sending any coin other than QORT, and ARRR wallet reads; the error says the action can't be done through a public node. Publishes fail there too, because the public node takes no uploads without its API key. Handle these quietly and explain what the user's own node would add.

entries.q: How long does the Q-App approval window wait for the user?
entries.a: About a minute. The window shows a countdown, and when it runs out the request counts as declined. Requests from apps queue one at a time, and Decline all answers every waiting request from the same app.

entries.q: Can my app change what the approval window says?
entries.a: No. Hub and GO write the question, such as Allow this app to publish to QDN?, and fill in the details themselves from your request: service, identifier and name, or recipient, amount and fee, or the first characters of a chat message. The app name and icon under Requested by come from Hub's own record of the tab, never from your request. Make your own screen explain the why before you call.

entries.q: Will my app get the authenticate popup on every GET_USER_ACCOUNT call?
entries.a: No. Once the user accepts, later GET_USER_ACCOUNT calls in that tab return without asking. If they also ticked Always authenticate automatically, Hub remembers that for your app's name, and even new tabs skip the popup. Still call it only after a user action, and keep the result for the session.

entries.q: What else does accepting GET_USER_ACCOUNT allow for that tab?
entries.a: For that tab's session, Hub then also lets your app run GET_USER_WALLET, GET_WALLET_BALANCE, GET_USER_WALLET_INFO, GET_USER_WALLET_TRANSACTIONS, GET_LIST_ITEMS, SIGN_FOREIGN_FEES and START_CROSSCHAIN_SERVER without asking again (ARRR wallet reads still ask first). Publishes, payments and messages still ask every time unless granted another way.

entries.q: What is SESSION_PERMISSIONS?
entries.a: SESSION_PERMISSIONS lets an app ask once for a list of actions, in a permissions array, that may then run without approvals while that tab is open. The user sees the list and has to tick I trust this app and understand these permissions will auto-execute. Ask only for what you need, and only when the user is about to do something that needs it.

entries.q: Which actions can SESSION_PERMISSIONS grant?
aliases: which actions auto approve session q-app
entries.a: JOIN_GROUP, GET_USER_ACCOUNT, GET_USER_WALLET, GET_WALLET_BALANCE, GET_USER_WALLET_TRANSACTIONS, GET_USER_WALLET_INFO, GET_LIST_ITEMS, PUBLISH_QDN_RESOURCE, PUBLISH_MULTIPLE_QDN_RESOURCES, LOCK_TAB, CREATE_GROUP, the group admin actions (invite, kick, ban, cancel ban, add and remove admin), the foreign server and fee settings, SIGN_FOREIGN_FEES, REENCRYPT_GROUP_KEYS, START_CROSSCHAIN_SERVER and NOTIFICATION_PERMISSION. Anything else fails with Invalid permissions. SEND_COIN can't be granted this way.

entries.q: When do session permissions end?
aliases: how long session permission lasts q-app
entries.a: They're kept in memory for that tab and your app's name only, and they end when the tab is closed (or all tabs are). A new tab, or opening the app again, starts without them.

entries.q: Which approvals have an always allow box?
aliases: which q-app popups can be skipped
entries.a: Authenticate (GET_USER_ACCOUNT), chat messages from this app (SEND_CHAT_MESSAGE), lists (GET_LIST_ITEMS), and the balance, wallet and wallet transaction reads. The user decides; your app can't tick it for them. Payments and publishes have no such box.

entries.q: Which qortalRequest actions need the user's confirmation tick?
aliases: which requests require i have read tick
entries.a: Hub keeps Accept off until the user ticks the confirmation for requests that move value or sign things: SEND_COIN for every coin, TRANSFER_ASSET, MULTI_ASSET_PAYMENT_WITH_PRIVATE_DATA, SIGN_TRANSACTION, SIGN_FOREIGN_FEES, trade buy and sell orders, BUY_NAME and SELL_NAME, a publish that carries an app fee, and SESSION_PERMISSIONS. Expect these to take the user a little longer.

entries.q: What error does GET_USER_ACCOUNT give when the user declines?
entries.a: Hub answers with Unable to get user account, whether the user declined or something else failed. Show your Sign in or Connect button again rather than an error, and don't call it again by itself.

entries.q: Why does GET_USER_ACCOUNT sometimes hang?
entries.a: If Hub is locked or busy, the request can wait until Hub's 30-second limit. Retry once, then show a Sign in button so the user can try when Hub is ready.

entries.q: What does GET_PRIMARY_NAME return?
aliases: primary name of an address q-app
entries.a: GET_PRIMARY_NAME takes an address and returns that account's primary name as text, or an empty string when it has none. It needs no approval, so it's a cheap way to show a name beside an address. Cache the answers, since the same names come up again and again in lists.

entries.q: Which name does a publish use if my app leaves out name?
aliases: user has no qortal name error
entries.a: Hub then publishes under the account's primary name. If the account has no registered name, the request fails with User has no Qortal name. When a user owns several names, pass name yourself and let them choose; it must be one of their names.

entries.q: How do I show a user's level or blocks minted in my app?
entries.a: Call GET_ACCOUNT_DATA with the address. Among its fields are level, blocksMinted, blocksMintedAdjustment and blocksMintedPenalty, along with publicKey and defaultGroupId. It's read-only and needs no approval.

entries.q: How can my app show the node's sync state or version?
entries.a: GET_NODE_STATUS answers with isSynchronizing, syncPercent, height, numberOfConnections, numberOfDataConnections and isMintingPossible. GET_NODE_INFO answers with buildVersion, buildTimestamp, uptime, currentTimestamp, nodeId, isTestNet and type. Both read the node Hub or GO is connected to and need no approval.

entries.q: How do I show a person's details in Hub from my app?
aliases: show user details hub from app
entries.a: Call OPEN_USER_LOOKUP with user set to a name or an address. Hub opens its user lookup panel for that person. It needs no approval.

entries.q: How do I get the user's own QORT balance?
entries.a: Call GET_WALLET_BALANCE with coin set to QORT. The user is asked Allow this app to fetch your QORT balance?, with a box to always allow it, and the answer is a number. To read the balance of any address without asking, use GET_BALANCE with that address instead.

entries.q: How do I read an asset balance from a Q-App?
entries.a: Use GET_BALANCE with the address and assetId set to the asset's number. Without assetId you get the QORT balance. It's read-only and needs no approval.

entries.q: Can my app register a name for the user?
entries.a: Yes. REGISTER_NAME takes name and an optional description, and the user sees Allow this app to register this name? with the fee. UPDATE_NAME takes oldName and newName (and an optional description) to change a name. Both create transactions, so they cost QORT and need the user's approval.

entries.q: Can my app buy or sell names for the user?
entries.a: Yes. SELL_NAME takes nameForSale and salePrice, CANCEL_SELL_NAME takes nameForSale, and BUY_NAME takes nameForSale. Each one shows the user what will happen, such as buying a name for a price in QORT, and needs their approval.

entries.q: How do I search only one publisher's resources?
entries.a: Pass name together with exactMatchNames set to true in SEARCH_QDN_RESOURCES. Without exactMatchNames, name is matched partially, so a search for one name can also return names that merely contain it.

entries.q: How do I search several names at once?
entries.a: Give SEARCH_QDN_RESOURCES a names array instead of name, for example the names a user follows. Add exactMatchNames set to true so only those exact names come back. One search like this is cheaper than one per name.

entries.q: What does limit 0 mean in a QDN search?
entries.a: To Core, limit 0 means no limit: every matching resource comes back, which can be huge and slow. Ask for pages of about 20 and load more as the user scrolls.

entries.q: How do I page through QDN search results?
entries.a: Use limit for the page size and offset for how many to skip: offset 0 for the first page, 20 for the next with limit 20, and so on. Set reverse to true to get the newest first. Stop when a page comes back shorter than limit.

entries.q: Can I search QDN by title or description?
entries.a: Yes. Besides query (which looks in the name and identifier), q-apps.js passes title, description and keywords to the node's search. Keep the payload small and use only the filters you need, since unknown or extra keys can make a search come back empty.

entries.q: How do I get QDN resources from a time range?
entries.a: Add after and before to SEARCH_QDN_RESOURCES, each a time in milliseconds. after gives resources created after that moment and before gives those created before it, so you can fetch only what is new since your last check.

entries.q: When should I set includeMetadata in a search?
entries.a: Only when you show titles, descriptions or tags. It makes each result carry its metadata, but the node takes longer to answer. For a list of identifiers you'll open anyway, leave it out.

entries.q: What does includeStatus do in a QDN search?
entries.a: It adds each resource's download status to the results, so you can mark which ones are ready on this node. It makes the search slower, so ask only when you need it.

entries.q: How do I show only content from followed names?
entries.a: Set followedOnly to true in SEARCH_QDN_RESOURCES or LIST_QDN_RESOURCES. The node then returns only resources from names it follows, which on the user's own node means the names they follow.

entries.q: How do I hide content from blocked names?
entries.a: Set excludeBlocked to true in SEARCH_QDN_RESOURCES or LIST_QDN_RESOURCES, and the node leaves out resources from names it has blocked. Most apps should always send it.

entries.q: What is nameListFilter in a QDN search?
aliases: filter by list of names qdn
entries.a: nameListFilter takes the name of a list kept on the node, and the search returns only resources from names in that list. Apps can keep such a list with ADD_LIST_ITEMS. Lists live on the user's own node, so this doesn't help on a public node.

entries.q: What does default true do in a QDN search?
entries.a: It returns only default resources, the ones published without an identifier, such as each name's main APP or WEBSITE. Leave it out to get both kinds.

entries.q: What does minLevel do in a QDN search?
entries.a: minLevel filters results by the publisher's account level, so only accounts at or above that level are returned. Use it where you want to show content only from established accounts.

entries.q: What fields does a QDN search result have?
entries.a: Each row has name, service, identifier, size, created and updated (times in milliseconds). With includeMetadata it also has metadata: title, description, tags, category, categoryName and mimeType when they exist. Some versions wrap the list in an object, so make sure you end up with an array.

entries.q: What fields does GET_QDN_RESOURCE_STATUS return?
entries.a: It returns status, id, title and description for the state, plus localChunkCount, totalChunkCount and percentLoaded. Show percentLoaded as progress while the node downloads, and wait for READY before you fetch large data.

entries.q: How should my app react to each GET_QDN_RESOURCE_STATUS value?
aliases: status MISSING_DATA what to do app
entries.a: READY means the data can be fetched. PUBLISHED, DOWNLOADING, DOWNLOADED and BUILDING mean the node is still getting it, so show progress and wait. MISSING_DATA and BUILD_FAILED mean try again later. NOT_PUBLISHED means it doesn't exist, BLOCKED means the name is blocked on this node, and UNSUPPORTED means the request isn't supported.

entries.q: How do I make the node start downloading a resource?
aliases: ask node to fetch data from app
entries.a: Call GET_QDN_RESOURCE_STATUS with build set to true. The node starts fetching and building the resource in the background, and you can call the status again until it says READY.

entries.q: How should my app show a resource the node hasn't downloaded yet?
aliases: data not on node yet app
entries.a: Show Fetching from peers... with the progress from GET_QDN_RESOURCE_STATUS, and try again after 2, 4, 8 and 16 seconds. Don't tell the user to check their node: the data simply isn't there yet. Never show a broken image.

entries.q: What should my app show if a resource still won't load?
aliases: not available on your node right now
entries.a: After about three failed tries, show the title and date you already have from the search row, with Not available on your node right now and a retry. Never leave a loading skeleton that never ends.

entries.q: Why does GET_QDN_RESOURCE_URL say Resource does not exist?
entries.a: q-apps.js checks the status first and gives that error when the node knows no such resource (NOT_PUBLISHED) or has no status for it. Check the name, service and identifier, which are case-sensitive, and show a placeholder instead of a broken image.

entries.q: What address does GET_QDN_RESOURCE_URL give?
entries.a: It gives an address on the node: /arbitrary/<service>/<name>/<identifier>, with ?filepath=<path> added for one file inside a multi-file resource. It works as an image or video source, or for fetch, inside Hub and GO.

entries.q: How do I list the files inside a published APP or WEBSITE?
aliases: what files are in this app qdn
entries.a: Call GET_QDN_RESOURCE_METADATA for it: the answer includes files, the list of paths inside the resource. Paths published from Windows can use backslashes, so treat a backslash as a slash. Then fetch a file with FETCH_QDN_RESOURCE and filepath.

entries.q: Why does GET_QDN_RESOURCE_METADATA fail for some resources?
entries.a: The node answers 404 when it has no metadata for that resource, for example when it was published without a title, description or tags, or when the node hasn't fetched the metadata file yet. Fall back to the name and identifier.

entries.q: Why should my app encode names in its own node requests?
entries.a: Names can contain spaces, + and other characters, and q-apps.js puts some names into addresses as they are, for example in SEARCH_NAMES, GET_QDN_RESOURCE_STATUS and GET_QDN_RESOURCE_PROPERTIES. In your own fetch calls, encode every name and path part with encodeURIComponent. Test with names that have a space, a + or non-English letters.

entries.q: Can I trust the publisher name written inside fetched JSON?
entries.a: No. Anyone can publish under your app's identifiers with their own name, and a JSON body can claim any author. Trust the name and identifier from the search row or request, key your caches by both, and ignore author fields inside the body.

entries.q: How do I read a group's chat messages from my app?
entries.a: Use SEARCH_CHAT_MESSAGES with txGroupId set to the group's id, or involving with two addresses for a private chat, plus before, after, limit, offset and reverse. Set encoding to BASE64 to get the data as base64 instead of base58, then decode it. Private messages come back encrypted.

entries.q: How do I check that a payment reached an address?
entries.a: Use SEARCH_TRANSACTIONS with txType set to PAYMENT, address set to the receiving address and confirmationStatus CONFIRMED, newest first. Match the amount, sender and time you expect, because payments carry no order number of their own. Keep your own record of what you're waiting for.

entries.q: How do I get the results of a poll?
entries.a: Fetch /polls/votes/<pollName> from the node with a relative fetch; it returns the votes for that poll. Encode the poll name, and create polls with unique names so you read the right one.

entries.q: Should my app merge identical QDN searches?
entries.a: Yes. Keep one promise per set of search parameters, and let a second identical call wait for the first. q-apps.js already shares some identical reads that are in flight, but your own merging cuts the work, especially in GO where every request makes an extra hop.

entries.q: Should my app cache QDN search results?
entries.a: Yes, for the session: reuse results for 1 to 3 minutes, and drop the affected entries right after the user publishes something. That keeps lists fast without showing stale data for long.

entries.q: How should I load thumbnails in a long list?
entries.a: Load each image only when its row scrolls into view, with an IntersectionObserver, and show the THUMBNAIL rather than the full IMAGE in lists. Some UI components start loading their image as soon as they mount, so check that yours really waits.

entries.q: Which optional fields can PUBLISH_QDN_RESOURCE take?
aliases: what can i set when publishing from app
entries.a: Besides service, the data (data64, base64 or file) and usually name and identifier, Hub accepts filename, title, description, category, tags (an array) or tag1 to tag5, encrypt with publicKeys, appFee with appFeeRecipient, and isMultiFileZip for a zip that should become a multi-file APP or WEBSITE. Unknown keys are ignored.

entries.q: What does filename do when my app publishes?
entries.a: It names the file the node stores, which helps apps and downloads tell its type. If the name has no proper extension, Core detects the type and adds one; with no filename at all it uses a qortal-<time> name. Give a real name such as photo.jpg when users will download the file.

entries.q: Can I pass tags as an array when publishing?
aliases: how to add tags in PUBLISH_QDN_RESOURCE
entries.a: Yes. Hub takes a tags array and uses the first five, or the older tag1 to tag5 fields; both end up as the same five tags. Keep them short, since Core drops a tag that is too long.

entries.q: How can my app charge a fee when users publish?
aliases: add app fee to publish q-app
entries.a: Add appFee (in QORT) and appFeeRecipient to PUBLISH_QDN_RESOURCE or PUBLISH_MULTIPLE_QDN_RESOURCES. Hub pays it after the publish succeeds. The approval shows the app fee with an Accept app fee box, ticked at first, and the user must also tick the confirmation; the fee is paid only if Accept app fee stays ticked. Say in your app what the fee is for.

entries.q: How does Hub report publish progress to my app?
entries.a: While it uploads, Hub posts PUBLISH_STATUS messages to your app's window with publishLocation (name, identifier, service), chunks sent, totalChunks, retry, filename and processed. processed is true once the node has taken the publish. Listen for message events and show the progress per file.

entries.q: How should my app handle users who can't publish from the public node?
aliases: publish refused api key q-app users
entries.a: The public node takes no uploads without its API key, so publishes from users on it are refused, and GO tells them Your node needs its API key to publish, with a way to open node settings. Check IS_USING_PUBLIC_NODE before the user fills in a long form, and explain that publishing needs their own node, while reading still works.

entries.q: How does Hub upload a big file to QDN?
entries.a: Hub first asks the node whether it has room (if not: Not enough space on your hard drive), then sends the file in 5 MB chunks, retrying a failed chunk up to three times, and finally asks the node to join them and build the transaction. You get PUBLISH_STATUS for each step.

entries.q: How long can a publish take before Hub gives up?
entries.a: Hub waits up to an hour for one PUBLISH_QDN_RESOURCE and 30 minutes per resource for PUBLISH_MULTIPLE_QDN_RESOURCES, because big uploads and the proof-of-work on slow machines take time. So never give up on a publish after 30 seconds; show progress instead.

entries.q: Which publish errors should my app retry?
aliases: your node did not answer publish
entries.a: Only those where the node didn't answer. Hub already retries network errors, timeouts and busy replies by itself. A refusal from the node (such as a missing API key or a validation error) comes back at once with Core's own words and won't change if you retry, and a decline is the user's choice. And after any unclear failure, check whether the resource exists before publishing again.

entries.q: What happens when some files in PUBLISH_MULTIPLE_QDN_RESOURCES fail?
entries.a: Hub publishes the others, then rejects with Some resources have failed to publish and a list, unsuccessfulPublishes, giving each failed file's reason, identifier, service and name. Retry only those, not the whole batch.

entries.q: Can one batch publish use several of the user's names?
aliases: name does not belong to the publisher
entries.a: Yes. Each resource in PUBLISH_MULTIPLE_QDN_RESOURCES can set its own name, as long as every one belongs to the user; one that doesn't stops the batch with The name X, does not belong to the publisher. A resource without a name uses the account's primary name.

entries.q: How do I encrypt every file in a batch publish?
entries.a: Set encrypt to true and publicKeys (the readers' public keys) at the top of PUBLISH_MULTIPLE_QDN_RESOURCES. Every encrypted resource must use a service ending in _PRIVATE; give one resource disableEncrypt set to true to leave it public, for example its thumbnail. Q-Mail publishes mail this way.

entries.q: What do the _PRIVATE errors mean when my app publishes?
aliases: only encrypted data can go into private services
use a service that ends with _PRIVATE
entries.a: Only encrypted data can go into private services means you sent plain data to a _PRIVATE service: turn on encrypt with publicKeys, or encrypt it first. For an encrypted publish please use a service that ends with _PRIVATE means the reverse: you asked to encrypt into a public service, so switch to one such as DOCUMENT_PRIVATE.

entries.q: Why does the node refuse encrypted data in a public service?
entries.a: Core checks single-file data when it's published: data in a _PRIVATE service must start with Qortal's encrypted-data marker, and data in a public service must not. A mix-up fails with DATA_NOT_ENCRYPTED or DATA_ENCRYPTED. Hub's encrypt option adds the marker for you.

entries.q: Are the title and tags of an encrypted publish private?
aliases: what is public in private publish
entries.a: No. Only the data is encrypted. The name, service, identifier, title, description and tags stay public plain text that anyone can search, so never put private details in them.

entries.q: How does encrypt work in PUBLISH_QDN_RESOURCE?
entries.a: Set encrypt to true and publicKeys to the list of readers' public keys, and use a _PRIVATE service. Hub encrypts the data before upload so those keys, and the publisher, can read it. Without publicKeys it fails with Encrypting data requires public keys. Older docs show recipientPublicKey; current Hub uses publicKeys.

entries.q: How can my app keep a user's settings privately on QDN?
entries.a: Publish them as DOCUMENT_PRIVATE under the user's name with a fixed identifier for your app, encrypt set to true and publicKeys holding only the user's own public key. Read it back with FETCH_QDN_RESOURCE and DECRYPT_DATA. Q-Mail keeps its mail state this way, and the latest publish replaces the old one.

entries.q: Do I need a public key to decrypt with DECRYPT_DATA?
entries.a: Only for data in the older single-recipient format: then pass publicKey, the other person's key, with encryptedData. Data encrypted for a list of public keys, which is what Hub's encrypt and ENCRYPT_DATA produce, needs only encryptedData. The answer is the plain data in base64.

entries.q: How do I publish a zip as an APP or WEBSITE from my app?
aliases: publish zip as app from code
Can I publish multi-file WEBSITE or APP from inside a Q-App via qortalRequest
entries.a: Call PUBLISH_QDN_RESOURCE with service APP or WEBSITE, the zip as file, and isMultiFileZip set to true; add title and description as usual. The node then unpacks it into a multi-file resource. Without isMultiFileZip the zip is stored as one file, and a WEBSITE fails with MISSING_INDEX_FILE. Older Hubs may not support this, so tell users to update if it fails.

entries.q: Does the node accept a zip with everything inside one folder?
aliases: Why must index.html be at the zip root
What is a flat dist zip
entries.a: Yes, in one case: when the zip holds exactly one top-level folder (folders starting with an underscore, such as __MACOSX, are ignored), Core uses that folder as the root. With more than one item at the top it doesn't. The safe way is still to zip the contents, so index.html sits at the top.

entries.q: Can I publish under an identifier from Hub's publish screen?
entries.a: No. My apps, then Publish app or Publish website, publishes the name's default APP or WEBSITE; it has no identifier field, which is why it says only one App and Website is allowed per Name. To publish another APP under the same name, such as a GO widget, publish from code with an identifier.

entries.q: Which identifiers can't my app publish to?
entries.a: Hub refuses identifiers that start with symmetric-qchat-group-, which hold group chat keys, with Invalid Data. Identifiers can be at most 64 characters, and they are case-sensitive.

entries.q: What happens if my app publishes without an identifier?
entries.a: Hub publishes it as default, the one resource for that name and service with no identifier. A second publish without an identifier replaces it, so app data should always have its own identifier; leave it out only for the main item, such as the name's website.

entries.q: Why does a publish fail while the node is syncing?
aliases: node not up to date publish
entries.a: Core refuses new uploads until it's up to date: its latest block has to be less than about an hour old. Wait for the node to finish syncing, then publish again.

entries.q: What does a successful publish return?
entries.a: The ARBITRARY transaction: type, timestamp, signature, fee, name, identifier, service (as a number), size, and more. Keep the signature if you want to point to that exact publish. PUBLISH_MULTIPLE_QDN_RESOURCES returns a list of them.

entries.q: What do the service numbers in a publish response mean?
entries.a: Each service has a number: for example FILE 140, WEBSITE 200, IMAGE 400, THUMBNAIL 410, VIDEO 500, AUDIO 600, BLOG_POST 777, DOCUMENT 800, APP 1000 and JSON 1110. Private versions end in 1, such as IMAGE_PRIVATE 401 and DOCUMENT_PRIVATE 801.

entries.q: Why does my app's own publish dialog disappear in GO?
aliases: go publish bubble hides app dialog
entries.a: For a file of 5 MB or more, or a publish that takes over 8 seconds, GO hides your app's progress window and shows its own Publishing to QDN window instead, which can shrink to a bubble so the user keeps using your app. When the publish ends, your window comes back if it's still open, for example to show a failure with Retry. PUBLISH_STATUS messages still reach your app as usual.

entries.q: What should my app do with an item replaced by a delete marker?
aliases: handle delete marker in q-app code
entries.a: Treat it as gone: if the fetched data is just the letter D, or your app's own delete marker, show that the publisher deleted it and drop it from your lists. Apps publish such markers at the same name, service and identifier because QDN has no real delete. Decide on one marker for your app and document it.

entries.q: What does DELETE_HOSTED_DATA do?
aliases: remove node copies from q-app code
entries.a: It removes copies from the user's own node, not from QDN. Pass hostedData, a list of service, name and identifier; the user is asked Allow this app to delete N hosted resources?, and you get deletedCount, failedCount and failures back. It doesn't work on a public node.

entries.q: What does GET_HOSTED_DATA do?
entries.a: It lists the QDN resources the user's own node is storing, 20 at a time by default, with limit, offset and an optional query. The user is asked Allow this app to get a list of your hosted data? first, and it doesn't work on a public node.

entries.q: How can my app show the publish fee before asking?
entries.a: Fetch /transactions/unitfee?txType=ARBITRARY from the node; the answer is in units of 1/100,000,000 QORT, so divide by 100,000,000. Hub reads the same value for its approval, which shows the fee again before the user accepts. Multiply by the number of resources for a batch.

entries.q: Should likes and votes wait for the publish to finish?
entries.a: No. For likes, votes, follows and small edits, update the screen at once, publish in the background, and roll the change back if the publish fails. Waiting for each publish makes the app feel stuck.

entries.q: How do I warn the user before they close my app mid-task?
entries.a: Call LOCK_TAB with lockMessage, for example while an upload runs; the user is asked once to allow it. If they then close the tab, Hub shows Close Tab Confirmation with your message, and they can cancel. Call UNLOCK_TAB when the work is done.

entries.q: How can I check that the published app is the build I meant?
entries.a: Open the published index.html from the node (for example with FETCH_QDN_RESOURCE and filepath index.html) and compare the script and style files it references with a fresh build of the same commit. Different hashed file names mean an old or different zip went up.

entries.q: What shouldn't my app put in identifiers?
entries.a: Anything private. Identifiers, like titles and tags, are public and searchable by anyone, so keep them to your app prefix and neutral ids. Never put a user's private details, or data from one person meant for another, into an identifier or a link.

entries.q: Which fields does SEND_COIN need?
entries.a: coin (such as QORT), amount, and the receiver in destinationAddress or recipient. For a foreign coin you may add fee, a fee per byte; leave it out to use the default. The user always gets an approval with a confirmation tick.

entries.q: Can SEND_COIN pay a registered name?
aliases: send qort to name from app
entries.a: Yes, for QORT. Hub looks the name up before it asks, shows the name with its full address in the approval, and pays that address; nothing is looked up again after the user accepts. Foreign coins need a real address for that chain.

entries.q: What amount format does SEND_COIN take?
aliases: amount in qort or 1e8 send coin
how to write amount send coin
entries.a: A plain decimal amount in whole coins of the coin you send, such as 1 or 0.25 (QORT, or LTC for a Litecoin send), with at most 8 decimal places, not the 1/100,000,000 units some read APIs return. Forms like 1e3 or 0x10 are refused, and the approval shows the exact amount that will be sent.

entries.q: Does SEND_COIN check the user's balance first?
aliases: amount must be above zero send coin
entries.a: Yes. For QORT, Hub refuses with Insufficient funds when the amount plus the fee is more than the balance, and an amount of zero or less is refused too. Check the balance yourself first if you want to warn the user before the approval.

entries.q: Which coins does SEND_COIN support?
entries.a: QORT, BTC, LTC, DOGE, DGB, RVN and ARRR. Foreign coins can't be sent through a public node, and the approval warns that the coin's private key is sent to the node that makes the payment, so only the user's own node should do it.

entries.q: What does SEND_COIN return for a QORT payment?
entries.a: The PAYMENT transaction: amount, fee, recipient, creatorAddress, senderPublicKey, timestamp, reference and signature, among others. Store the signature with your order so you can show it and look the payment up later.

entries.q: Which formats do Qortal payment links accept?
entries.a: qortal://pay?recipient=<address or name>&amount=<QORT> is the one to use. GO also reads qortal://send, qort:<address>?amount= and qortal://<address>. The receiver may be called recipient, to, address or r, and the amount amount, qty, qort or value; the amount is optional. Write the amount with a dot and URL-encode names, so a space becomes %20.

entries.q: What is MULTI_ASSET_PAYMENT_WITH_PRIVATE_DATA?
entries.a: It pays one or more recipients in a single approval, with payments (each a recipient and amount) and assetId, and can publish data encrypted for each recipient alongside, such as an order's details. The user sees Allow this app to make the following payments and publishes? If one payment fails midway, the error says how many were already sent.

entries.q: Which fields does SEND_CHAT_MESSAGE need?
entries.a: message, plus groupId for a group chat or destinationAddress (or recipient) for a private chat; without either it fails with Please provide a recipient or groupId. The account needs at least 4 QORT, and the user approves each message unless they ticked always allow for your app.

entries.q: Are chat messages sent from my app encrypted?
entries.a: A private message is encrypted to the recipient's public key. A group message sent with SEND_CHAT_MESSAGE is sent unencrypted, so treat it as public to anyone who can read that group's chat.

entries.q: Why can't my app send a private message to some users?
aliases: dm fails no public key q-app
entries.a: Private messages are encrypted to the recipient's public key, and some accounts have none on chain yet. Hub then refuses with Cannot send an encrypted message to this user since they do not have their publickey on chain. Tell the user that this account can't get private messages yet.

entries.q: What happens when a user ticks always allow chat messages for my app?
entries.a: Hub remembers it for your app's name, and later SEND_CHAT_MESSAGE calls are sent without asking. That trust is easy to lose, so send messages only when the user has just pressed a send button.

entries.q: How does Hub format a plain chat message sent from my app?
aliases: hub chat format for app messages
entries.a: Hub wraps your message text in its own chat format (messageText as rich text, images, repliedTo, version 3), so it shows like any message in Q-Chat. To send your own format instead, pass fullMessageObject or fullContent as a string, base64 or an object; anything else fails with fullContent is in an invalid format.

entries.q: What is chatReference in SEND_CHAT_MESSAGE?
entries.a: chatReference ties a new message to an earlier one, by that message's signature. Q-Chat uses it for reactions and edits, and SEARCH_CHAT_MESSAGES can filter by chatReference or hasChatReference.

entries.q: Why does sending a chat message from my app take a few seconds?
entries.a: Each chat message needs a small proof-of-work, which Hub computes on the device before it sends, so slow phones take longer. q-apps.js allows 60 seconds for SEND_CHAT_MESSAGE. Show that the message is sending rather than freezing the screen.

entries.q: Can my app create a group?
entries.a: Yes, with CREATE_GROUP and groupName, type, approvalThreshold, minBlock and maxBlock, plus an optional description. The user sees Allow this app to create a group? with the name and fee. UPDATE_GROUP changes one later, with groupId and newOwner among its fields.

entries.q: Which group member actions can my app request?
entries.a: INVITE_TO_GROUP (groupId, inviteeAddress, inviteTime), CANCEL_GROUP_INVITE, KICK_FROM_GROUP, BAN_FROM_GROUP, CANCEL_GROUP_BAN, ADD_GROUP_ADMIN and REMOVE_GROUP_ADMIN (each with groupId and qortalAddress), plus JOIN_GROUP and LEAVE_GROUP with groupId. Each one shows the user what it will do, with its fee, before anything is sent.

entries.q: How can my app send users notifications?
aliases: notify users of new posts app
entries.a: First call NOTIFICATION_PERMISSION; the user sees <your app> notifications with Allow this app to send you GO notifications? and Allow or Don't allow. Then add rules with NOTIFICATION_ADD. Hub and GO watch for new QDN publishes that match a rule and notify the user, so your app doesn't have to stay open. NOTIFICATION_ADD without the permission fails.

entries.q: What does a NOTIFICATION_ADD rule need?
entries.a: A notifications array, each item with notificationId (your name for the rule), link (the qortal:// link to open), filters (which publishes count) and message with at least an en text, plus other languages if you like; image is optional. Adding a rule with an existing notificationId replaces it.

entries.q: Which filters can a notification rule use?
entries.a: service, query, identifier, names, title, description, keywords, prefix, defaultResource, followedOnly, excludeBlocked, after and before, much like the filters of SEARCH_QDN_RESOURCES. Any other key fails with Unknown filter key, and each value must have the right type, such as names as a list of strings.

entries.q: How does my app read or remove its notification rules?
entries.a: NOTIFICATION_GET returns your app's own rules in the same shape you added them. NOTIFICATION_REMOVE with notificationIds removes those rules; without notificationIds it removes all of your app's rules. Apps only see and change their own rules.

entries.q: What is NOTIFICATION_MARK_SEEN?
entries.a: It tells Hub or GO that the user has seen your app's notifications for the given notificationIds, optionally for one identifier, so they aren't shown again. Call it when the user opens the item inside your app.

entries.q: How can my app check notification permission without asking?
entries.a: Call NOTIFICATION_HAS_PERMISSION. It answers true or false without showing anything, so you can show your notification settings correctly and only ask when the user turns them on.

entries.q: How should my app handle a user revoking its notifications?
entries.a: Users can tap Revoke for your app in GO's or Hub's notification settings, which removes every rule your app added; they can also just turn off phone alerts for it. So don't assume your rules are still there: check with NOTIFICATION_HAS_PERMISSION and NOTIFICATION_GET when your settings screen opens, show notifications as off if they're gone, and ask again only when the user turns them on.

entries.q: What does CREATE_AND_COPY_EMBED_LINK do?
entries.a: It builds a qortal://use-embed/ link and copies it to the clipboard, and also returns it. type POLL needs name (ref optional); type IMAGE or ATTACHMENT needs name, service and identifier, and for private encryption also key. People paste the link into chat, where it shows as the item.

entries.q: What does ADMIN_ACTION do?
entries.a: It runs a node admin command for apps like a node manager: stop, restart, bootstrap, addmintingaccount, getmintingaccounts, removemintingaccount, getpeers, addpeer, removepeer, adddatapeer, removedatapeer and forcesync; several need a value. The user is asked Allow this app to perform the admin action: <type>?, and it doesn't work on a public node.

entries.q: How do I show a PDF in Hub's reader from my app?
aliases: open pdf in hub reader from app
entries.a: Call SHOW_PDF_READER with blob set to the PDF as a Blob of type application/pdf. Hub or GO opens its own reader. It fails with Missing blob, or blob type must be application/pdf, when the blob is missing or has another type.

entries.q: Why is a PDF blank inside my Q-App?
entries.a: An iframe or embed showing a PDF stays blank: Hub's window has no PDF plugin and GO's WebView has no PDF viewer. Use SHOW_PDF_READER, or bundle pdf.js in your app; Torq does that and runs pdf.js's worker on the main thread, because a lazily loaded worker file fails to load.

entries.q: How do I save a big QDN file without loading it into memory?
entries.a: Call SAVE_FILE with filename and location set to the resource's service, name and identifier, plus mimeType if you know it. Hub then streams it from the node straight to disk: the desktop shows a Save As window, and GO saves it natively. Nothing large passes through your page.

entries.q: When should SAVE_FILE use a blob and when a location?
entries.a: In the desktop Hub, a blob under about 100 MB saves to Downloads in one step. In GO, and for files over 100 MB, save by location so the file streams from the node. Either way, a user who declines the save prompt isn't an error.

entries.q: Why does SAVE_FILE say a mimeType could not be derived?
aliases: file extension could not be derived
entries.a: Hub needs to know the file's type: from the blob's type or from mimeType in your request. Give the blob a type, or pass mimeType, and use a filename with an extension; otherwise it fails with A mimeType could not be derived or A file extension could not be derived. A missing filename fails too.

entries.q: How do I open an app at a page without opening a second tab?
entries.a: Call OPEN_NEW_TAB with qortalLink, such as qortal://APP/<name>/<path>, and navigateIfAlreadyOpen set to true. If that app is already open, Hub switches to its tab and moves it to the path; otherwise it opens a new tab.

entries.q: Why does OPEN_NEW_TAB fail with Invalid qortal link?
entries.a: qortalLink must be a qortal:// link with at least a service and name, such as qortal://APP/<name>. Hub also refuses names or paths that would climb out of that app, for example with ../ segments. Build links from encoded parts instead of joining raw strings.

entries.q: How does a qortal:// link decide what is the identifier and what is the path?
entries.a: For a link like qortal://SERVICE/name/x/rest, q-apps.js asks the node whether that name has a resource with identifier x. If it does, x is the identifier and the rest is the path; if not, x is the first part of the path. Use default as the third part to say clearly that there is no identifier.

entries.q: How does my app ask GO for full screen?
aliases: hide go bars from q-app code
entries.a: Call qortalRequest with action SET_FULL_SCREEN and enabled set to true, and set it to false when you're done. On GO phones the bars hide for your tab; elsewhere it's simply acknowledged. When full screen ends for another reason (Android back, leaving or closing the tab), GO sends your page FULL_SCREEN_CHANGED with enabled false, so close your viewer then. Widgets can't use it.

entries.q: How is a private Q-App stored on QDN?
entries.a: Your zip (50 MB at most), a logo and the app's name are packed together, encrypted for one private group, and published as a DOCUMENT under your name with an identifier you choose. Only groups where you are an admin can be picked. Members open it from + private app with the group, your name and that identifier; GO builds it on the phone, and the desktop Hub through the user's own node.

entries.q: How does my Q-App notice when the user switches Hub's theme?
entries.a: Hub doesn't reload your app when the user flips light and dark; it posts a THEME_CHANGED message to your page with theme set to light or dark. Listen for message events and restyle. At start, read _qdnTheme or the theme query parameter.

entries.q: How does my Q-App follow the user's language?
entries.a: Hub opens your app with lang set to the user's language code, and the node also puts it in _qdnLang. When the user changes language, Hub posts LANGUAGE_CHANGED with language. Fall back to English for languages you don't have.

entries.q: Which language codes can Hub and GO send to my app?
entries.a: The 12 languages of Hub and GO: en, de, es, et, fi, fr, it, ja, pt, ru, zh and ar. Remember that ar is written right to left.

entries.q: Does Hub pass its custom theme colours to my Q-App?
entries.a: No. Hub tells your app only whether it is in light or dark mode, through the theme parameter, _qdnTheme and THEME_CHANGED. Pick your own colours for each mode.

entries.q: How do I stop a wrong-colour flash when my Q-App loads?
entries.a: Put a small script at the very top of the head in index.html that reads _qdnTheme (or the theme query parameter) and sets the page's background and colour scheme at once, before your bundle loads. Then the first paint already has the right colours, and your app takes over from there.

entries.q: What colours and type match Hub 3.0?
entries.a: Hub 3.0's dark chat surfaces are #0E0F14 and #1D1F27, with one soft blue accent, #84AFF0, 8 px corners and the Inter font. Torq's Hub 3.0 theme, a worked example of that look, pairs them with a warm paper colour, #F6F2EA, in light mode. If you use Inter, bundle the font files in your app.

entries.q: Why shouldn't my Q-App use 100vh?
entries.a: Size the app to the frame Hub or GO gives it, not to 100vh, or parts end up hidden. A phone held sideways gives an app in Hub a frame only about 266 px tall, so plan a compact landscape layout with a low top bar.

entries.q: Why do sticky headers scroll away in my Q-App?
entries.a: overflow-x: hidden on html or body turns body into a scroll container, so sticky headers and back bars scroll away. Use overflow-x: clip instead.

entries.q: How should Back work inside my Q-App?
aliases: history back goes to other tab
entries.a: Use your router's own history for Back, never window.history directly, because all of Hub's tabs share the window's history. A plain history.back() can leave your app or jump to another tab.

entries.q: How does Hub's Back button move inside my app?
entries.a: q-apps.js tells Hub which paths your app has shown. When the user presses Hub's Back or Forward, Hub posts NAVIGATE_TO_PATH with a path; move your router there and answer with NAVIGATION_SUCCESS and the same path. If Hub hears nothing within a fraction of a second, it reloads your app at that path instead.

entries.q: How should my Q-App lay out on phones?
entries.a: Design for 360 to 430 px first: one column, nothing scrolling sideways, text at least 14 px, a bottom bar with at most five items, dialogs full screen or as bottom sheets, and tap targets of at least 44 px. Nothing should work on hover only. Use the phone layout below 600 px wide, since Hub also runs apps in narrow panes.

entries.q: Which screen sizes should I test my Q-App at?
entries.a: At least 360 by 740 and 390 by 844 (phones), 844 by 390 (a phone sideways), 700 px wide (a narrow Hub window) and 1280 px wide, in light and dark mode.

entries.q: How do I keep inputs visible above the phone keyboard?
entries.a: Keep the focused input and its send or publish button above the keyboard by following visualViewport, and don't pin things to the bottom with 100vh. Use the right inputMode, such as decimal for amounts, so phones show the right keys.

entries.q: How do I publish my Q-App from Hub?
aliases: publish app button my apps tab
how to put my app on qdn
entries.a: Open the Q-Apps library, go to My apps and choose Publish app. Pick the name, keep the type APP, fill in title, description, category and up to five tags, choose your .zip (50 MB at most), and press Publish. Hub shows the fee to confirm, publishes, then opens your app.

entries.q: Which fields does Hub's publish screen require?
entries.a: Name, title, description, category, the type (APP or WEBSITE) and the zip; if one is missing Hub lists it under Missing fields. The title takes up to 80 characters, the description 240, and each of the five tags 20.

entries.q: How do I update my published Q-App?
aliases: upload new zip for my app
entries.a: In the Q-Apps library, open My apps: Your published apps lists them, each with Update. That opens the publish form for that name with the old title, description, category and tags filled in. Choose the new zip and publish; it replaces the old version at the same name.

entries.q: How do I start a new Q-App project quickly?
entries.a: The create-qortal-app package from npm sets up a project from a template, such as react-default-template, after you give the app a name. You need Node.js, an editor and Qortal Hub. Its development server runs on port 5173, ready to open in Hub's Dev Mode.

entries.q: How do I turn on Dev Mode in Qortal Hub?
aliases: where is dev mode in hub
entries.a: Open Hub's settings, go to the Developer tab and turn on Enable Dev Mode. A Dev Mode button then appears in the left sidebar; you may need to move the mouse to the left edge to see it.

entries.q: What can I open from Hub's Dev Mode?
entries.a: Server opens your development server through the node, Zip previews a zip file, and Directory zips a folder and previews it, all with the real qortalRequest and your account. Q-Sandbox opens the Q-Sandbox app, and API opens your node's API documentation page.

entries.q: How do I run my development server inside Hub?
entries.a: In Dev Mode, choose Server, enter the domain (127.0.0.1 or localhost) and your port, such as 5173, and press Add. The app opens in a Hub tab through your node's dev proxy, with the real qortalRequest, your account and Hub's theme. If changes don't show, use the refresh button.

entries.q: Why does Hub's Dev Mode tell me to use my local node?
aliases: please use your local node for dev mode
entries.a: Hub's Dev Mode needs the node on your own computer: the dev proxy runs on the node's machine and reaches your development server there, and building a zip preview needs the node's API key, which a public node never accepts. So Hub stops with a request to log out and use Local node. GO's Dev Mode works differently and runs on the public node too.

entries.q: Why does Dev Mode Zip say I need a name?
aliases: you need a name to use preview
entries.a: Hub builds the preview of your zip under your registered name, the way it would be published. Without a name it stops with You need a name to use preview. Register a name first; the preview itself costs nothing.

entries.q: How do I test my exact zip in Hub before publishing?
aliases: test zip in hub dev mode
entries.a: In Dev Mode choose Zip and pick the file. Hub previews it under your name without publishing anything, served the way the node would serve the published app. The tab's refresh reads the same file again, so you can rebuild and refresh.

entries.q: What does Directory do in Hub's Dev Mode?
entries.a: It zips the folder you pick, for example your build output, and previews it like Zip does. Refreshing the tab zips the folder again, so a new build shows without making a zip by hand.

entries.q: Why does my app lose qortalRequest on a deep path in Dev Mode?
aliases: dev proxy deep link no qortalRequest
entries.a: The node's dev proxy only adds q-apps.js to the root page and to .html files, so a deep path loads without qortalRequest. Reload at the root and move to the page with your app's router.

entries.q: Why is my built app blank in Dev Mode Server?
aliases: built app blank dev mode server
entries.a: Core 6.1.9's dev proxy answers 404 for every path under /assets/, which is where Vite puts built files. Test a build with Dev Mode's Zip instead, or use the development server; for a quick check you can build with another assets folder, but don't publish it that way.

entries.q: Why doesn't hot reload work through Hub?
entries.a: Vite's live-reload connection never gets through the node's proxy, so reload the tab yourself. After Vite optimises new dependencies a page can load two copies of React (Invalid hook call): reload again or restart Vite with --force. If the proxy stops after Vite restarts, add the server again in Dev Mode and close the dead tab.

entries.q: How do I see my Q-App's console in Hub?
entries.a: In the desktop Hub, open View, then Toggle Developer Tools. The console and network tabs show your app's errors and requests; check that nothing fails and that it doesn't fire request storms.

entries.q: Can I test Q-App publishing on a testnet?
entries.a: Yes. Qortal's docs suggest the official testnet, or a single-node testnet (often called a devnet) on your own machine, for an end-to-end test of publishing. Publishing an unfinished app to mainnet isn't recommended; for most checks a preview is enough.

entries.q: How do I unit-test a Q-App without a Qortal node?
entries.a: Use a test runner such as vitest with jsdom, and put a global qortalRequest mock in your test setup that answers by action. Then you can check which calls your code makes and how many, for example that the first screen makes only a few SEARCH_QDN_RESOURCES calls.

entries.q: How do I check my Q-App for request storms?
entries.a: Count the SEARCH_QDN_RESOURCES calls on first load, with a small wrapper or a test spy, and watch the console in Hub. Write down the numbers before and after a change, along with your biggest bundle chunk.

entries.q: How is testing in GO different from testing in Hub?
entries.a: GO renders Q-Apps in Android System WebView, which is Chromium updated through the Play Store, inside a phone-sized frame. So check touch, the keyboard, narrow layouts and GO's own behaviour, such as its publish window, full screen and sideways swipes between sections, on a real phone.

entries.q: How do I publish a GO widget?
entries.a: Publish it as service APP under your name with identifier go-widget-<slug> (lowercase letters, digits and dashes) and the tag go-widget, a short title of up to about 24 characters and a one-sentence description. From code, use PUBLISH_QDN_RESOURCE with the zip as file and isMultiFileZip set to true, index.html at the zip's top. GO's picker shows that title and description, with your name's avatar as the icon.

entries.q: Should my widget use the go-widget identifier or the tag?
entries.a: Both if you can. An identifier starting with go-widget is filtered by Core on the node, so GO finds it fast, and it lets a name publish its widget next to its main app. The go-widget tag also works, for a name whose default APP is the widget, but GO finds tags by reading every APP's metadata, which is slower.

entries.q: How do I turn my QDN website into a GO widget?
entries.a: GO lists only APP resources, never a WEBSITE. Make a small page for the widget view and publish it as an APP under your website's name, with identifier go-widget-<slug> and the tag go-widget. Link to the full site with qortal://WEBSITE/<name>/<path> through OPEN_NEW_TAB, and don't embed outside web content.

entries.q: What address does GO load my widget at?
entries.a: <node>/render/APP/<name> with theme (dark or light), lang (GO's language code), identifier (empty for a default APP) and goWidget=1 in the query. Core injects qortalRequest into the page as for every Q-App.

entries.q: How does my page know it is running as a GO widget?
aliases: is my app a widget now
entries.a: goWidget=1 is always in the address on GO's widgets screen. Read it when the page starts and draw your widget view from the very first frame, so a full app never flashes in the small frame.

entries.q: What background should my GO widget have?
entries.a: Transparent. The frame sits on GO's own card, with 16 px rounded corners and GO's card colour, so a transparent page blends in; a solid background shows as a box inside the card.

entries.q: What grid does GO's widgets screen use?
entries.a: 4 columns and 40 px rows with 12 px gaps, at most 560 px wide. A widget is 1 to 4 columns wide and 2 to 14 rows tall, and a new one starts full width and 5 rows tall until the widget or the user sizes it. Height in px is rows times 40 plus 12 for each gap between rows.

entries.q: Which pixel sizes must my GO widget handle?
entries.a: On a 375 px wide phone, anything from 79 by 92 (1 by 2 cells) to 351 by 716 (4 by 14), because users resize widgets at any time. Check at least 79 by 92, 170 by 144, 351 by 248 and 351 by 716. Use vw, vh, min() and clamp() (the frame is your viewport) or listen to resize, and hide details that don't fit.

entries.q: How does my widget ask GO for a size?
entries.a: Call GO_WIDGET_SET_SIZE once at start with width small (1 column), half (2) or full (4) and height in CSS px; GO rounds up to whole rows and remembers it. It only applies until the user resizes the widget; after that the answer's applied is false and the user's size stays. Never call it in a loop.

entries.q: What does GO_WIDGET_INFO return?
entries.a: widget (true), platform (GO 3.0), theme, language, visible, the frame's width and height in px, its columns and rows, gridColumns, minRows, maxRows, and sizedBy: default, widget or user.

entries.q: What happens if my widget calls GO_WIDGET requests outside GO?
entries.a: In the Hub or a normal Q-App tab they may fail or never answer. Send them only when goWidget=1 is in the address, never wait for them before drawing, and give any answer you need a short timeout, such as 1.5 seconds.

entries.q: Which messages does GO send to a widget?
entries.a: GO_WIDGET_VISIBILITY with payload.visible when the widgets screen comes into view or leaves it (or GO goes to the background), THEME_CHANGED with theme, and LANGUAGE_CHANGED with language. All three are also sent right after your widget loads.

entries.q: What must my widget do while it isn't visible?
entries.a: Pause timers, animations and polling when GO_WIDGET_VISIBILITY says visible false, and also when document.visibilityState is hidden; start again when it's visible. When showing, poll no more than every 30 seconds, and once a minute is better.

entries.q: Which read requests work in a GO widget?
entries.a: The read-only ones Core answers in your frame, as in any Q-App: SEARCH_QDN_RESOURCES, FETCH_QDN_RESOURCE, LIST_QDN_RESOURCES, GET_QDN_RESOURCE_URL, GET_QDN_RESOURCE_STATUS, GET_QDN_RESOURCE_PROPERTIES, GET_QDN_RESOURCE_METADATA, GET_ACCOUNT_DATA, GET_ACCOUNT_NAMES, GET_NAME_DATA, SEARCH_NAMES, GET_BALANCE, GET_PRICE, LIST_GROUPS, SEARCH_CHAT_MESSAGES, SEARCH_TRANSACTIONS, and the block and AT reads. Of GO's own requests, GET_PRIMARY_NAME, GET_NODE_INFO, GET_NODE_STATUS, IS_USING_PUBLIC_NODE, WHICH_UI, GET_DAY_SUMMARY and the GO_WIDGET ones always work.

entries.q: Which requests work in a widget only while the widgets screen shows?
aliases: the widgets screen is not showing error
entries.a: OPEN_NEW_TAB, SET_TAB, OPEN_USER_LOOKUP, GET_USER_ACCOUNT and GET_WALLET_BALANCE; the last two ask the user as in any Q-App. When the screen is hidden they fail with The widgets screen is not showing.

entries.q: Which requests are refused in GO widgets?
aliases: not available in go widgets error
entries.a: Everything else, including SEND_COIN, both publishes, SIGN_TRANSACTION, every ENCRYPT and DECRYPT action, SEND_CHAT_MESSAGE, SAVE_FILE, the NOTIFICATION actions, SET_FULL_SCREEN, trade, name, group and list changes, and unknown actions. They fail with a message starting Not available in GO widgets, so handle that without breaking.

entries.q: How does my widget do something it isn't allowed to do?
entries.a: Open your full app at the right page: OPEN_NEW_TAB with qortalLink set to qortal://APP/<your app>/<path>. GO switches to Apps with your app open there, and the payment, publish or message happens in the app, with GO's usual approval.

entries.q: What can't a widget's frame do?
entries.a: The frame is sandboxed with scripts, same-origin and forms only. alert, confirm and prompt do nothing, and there are no pop-up windows, downloads, full screen, clipboard, camera, microphone or location. Use inline UI instead of dialogs.

entries.q: Can my widget use sideways swipes or long presses?
entries.a: No. GO takes a swipe once it's clearly sideways (about 10 px, wider than tall) and takes a long press at 400 ms to pick the widget up; your page then gets a touchcancel. Build with buttons and vertical lists, not carousels or long-press menus. While the user arranges the screen, your widget gets no touches at all.

entries.q: How fast should my widget start?
entries.a: Show something useful within about 300 ms, because GO unloads widgets a few minutes after the screen was last seen and loads them again each visit. A single index.html with inline CSS and JS starts fastest; keep the bundle under about 200 KB and draw from cache before you refresh.

entries.q: Where should my widget keep its settings?
entries.a: In localStorage, under keys prefixed with your name, such as yourname.clock.hour12, since every Q-App from the node shares that storage. For the setting itself use a small inline form inside the widget; inputs work, dialogs don't.

entries.q: What privacy rules should a GO widget follow?
entries.a: Load your code and data only from your bundle and QDN: outside web services may be blocked and leak the user's IP address and activity. Ask only for what you show, so no GET_USER_ACCOUNT unless the widget is about their account, and never put user data in links, identifiers or anything you publish.

entries.q: Should I build a separate widget or a widget mode in my app?
entries.a: A separate small widget beside your app is better for almost everyone: publish a light page as APP with identifier go-widget-<slug> under your app's name, reusing only your data code. A widget mode inside your app, shown when goWidget=1, suits only apps that are already small and fast; if your app takes more than about a second to show on a phone, make a separate widget.

entries.q: How do I add a widget mode to my existing Q-App?
entries.a: Check goWidget=1 once at start, before routers and providers, and then show a compact view: transparent background, no bars, menus or splash screen, data from cache first, fitted to the frame, no sideways swipes or dialogs, and every action opening your full app with OPEN_NEW_TAB. Pause timers on GO_WIDGET_VISIBILITY, avoid requests widgets refuse, add the tag go-widget, and publish.

entries.q: How do I test my GO widget?
entries.a: Open it as a normal app with ?goWidget=1&theme=dark (and light) added to its address, at several window sizes. Then publish it, and in GO swipe to the widgets screen, tap +, find it and add it: check that it starts quickly, follows theme changes and pauses when you leave. Hold it to resize it to its smallest and largest, move it and drop it on Remove, and swipe sideways across it.

entries.q: Is there an example GO widget I can start from?
entries.a: Yes. docs/go/go-widgets.md in the Qortal Hub repo has a template that handles theme, language, visibility and sizing, and the GO Clock example is tools/preview/fake-node/render/APP/GOClock.html; publish it as APP under your name with identifier go-widget-clock.

entries.q: Why doesn't my widget update right after I publish a new version?
entries.a: After its first load, GO keeps a copy of your widget's published files on the phone and opens it from there, while the data it shows still comes from QDN live. At most once an hour GO checks for a newer publish and fetches it in the background, and the new version shows from the widget's next load. The menu's Reload reloads the widget.

entries.q: What checklist should my GO widget pass?
entries.a: Published as APP with a go-widget identifier or tag, short title and one-line description. Draws the widget view from goWidget=1 on the first frame, with a transparent background that follows theme. Looks right from 79 by 92 to 351 by 716 px, pauses when hidden, uses only allowed requests and opens the full app for actions. No sideways or long-press gestures, dialogs or outside web requests; shows something within about 300 ms, with empty and error states; prefixes its storage keys.

entries.q: How do I show the latest items from my app in a widget?
entries.a: Search with SEARCH_QDN_RESOURCES for your app's service and identifier prefix, with prefix true, includeMetadata, excludeBlocked, a small limit such as 5 and reverse true for newest first. Draw each as a row at least 40 px tall that opens the full app at that item with OPEN_NEW_TAB, and show only as many rows as fit the frame's height.

entries.q: Why do some files of my widget fail to load?
entries.a: For an APP under an identifier, the node picks files by the identifier in the address. In HTML pages it adds that identifier to relative script and link tags for you, but other relative loads, such as images, fetches or lazily loaded script chunks, don't get it and are looked up in the name's default app instead. A single index.html with its CSS and JS inline, as GO's widget guide suggests, avoids this.

entries.q: Why does my Q-App's size matter so much?
entries.a: The zip is downloaded from peers, so every KB counts: a node that doesn't have your app yet must fetch all of it before the first open. Keep the biggest JavaScript chunk well under 1 MB where you can, lazy-load heavy screens and libraries (editors, PDF, emoji, charts, video), and remove dependencies you don't use.

entries.q: How do I make my Q-App's first screen appear faster?
entries.a: Show cached data at once and refresh after; use skeletons shaped like the final layout instead of a spinner on a blank page; load only the first page of results; and fetch images as they scroll into view. Code-split so the first screen loads only what it needs.

entries.q: Should my Q-App poll QDN on a timer?
entries.a: Only gently: never a fixed short setInterval. Poll while document.visibilityState is visible, back off when nothing changes, and stop when the view closes. Every search is a round trip to the node, and in GO it also takes an extra hop.

entries.q: What states should every screen in my Q-App have?
entries.a: Loading, with a skeleton like the final layout; empty, with one line saying why and the next action (for example No mail yet, Compose); error, saying in plain words what failed, with Retry; and for QDN data not downloaded yet, Fetching from peers... with progress.
