Never show a raw error or [object Object].

entries.q: Should my app confirm before it publishes or pays?
entries.a: Yes. Before you call the request, say in your own screen what will happen and what it costs, for anything that publishes, spends QORT or deletes. Hub's approval then confirms it, but the user should already know why it's coming.

entries.q: How do I show names and avatars in long lists efficiently?
entries.a: Cache them: the same primary names and avatars come up again and again across lists, so keep one cache for name lookups and one for avatars, and load avatars only for rows on screen. Torq does this with its primary names and profile caches.

entries.q: Which details matter when my Q-App shows user-written HTML?
entries.a: Sanitise it with DOMPurify 3.4 or newer, since older versions have known bypasses. Build links on the DOM, never with a regex over sanitised HTML; one Q-App had a stored XSS hole from exactly that. Drop inline text colours, because white text pasted from dark pages is invisible in light themes.

entries.q: What does qapp-core's GlobalProvider give my app?
entries.a: Auth, lists, identifier hashing and caching, through hooks such as useGlobal, usePublish, useResources and useResourceStatus, plus ResourceListDisplay for lists and VideoPlayer and AudioPlayerControls for media. Torq is one of the apps built on it.

entries.q: Why must I keep my app's qapp-core publicSalt and app name?
entries.a: qapp-core builds your identifiers from them, so changing either one makes the app stop finding the data it already published. Keep the existing publicSalt and app name in its config, even in a fork or redesign.

entries.q: Why keep my app's name and storage prefix in one place?
entries.a: Put the app's name, the name used in copied qortal://APP links, the browser storage prefix, the settings identifier and the repository links in one module. Then a rename or a fork changes one file, and storage keys can't clash with another version of the app on the same node.

entries.q: What does LINK_TO_QDN_RESOURCE do for my own app and for other apps?
aliases: link to other app new tab
entries.a: It takes service, name, identifier and path, and without service it assumes WEBSITE. A link to another name asks Hub to open it in a new tab; if Hub doesn't confirm within 200 ms, or the link points to your own app, the page itself moves there. qortal:// links clicked in your HTML go the same way.

entries.q: Do the encrypt and decrypt actions ask the user?
entries.a: No. ENCRYPT_DATA, DECRYPT_DATA, ENCRYPT_QORTAL_GROUP_DATA, DECRYPT_QORTAL_GROUP_DATA and the sharing-key pair run without an approval window. Decryption only works for data meant for the user's keys or groups. Say in your own screen what you decrypt and why; GO widgets can't use these actions at all.

entries.q: How does my app add or remove items in a node list?
aliases: change node list from q-app code
entries.a: ADD_LIST_ITEMS takes list_name and items, an array; DELETE_LIST_ITEM takes list_name and a single item, so removals go one at a time; GET_LIST_ITEMS takes list_name and returns the list as an array. Each asks the user first, and they work only on the user's own node, since lists are kept there and not on QDN.

entries.q: What is the difference between ENCRYPT_DATA and ENCRYPT_QORTAL_GROUP_DATA?
entries.a: ENCRYPT_DATA with publicKeys encrypts for that fixed list of people, and you. ENCRYPT_QORTAL_GROUP_DATA uses a group's own key, which the group's admins publish for its members: pass groupId (and isAdmins for the admins-only key), and members read it with DECRYPT_QORTAL_GROUP_DATA. It fails with No group key found when the admins haven't published one, and a public node may fail to deliver the key.

entries.q: What are ENCRYPT_DATA_WITH_SHARING_KEY and DECRYPT_DATA_WITH_SHARING_KEY?
entries.a: The first encrypts data for the listed public keys and you, like ENCRYPT_DATA, but seals a sharing key inside, so readers get the key along with the data. Anyone who has that key can then open it with DECRYPT_DATA_WITH_SHARING_KEY, passing encryptedData and key, without a wallet. That is how a link can carry the key to a private image or file, so guard the key like the data itself.

entries.q: How do I play encrypted video from my app?
entries.a: On the desktop Hub, call PLAY_ENCRYPTED_MEDIA with mediaId, key, iv, location (service, name, identifier) and optionally mimeType, for media published with streamed-v1 encryption, and use the streamUrl it returns as the player's source. It runs on Hub's local media server, so it isn't available in GO. It needs no approval and is cleaned up when the tab closes.

entries.q: What is streamed-v1 encryption in a publish?
entries.a: A way to let Hub encrypt a big file as it uploads: give the resource encryption with encryptionType streamed-v1 and your own iv (16 bytes) and key (32 bytes), both base64, and pass the data as file. You keep and share the key yourself, for example encrypted for the recipients. Later, SAVE_FILE by location with the same encryption, or PLAY_ENCRYPTED_MEDIA, decrypts it.

entries.q: Can my app create trade orders?
aliases: sell qort order from q-app code
entries.a: Yes. CREATE_TRADE_SELL_ORDER takes qortAmount, foreignBlockchain and foreignAmount; CREATE_TRADE_BUY_ORDER takes crosschainAtInfo (the offers to buy) and foreignBlockchain; CANCEL_TRADE_SELL_ORDER takes atAddress. Each shows the amounts and an estimated fee and needs the confirmation tick. Trading uses the foreign coin's private key, so the approval says where it goes: the user's own node, or the trade proxy on a public node.

entries.q: What does DEPLOY_AT need?
entries.a: name, description, tags, type, creationBytes (base58), amount and assetId. An AT is an automated transaction, Qortal's kind of smart contract; Q-Fund deploys one for each crowdfund. It's for advanced apps, the user is asked Would you like to deploy this AT?, and it costs a fee.

entries.q: How can my app read its rating from the Q-Apps library?
entries.a: The library keeps ratings in a poll on the blockchain named app-library-APP-rating-<app name> (WEBSITE instead of APP for a site), with the options 1 to 5. Read its votes with a relative fetch of /polls/votes/<that poll name>, encoding the name.

entries.q: Why does Copy link ignore my app's path?
entries.a: Copy link, Share and Refresh use the path your app last reported with QDN_RESOURCE_DISPLAYED, which q-apps.js also sends on load and on navigation. Hub and GO ignore a path that would climb out of your app, for example one with ../ in it. Keep paths inside your app and encode each part.

entries.q: Can my Q-App use the node's API key?
entries.a: No. Hub and GO keep the node's API key to themselves; even private app previews now load without it in their address, because the app could read it there. Don't build on protected node endpoints in your own fetch calls; for node admin tasks use ADMIN_ACTION, which asks the user.

entries.q: What is UPDATE_SUBSCRIPTIONS?
entries.a: Only the Subscriptions app may call it. It tells Hub to fetch the user's group memberships again, for example right after a subscriber has been accepted into a group; any other app gets an error saying so.

entries.q: Which foreign coin server actions can a wallet app use?
entries.a: GET_CROSSCHAIN_SERVER_INFO (servers, remainingServers and uselessServers for a coin), GET_SERVER_CONNECTION_HISTORY, SET_CURRENT_FOREIGN_SERVER, ADD_FOREIGN_SERVER and REMOVE_FOREIGN_SERVER, plus GET_FOREIGN_FEE and UPDATE_FOREIGN_FEE. The ones that change something ask the user first and don't work on a public node.

entries.q: Why does my app's ARRR request show a private key warning?
entries.a: Every ARRR wallet read, whether address, balance, transactions or sync status, sends the ARRR seed to the node. So before the first one in a tab, Hub shows that warning with a tick box, and one consent covers that tab, app, account and node until the tab closes; the authenticate grant and the always boxes don't cover it. A public node refuses these requests.

entries.q: How can I automate testing my Q-App inside the desktop Hub?
entries.a: Start a second, test copy of the desktop Hub with a remote debugging port and drive it through the Chrome DevTools Protocol: list the app frames, run read-only checks inside your app, take screenshots, and emulate phone sizes and touch. The port listens on 127.0.0.1 only, but while it's open other programs on that computer can control that Hub, so close it when you're done.

entries.q: Which app does GO open when a user taps my notification?
entries.a: Your app, the one that added the rule: GO opens it at the path in the rule's link and shows your app's icon, or the post publisher's avatar, even when the rule's link or image names another app. So point notification links into your own app. The rule itself stays stored as you sent it.

entries.q: What should my Q-App's settings page contain?
entries.a: Make it a full page reached from your navigation, not a small dialog. A good order is Account (the active name, with a switcher if you support several), Appearance (theme and display options), your app's own options, optional Sync of settings to QDN under the user's name, and About with the version and a changelog. Torq's Settings page is laid out this way.

entries.q: What accessibility basics should a Q-App follow?
entries.a: Give every icon button an aria-label, keep keyboard focus visible, and keep text contrast at least 4.5 to 1 in light and dark. Keep motion short, about 150 to 200 ms, and honour prefers-reduced-motion. Write short, plain text and keep every string translatable.

entries.q: Why doesn't my new widget show in GO's Add a widget list yet?
entries.a: GO keeps the widget list for about 10 minutes per node, and the user's node must also have your publish. Widgets found only by their tag show up more slowly, since GO reads every APP's metadata for tags; an identifier starting with go-widget is found faster.

entries.q: Which browser engine runs my Q-App in Hub and GO?
entries.a: Chromium in both. The desktop Hub renders apps with the Chromium inside its Electron shell, and GO on Android uses Android System WebView, which the Play Store updates separately from the system. Android 8 and 9 phones stop at Chromium 138, so check newer browser features against that if you support those phones.

entries.q: Do Hub's own React and MUI versions affect my Q-App?
entries.a: No. Each Q-App ships its own libraries inside its zip and runs in its own frame, so you can use the React, MUI or other versions you like, as long as the browser engine supports them.

entries.q: Where does the Q-Apps library get my app's icon, title and description?
entries.a: The title, description, category and tags come from your publish, as you set them in the publish form. The icon is your name's avatar (THUMBNAIL with identifier qortal_avatar), so change the avatar to change the icon. GO keeps icons in a device cache and re-checks each about once a day, so a new one can take up to a day to show there.

entries.q: Will GO's sideways section swipe take swipes from my Q-App?
aliases: horizontal swipe in my app go
entries.a: No, in a normal Q-App tab your page keeps its own swipes. GO switches sections from inside an app only when the user swipes along the round buttons at the bottom. The exception is the widgets screen, where sideways swipes belong to GO.

entries.q: What is DECRYPT_AESGCM?
entries.a: It decrypts AES-GCM data another account encrypted for the user. Pass encryptedData and iv, both base64 with a 12-byte iv, and senderPublicKey in base58; Hub derives the key from the user's private key and the sender's public key and returns the plain data as base64. Wrong data or keys fail with Failed to decrypt the message.

entries.q: How should my Q-App lay out in a wide Hub window?
entries.a: From about 900 px wide: a left navigation rail with icons and labels, the main column centred at a comfortable width (about 600 to 760 px for feeds and lists, wider for grids), and an optional right rail for context such as filters. Use sticky headers with a thin bottom border, and switch to your phone layout below 600 px, since Hub also runs apps in narrow panes.

entries.q: How should my Q-App show images and video on phones?
aliases: let video go full screen in my app
entries.a: Fit images and video to the screen width, let video go full screen, and load thumbnails rather than the originals in lists and on phones. Keep animations short and cheap, since many users run mid-range Android phones.

entries.q: Can an AI coding agent build a GO widget for my app?
entries.a: Yes. Give the agent docs/go/go-widgets.md from the Qortal Hub repository and your app's source; the guide has a ready prompt in section 3.5. It asks for a separate widget drawn from goWidget=1 on the first frame, transparent, following theme, language and visibility, fitting 79 by 92 to 351 by 716 px, using only allowed requests, opening the full app for every action, and passing the guide's checklist.

entries.q: Where can I get help building a Q-App?
entries.a: Qortal's wiki on qortal.dev suggests asking in the ui-extension group on Qortal. The Q-Apps API documentation is on qortal.dev too, and it points to a React tutorial video series that goes from starting a project to publishing it on Qortal.

entries.q: How can my Q-App earn QORT?
entries.a: Through payments the user approves: SEND_COIN for tips or purchases after a clear button press, an appFee on publishes made in your app, or MULTI_ASSET_PAYMENT_WITH_PRIVATE_DATA for orders. Q-Tube's super likes, paid in QORT, are one example. Payments can't be taken back, so always say what a payment is for.

entries.q: What can users without a registered name do in my Q-App?
aliases: app for users with no name
entries.a: They can sign in with GET_USER_ACCOUNT, read everything public, send QORT with SEND_COIN and decrypt data meant for them. They can't publish to QDN (Hub says User has no Qortal name) or rate apps in the library, and chat messages need at least 4 QORT either way. Let them read first and explain what a name adds.

entries.q: Will updating my Q-App lose my users' data?
entries.a: No. Your users' data lives on QDN under their own names, apart from your APP, so publishing a new version of the app doesn't touch it. What can break it is changing how the app finds that data, so keep your services, identifier prefixes and readers for older schemas, and with qapp-core the same publicSalt and app name.

entries.q: Why does my Q-App work in Hub but not in GO?
aliases: q-app works in hub not go
entries.a: Usually one of GO's differences: many GO users are on the public node, which takes no uploads and refuses lists, hosted data and foreign coins; GO's WebView has no PDF viewer; service workers, camera, microphone and location aren't available to apps; and the screen is small and touch-only. Check IS_USING_PUBLIC_NODE, test at phone sizes, and use Dev Mode to try your zip on a phone.

entries.q: Can my Q-App do anything while it's closed?
entries.a: No. Your code runs only while the app is open in a tab. To tell users about new content while it's closed, add notification rules with NOTIFICATION_ADD: Hub and GO watch for matching QDN publishes and notify the user, and the notification opens your app.

entries.q: When should my app publish a file instead of base64?
entries.a: Use data64 (or base64) for small data such as JSON: it goes to the node in one request. Pass a File or Blob as file for anything bigger: Hub checks the node's free space, sends it in 5 MB chunks with retries and reports progress with PUBLISH_STATUS, and your page never has to build a huge base64 string.

entries.q: My Qortal node won't sync. What should I check?
entries.a:
Most sync problems come from too few peers, a wrong clock, a firewall, or a computer that sleeps.
1. Keep Qortal Core running and stop the computer from sleeping.
2. Check that the system clock is right and set to update automatically.
3. Allow TCP 12392 (blockchain peers) and 12394 (QDN data) in your firewall, and turn on UPnP or port forwarding in the router.
4. Make sure Core is up to date.
5. If the node is more than about 1,500 blocks behind, bootstrap it instead of waiting.

entries.q: My first Qortal sync has been running for hours. Is something wrong?
entries.a: Usually not: the first sync gets the whole chain, which can take hours depending on your connection and hardware. Core starts from a bootstrap (a compressed copy of the chain), then syncs the blocks made since that copy, which is rebuilt every 12 hours. Keep the device awake and online until it finishes; it only happens once. The tray icon turns from red to blue when the node is synced.

entries.q: My node is far behind the network. Should I bootstrap it?
entries.a:
If it is more than about 1,500 blocks behind, a bootstrap is usually faster than syncing block by block.
In Hub: open Set up Qortal Core (the Core controls gear on the sign-in screen), then Advanced, then Bootstrap chain.
By hand: stop Core, delete the db folder, and start Core again; it downloads a fresh bootstrap.
Your wallet is stored separately and is not touched. Afterwards the node still syncs the last few hours of blocks.

entries.q: My node is stuck at the same block height. What do I do?
entries.a:
A height that stops moving for several minutes means the node has stalled, often after a network problem or a fork (a side branch of the chain).
1. Blocks come about once a minute, so wait a few minutes first.
2. Restart Core.
3. Compare your height with a block explorer such as exqlorer.com.
4. If it is still stuck or far off, bootstrap the node.
The QORTector auto-fix script works the same way: if the height has not moved since its last run and still does not move over about 3 more minutes, it forces a bootstrap.

entries.q: My node seems to be on a fork. How do I get back on the main chain?
entries.a:
If your height or blocks differ from the explorer and do not fix themselves, the node has followed a side branch the network left.
The simple fix is a bootstrap: Bootstrap chain in Hub, or stop Core, delete the db folder and start it again.
Advanced users can roll back instead with Core's orphan API call, a lower height in steps of 1,000 to 2,000 blocks, and let it sync forward. Keep Core running while it rolls back.

entries.q: My node's connections go up and then drop back to 0. Why?
entries.a:
This is usually a wrong system clock or a firewall. Other nodes refuse a node whose time is too far off, which is common on Windows.
1. Compare your computer's clock with an internet time source and turn on automatic time.
2. Allow TCP 12392 (and 12394 for QDN data) in your firewall. There is no need to turn the firewall off.
3. Restart Core.

entries.q: My node has very few peers. How can I get more?
entries.a:
Few peers usually means other nodes cannot connect in to yours.
1. Turn on UPnP in your router; for a single node that is often enough.
2. Without UPnP, give the node a fixed local address and forward TCP 12392 and 12394 to it.
3. Check that your firewall allows those two ports.
Keep port 12391 closed to the internet: that is the node's API. Some providers filter ports, so forwarding can be needed even with UPnP.

entries.q: Can a wrong clock on my computer break Qortal?
entries.a: Yes. Nodes refuse peers whose time is too far off, and Core refuses transactions until its clock is in sync, with errors like "no clock synchronization yet" or "clock not synchronized". Turn on automatic date and time, check the time zone, and restart Core.

entries.q: What does "blockchain needs to synchronize first" mean?
entries.a: Your node is not synced yet, so it refuses actions that need an up-to-date chain. Wait until Core has caught up (the tray icon turns blue, or Hub shows it as synchronized) and try again. If it stays behind, treat it as a node that won't sync, or bootstrap it.

entries.q: Core says "Repository in use by another process". What should I do?
aliases: repository in use by another process
entries.a: Another copy of Qortal Core is already running and holding the database. Stop that one first, from the tray icon (Exit) or with ./stop.sh in the qortal folder, wait until it has ended, then start Core once.

entries.q: Hub says "error: Unable to start repository". How do I fix it?
entries.a:
Core could not open its chain database.
1. Make sure only one Core is running, then start it again.
2. If it keeps failing, use Bootstrap chain in Hub (Set up Qortal Core, Advanced). It bootstraps, or clears the local chain database and starts Core again.
Your wallet files are stored separately and are left alone.

entries.q: Will bootstrapping or deleting the db folder lose my wallet or QORT?
aliases: is bootstrap safe for my account
entries.a: No. The db folder only holds the node's copy of the blockchain, which Core downloads again. Your QORT is recorded on the blockchain itself, and Hub keeps wallet files separately, so they are left alone. Keep your backup file and seed phrase safe offline anyway.

entries.q: My bootstrap finished but the node still isn't synced. Is that normal?
entries.a: Yes. A bootstrap is a snapshot rebuilt every 12 hours, so after it is applied the node still syncs the blocks made since then. Leave Core running; the tray icon turns from red to blue when it has caught up.

entries.q: My bootstrap keeps failing or takes forever. What can I do?
entries.a:
The bootstrap servers fail now and then, and Core retries by itself; slow connections can also struggle. A bootstrap usually takes 15 to 60 minutes.
1. Leave it running and check that the disk has free space.
2. If it never completes, bootstrap by hand: download a bootstrap archive listed on the Qortal wiki's bootstrap page, extract it, and put the blockchain files into the db folder inside the qortal folder.

entries.q: Hub says "Core maintenance tools are unavailable". Why?
entries.a: Hub turns off Stop Core and Bootstrap chain while Core is still starting up, including while it downloads or applies a bootstrap, so they cannot interrupt it. Wait until Core is running; the tools under Advanced in Set up Qortal Core become available again.

entries.q: Hub says the chosen folder "does not contain a qortal.jar". What now?
entries.a: Hub's custom Core location must point to the folder that holds qortal.jar. On Linux and macOS that is usually the qortal folder in your home folder. In Set up Qortal Core, under Core location, use Change to pick the right folder, or Clear to go back to the default.

entries.q: Hub shows "Core not detected". What should I do?
aliases: please turn on your local node
entries.a: Hub cannot find a Qortal Core running on this computer. Open Set up Qortal Core to download and start Core (it then syncs in the background), and use a public node meanwhile. If Core is installed in an unusual place, set its folder under Core location.

entries.q: Hub says "Core setup needs attention". What does that mean?
aliases: unable to download or install the core
entries.a: A step of the Core download, Java setup or start-up stopped. Tap Open setup to see which step failed, for example "error downloading Java" or "error unzipping Qortal Core". Check your internet connection and free disk space, then try that step again.

entries.q: My manually installed Core won't start on Mac or Linux. Could it be Java?
entries.a: That is a common cause: Qortal Core needs Java 11 or newer. Install a current Java (OpenJDK 11 or later), then run ./start.sh in the qortal folder again. Hub's own Core setup installs Java for you, so this mostly affects manual installs.

entries.q: Windows SmartScreen blocks the Qortal installer. Is it safe to continue?
entries.a: SmartScreen warns about software that Microsoft does not see often yet, which is normal for open-source apps, and Qortal's installer is code-signed. If you downloaded it from qortal.dev or qortal.org, click "More info" and then "Run anyway".

entries.q: macOS says Qortal can't be opened because it is from an unidentified developer. What do I do?
entries.a: That is Gatekeeper being careful on first launch. In Finder, right-click the Qortal app, choose Open and confirm. Or open System Settings, Privacy & Security, and click "Open Anyway" next to Qortal. Only do this for a copy you downloaded from qortal.dev or qortal.org.

entries.q: My antivirus flags Qortal as suspicious. Is it a virus?
entries.a: Usually it is a false positive: node software talks to many peers and writes a lot of blockchain data, which some scanners dislike. If you got Qortal from qortal.dev, qortal.org or the official Qortal GitHub, add the Qortal folder to your antivirus exclusions. Never use builds from unofficial sources.

entries.q: Hub says my local node's API key is invalid. How do I fix it?
entries.a: Hub's saved key no longer matches your local Core's key file, for example after a reinstall. Use reset apikey in that dialog: Hub deletes apikey.txt and makes a new key. Any other device that uses this node, such as GO, then needs the new key in its node settings.

entries.q: A Q-App loading page says "Waiting for data from peers...". What can I do?
aliases: missing data unable to locate all files
entries.a: Your node knows the app or file exists but has not yet found a node that holds all of its pieces. Keep the page open for a while; when peers have it, the page shows how many are available and the download moves on. If nothing changes, the nodes that hold it may be offline: try again later. Apps and files you open on your own node stay there for next time.

entries.q: A loading page says "This resource has not been published to the network". Why?
aliases: no q-app resource found for this link
entries.a: Your node found no publish at that name, service and identifier. Check the link: the name and identifier must match exactly (identifiers are case-sensitive), and the type must be right, such as APP or WEBSITE. It can also mean the publish has not been confirmed on the chain yet, so try again in a few minutes.

entries.q: I lowered my node's peer settings and now it won't sync or mint. Why?
entries.a: Too few peers can stall syncing and minting. minBlockchainPeers is how many peers at a height your node needs before it syncs a block, and 1 never mints, because your own node does not count. About 10 is a safe value and 3 is about the lowest that works. For low data use, the wiki suggests maxPeers 7 with minBlockchainPeers 3.

entries.q: I edited settings.json and now Core won't start. What did I break?
aliases: core wont start after editing settings
entries.a: Usually the JSON format. The file needs a curly brace at the start and end, straight double quotes around each setting name and text value, a colon after each name, and a comma between settings but not after the last one. Numbers and true/false need no quotes. Fix the file, or take out the setting you added, and start Core again. Changes only apply when Core starts.

entries.q: What should I send when I ask for help with my node?
aliases: help with my node what to send
entries.a:
The node's status and the end of its log help most. On Linux and macOS, in a terminal in the qortal folder:
1. ./qort admin/status shows whether the node is syncing and its height.
2. tail -f qortal.log shows the live log (older installs wrote log.txt files).
Say which Core version you run and what you already tried. Never send your seed phrase, backup file or API key.

entries.q: My node didn't auto-update and is on an old Core version. How do I update it?
entries.a:
Core updates itself once the developer group approves a release, unless "autoUpdateEnabled": false is set in settings.json, so check that first. An update takes about 2 hours to reach the whole network.
To update by hand on Linux or macOS: stop Core with ./stop.sh, delete qortal.jar, download the latest qortal.jar from the official Qortal releases, and run ./start.sh.
On Windows, run the newest installer from qortal.dev and keep the blockchain data.

entries.q: My minting isn't working. What should I check?
entries.a:
Go through these in order:
1. You need your own node: minting is not possible on a public node.
2. The node must be fully synced; while it syncs, Hub shows Synchronizing.
3. Your account must be in the MINTER group, which needs an approved nomination.
4. The account's minting key must be on this node (Start minting in Hub's minting panel); a node holds at most 2 keys.
5. Core must run all the time, so the computer must not sleep.
Level progress is credited in batches of about 1,000 blocks, so it moves in steps.

entries.q: My node falls one or two blocks behind now and then. Is that a problem?
aliases: node lags a couple of blocks
entries.a: No. Nodes regularly trim old AT (smart contract) state, which takes about the time of a block or two, so many nodes are briefly a block or two behind. It only needs attention if the gap keeps growing.

entries.q: My node stopped working for a few minutes after running for days. Why?
entries.a: That is probably automatic database maintenance (trimming), which runs at a random time 3 to 14 days after Core starts. Core stops answering for about 3 to 10 minutes while it works, depending on the hardware. Let it finish. Restarting Core every day means maintenance never runs.

entries.q: What does the QORTector auto-fix script do?
entries.a: It is crowetic's maintenance script for QORTector-style nodes. Each run it checks the internet, picks a start script for your amount of RAM, compares your Core version with the latest release and updates it if needed, and merges recommended values into settings.json. It also compares your block height with two public nodes; if your node is more than 2,500 blocks behind (older copies of the script used 1,500), or its height has not moved since the last run, it bootstraps. Let it finish once it starts.

entries.q: What does refresh-qortal.sh do? Will it delete anything?
entries.a: It is a full reset of the node software, not of your account. It force-stops every Java program on the machine, deletes the db folder, qortal.jar and old log files, downloads the latest qortal.jar and starts Core, which then bootstraps. settings.json and apikey.txt stay. Close any other Java programs first.

entries.q: Core says "API call unauthorized". What does that mean?
entries.a: That call needs the node's API key, and none or the wrong one was sent. Use the key from apikey.txt in the Core folder: Hub and GO send it from their node settings, and API tools send it as the X-API-KEY header. If the key was reset, update it everywhere you use this node.

entries.q: My transaction was refused. What do the usual reasons mean?
entries.a:
Core says why in the error. The common ones:
1. Insufficient balance: you need enough QORT for the amount plus the fee.
2. Clock not synchronized, or timestamp too old or too new: fix the device's clock.
3. Too many unconfirmed transactions pending: wait a few minutes for earlier ones to confirm.
4. Node's blockchain currently busy: try again in a moment.

entries.q: I added a custom node in Hub but nothing changed. Why?
entries.a: Hub only switches after a reload, so it shows "Reload required" when you add a node. Tap Reload app. Then check the sign-in screen: it should say "Using" with your node's name. If it still shows the old node, open Connection Mode, select the custom node and save.

entries.q: Hub says "url invalid: incorrect url or node not running". What should I check?
aliases: incorrect url or node not running
entries.a:
Hub could not reach a node at that address.
1. Check the whole address, including http or https and the port, for example 127.0.0.1 with port 12391 for a node on the same computer.
2. Make sure that node's Core is running.
3. For a node on another computer: the settings shipped with Core already accept other devices; if the whitelist was turned on, add your device's address to "apiWhitelist" in that node's settings.json (or use an SSH tunnel) and restart Core. Then enter the node's API key.

entries.q: Hub's Bootstrap chain says it could not bootstrap, clear chain data, or start Core. What now?
aliases: could not bootstrap clear chain data or start core
entries.a:
Hub's own tool did not get through, so do it by hand.
1. Stop Core: Exit from the tray icon, or ./stop.sh in the qortal folder, and wait until it has ended.
2. Delete the db folder: in the qortal folder in your home folder on Linux and macOS, or in AppData, Local, Qortal on Windows.
3. Start Core again; it downloads a fresh bootstrap.
Wallet files are not in the db folder.

entries.q: Hub says "Qortal Hub is locked". How do I get back in?
entries.a: The app locked itself after being idle, or someone chose Lock now. You are still signed in: enter your Qortal account password to unlock (GO can also use your fingerprint). Chats and calls stay connected while it is locked. After a wrong password you may have to wait a few seconds before the next try. Auto-Lock When Idle in the settings sets how long it waits.

entries.q: Qortal Hub says blocking users is unavailable on a public node. Why?
entries.a: Blocking is done by the node you use, so on a public node its operator decides who is blocked, not you. Switch Hub to your own node (local Core or a custom node) and you can block names and addresses in the settings' Blocked tab. In Torq you can also hide people, but that only hides them inside Torq.

entries.q: I changed Hub's Reticulum settings but nothing happened. Why?
entries.a: Reticulum reads its settings when it starts. After saving the Reticulum config or switching Community transport, restart Reticulum or Qortal Hub. Community transport also needs Managed Reticulum config turned on, and UPnP or a forwarded Reticulum port to help relay for others.

entries.q: Qortal Hub stopped showing desktop notifications. How do I get them back?
entries.a: Desktop alerts are probably muted. In Hub's settings, check that "Reduce app notifications" and "disable all push notifications" are off. For one Q-App, open its notification settings and make sure Disable OS push is off. Also check that your computer's own notification settings allow Qortal Hub.

entries.q: Qortal Hub won't start on Linux from the AppImage. What do I do?
entries.a: The AppImage must be allowed to run as a program first. Right-click the file, open Properties, Permissions, and tick "Allow executing file as program". Or in a terminal in that folder run chmod +x on the file, then start it with ./ and its name.

entries.q: My password doesn't work after I imported a backup file. Why?
entries.a: A backup file can be saved with a new password: the backup window offers "new password for this backup" or keeping the current one. Try the password you chose when that file was made. If you have your seed phrase, you can also import the account with it and set a new password.

entries.q: GO says "That password is not correct" and makes me wait. What can I do?
aliases: please wait seconds and try again
entries.a: Each saved account has its own wallet password, and after wrong tries GO makes you wait a few seconds. Check the keyboard language and caps, and that you picked the right account. If you have forgotten it, restore the account with your seed phrase and set a new password. Nobody can reset it for you.

entries.q: My GO voice call won't connect. What should I check?
entries.a:
1. You and the other person must be DM friends, as on the Hub; otherwise the call is declined.
2. They must be online on the network: a contact shown as offline cannot be called.
3. Calls get ready about half a minute after GO connects, so wait a moment after opening GO.
4. Check the Reticulum badge: with Hubs 0 nothing can connect.
If it still fails, send Copy diagnostics, which has a Calls section.

entries.q: GO says my saved account "does not match its key". What happened?
aliases: account does not match its key
local signer is not a group member
entries.a: The saved copy of that account on this phone is damaged: its key belongs to a different address, so GO refuses to use it. Older builds kept going and chat then failed with "author mismatch". Remove the account from GO and add it again with your seed phrase or a fresh backup file made in Hub. Your account and QORT on the chain are fine.

entries.q: GO says the saved account looks incomplete or damaged. What do I do?
aliases: account could not be found go
entries.a: The copy of that account stored on this phone is missing part of its locked wallet data. Choose another account, or remove this one and restore it from your backup file or seed phrase. Restoring makes a fresh copy; your QORT and names are on the chain and are not affected.

entries.q: GO says "the wallet signed as" another address. What should I do?
aliases: log out and unlock the wallet again
entries.a: Signing came back from the wrong address or did not answer. Log out, then unlock the account again. If it keeps happening, remove the account from GO and add it again with your seed phrase or a fresh backup file.

entries.q: Importing my backup file into GO fails. Why?
aliases: does not contain a valid account
entries.a: GO says "This backup file does not contain a valid account" when the file is not a Qortal wallet backup or is incomplete. Pick the .json backup file made with Backup wallet or Download account, not a copy of the seed phrase or another file. If the file cannot be read, copy it to the phone's own storage and try again, or import with your seed phrase.

entries.q: GO can't import my seed phrase. What could be wrong?
aliases: restore with seed phrase fails go
entries.a: GO does not check the words against a list: a phrase with a typo still imports, but as a different, empty account, and "Unable to import this seedphrase" only shows if building the account fails. If the imported account has the wrong address or no funds, remove it and import again, checking each word's spelling and the order. Type it yourself on your own phone; never paste it into a chat or a website.

entries.q: My call was declined because they don't have me as a friend. What do I do?
aliases: does not have you as a friend
calls unlock when they add you back
entries.a: Calls only work between DM friends, in both directions. Open the DM, tap Add friend, and ask the other person to add you back. GO tells you when calling is available: "Calls unlock when they add you back".

entries.q: A Qortal item says "Name is blocked so content cannot be served". Why?
aliases: name is blocked so content cannot be served
entries.a: The node you use has that publisher's name on its block list, so it will not serve their data. On your own node, open the settings' Blocked tab and unblock the name if it was a mistake. On a public node, its operator's list applies and you cannot change it.

entries.q: GO takes 30 seconds or more to log in. How do I make it faster?
entries.a: Update GO. Builds before v0.0.14 were debug builds, which run very slowly on some phones, GrapheneOS above all, and the fingerprint path did the slow step twice. Release builds since v0.0.14 unlock in about a second on most phones. If it is still slow, send the Unlock section from Copy diagnostics with your report.

entries.q: A Q-App opens but stays blank. What can I do?
entries.a:
Often the node has not finished getting the app's files, or the app itself is broken.
1. Wait a moment, then use Refresh in the address bar.
2. Close the tab and open the app again.
3. Try later, or on your own node: the public node drops apps within hours.
4. If it is blank everywhere, tell the app's publisher; a faulty build, such as index.html not at the top of the zip, looks exactly like this.

entries.q: A private Q-App won't open. What can I check?
entries.a:
The node has to fetch the app's encrypted files and the group's key, and a public node often cannot.
1. Check that you are a member of the group the app is shared with.
2. "couldn't download this private app" or "couldn't download the group's key" means the node could not get the data: try again later, or use your own node.
3. Update GO if it shows "Failed to execute 'atob'": since v0.0.17 GO builds private apps on the phone, so they open on the public node too.

entries.q: GO can't connect to my private node. What should I check?
entries.a:
Usually the phone cannot reach the node, or the node does not allow the phone.
1. In the avatar menu, tap Node and check the URL: http or https, the address and the port (12391 by default).
2. Use an address the phone can reach: the computer's home network address on the same Wi-Fi, a VPN address such as Tailscale, or 127.0.0.1 for an SSH tunnel on the phone.
3. The settings shipped with Core accept other devices; if the whitelist was turned on, add the phone's address range to "apiWhitelist" in the node's settings.json and restart Core.
4. Enter the node's API key from apikey.txt.

entries.q: An approval window says "Unknown Q-App". Should I accept it?
entries.a: Not unless you just asked for exactly that yourself. GO shows Unknown Q-App when it cannot tell which app sent the request. Decline it, then repeat the action from the app you trust.

entries.q: One Q-App keeps sending me approval windows. How do I stop them?
entries.a: GO queues each request instead of replacing the open one, and shows how many more are waiting. Answer them one by one, or tap Decline all from this app if you did not expect them. Some apps ask once per item, such as each like or file.

entries.q: A link in a Q-App won't open my dialer, the Play Store or another app. Why?
aliases: q-app link wont open other app
entries.a: For safety, GO keeps Q-Apps inside the Qortal node: they cannot open other apps through intent:, market:, tel: and similar links. Copy the number or address and open it yourself.

entries.q: Notifications don't come when my phone's screen is off. What should I check?
aliases: messages only arrive when i open go
entries.a:
Usually Android or the phone maker is stopping GO in the background, or Background sync is set too low.
1. In the notification settings (avatar menu, Notifications, then the gear), set Background sync to While charging or Always. Always works on battery too but uses noticeably more battery.
2. Let GO run in the background: when GO asks to keep Qortal Go reachable, tap Allow in background, or set its battery use to Unrestricted in Android settings.
3. Don't swipe GO away from your recent apps.
4. If GO shows "GO was stopped in the background", follow the steps it gives for your phone's brand.

entries.q: A video in GO stalls at a low percentage. What can I do?
entries.a: Your node needs the whole video before it plays, and it gets the pieces from other nodes; a very low percentage often means only the first small piece has arrived. Keep it open a while. The public node drops files within hours and has to fetch them again, so long videos are slow there; your own node keeps them. If it never moves, no node holding the rest is online right now.

entries.q: A big download from a Q-App shows no progress for minutes. Is it stuck?
entries.a: Probably not. First your node gathers the file from other nodes (GO's card at the top says "Gathering from QDN" with a percentage), then the app reads it and GO saves it, which on mobile data can take minutes. Hide keeps it going in the notifications, and the bell shows the file when it is ready.

entries.q: GO says a file was "Not saved". How do I keep it?
aliases: not saved tap save to keep it
entries.a: The file was downloaded but the save was declined or did not finish. Open Notifications from the avatar menu: the file waits there with a Save button for about 30 minutes. Tap Save to keep it.

entries.q: Where does GO put files that Q-Apps save?
entries.a: In the phone's Documents folder, under Qortal Go; the "Saved to" message names the exact folder. Tap that message to open the file with another app or share it. App packages (APKs) are saved there too, but GO never opens or installs them.

entries.q: Chat stops syncing about a minute after I leave GO. Why?
aliases: chat stops when i leave go
entries.a: Android freezes GO's hidden page about a minute after you leave, and the chat engine runs in that page. With Background sync Off, chat then waits and catches up when you open GO again. Set Background sync to While charging (the default) or Always in the notification settings. On battery, GO still finishes sending your waiting messages for up to 3 minutes after you leave.

entries.q: GO says it needs storage permission to save files. Why?
entries.a: On Android 8 and 9, saving into Documents needs the storage permission. Allow it when GO asks, or turn it on in Android Settings, Apps, GO, Permissions, then save again.

entries.q: GO says no app on this phone can open the file. What now?
aliases: no app can open this file
entries.a: Android found no installed app for that kind of file. Save it to the device and open it later with a suitable app, or share it to an app that can read it. Web pages are only shown as plain text inside GO, on purpose.

entries.q: A chat attachment says "this file could not be opened". Why?
aliases: this file could not be opened
file no longer stored on this device
entries.a: It may still be downloading, or it is no longer on this phone, because received files are removed when you log out. Wait for the download to finish and try again; if it is gone, ask the sender to send it again.

entries.q: Dev Mode says it couldn't open my zip as a Q-App. What's wrong?
entries.a: Dev Mode needs a .zip with index.html at its top level, not inside a folder. Zip the contents of your build folder (such as dist) rather than the folder itself, keep it under 64 MB, and pick it again.

entries.q: I can't find the Dev Mode button in GO. Where is it?
entries.a: Turn it on first: Home settings, System, Dev Mode. The Dev Mode button then shows next to New folder in the library's Pinned tab.

entries.q: My GO widget is stuck on the loading page. What can I do?
entries.a: A widget is a small Q-App, so the first time it needs the node to have its files, and the public node drops apps within hours. After the first load GO keeps the widget's files on the phone, so later it opens at once. Tap the widget and choose Reload, or remove it and add it again.

entries.q: The widget list is empty when I tap the plus button. Why?
entries.a: The list comes from QDN: apps tagged go-widget, or with an identifier starting with go-widget. If your node has not got that data yet, the list stays short or empty. Try again in a few minutes, or on your own node.

entries.q: My Home, Apps and Chat buttons are in the wrong order. How do I fix it?
entries.a: Open Home settings, System, Bottom buttons: drag the round buttons into the order you want, or tap Reset. The sideways swipe between sections follows the same order.

entries.q: GO's top bar and bottom buttons disappeared. How do I get them back?
entries.a: That is Immersive mode. In Auto, scroll up a little or go back to the top and the bars return; in Manual, tap the small floating button, which brings them back for a few seconds. To keep them always, set Immersive mode to Off in Home settings, System. A swipe down from the top shows the phone's status bar for a moment.

entries.q: Swiping between Home, Apps and Chat doesn't work inside a Q-App. Why?
entries.a: Swipes inside Q-Apps, websites, carousels and open chats belong to them. Swipe sideways on the round Home, Apps and Chat buttons or the strip at the bottom, or just tap a button.

entries.q: I pinned an app in the library but can't find it. Where did it go?
entries.a: On phones the pin adds the app to a Library folder in Tabs. Open Tabs, by pulling down on Home or tapping the Tabs button, and look in the Library folder.

entries.q: Avatars and app icons in GO look old or don't load. Why?
entries.a: GO keeps avatars and icons on the phone so they show quickly, even on a slow node, and re-checks each one about once a day. A new avatar can therefore take up to a day to appear. A missing picture usually means the node could not fetch it yet.

entries.q: Hub says it was unable to stop the Core. How do I stop it?
entries.a: Stop it outside Hub: on Windows right-click the Qortal tray icon and choose Exit; on Linux and macOS run ./stop.sh in the qortal folder and wait for the message that Qortal ended. Give it a minute, since Core saves its data while it shuts down.

entries.q: I swiped away a notification in GO's bell. Can I see it again?
entries.a: Yes. Open Notifications from the avatar menu and tap Notification history: it keeps the last 30 days (up to 300 items), including ones you swiped away or cleared with Clear all. Tap an entry to open it.

entries.q: I can't hear anything in a GO call, or the sound comes from the wrong place. What do I do?
aliases: other person cant hear me go
entries.a: Open the audio route sheet in the call ("Play call audio on") and pick Phone, Speaker, Bluetooth or Headset. One-to-one calls start on the earpiece, so hold the phone to your ear, or choose Speaker; group calls use the speaker. Also check that neither side is muted. If the call ends at once, the other person's microphone may be unavailable.

entries.q: How do I send a useful problem report from GO?
entries.a: Tap the Reticulum status badge next to the Qortal logo at the top, then Copy diagnostics, or Save as .md file to attach a file. Send it with a short note on what went wrong and when. Addresses, names, IDs and IP addresses in it are replaced with stand-in names.

entries.q: GO's notification says "Chat paused". What does that mean?
aliases: chat paused open go to sync
entries.a: GO's chat engine is frozen in the background, so nothing syncs until you open the app. Open GO and it reconnects and catches up. To keep chat going in the background, set Background sync to While charging or Always and allow GO to run in the background.

entries.q: GO says it paused its background connection after 6 hours on battery. Why?
entries.a: On Android 15 and newer, after 6 hours in a row off screen and unplugged, GO pauses its background connection itself to save power (in the While charging and Off modes). Open GO to reconnect; plugging in or opening GO resets the count. Background sync set to Always never takes this pause.

entries.q: GO says "Android paused GO's background connection". What now?
entries.a: Android itself stopped GO's background service, which it does to some apps after a time limit. Open GO and it reconnects. If it happens often, set GO's battery use to Unrestricted and keep Background sync on While charging or Always.

entries.q: Chat messages are not arriving in GO. What should I check?
entries.a:
Start with the Reticulum status badge next to the Qortal logo at the top.
1. Offline, or Hubs 0: the phone is not on the mesh yet. Check its internet and give it a minute.
2. Chat engine not ready: wait while it says starting; if it says failed, restart GO.
3. Messages only arrive while GO is open: set Background sync to While charging or Always and allow GO in the background.
4. Still stuck: send Copy diagnostics with your report.

entries.q: My messages from GO don't show up on my Hub or for others. Why?
aliases: others dont see my go messages
entries.a: Messages travel peer to peer: another node, such as your Hub or a member's node, has to fetch each one from your phone while the phone is reachable. Watch the small icon by your message: a clock means sending, a crossed-out cloud means no node has fetched it yet, and a double tick means a node got it. Keep GO open, or in the background with Background sync on, until it shows delivered.

entries.q: A chat shows "error loading content: Invalid Data". What is it?
entries.a: One message could not be drawn, usually because some of its data is damaged. GO tries again by itself and redraws it when its data changes. If the box stays, leave the chat and open it again, and update GO if you use v0.0.16 or older.

entries.q: GO stays offline on Reticulum even though my internet works. What can I do?
entries.a:
The phone has no working link to the community Reticulum hubs yet; the badge then shows Hubs 0, where 2 is typical.
1. Give it a minute: after a switch between Wi-Fi and mobile data GO reconnects by itself.
2. If it stays at 0, close and reopen GO once.
3. Avoid restarting it over and over: a hub can briefly block an address that keeps reconnecting.
4. If nothing helps, send Copy diagnostics with your report.

entries.q: GO asks me to "Keep Qortal Go reachable". What should I do?
entries.a: GO is asking to be freed from Android's battery limits so calls and messages arrive reliably. Tap Allow in background and confirm Android's dialog, or Open settings to set it yourself (unrestricted battery use, and "Pause app activity if unused" off). Not now asks again in 14 days; Never show this again stops the prompt.

entries.q: The badge says online but shows only 1 online. Am I connected?
entries.a: Not necessarily: the online count includes your own account. Check Hubs in the badge; if it is 0, the phone is not on the mesh yet.

entries.q: GO uses a lot of battery. What can I change?
entries.a: Background sync set to Always keeps chat running whenever GO is in the background, which uses noticeably more battery. While charging (the default) only keeps it running on the charger, and Off lets chat pause about a minute after you leave and catch up when you return. Open Q-Apps are paused in the background either way.

entries.q: Several old messages notify at once when I open GO. Why?
entries.a: GO was frozen or offline, so the messages waited and arrived as GO caught up. GO still notifies you about DMs and mentions you have not read elsewhere, and several at once make only one sound. Background sync on While charging or Always makes this happen less.

entries.q: Some older messages are missing in GO. Can I get them back?
entries.a: Phones only serve each other the last 29 days of group history, so older pages come from Hubs. Scroll up in the chat and GO loads older pages from peers that have them. Messages also disappear when they expire: DMs expire after a month by default, and channels can set their own expiry.

entries.q: A group shows no messages or its channels never load. What can I do?
aliases: unable to finish loading reticulum chat channels
entries.a:
The chat engine may still be fetching history, or the node cannot confirm that you are a member.
1. Leave the group open for a minute; GO asks peers again by itself.
2. Check your node connection, since membership checks go to the node.
3. Update GO: v0.0.19 fixed channels that stopped loading after long use.
4. If it stays empty, send Copy diagnostics.

entries.q: My group only shows the General channel. Where are the others?
entries.a: Channel lists come from snapshots signed by the group's admins, which your phone fetches from peers. Until one arrives you may see only the built-in channels, and GO asks again by itself. Some channels are only visible to certain members, and some groups simply have no others.

entries.q: GO says "Composer failed to load. Close and reopen this chat." What do I do?
entries.a: The message box did not start properly. Close the chat and open it again; if it keeps happening, restart GO.

entries.q: Joining a group failed. Why?
entries.a: Joining is a blockchain transaction, so it needs a small QORT fee and a working node connection. Core also refuses if you are banned from that group, already a member, or already have a join request waiting. For a closed group, your request waits until an admin accepts it.

entries.q: I joined a private group but it says I'm not part of the encrypted group. Why?
aliases: not part of the encrypted group
entries.a: A private group's Threads (and its chat when Reticulum chat is off) are encrypted with a group key that admins publish, and each key only covers the members at the time it was made. Wait until an admin re-encrypts the key; after that it takes a few minutes to spread.

entries.q: A private group says there is no group key yet. What now?
entries.a: The group's first encryption key is still being created, or no admin has published one. Wait a few minutes; GO checks again every 2 minutes. If you are an admin and there is no key, publish one from the group's Admin keys panel.

entries.q: As a group admin I'm told the member list changed and to re-encrypt the key. What do I do?
entries.a: New members cannot read the private group until the key includes them. Open Admin keys from the group's menu and re-encrypt the group key; it costs a small amount of QORT. It takes a couple of minutes to spread, so refresh the group after about 5 minutes.

entries.q: A group action says "awaiting confirmation". How long does that take?
entries.a: Joining, leaving, creating a group and member changes are blockchain transactions, so they wait until a block includes them, usually a couple of minutes. Until then the old state can still show; member changes are marked Pending.

entries.q: My group invite link doesn't work. Why?
aliases: not a valid qortal group invite link
entries.a: GO says "This doesn't look like a valid Qortal group invite link" when the pasted text is not a complete invite link. Ask for the link again (copy invite link in the group) and paste all of it. For a closed group, the link sends a request that an admin must accept.

entries.q: I can't see someone's messages any more. Did I hide them?
entries.a: Maybe: hidden people stay out of that group's chat until you unhide them, or until the time you picked (1 hour, 24 hours) runs out. Open their user card from the member list and choose unhide. They may also have left the group, or their messages expired.

entries.q: My Hub keeps ringing after I answered the call on GO. Is that normal?
aliases: call rings on hub and go
entries.a: It can happen when the same account is signed in on both: the other device may keep ringing for a while after you answer. Just ignore it there; the call you answered carries on. Calls between two GO phones are still being improved.

entries.q: Qortino says it can only be assembled from a private node. Why?
entries.a: Older GO versions said that. Now the model also comes through the public node, but a private node is still highly recommended: the public node is shared, cuts long downloads and can drop what it fetched. On the public node GO downloads the model in three smaller parts and keeps trying by itself, and parts that already arrived are kept.

entries.q: Qortino's download stopped or failed. What can I do?
aliases: no peer is sending the rest
qdn could not deliver the model
entries.a:
The model comes from other nodes, and sometimes none is sending the rest, or too few host it.
1. Keep GO open and your node online, and try again later.
2. Parts that already arrived and passed the check are kept, so a retry only fetches what is missing.
3. If it says the model is not on QDN yet, your node cannot see it yet; try again a little later.

entries.q: Qortino says a downloaded part was damaged. What now?
entries.a: Each part is checked after download, and one did not match, so GO deleted it. Tap Assemble Qortino again: it fetches that part again and keeps the parts that were fine.

entries.q: Qortino says saving the model to this phone failed. What should I check?
entries.a: Check the free space on the phone and your node connection, then try again. Parts already saved and checked are kept.

entries.q: Qortino says the model files are missing. What happened?
entries.a: The model's files are no longer where GO saved them, for example after a storage cleanup. Close Qortino and assemble it again.

entries.q: Qortino says no reply came back. What should I do?
aliases: qortino could not write a reply
entries.a: Try a shorter question, or close Qortino and open it again. If it says it could not start at all, close and reopen it once more, and assemble it again if it reports missing files.

entries.q: Qortino gave me a wrong answer. What should I do?
entries.a: Qortino can be confidently wrong, so double-check anything important. Use the report button under the answer to flag it, which helps improve Qortino's answers.

entries.q: Qortino stopped in the middle of an answer. How do I get the rest?
entries.a: If the answer was cut short, tap "Continue answer" under it and Qortino carries on. If you pressed Stop, ask the question again.

entries.q: Why doesn't Qortino know today's prices or news?
entries.a: Qortino works offline from what it knows and from a curated set of Qortal answers, so it has no live data such as prices, balances or news. For those, open the right Q-App, for example Q-Trade for prices or your wallet for balances.

entries.q: Can I stop Qortino assembling and finish it later?
entries.a: Yes. Tap Cancel; GO says assembling was cancelled. Parts that already finished and passed the check stay on the phone, so the next Assemble picks up from there.

entries.q: My QORTector shows no Qortal tray icon. Is Core running?
entries.a: Probably yes. A QORTector's auto-start script starts Core at power-on without the tray icon; the icon only shows if you stop Core and start it again yourself. To check, open a terminal and run cd qortal, then ./qort admin/status.

entries.q: Q-Trade or Q-Wallets says "foreign blockchain or ElectrumX network issue". What does it mean?
aliases: foreign blockchain or electrumx network issue
entries.a: Your Qortal node could not reach the servers it uses for that coin's network (ElectrumX servers for coins such as Litecoin). Usually it is a temporary network problem, not a problem with your coins. Wait a few minutes and try again.

entries.q: A trade says it is "too soon to broadcast foreign blockchain transaction". What now?
aliases: too soon to broadcast foreign blockchain transaction
entries.a: Part of a cross-chain trade can only be sent after a set time on the other coin's chain (its lock time). Nothing is wrong; leave your node running and the trade continues once that time has passed.

entries.q: Core says "peer didn't reply within the allowed time". What does that mean?
aliases: peer didn't reply within the allowed time
entries.a: Your node asked another node for data and it did not answer in time, usually because that peer is slow or went offline. Try again; the node asks other peers as well.

entries.q: GO's screen goes black for a moment every few minutes. Why?
entries.a: That was a bug in older GO versions: an idle-time animation pause replayed animations that had already finished. Update GO; v0.0.16 fixed it.

entries.q: A file someone offered me in a DM says the offer has expired. What do I do?
entries.a: Direct file offers only stay open for a while, and this one ran out before the file was fetched. Ask the sender to send the file again, and keep GO open while it downloads.

entries.q: GO says it blocked a request to the node because its address was not safe. Why?
aliases: blocked a request to the node
entries.a: A Q-App asked the node for an address GO considers unsafe, which could reach parts of the node it should not. GO refused it to protect you. Nothing is wrong with your account; tell the app's developer.

entries.q: Qortal Hub disappears when I close it but keeps running. Why?
entries.a: Closing the window was set to Minimize to Tray (or you chose it when Hub asked), so Hub keeps running in the system tray (the Dock on a Mac). Open it again from the tray icon, or choose Quit Completely. To change what closing does, use "When closing the window" in Hub's settings.

entries.q: GO says only some of my payments were sent. What should I do?
aliases: payments were sent then the next one failed
entries.a: When one request pays several people, GO sends them one by one, and it stopped at a failure: the message says how many went through. Check your wallet history to see which ones were sent before you pay again, so nobody is paid twice.

entries.q: Qortal Hub says "Reticulum chat is disabled". How do I turn it on?
entries.a: Hub's Reticulum group chat setting is off. Turn on "Reticulum group chat" in the System tab of Hub's settings. Group chat in Hub 3.0 and GO runs over Reticulum.

entries.q: GO shows 0 online and connecting until I restart it. Why?
entries.a: In older GO versions, if Android reloaded GO's screen right after sign-in, the new screen never heard from Reticulum. Update GO; since v0.0.16 the screen asks again by itself. On an old version, restarting GO fixes it.

entries.q: The first tap after a swipe does nothing in GO. Why?
aliases: first tap after swipe not working
entries.a: That was a bug in older GO versions: a swipe left an invisible scroll behind and the next tap was swallowed. Update GO; v0.0.16 fixed it.

entries.q: The Tabs window closes when I try to scroll it. How do I scroll?
entries.a: On the Tabs window a short swipe up scrolls the tabs and a long one closes the window. Use short swipes to scroll, and update GO if yours is older than v0.0.16.

entries.q: I can't tap the last items of long lists in GO. Why?
entries.a: Android's navigation buttons, or GO's round Home, Apps and Chat buttons, covered the bottom of some lists. Update GO: v0.0.18 makes the round buttons step aside for the channel list and in-chat search, and v0.0.19 ends GO's view above Android's 3 navigation buttons.

entries.q: Hub or GO says "invalid qortal link". What is wrong with it?
entries.a: The link is not in a form Qortal can open, or it points somewhere a Q-App is not allowed to open. A working link looks like qortal://APP/Name, or qortal://SERVICE/name/identifier. Ask the sender for the full link again.

entries.q: Hub asks whether to overwrite my QDN-saved pinned apps. What should I answer?
aliases: unable to download your existing qdn-saved pinned apps
entries.a: Hub could not download the pinned-app list you saved to QDN before, so it cannot tell whether that list is newer. Answer no if you want to keep the saved list, and try again later when your node has it; answer yes only if the pins on this computer are the ones you want. GO does not offer this backup, so a phone cannot overwrite Hub's pins.

entries.q: GO uses a lot of mobile data. What can I change?
aliases: go uses a lot of data
entries.a: GO's data use comes from Reticulum chat traffic and from the Q-Apps, videos and files you open. On mobile data GO keeps a light phone profile; it relays group traffic for others only while charging on Wi-Fi. Open Q-Apps pause in the background, and Background sync set to Off or While charging limits background traffic. Received and Sent in the Reticulum badge show how much GO has used since Reticulum started.

entries.q: GO is slow for a while right after it starts. Why?
entries.a: At start GO opens its chat database, connects to Reticulum and catches up on new messages, which takes some work, and it settles after a short while. On GrapheneOS with WebView JIT off for GO, this start-up phase is much slower; allowing WebView JIT makes it faster. Updating GO helps too: v0.0.19 made start-up lighter.

entries.q: My Core log says "Blockchain too divergent with peer". Is my node on a fork?
entries.a: Core writes this when the last block it shares with that peer is more than 240 blocks back, so the two are on very different branches and it stops trying that peer. Seen now and then, it is about the peer. If it shows for most peers and your height stops moving, your node is probably the one on a fork: bootstrap it.

entries.q: My Core log says "Failed to synchronize with peer ... cooling off". Is that a problem?
aliases: failed to synchronize with peer cooling off
entries.a: Usually not. Syncing with that one peer failed (the reason is in brackets), so Core leaves it alone for a while and syncs from others. It only matters if your height stops moving; then see the steps for a node that won't sync.

entries.q: My Core log says "Higher weight chain found in peers, so not signing a block this round". Is minting broken?
aliases: higher weight chain found in peers
not signing a block this round
entries.a: No, that is normal. A peer has a better chain than yours, so your minter waits up to 30 seconds to sync to it instead of minting on the weaker one. After that it carries on by itself.

entries.q: My Core log says "NO LONGER MINTING". What should I do?
aliases: repository issue while running block minter
entries.a: Core's minter stopped after a database error. Core checks every 10 minutes and restarts the minter by itself (the log then says "Restarting block minter"). If the message keeps coming back, restart Core, and bootstrap if the database errors continue.

entries.q: GO shows a "GO runtime error" window. What should I do?
entries.a: Part of the app hit an error after login, and GO shows it instead of leaving a white screen. Tap Reload app; your lock and account stay as they were. If the window has no buttons, close GO fully and open it again. If it keeps coming back, update GO, and send Copy diagnostics with your report (it lists recent app errors).

entries.q: Why does Qortino's download stop near 1 GB on the public node?
aliases: qortino stuck saving to this phone
entries.a: The public node cuts long downloads near 1 GB and sometimes drops files it fetched, so a big download through it can stop part way. GO keeps what already arrived and carries on by itself, and on the public node it downloads the model in three parts under 1 GB. Your own node avoids all this and is highly recommended for Qortino.

entries.q: How do I open the chat in Qortal GO?
aliases: where is chat in qortal go
entries.a: Tap the round Chat button at the bottom of GO, next to Home and Apps, or swipe sideways between the sections. Chat opens Q-Chat with two lists under one header: Groups and DMs. Tap the switch at the top or swipe the list sideways to move between them. GO keeps Chat ready in the background, so coming back to it is instant.

entries.q: What is the difference between Groups and DMs in GO chat?
aliases: go chat groups and direct messages
what are dms in qortal go
difference group chat and dm go
entries.a: Groups are chats for the members of a Qortal group, split into channels by topic. DMs are private chats between you and one other account. Saved Messages, your private notes, sits at the top of the DMs list. Switch between the two lists with the Groups / DMs switch or a sideways swipe.

entries.q: How does chat work in Qortal GO?
entries.a: Q-Chat in GO, like in Hub 3.0, runs over Reticulum, a peer-to-peer network: messages go from device to device instead of through a server or the blockchain. Every message is signed with your Qortal account, and group membership comes from the Qortal chain. Your phone keeps its own chat database and fetches missed messages from other members' devices. Messages are not blockchain transactions, so sending one costs no QORT.

entries.q: Does chat in GO work on the public node?
aliases: need my own node for go chat
entries.a: Yes. The messages travel over Reticulum, not through the node. GO only asks the node it is connected to, public or your own, to confirm group memberships and to look up names. If the node is slow or down, sending and loading can take longer, but GO keeps your messages queued and tries again.

entries.q: Do I pay a fee to send a chat message in GO?
aliases: is chatting free in qortal go
cost to send messages go chat
entries.a: No. Chat messages in GO travel over Reticulum and are not blockchain transactions, so they cost no QORT. Actions that are recorded on the Qortal chain still have their normal fee, for example joining or creating a group, making someone an admin or registering a name.

entries.q: How do I start a direct message in GO?
entries.a: Open Chat, switch to DMs and tap the new chat button at the top. Type the person's registered name or Qortal address, then write your message. You can also tap someone's name or avatar in a group chat and choose Message on their card.

entries.q: What is Saved Messages in GO?
entries.a: Saved Messages is a private chat with yourself, always first in the DMs list. Use it for notes, links and files you want to keep. If the same account is signed in on another device, such as your Hub at home, your Saved Messages reach that device too when both are online. The share sheet's "GO Self-DM" entry puts a shared item straight into it.

entries.q: Where do I find groups to join in GO?
entries.a: Open Chat, stay on Groups and tap the search button at the top to open Find groups. Search by name, sort by Top (Group Score), Active, Largest, Newest or QORT Holdings, and filter Open or Private groups. Tap Join on an open group, or Request on a closed one, where an admin has to accept you. Joining is a blockchain transaction, so it needs a small QORT fee and a couple of minutes to confirm.

entries.q: Why is my Groups list empty in GO?
aliases: not part of any communities go
entries.a: You have not joined any groups yet. GO then shows "Welcome to the new, improved Q-Chat" with two ways in: Find Communities, which opens the group search, or a field where you paste a group invite link someone sent you. A group you join shows in the list once the join is confirmed on the chain.

entries.q: How do I use a group invite link in GO?
aliases: join group from invite link go
entries.a: In a chat, an invite shows as a card with the group's name, description and Group Score: tap Join for an open group or Apply for a closed one. If someone sent you the link somewhere else, paste it into the "Paste a Group Invite Link" field that Chat shows while you have no groups yet. Invite links look like qortal://use-group/action-join/groupid- followed by the group's number.

entries.q: How do I copy a group's invite link in GO?
aliases: invite friends to my group go
entries.a: Long press the group in the Groups list and tap Copy invite link. Send the link to anyone you want to invite: in GO or Hub it opens the group, where they can join an open group or ask to join a closed one.

entries.q: What are channels in a GO group chat?
entries.a: Groups can split their chat into channels, one per topic, sorted into categories, so one community does not need a separate group for every subject. A group opens in its default channel, or in the channel where you left a draft. Tap the channel name under the group name at the top to see all channels and switch.

entries.q: How do I switch channels in a group on GO?
entries.a: In the open group, tap the channel name under the group name at the top; it has a small arrow. The channel list slides in with its categories and unread badges; tap a channel to open it. A dot by the arrow means new messages in another channel: blue for unread, red for a mention.

entries.q: Why can't I write in this channel?
aliases: no message box in channel go
entries.a: That channel is limited to admins. In a read-only channel everyone can read but only admins can post, and GO shows "Only group admins can write in this channel" instead of the message box. Admin channels can only be opened by admins and the group owner. Pick another channel to write in.

entries.q: What do the numbers and marks on group rows mean in GO?
entries.a: A number shows how many messages you have not read, and a red mark means someone mentioned you. "Draft" means you left an unsent message there. A pin means you pinned the group, and a call count shows that a group call is running in it.

entries.q: How do I pin a group to the top of the list in GO?
entries.a: Long press the group in the Groups list and tap Pin group. Pinned groups stay at the top under Pinned. To change their order, hold the pin icon on a pinned row and drag it. Long press the group again and tap Unpin group to undo.

entries.q: How do I mark a group as read in GO?
entries.a: Long press the group in the Groups list and tap Mark as read. Mark all as read clears the unread marks of every group at once. Reading a channel on another device with the same account, such as your Hub, also clears it in GO.

entries.q: What is in the three-dot menu of a group chat in GO?
entries.a: Tap the three-dot button at the top of the group chat. It opens Members (who is in the group), Calendar (group events), Files (the group's shared files), Admins (admin keys, shown to admins only) and Land (the group's Qortal Land space). Threads only shows if you turned on legacy Threads in Q-Chat settings. Each panel opens full screen; close it with the X at the top right or Android back.

entries.q: How do I see who is in a group in GO?
aliases: who is in this group go
entries.a: In the group chat, tap the three-dot button and choose Members. The list is sorted into sections such as admins and members. Swipe sideways to reach the other tabs: invite, invites, bans and join requests. Tap the magnifier in the header to search for a member.

entries.q: How do I search a group's members in GO?
entries.a: Open the group's Members panel and tap the magnifier in its header. Suggestions show as you type: names starting with your text first, then names containing it, then addresses, each with an Owner or Admin tag. Tap one, or press Enter for the first, and GO jumps to that member in the list with a short highlight.

entries.q: How do I make someone an admin of my group in GO?
entries.a: Only the group owner can do this. Open the group's Members panel: every regular member has a shield button for Make admin, and every admin one for Remove admin. GO asks you to confirm the fee, then the row shows Pending until the blockchain confirms, which can take a couple of minutes.

entries.q: How do I kick or ban a member in GO?
entries.a: If you own the group, open its Members panel and tap the three-dot menu on the member's row, or hold the row: it offers Kick and Ban. Qortal Core takes kicks and bans only from the owner, so admins don't get these buttons; the panel tells them why. In a group with no owner they need approval from its admins, which GO can't send. Nobody can kick or ban the owner. Each action is a blockchain transaction with a fee, and the row shows Pending until it is confirmed.

entries.q: What does Pending mean on a member in GO?
entries.a: You started an admin action on that member (make or remove admin, kick or ban) and it was sent to the blockchain. The row shows Pending until the chain confirms it, usually within a couple of minutes, and GO re-checks the list every 15 seconds. Pending stays even if you close and reopen Members.

entries.q: How do I send a message in GO chat?
entries.a: Open a group channel or a DM, tap the message box at the bottom, type and tap the send button. In GO the keyboard's Enter key starts a new line; only the send button sends. Your own message then shows a small icon beside the time that tells you how far it got.

entries.q: Why does Enter make a new line instead of sending in GO?
aliases: enter makes new line instead of send
enter does not send go chat
entries.a: Like Telegram and other phone chat apps, GO uses Enter for a new line and the send button to send. To change it, tap Aa next to the message box: the toolbar has a button that reads "Enter: new line". Tap it to switch to "Enter: send", and the keyboard then shows a send key. Your choice is kept.

entries.q: How do I format text in a GO chat message?
entries.a: Tap Aa next to the message box to open the formatting toolbar. It has bold, italic, strikethrough, inline code, clear formatting, bullet and numbered lists, code block, quote, horizontal line, heading, and undo and redo. Select text first to format it, or turn a style on and keep typing.

entries.q: How do I add emoji to a chat message in GO?
