entries.a: Tap the smiley button in the message box. GO swaps the keyboard for its emoji panel; tap the keyboard button to switch back. The switch at the top of the panel moves between Emojis and GIFs. A tap outside the message box closes the panel, just like the keyboard.

entries.q: Where is the GIF picker in GO chat?
entries.a: Tap the smiley button in the message box, then switch the panel from Emojis to GIFs. Search with the Search GIFs box or pick from Most used, the GIFs you send most. Tapping a GIF adds it to your message, and you can remove it again before you send. The GIFs come from the community library on the Qortal network, so a new one can take a moment to load.

entries.q: How do I mention someone in a GO chat?
entries.a: Type @ in the message box. GO suggests people in the group with their role, its channels and the group itself; keep typing to narrow the list and tap a suggestion. The person you mention gets a red mark on the group and, if they allow it, a phone alert.

entries.q: What do @here and @everyone do in GO chat?
entries.a: They are special mentions for group admins. @here notifies the members who are online right now, and @everyone notifies all members of that space. Only admins see them in the @ suggestions.

entries.q: How do I reply to a message in GO?
entries.a: Tap the message and choose Reply. A reply strip shows above the message box; write your answer and send it, and your message shows a quote of the one you answered. If that message had a picture, a small thumbnail of it shows in the strip and in the quote. Tap the X on the strip to cancel the reply.

entries.q: What is Reply in discussion in GO?
entries.a: It starts a side conversation under one message, so a long exchange does not fill the channel. Tap a message and choose Reply in discussion, or View N replies when a discussion already exists. The discussion opens in its own window with the first post on top and the replies below it.

entries.q: How do I edit a message I sent in GO?
entries.a: Tap your message and choose Edit. The message box shows an "Editing message" card with your text; change it and send. Tap the X on that card to cancel the edit. You can only edit your own messages, and the expiry cannot be changed while editing.

entries.q: How do I delete a message in GO?
entries.a: Tap your message and choose Delete. Edit and Delete only show on your own messages. The delete goes out to the other members' devices like a message does, so it takes effect there once they receive it.

entries.q: How do I copy the text of a message in GO?
aliases: copy part of a message go
entries.a: Tap the message and choose Copy to copy all of its text. To copy only part of it, long press the message, choose Select text and pick the words you want.

entries.q: How do I see when a message was sent or when it expires?
entries.a: Long press the message. Next to the usual menu, GO shows a details card: when the message was sent, when it was edited, and when it expires, or that it does not expire.

entries.q: How do I discard what I typed in GO chat?
aliases: x next to send button go
entries.a: Tap the small X next to the send button. It throws away the text, the saved draft, the reply you were writing and any attached file or GIF, and keeps the keyboard open. The X only shows while the message box has something in it.

entries.q: What happens if my message is too long in GO?
entries.a: A chat message holds up to 4,000 bytes. Longer text is not refused: GO sends it as several messages in a row, up to 15, and the message box tells you how many ("Long message: it will be sent as N messages"). Text that would need more than 15 parts cannot be sent, so shorten it first.

entries.q: Why can't I save a long edit in GO?
entries.a: Long new messages are split into several, but an edit has to fit into the one message it changes. GO then shows "Edited messages cannot be split" with the limit. Shorten the text to 4,000 bytes or less, or send the extra part as a new message.

entries.q: Does GO keep my unsent message if I leave the chat?
entries.a: Yes. Each channel and each DM keeps its own draft, and the lists mark them "Draft". A group with a draft opens in the channel you typed in last. Going to Home or Apps and back also keeps the channel, the text, the reply you were writing and the expiry you picked.

entries.q: How do I make a message disappear after a while in GO?
entries.a: Tap the expiry button in the message box before you send and pick 1 day, 2 days, 3 days, 1 week or 1 month; the message deletes itself after that time. In a group the choice is for the message you are about to send, and afterwards the box goes back to Channel default. In a DM it is a setting for that conversation (No expiry is also offered) and stays for your new messages there.

entries.q: Do group messages in GO expire?
aliases: how long do group messages last
do channel messages get deleted go
entries.a: It depends on the channel. Messages in the built-in General channel are kept for 30 days and in the Qortal Land channel for 1 day; admins cannot change those two. Other channels use the expiry their admins set, or none. For a single message you can pick a shorter time (1 day, 2 days, 3 days, 1 week or 1 month), never longer than the channel's own limit.

entries.q: How long do DMs last in GO?
aliases: how long are direct messages kept
entries.a: Direct messages expire after 1 month by default, to save space on your devices. You can pick a different time, or No expiry, with the expiry button in the DM's message box. The change only affects new messages: messages already sent keep the expiry they had.

entries.q: What is a channel expiry in a GO group?
entries.a: Group admins can give a channel its own expiry in its channel settings, except the built-in General and Qortal Land channels. It applies to the messages already in the channel and to new ones, and the channel shows "Messages auto-delete in" that time. A member can still pick a shorter expiry for one message, but not a longer one.

entries.q: Why can't I pick a longer expiry in this channel?
entries.a: The channel has a maximum expiry set by its admins. Times longer than that are greyed out in the expiry menu, and the menu shows the maximum. Shorter times still work.

entries.q: How do I make the message box bigger in GO chat?
entries.a: Tap the expand button in the message box. It opens the composer full screen, which helps with long messages. Tap shrink to go back to the normal message box.

entries.q: Why does the bottom bar disappear while I type in GO chat?
aliases: home apps chat buttons gone keyboard
entries.a: While the keyboard is open in Chat or a Q-App, GO hides the Home, Apps and Chat buttons so the conversation gets that space. They come back as soon as the keyboard closes. Home keeps its buttons.

entries.q: What does Highlight my messages do in GO?
entries.a: It adds a faint background to the messages you send, so they are easier to spot in a busy chat. Turn it on in Q-Chat settings (the gear at the top of the Groups or DMs list) under Messages.

entries.q: How do I react to a message in GO?
entries.a: Tap the message. A popup opens with a row of quick reactions above a short menu; tap one to react. The arrow at the end of the row opens the full emoji grid. Your reaction shows under the message at once.

entries.q: How does double tap to react work in GO?
entries.a: Double tap a message to react with that chat's double tap emoji, a thumbs up unless you changed it. The emoji flies onto the message. Double tap again to take the reaction back.

entries.q: How do I change the double tap reaction in GO?
entries.a: Tap a message to open the reaction row, then long press the emoji you want: it becomes this chat's double tap reaction and gets a blue ring. For more control, open the full emoji grid and tap its gear: you can set one emoji for this chat and another for all other chats.

entries.q: How do I find more emoji to react with in GO?
entries.a: Tap the message, then the arrow at the end of the quick reactions. The full emoji grid opens with category tabs, a Recently used row and a search box. Emoji that your phone cannot draw are left out, so you never see empty boxes.

entries.q: How do I remove my reaction in GO?
entries.a: Tap your reaction under the message to take it back. In the reaction row, the ones you already gave are marked, and tapping them again removes them too.

entries.q: How do I see who reacted to a message in GO?
entries.a: Long press a reaction under the message. A list opens with the people who reacted with that emoji. Tap anywhere in the chat to close it.

entries.q: Can I change the quick reactions in GO?
entries.a: Yes. Open the full emoji grid from the reaction row and tap its gear. Under Quick reactions, tap a slot to swap it for another emoji, or switch to Most used to show the reactions you use most. Reset to default brings back the original set.

entries.q: What happens when I tap a message in GO?
entries.a: A popup opens where you touched: quick reactions on top and a short menu below with Reply, Reply in discussion (or View replies), Copy, and Edit and Delete on your own messages. GO waits a moment first, because a second tap is a double tap reaction. Android back closes the popup.

entries.q: What does a long press on a message do in GO?
entries.a: It opens the same popup as a tap, with two extras: Select text, to copy part of the message, and a details card with when it was sent, edited and when it expires. A long press on a picture also opens the popup, so you can react to picture-only messages.

entries.q: Why does tapping a picture open it instead of the message menu?
entries.a: On a picture, a tap opens the picture full screen. To react, reply or copy, long press the picture instead: that opens the message popup.

entries.q: Can I react to messages inside a discussion in GO?
entries.a: Discussions show their messages read-only: a tap does not open the reaction popup, and a long press only offers Copy, Select text and the message details. Reply with the box at the bottom of the discussion.

entries.q: How do I send a photo in GO chat?
entries.a: Tap the + (add attachment) button in the message box and pick the photo. GO asks how to send it: Compress, which shows it in the chat and is easier on the network, or As attachment, which sends the original file. Location and camera details are removed before it leaves your phone.

entries.q: What is the difference between Compress and As attachment for photos?
entries.a: Compress makes a smaller copy that shows right in the chat; it is easier on the network and loads faster for others. As attachment sends the original image as a file that others download and open. Use As attachment when full quality matters.

entries.q: How do I send a file in GO chat?
entries.a: Tap the + (add attachment) button in the message box and pick the file, such as a PDF, a zip or a text file. It shows as a file card above the message box; add text if you like and send. The other person taps Open to view it.

entries.q: Can I send more than one file in one message in GO?
aliases: send many photos at once go
entries.a: No, a chat message holds one file or one picture. Picking another replaces the one waiting in the message box. Send several files as several messages. When you share many files into GO from another app, only the first is added.

entries.q: Does GO remove location data from photos I send in chat?
entries.a: Yes. Before a photo or video leaves your phone, GO strips its hidden metadata, such as the GPS position, phone model and time. A pasted or shared picture that cannot be cleaned is not added at all, and GO tells you so.

entries.q: How do I paste an image into a GO chat?
aliases: paste an image in go chat
entries.a: Copy the picture in another app, then tap the message box in GO. A small "Paste image" chip appears above it; tap it to add the picture, or its X to dismiss it. Pictures from your keyboard's clipboard bar or its image suggestions can be inserted too. GO cleans every pasted picture of its location and device data first.

entries.q: Why couldn't GO paste my picture?
entries.a: GO only adds pictures it can clean of their location and device data. If a picture cannot be cleaned, GO shows a message and leaves it out. Save it as a JPEG or PNG picture and try again.

entries.q: How do I open a photo full screen in GO chat?
entries.a: Tap the picture. It opens in GO's image viewer over a blurred chat, with buttons to share, save, copy and zoom. Close it with the X at the top left or Android back.

entries.q: How do I swipe through the pictures of a chat in GO?
entries.a: Open any picture, then swipe: to the right for older pictures and videos, to the left for newer ones, as in a photo gallery. A counter shows where you are, and videos play right in the viewer.

entries.q: How do I zoom into a picture in GO chat?
entries.a: Open the picture, then pinch with two fingers or double tap it. The zoom buttons in the bottom bar work too. Drag to move around a zoomed picture.

entries.q: How do I save a chat picture to my phone in GO?
entries.a: Open the picture and tap Save in the bottom bar. GO saves it in your phone's Documents folder under Qortal Go, in the Images folder, and shows where it went.

entries.q: How do I share or copy a picture from a GO chat?
aliases: send chat photo to another app
entries.a: Open the picture and use the bottom bar: Share sends it to another app through Android's share sheet, and Copy puts it on the clipboard so you can paste it elsewhere. GO cleans the copy of hidden location data first.

entries.q: How do I hide the buttons in GO's image viewer?
entries.a: Tap the picture, or next to it, once. The close button, the bottom bar and the counter slide away; tap again to bring them back. To close the viewer, use the X or Android back.

entries.q: How do I open a file someone sent me in GO?
entries.a: Tap Open on the file card in the chat. GO opens it in its own viewer, with Share, Save to device and Open with another app, and back closes it. Files that GO cannot show get a card that hands them to another app.

entries.q: Which files can GO show inside the app?
entries.a: GO's viewer shows Markdown formatted, plain text, code, JSON and CSV as text, images with zoom, video and audio with playback, and PDFs in its reader. Web pages are shown as source code and never run. Anything else, such as zip, apk or docx, gets a card to open it in another app, share it or save it.

entries.q: Where are files I receive in GO chat kept?
entries.a: Received files stay in GO's private storage, not in your public Downloads, and open in GO's viewer. Logging out deletes them. To keep one, tap Save to device: GO copies it into your phone's Documents folder under Qortal Go, sorted by type.

entries.q: Why is a file I received in GO no longer there?
aliases: chat file no longer on device
entries.a: GO removes received files from the phone when you log out, so a file from before then is gone from this device. Ask the sender to send it again. Files you saved with Save to device stay in your Documents folder.

entries.q: How do I open a chat file with another app in GO?
aliases: send chat file to another app
entries.a: Open the file from the chat, then tap Open with another app to pick an app on your phone, or Share to send it on. Both work on every file type, including ones GO cannot show itself.

entries.q: Why does a web page file show as code in GO?
entries.a: For your safety, GO never runs web pages that arrive as files. It shows their source code instead. To see the page, use Open with another app, if you trust where it came from.

entries.q: How do I read a PDF from a GO chat?
entries.a: Tap Open on the PDF. GO's reader fills the screen: swipe left or right to turn pages, pinch or double tap to zoom, and tap a page to hide the top bar. The contrast button picks the page look: Light, Dim or Smart. Share and Open with send the PDF to another app.

entries.q: Why don't images from websites load in GO messages?
entries.a: It protects you from tracking. A picture in a message that points at an outside web server would tell that server your IP address and when you read the message. GO only loads pictures from itself and the Qortal node, and shows other ones as a link you can choose to open.

entries.q: What does "Image unavailable right now (no peers)" mean?
entries.a: No device that has the picture is online right now, so GO cannot download it. Pictures and files in chat come from other members' devices, not from a server. Tap Try again later, when the sender or someone who has the picture is online.

entries.q: Can I send voice messages in GO chat?
entries.a: GO's chat has no record button for voice notes. You can send an audio file you recorded with another app as an attachment with the + button, and it plays in GO's viewer. For talking live, use a voice call.

entries.q: Can I send videos in GO chat?
entries.a: Yes, send a video with the + button like any attachment. The other person can play it in GO's viewer, where they can also swipe between the chat's pictures and videos. Location data is removed from videos before they are sent.

entries.q: How do I search my DMs in GO?
entries.a: Open Chat, switch to DMs and tap the search button at the top. Type at least 2 characters: GO searches the text of every direct message on the phone, Saved Messages included, and lists the matches newest first with who it is with, when, and the words around the match. Tap a result to open that chat at the message.

entries.q: Does DM search in GO find deleted or edited messages?
entries.a: Edited messages are found by their current text. Deleted messages are not found, and neither are messages from people you hid. The search only covers what is stored on this phone.

entries.q: How do I search messages in a group in GO?
entries.a: Open the group and tap the search button in its header. Type at least 2 characters, or pick a filter: from: a member, in: a channel, has: an attachment or a link, date: a range, and sort: newest, oldest or most relevant. Tap a result to jump to that message.

entries.q: How do I make the chat text bigger in GO?
entries.a: Open Q-Chat settings with the gear at the top of the Groups or DMs list, then Text size. Pick Small, Default or Large; a live preview shows how a chat looks. The size applies to groups, DMs and discussions, including names, times, replies and the message box. File cards, invites and link previews keep their layout.

entries.q: Where are the Q-Chat settings in GO?
entries.a: Tap the gear at the top of the Groups or DMs list. Q-Chat settings has Text size and Messages (Highlight my messages), Notifications with the Mention notifications switch, and Legacy with the Threads switch. Android back closes it.

entries.q: What happened to the Medium and High chat text sizes?
entries.a: They were replaced by Small, Default and Large, because Medium and High were only 1 and 2 pixels bigger. If you had picked Medium or High before, GO now shows your chats in Large.

entries.q: What are Threads in GO chat?
entries.a: Threads are the older thread board of a group. They are hidden by default; to show them, turn on Threads under Legacy in Q-Chat settings, and they appear in the group's three-dot menu. Threads will be removed in an upcoming release, so move anything important to a channel. For a side conversation, use Reply in discussion.

entries.q: How do I go back from a chat to the list in GO?
entries.a: Tap the back arrow at the top left, use Android back, or swipe the chat to the right. In a DM or Saved Messages that takes you to the DMs list; in a group chat, to the Groups list.

entries.q: What does swiping left on a group chat do in GO?
entries.a: In an open group chat, a swipe to the left takes you to the DMs list and a swipe to the right to the Groups list. The chat follows your finger and the list comes out from under it; a short, slow drag springs back. The message box, pictures and the channel list keep their own swipes.

entries.q: Why do the Home, Apps and Chat buttons disappear in a group?
entries.a: While the channel list or the in-chat search is open, the round Home, Apps and Chat buttons slide off the bottom edge so they do not cover the last rows or results. They come back when you close it. They also hide while the keyboard is open.

entries.q: What do the icons next to my DMs mean in GO?
aliases: sending only on this phone delivered
entries.a: Each DM you send shows its state beside the time: Sending (trying to reach the recipient now), Only on this phone (not sent yet, GO retries by itself), On your other device (your Hub or other device has a copy and can pass it on) and Delivered (the recipient's device fetched it). Tap the icon for a short explanation.

entries.q: What does "Only on this phone" mean on a DM?
entries.a: The message is saved on your phone but has not reached the recipient or any of your other devices yet, usually because they were not online at the same time. GO retries by itself for up to 7 days, more often at first. If you also run Hub with the same account, GO hands the message to it so it can deliver after GO closes.

entries.q: What does "On your other device" mean on a DM?
entries.a: Another device signed in with your account, such as your Hub at home, has a copy of the message and can send it when the recipient comes online. It is not confirmed as delivered yet. Once the recipient's device fetches it, the icon changes to Delivered.

entries.q: Does Delivered mean the person read my message in GO?
entries.a: No. Delivered means the recipient's device fetched the message, not that they opened or read it. GO has no read receipts. In groups, Delivered on your post means a member's node or your own device fetched it.

entries.q: What do the clock, cloud and double tick on my group posts mean?
entries.a: They show how far your post got. A clock means sending, usually a few seconds. A crossed-out cloud means not picked up yet: no other node has fetched it from your phone. A double tick means delivered: a group member's node, your Hub or another of your devices fetched it. Tap the icon for the details.

entries.q: What does "not picked up yet" mean on my group post?
entries.a: No other node has fetched the post from your phone yet. Members' nodes fetch it when they come online while your phone is reachable, so keep GO open or use background sync until it turns into a double tick. The cloud goes away after 29 days, when your phone stops offering the post.

entries.q: Why don't my Saved Messages show a delivery icon?
entries.a: GO only shows the icon on Saved Messages once it knows you have another device that fetches them, such as your Hub. A phone-only account sees no icon, so there is no warning that could never go away.

entries.q: Why isn't my DM getting delivered in GO?
aliases: dm only on this phone long
entries.a: A DM travels directly between devices, so it needs your phone and one of the recipient's devices online at the same time. GO keeps the message and retries for up to 7 days. Keeping GO open, or using background sync while charging, gives it more chances. A Hub that runs at home on your account can also deliver it for you.

entries.q: How long does GO keep trying to send an undelivered DM?
entries.a: Up to 7 days. During the first day GO announces the message again about every 30 minutes, then about every 2 hours. It stops as soon as the recipient has it, or once your own Hub holds a copy. The retry plan is saved, so restarting GO does not set it back.

entries.q: What does "failed to send" mean in GO chat?
entries.a: GO gave up on sending that message. The reason shows in small text under "failed to send", for example when your node could not confirm your group membership. Check that Reticulum is online and your node answers, then send the message again. If it keeps failing, use Copy diagnostics on the Reticulum badge and send that report.

entries.q: Can people see when I'm typing in GO chat?
entries.a: Yes. While you write in a group or a DM, the others see a line such as "name is typing..." for a short while, and you see the same for them. Typing notices are not stored and vanish when the person stops.

entries.q: What happens to messages I send while offline in GO?
entries.a: They are kept on your phone and go out once GO reaches the network again. A DM shows Only on this phone until it is delivered, and GO retries for up to 7 days. A group post shows the crossed-out cloud until a member's node fetches it from your phone.

entries.q: Which chat settings stay on one device in GO?
aliases: settings that don't sync go chat
entries.a: Drafts, the chat text size, Highlight my messages, your reaction choices (double tap and quick reactions), Background sync and the Disable push notifications switch stay on the device where you set them. Notification rules, Q-App notification permissions, muted apps, the mention alert switch and your Online, Busy or Offline status can follow your account to your other devices through notification sync.

entries.q: If I read a chat on my Hub, does GO's notification go away?
aliases: read on hub clears go notification
entries.a: Yes. When you read a DM or a mention on another device with the same account, GO removes the matching alert from your phone's notification shade and clears the unread mark. It only touches alerts this phone showed itself.

entries.q: What does "Your notification settings were updated from another of your devices" mean?
aliases: notification settings updated from another device
entries.a: You changed notification settings on another device signed in with the same account, such as your Hub, and GO has just applied them. GO shows this notice once so the change does not surprise you. To change them back, open the notifications panel and tap the gear.

entries.q: Which notification settings sync between GO and Hub?
entries.a: App notification rules, which Q-Apps may notify you, muted apps and what you have already seen are shared between GO and Hub over Reticulum. Both must be signed in to the same account, be online together at least once, and run a version with notification sync. The Disable push notifications switch stays on each device.

entries.q: What does the Synced across your devices line in notification settings mean?
entries.a: It tells you whether notification settings can sync right now. "Linked with N of your devices" means it works. "Ready, waiting for your other device" means your other device is not online. Other lines say the other device's version does not support it yet, the chat engine is still starting, or chat is off, so settings stay on this device.

entries.q: How do I share a photo or file from another app into a GO chat?
aliases: send picture from gallery go chat
entries.a: Use Share in the other app (your gallery, files or browser) and pick GO Groups, GO DMs or GO Self-DM. GO opens that list with the item waiting at the top; tap the chat it should go to, and it lands in the message box. A picture then asks Compress or As attachment, as when you attach one. Add text if you like and send.

entries.q: What are GO Groups, GO DMs and GO Self-DM in the share sheet?
entries.a: They are GO's three entries in Android's share sheet. GO Groups opens your Groups list and GO DMs your DMs list, so you can pick where the shared item goes. GO Self-DM puts it straight into Saved Messages, your private chat with yourself. They work for photos, videos, files, links and text.

entries.q: How do I share into a specific channel of a group in GO?
entries.a: Share to GO Groups and tap the group. Its channel list slides in over the Groups list, with the item still waiting at the top ("pick a channel"). Tap the channel and the item goes into its message box. A group with only one channel you can post in opens straight away.

entries.q: Why is a channel greyed out when I share into a group?
entries.a: Only admins can post in that channel, so it says "admins only" and cannot take the shared item. Pick another channel, or go back and choose another chat. If a group has no channel you may post in, GO tells you so.

entries.q: How do I cancel sharing something into GO?
entries.a: Tap the X on the shared item at the top of the list, or press Android back. In the channel step, back first returns you to the Groups list with the item still waiting; back again drops it.

entries.q: Can I share text or a link into a GO chat?
aliases: send link from browser to go
entries.a: Yes. Choose GO Groups, GO DMs or GO Self-DM in the other app's share sheet, then tap a chat: the text or link is put into its message box, ready to send.

entries.q: Why didn't my shared file arrive in the GO chat?
entries.a: GO says why in a short note. A message holds one file, so only the first of several is added. Files over 100 MB are left out, and a picture that cannot be cleaned of its location data is left out too. If GO could not read the file at all, share it again from the other app.

entries.q: Why can't I share straight to one person from the share sheet?
entries.a: GO only offers its three lists in the share sheet: GO Groups, GO DMs and GO Self-DM. Pick GO DMs and then tap the person in your DMs list. GO does not put single chats or contacts into the share sheet or the launcher.

entries.q: Can I share into GO while it is locked?
entries.a: Yes. GO holds the shared item while it is locked and opens the chat list once you unlock with your fingerprint or password. Unlock within 5 minutes, or the held share is dropped and you share again.

entries.q: Where do I find notifications in GO?
entries.a: Tap your avatar at the top right and choose Notifications. When something new is waiting, a small green bell sits on your avatar; tapping that bell opens the panel straight away.

entries.q: What shows in GO's notifications panel?
aliases: what is in the bell go
entries.a: Mentions (one card per group), missed calls, group calendar reminders, payments you received, notifications from Q-Apps you allowed, such as Torq, new Q-Mail, and your downloads and saved files. Notices from GO itself show there too, for example when your phone stopped GO in the background. Tap an item to open it.

entries.q: How do I clear notifications in GO?
entries.a: Swipe an item sideways to clear it, or tap Clear all at the top of the panel to empty it at once. Cleared items stay out of the panel and the badge, but you can still find them in Notification history for 30 days. A group's mention card comes back when new mentions arrive.

entries.q: How do I turn off all phone notifications from GO?
entries.a: Open the notifications panel and turn on Disable push notifications at the top. GO then shows no alerts on your phone at all, but everything still appears inside GO's panel. The switch only affects this device. Turn it off again to get alerts back.

entries.q: Where are GO's notification settings?
entries.a: Open the notifications panel and tap the gear at the top. Notification settings shows whether your settings sync with your other devices, the Background sync choice, and two tabs: Hub, with the Q-Chat mention switch, and Q-Apps, with every app allowed to notify you.

entries.q: How do I stop a Q-App from sending me notifications in GO?
entries.a: Open the notifications panel, tap the gear and go to the Q-Apps tab. Find the app and tap Revoke, and it can no longer send you notifications. On the same tab, Disable OS push only silences its phone alerts instead.

entries.q: How do I keep a Q-App's notifications in GO but stop its phone alerts?
aliases: mute app alerts keep in go
entries.a: In Notification settings, on the Q-Apps tab, turn on Disable OS push for that app. Its alerts stop popping up on your phone, while its notifications still show in GO's panel.

entries.q: How does a Q-App get permission to send me GO notifications?
aliases: allow this app to send notifications
entries.a: The first time an app wants to notify you, GO asks "Allow this app to send you GO notifications?" with Allow and Don't allow. Only apps you allow can notify you, and you can revoke that later in Notification settings, on the Q-Apps tab.

entries.q: How do I turn off mention notifications in GO?
entries.a: Open Q-Chat settings with the gear on the Groups or DMs list and turn off Mention notifications under Notifications. The same switch is on the Hub tab of Notification settings. Mentions still show in the group itself.

entries.q: Do I get a phone notification for every group message in GO?
entries.a: No. Ordinary group messages only show as unread counts in the Groups list. GO alerts you when someone mentions you, for DMs from people you added as friends, for calls and missed calls, for group calendar reminders, for payments you receive, and for Q-Apps you allowed.

entries.q: Why don't I get notifications for DMs in GO?
entries.a: GO only alerts you about DMs from people you added as friends (the Add friend button in the DM's header). It also stays quiet while you are using GO, and when Disable push notifications is on in the panel. If alerts only come when you open GO, your phone is stopping GO in the background: set Background sync and allow GO in the background.

entries.q: What does a GO DM notification show?
entries.a: It says "New message from" with the sender's name and "Open Q-Chat to view it". The message text itself is not shown on your lock screen or in the notification shade. Tap the alert to open that conversation.

entries.q: What happens when I tap a chat notification in GO?
entries.a: A DM alert opens that conversation, and a mention alert ("Mention in" the group's name) opens the group chat. Alerts for the same chat update one entry instead of piling up, and they disappear by themselves once you read that chat, here or on another of your devices.

entries.q: How do I change the sound of GO's notifications?
entries.a: Use Android's settings: Settings > Apps > GO 3.0 > Notifications. GO has separate categories, such as Private messages, Group messages, Qortal alerts, Calls, Call in progress, File transfers, Saved files and Qortal status, so you can set the sound or turn off each one. Incoming calls ring with the phone's ringtone.

entries.q: Why does GO always show a notification?
entries.a: That is GO's status notification. It belongs to the background service that keeps GO's Reticulum connection and background sync running, and it shows the connection state, how many accounts are online, and how many of your messages are waiting to send. Android requires such a notification while an app runs in the background.

entries.q: What are GO's Background sync modes?
entries.a: Background sync keeps chat working while GO is not on the screen. Off: chat stops about a minute after you leave and catches up when you return. While charging (the default): GO keeps syncing while the phone charges. Always: it keeps syncing whenever GO runs in the background, which uses noticeably more battery. Set it in the notifications panel, under the gear.

entries.q: What does Relaying for others mean in GO's Background sync?
entries.a: While your phone charges on Wi-Fi with background sync on, GO also helps pass group traffic on for other users, the way a desktop Hub does, and keeps more mesh neighbours. As soon as you unplug or switch to mobile data it drops back to the lighter phone mode.

entries.q: Can GO keep chat syncing all night on the charger?
entries.a: Yes. With While charging or Always, GO runs its background connection as a messaging service, which Android does not stop after a few hours, so it can sync all night on the charger. Some phone makers still freeze apps when the screen is off; if GO notices that, it shows steps for your phone in the notifications panel.

entries.q: What does "GO was stopped in the background" mean?
aliases: go was stopped in the background
entries.a: Your phone's own battery manager froze GO while background sync was on, so chats only caught up when you opened GO again. GO shows this card in the notifications panel after it happened at least twice in a week, with steps for your phone's brand and an Allow GO in background button. Follow the steps, then keep GO in your recent apps.

entries.q: How do I stop the "GO was stopped in the background" warnings?
entries.a: Tick Don't show again on the card. To get the warnings back later, open Notification settings (gear in the notifications panel) and tap Turn warnings back on under Background sync. Without the tick, the card comes back at most every 14 days and no more than 3 times.

entries.q: How do I let GO run in the background on a Samsung phone?
entries.a:
1. Open Settings > Apps > GO 3.0 > Battery and choose Unrestricted.
2. In Settings > Battery > Background usage limits, make sure GO is not in Sleeping apps or Deep sleeping apps.
Menu names can differ a little between models and Android versions. Don't swipe GO away from your recent apps.

entries.q: How do I let GO run in the background on a Xiaomi, Redmi or POCO phone?
entries.a:
1. Open Settings > Apps > Manage apps > GO 3.0.
2. Turn on Autostart.
3. Tap Battery saver and choose No restrictions.
Menu names can differ a little between models. Don't swipe GO away from your recent apps.

entries.q: How do I let GO run in the background on a vivo or iQOO phone?
entries.a:
1. Open Settings > Battery > Background power consumption management.
2. Find GO and choose Allow (or Don't restrict).
3. In Settings > Apps > Autostart, turn GO on if your phone has it.
On vivo, the Open battery settings button in GO's notice can take you to the battery page. Don't swipe GO away from your recent apps.

entries.q: How do I let GO run in the background on an OPPO, realme or OnePlus phone?
entries.a:
1. Open Settings > Apps > App management > GO 3.0.
2. Tap Battery usage and turn on Allow background activity, and Allow auto launch if it is shown.
Menu names can differ a little between models. Don't swipe GO away from your recent apps.

entries.q: How do I let GO run in the background on a Huawei or Honor phone?
entries.a:
1. Open Settings > Battery > App launch.
2. Find GO and turn off Manage automatically.
3. Turn on Auto-launch, Secondary launch and Run in background.
Menu names can differ a little between models. Don't swipe GO away from your recent apps.

entries.q: How do I let GO run in the background on other Android phones?
entries.a:
1. Open Settings > Apps > GO 3.0 > App battery usage (or Battery).
2. Choose Unrestricted, or turn on Allow background usage.
On Android, also turn off "Pause app activity if unused" for GO. Don't swipe GO away from your recent apps.

entries.q: GO is already unrestricted but still gets stopped. Why?
entries.a: Some phones stop apps when the screen turns off even after you lifted their battery restrictions. GO then says so instead of asking again: background sync works while the screen is on, and chats catch up when you open GO. Plugging in does not always help on those phones.

entries.q: Can I make voice calls in Qortal GO?
entries.a: Yes. GO makes 1:1 voice calls and group calls with desktop Hubs and other GO phones, using the Hub's own call system. Calls are encrypted. A 1:1 call tries a direct link first and moves to Reticulum by itself if that fails. The calls are voice only.

entries.q: How do I call someone in GO?
entries.a: Open your DM with the person and tap the phone button in the chat's header. You must be DM friends: both of you tap Add friend in the DM's header. The other person also has to be online, and GO needs about half a minute after it connects before calls are ready.

entries.q: How do I add someone as a friend in GO?
entries.a: Open your DM with them and tap Add friend in the header. Calls unlock once they add you back, and GO notes in the chat when either of you adds the other. GO only alerts you about DMs from people you added as friends. Tap the button again to remove a friend.

entries.q: How do I see who is in a group call in GO?
entries.a: On the group call screen, tap the button that shows the count, such as "4 in call". A list opens with everyone in the call and how many places are taken out of the maximum, and people who are talking right now are marked Speaking.

entries.q: Why was my call declined in GO?
aliases: does not have you as a friend call
entries.a: GO says why. "The other person declined the call" means they rejected it. "does not have you as a friend" means they have not added you back, so calls are not possible yet. "their microphone may be unavailable" means their phone or computer could not use a microphone.

entries.q: How do I answer a call in GO?
entries.a: An incoming call rings with your phone's ringtone and shows a full-screen call screen and a notification with the caller's avatar. Tap Accept to answer or Decline to reject, on the screen or in the notification. If you are already in a call, the button says End & accept and ends the current call first.

entries.q: Can I answer a GO call while my phone is locked?
entries.a: Yes. The call screen shows over the lock screen and you can answer there. Only the call is shown: GO itself stays locked, and you unlock your phone to use anything else. On Android 14 and newer GO needs your OK to show calls over the lock screen; without it a call only shows as a notification.

entries.q: What does "Ringer off" mean on an incoming GO call?
entries.a: You silenced the ringtone, for example with Android back on the ring screen. The call is still waiting: you can still answer or decline it. Back only stops the ringing; it never declines the call.

entries.q: How do I switch a GO call to speaker or Bluetooth?
entries.a: During the call, open the audio button to see "Play call audio on": pick Phone (the earpiece), Speaker, Bluetooth or Headset. GO also switches by itself when you connect or remove a Bluetooth or wired headset. 1:1 calls start on the earpiece and group calls on the speaker.

entries.q: What do the buttons on a file in a GO chat mean?
entries.a: A file card shows its state and one button. Not downloaded with Download: tap to fetch it. Downloading with a percentage and Cancel. Downloaded with Save, to keep a copy in your phone's storage. File unavailable or Download failed with Try again, when no device that has it is online or the transfer broke off.

entries.q: How do I mute or hang up a GO call?
entries.a: Use Mute and Hang up on the call screen. They are also in the ongoing-call notification, so you can mute or hang up without opening GO. In a group call the button says Leave.

entries.q: Can I use GO for other things during a call?
entries.a: Yes. Minimize the call screen and keep using GO: a small call strip stays on every section, and tapping it (Return to the call) brings the call screen back. The microphone keeps working while GO is in the background.

entries.q: What do Encrypted · Direct and Encrypted · Relayed mean on a GO call?
entries.a: Every GO call is encrypted. Direct means the audio goes straight between you and the other person; it is faster, and they can see your IP address. Relayed means the audio goes over Reticulum, so your IP address stays hidden, though the sound can be a little slower.

entries.q: What does "Verification failed" mean on a chat file?
entries.a: GO checks every file it downloads against the fingerprint the sender's message gave it. Verification failed means the data that arrived did not match, so GO did not keep it. Tap Try again later; the file can come from another member who has it. Old GO versions before v0.0.11 failed this check by mistake on files over 1 MB, so update GO if yours is that old.

entries.q: What do the dots on GO's Chat button mean?
aliases: blue dot green dot chat go
entries.a: They show unread messages while you are elsewhere in GO. A dot on the left of the round Chat button means unread group messages, and a green dot on the right means unread DMs. They go away once you have read those chats.

entries.q: Does GO show previews for links in chat?
entries.a: Yes, for Qortal links. A qortal:// link to a post, video or article shows a small preview card, a group invite shows the group's name and Group Score with a Join button, and a calendar event link shows the event. Pictures from outside web servers are not loaded in previews, so nobody can tell when you read the message.

entries.q: How do I start or join a group call in GO?
entries.a: Open the group chat and tap the call button in its header. If a call is already running in that group, you join it; otherwise you start one and others can join. The Groups list shows a call count on groups with a call. Tap Leave to go.

entries.q: How do I jump to the newest or first unread message in a GO chat?
entries.a: When you scroll up or new messages arrive, a round button shows near the bottom of the chat: it jumps to the latest message or scrolls to your first unread message. A "New messages" line marks where the messages you have not read start.

entries.q: How do I see replies to my messages in a group in GO?
entries.a: A channel with unread replies to you shows it on its badge in the channel list ("Unread reply" or the number of unread replies). In the chat, a reply to your message carries a quote headed "Replying to you". Replies in a discussion show as View N replies under the message.

entries.q: What does "Replied to deleted message" mean?
entries.a: The message this one answered has been deleted, so its quote cannot be shown any more. The reply itself is unchanged.

entries.q: Why do chats open with their messages already there in GO?
entries.a: GO keeps a copy of chats you opened, and of your most recent ones, ready in memory, so they open at once and then refresh quietly. The copy is only in memory, never on disk, and is emptied when GO locks, when you log out or switch accounts. Nothing leaves the phone for it except sender-name lookups on your own node.

entries.q: Where can I see missed calls in GO?
entries.a: A missed call shows in the notifications panel as "Missed voice call from" the caller, and in your DM with that person as a call row. The DM also lists other calls: answered, declined, cancelled and no answer.

entries.q: Does my phone ring for GO calls when GO is in the background?
entries.a: Yes. GO rings natively even while it is in the background, with a ringing notification, the caller's avatar and Accept and Decline. Like messages, this works only while your phone lets GO run in the background, so allow GO in the background if calls do not come through.

entries.q: What is the overview next to the chat lists on a tablet?
entries.a: With no chat open on a tablet, GO shows a Q-Chat overview beside the lists: "Welcome back" with the groups that have new messages or mentions since you were away, or "You're all caught up" when there is nothing new. Tap a group to open it, or Browse Communities to find more.

entries.q: Does GO work on tablets?
entries.a: Yes. GO keeps its phone layout at every size, and on screens 760 pixels wide or more the chat list and the open chat show side by side. In landscape the Home, Apps and Chat buttons move into the top bar, and dialogs, viewers and Tabs fit shorter screens.

entries.q: Can I use GO in landscape?
entries.a: Yes, on phones and tablets. Turned sideways, GO puts the Home, Apps and Chat buttons in the top bar, leaves room for the navigation bar and the camera cutout, and keeps the message box on screen. The keyboard height is remembered separately for each orientation.

entries.q: Does turning my phone keep my open chat in GO?
entries.a: Yes. Turning the phone or tablet keeps the chat you have open, with what you were typing.

entries.q: Why don't I see chats side by side on my phone in landscape?
aliases: side by side chat phone landscape
entries.a: Side by side needs a screen at least 760 pixels wide that is not too short. Phones turned sideways are usually too short, so they keep one pane at a time; tablets get both.

entries.q: Can I edit or delete a DM in GO?
entries.a: Yes, like any message: tap your DM and choose Edit or Delete. The change is sent to the other person's devices and to your own, and takes effect there when they receive it. You can also react to DMs the same way as in groups.

entries.q: Does a full-screen video turn my tablet sideways in GO?
entries.a: No. On tablets a full-screen video no longer forces landscape; turn the tablet yourself if you want.

entries.q: Can anyone send me a DM in GO?
entries.a: Yes: anyone can start a DM to your name or address, and it shows in your DMs list. GO only gives phone alerts for DMs from people you added as friends. To stop seeing someone, tap their name, choose Hide user and pick until unhidden.

entries.q: What do the coloured dots on avatars in GO chat mean?
entries.a: They show each person's status: green is online, amber is idle, red is busy and grey is offline. You see them in the DM list, the Members panel, on messages and on user cards.

entries.q: How do I add an event to a group calendar in GO?
entries.a: As an admin or the owner, open the group's three-dot menu, tap Calendar, then Add event. Give it a title and description, a cover image if you like, start and end (or All day) with a time zone, a location and a link. You can make it repeat daily, weekly, monthly or yearly, and pick a reminder.

entries.q: What reminders can a group calendar event have?
entries.a: At start, 10 minutes before, 30 minutes before, 1 hour before, 1 day before, or None.

entries.q: What is Files in a GO group?
entries.a: Files opens the Q-Manager app inside the group, for the group's shared files. Open it from the group chat's three-dot menu and close it with the X at the top right or Android back.

entries.q: What happens when I tap someone's name in a GO chat?
entries.a: Their user card opens: avatar, name, Qortal address (with copy), QORT balance and minter level. From it you can open a DM with Message, send them QORT with Send QORT, view their profile, or hide them from that chat.

entries.q: How do I hide someone in a GO chat?
entries.a: Tap their name or avatar to open their card, choose Hide user and pick for 1 hour, for 24 hours or until unhidden. Their messages then stay out of that group's chat, or that DM, on your phone. To undo it, open their card again and choose Unhide. To see everyone you hid in a group, open its channel list, tap the group's name at the top and choose Hidden users.

entries.q: Do GO calls work on mobile data?
entries.a: Yes. Calls work on Wi-Fi and on mobile data. In a test on mobile data with a desktop Hub, the direct link was up in about 7 seconds with no audio lost. A call on a slow uplink can take longer to connect, and it falls back to Reticulum if the direct link fails.

entries.q: Does a GO call keep going if I leave the app?
aliases: does call continue if i leave app
entries.a: Yes. GO keeps the microphone on in the background, and an ongoing-call notification lets you mute or hang up without opening GO. Tap the notification or the call strip to go back to the call screen.

entries.q: How do I open the chat with someone during a GO call?
entries.a: On a 1:1 call screen, tap Message: it opens your DM with that person while the call keeps running, and the call strip brings you back to the call screen. While GO is locked, the Message button is hidden.

entries.q: How do I link to a channel or group in a GO message?
entries.a: Type @ in the message box. Besides people, the suggestions list the group's channels and the group itself; pick one and it becomes a link in your message that others can tap to open that channel or group chat.

entries.q: What do the Owner and Admin tags next to names in GO chat mean?
entries.a: They show the person's role in that group: Owner for the group's owner and Admin for its admins. Members have no tag. The same roles decide who can post in admin channels and who sees the admin buttons in Members.

entries.q: What is the number under someone's avatar in GO chat?
entries.a: It is their minter level. Accounts that mint show a small plate with their level under the avatar on their messages; hold or hover it to see "Minter Level" with the number. The plate takes the colour of their role when they are an owner or admin.

entries.q: Do Q-App notifications work on the public node in GO?
aliases: do notifications need my own node
entries.a: Yes. Q-App notifications come from the node each device is connected to, so the public node works as well as your own. Chat mentions and DMs arrive over Reticulum instead.

entries.q: Can a Q-App see which notifications I read in other apps?
entries.a: No. A Q-App only sees and marks its own notifications as read. It cannot learn which notifications of other Q-Apps you have read, and marking its own does not touch theirs.

entries.q: What does "Syncing in the background" mean in GO's notification?
entries.a: GO's background sync is keeping chat running while GO is not on the screen, because the phone is charging or you chose Always. New messages arrive and yours go out without opening GO. When the phone stops it, the notification says Chat paused instead.

entries.q: What does "Still setting up the secure audio link" mean on a GO call?
aliases: still setting up secure audio link
entries.a: The call was accepted, but the encrypted audio link between the devices is not up yet. This can take a little longer on a slow network. Wait a moment; if it never connects, hang up and call again.

entries.q: What is the card at the top of GO when a Q-App downloads a file?
entries.a: It shows a download from a Q-App, such as a file you save from Q-Share, with its progress. Tap the arrow, or swipe the card sideways, to tuck it into the notifications panel, where the download keeps going; it also tucks itself away after a few seconds. Several downloads stack, newest in front.

entries.q: What are the saved files in GO's notifications panel?
entries.a: Files you saved from Q-Apps are listed there with where they went, for example "Ready to open" in your Documents folder under Qortal Go, and an Open button. The X removes a file from the list; the file itself stays on your phone. GO never opens or installs app packages it downloaded; GO's own updates come from GO 3.0 Updates.

entries.q: What does the Friend mark in the GO DMs list mean?
entries.a: It marks people you added as friends with Add friend in their DM. GO gives you phone alerts for DMs from your friends, and once you have added each other you can call. Remove a friend with the same button in the DM's header.

entries.q: Why did a group open in a channel other than General?
aliases: why did group open this channel
entries.a: A group opens in the channel where you last left an unsent draft, so the draft is found where you started it. A tapped notification or a share into the group opens the channel it belongs to. Without either, the group opens in its default channel.

entries.q: What do Join, Apply, Pending and Joined on a group invite mean?
entries.a: On an invite card in chat, Join adds you to an open group and Apply asks to join a closed group, where an admin must accept you. Pending means your request or join is waiting for the blockchain or for an admin. Joined means you are already a member.

entries.q: What does "updating" under my message mean?
entries.a: You edited the message and GO is still sending the change. It goes away once the edit is out. If it turns into "failed to update", the edit did not go through, so edit the message again.

entries.q: Why does a DM show Unhide user in its header?
entries.a: You hid that person. Their messages stay out of your view until you tap Unhide user, or until the time you picked (1 hour or 24 hours) runs out.

entries.q: Does the person know when I hide them in GO chat?
entries.a: No. Hiding only changes what your own device shows, and it is set separately for each group and each DM. Nothing is sent to the other person, and your other devices, such as your Hub, keep showing them unless you hide them there too.

entries.q: How do group calendar reminders reach me in GO?
entries.a: When an event's reminder time comes, GO puts "Reminder" with the event's title in the notifications panel and, if GO is not on the screen, shows a phone alert with the start time. Tapping it opens the group's calendar.

entries.q: Why do my reactions wiggle now and then in GO?
entries.a: That is on purpose: every few seconds one of your own reactions on screen gives a small wiggle, hop or pulse, so you can spot which reactions are yours. It stops while you are not touching the phone and when the phone is set to reduce motion.

entries.q: Can I save or copy a GIF from a GO chat?
entries.a: Yes. Tap the GIF and it opens in GO's viewer like a picture, with Save and Copy in the bottom bar. You can swipe from there to the chat's other pictures, GIFs and videos.

entries.q: How do I move a file from my phone to my computer with GO?
aliases: send file from phone to computer
send file to my computer go
entries.a: Put it in Saved Messages: use Share in your gallery or files app and pick GO Self-DM, or attach it in Saved Messages with +. If your Hub on the computer is signed in with the same account, it gets the message and the file when both are online, and you can open or save it there.

entries.q: Why does my screen go dark during a GO call?
aliases: screen off at ear go call
entries.a: While a 1:1 call plays through the earpiece, GO uses the phone's proximity sensor: the screen turns off when you hold the phone to your ear, so your cheek cannot press buttons, and it comes back when you move the phone away. On the speaker or a headset the screen stays on.

entries.q: Which Android version do I need for Qortal GO?
aliases: does qortal go work on android 8
entries.a: Qortal GO (GO 3.0) needs Android 8.0 or newer. It is built for 64-bit phones and tablets (ARM64), so an old phone that only runs 32-bit apps cannot install it. NFC, a camera and a microphone are optional: GO installs without them, and only the features that need them are missing.

entries.q: Is there a Qortal GO app for iPhone?
entries.a: No. Qortal GO is an Android app only. On an iPhone or iPad, the Downloads page on qortal.dev points you to a web app that runs in the browser instead.

entries.q: Where do I download Qortal GO?
aliases: where to download qortal go apk
entries.a:
Qortal GO comes as an APK file that you install yourself. The newest build is in three places:
qortal.dev → Downloads → Android (it downloads GO-3.0.apk).
Q-Share, under the name GO 3.0, if you already use Qortal.
The releases of the GO-3.0 project on Qortal's Gitea.
Once GO is installed, it updates itself from QDN.

entries.q: How do I install the Qortal GO APK?
entries.a:
1. Download the APK on your phone, for example from qortal.dev → Downloads → Android.
2. Open the downloaded file.
3. If Android blocks it, allow "Install unknown apps" for the browser or file app you used, then go back.
4. Tap Install. The app shows up as GO 3.0.
5. Open it and create or import your account.

entries.q: Why is the app called GO 3.0 on my phone?
aliases: go 3.0 same app as qortal go
entries.a: GO 3.0 is the current Qortal GO app, and that is the name under its icon. It is built from the same code as Qortal Hub, the desktop app, with a phone layout and Android parts added. Its releases are numbered v0.0.1, v0.0.2 and so on, so you will see names like "GO 3.0 v0.0.19".

entries.q: Is Qortal GO open source?
entries.a: Yes. GO 3.0 is built from the Qortal Hub code and keeps its GPL-3.0 licence. Its code is public in the GO-3.0 repository on Qortal's Gitea, where each release also carries the APK.

entries.q: Does Qortal GO use Google services or trackers?
entries.a: No. GO contains no Google Play Services, Firebase or Chromecast code, makes no Google backup of its data, and has the WebView's usage reports and Safe Browsing switched off. The Exodus tracker scan finds none of the 432 trackers it knows. GO runs on phones without Google, such as GrapheneOS.

entries.q: Does Qortal GO work on GrapheneOS?
entries.a: Yes. Since v0.0.14 GO is a release build, so login on GrapheneOS takes a second or two instead of 30 seconds or more. If "WebView JIT" is turned off for GO, chats and the chat database run slower, mostly right after GO starts, and GO shows a calm notice once with the two steps to change it. Allowing JIT is your choice: it makes GO faster, keeping it off adds hardening.

entries.q: How do I turn on WebView JIT for GO on GrapheneOS?
entries.a:
1. Open Android Settings > Apps > GO 3.0 > "Exploit protection".
2. Allow "WebView JIT".
GO uses the new setting the next time it starts. It is a GrapheneOS security setting, so leaving it off is fine too; GO just runs slower.

entries.q: What permissions does Qortal GO use and why?
entries.a: Microphone: voice calls. Camera: the built-in QR scanner, which reads codes on the phone with no Google service. Notifications: messages, calls and downloads. NFC: the Qortal Card (testing), only while its screen waits for a tap. Install apps: GO's own updates, and Android still asks you to confirm each one. GO never asks for your location or for "Nearby devices".

entries.q: Why can't I take a screenshot on some GO screens?
entries.a: GO blocks screenshots, screen recording and the recent-apps preview on its most sensitive screens: the unlock and lock screens, the seed phrase, private key and backup screens, and while a payment or Q-App approval is open. This keeps your keys out of screenshots and away from other apps. Write a seed phrase down on paper instead.

entries.q: Does Qortal GO run a Qortal node on my phone?
aliases: run a lite node in qortal go
entries.a: No. GO connects to a Qortal Core node: the public node by default, or a node you run yourself. Login settings has a "Run a Lite Node" item, but Qortal Lite Nodes are still being built. Once they are live on the network, GO will let you run one from there.

entries.q: Can I use Qortal GO without internet?
entries.a: Mostly not: your balance, Q-Apps, QDN data and the blockchain all come from a Qortal node, so GO needs a connection to one. Qortino, GO's AI helper, is the exception. Once its model is assembled on the phone, it answers with no internet at all.

entries.q: Is Qortal GO free?
entries.a: Yes, GO costs nothing to download, install or update, and creating an account is free. Actions written to the blockchain, such as registering a name, publishing or sending QORT, cost a small fee in QORT, the same as on Qortal Hub.

entries.q: How do I update Qortal GO?
entries.a:
1. Tap your avatar at the top right and open GO 3.0 Updates.
2. If no update shows yet, tap Check for updates.
3. Tap Install update. GO fetches the build from QDN and checks it.
4. Confirm the install in Android's window.
Your accounts, settings and chats are kept.

entries.q: Does Qortal GO check for updates by itself?
aliases: how does go know new version
entries.a: Yes. GO looks for a newer build about half a minute after it starts, then every 6 hours, and again when you come back to it after a long break. When it finds one, your avatar gets a small update mark and GO 3.0 Updates in the account menu gets a badge. Nothing installs until you tap Install update and confirm.

entries.q: What is the GO 3.0 Updates screen?
aliases: see all versions of qortal go
entries.a: It is GO's update window, under Node in the account menu (tap your avatar). It shows the version installed on this phone, a Check for updates button with when it last looked, and an Install update card when a newer build is out. Below, Versions on QDN lists every published build, newest first, with its size, date and release notes (Show changes), and Open in Q-Share for each.

entries.q: Where can I read what changed in a GO version?
entries.a: Open GO 3.0 Updates from the account menu and tap Show changes under a version in Versions on QDN. The same notes are the description of that build's share in Q-Share: tap Open in Q-Share to see its share page.

entries.q: Why does a GO update ask me to allow installs?
entries.a: Android only installs apps from sources you have allowed. Tap Allow installs, turn on "Install unknown apps" for GO 3.0 in Android's settings, then come back to GO: the install carries on by itself.

entries.q: Will updating GO delete my accounts or chats?
aliases: update qortal go without losing chats
entries.a: No. Every GO 3.0 build is signed with the same key, so a new version installs over the old one and keeps your saved accounts, settings and chats. Only uninstalling GO removes its data from the phone.

entries.q: Can I go back to an older version of GO?
entries.a: Not on top of a newer one: Android does not install an older version over a newer one. That is why the Updates screen offers Install only for newer builds; older ones can only be opened in Q-Share. The only way back is to uninstall first, which deletes GO's data on the phone, so have your seed phrase or wallet backup ready.

entries.q: How do I check which version of GO I have?
entries.a: Tap the Qortal logo at the top left to open Core & settings: GO version shows the version on your phone. GO 3.0 Updates in the account menu also shows the installed version next to the published ones.

entries.q: Where do GO updates come from?
entries.a: From QDN. Each build is published with Q-Share under the registered name GO 3.0, and your node fetches it from peers when you tap Install update. GO only installs a file with GO's own package name, signed with the same key as the GO on your phone, and with a higher version number.

entries.q: Why did GO refuse to install an update?
entries.a: GO refuses a file that is not a genuine, newer GO: one signed with a different key, a different app, or a build that is not newer than yours. These checks stop fake updates. Check again later from GO 3.0 Updates, and never install a GO APK from a source you do not trust.

entries.q: Why won't GO download an update from my node?
aliases: go update could not reach qdn
entries.a: GO downloads updates only over HTTPS or from a node on the phone itself (127.0.0.1). If your private node uses plain HTTP across the network, switch to an HTTPS node, such as the public node, while you update. If the screen says it could not reach QDN, check the node connection and try again.

entries.q: Can I keep using GO while an update downloads?
entries.a: Yes. You can close the GO 3.0 Updates screen and the download carries on. Its steps are: fetching from the Qortal network, assembling the build, downloading, and then Android asks you to confirm. Fetching can take a while if the network is slow to deliver the build; if it times out, try again.

entries.q: Can I install a GO APK that I downloaded with Q-Share inside GO?
aliases: install apk from q-share in go
apk in qortal go apps folder
entries.a: No. GO saves an APK you download in a Q-App (to Documents/Qortal Go/Apps) but never opens or installs app packages itself. To update GO, use GO 3.0 Updates in the account menu, which checks the build first. To install any other APK, open it from your phone's file manager.

entries.q: What does Later do on a GO update?
entries.a: Later hides the offer for that version. To see it again, open GO 3.0 Updates and tap Check for updates.

entries.q: What happens if I uninstall Qortal GO?
entries.a: Uninstalling deletes what GO keeps on the phone: saved accounts, settings, the chat database and Qortino's model. Your account itself lives on the Qortal blockchain, so after reinstalling you add it back with your seed phrase or wallet backup file. Make sure you have one of them before you uninstall.

entries.q: How do I know my GO APK is genuine?
aliases: is my qortal go apk real
entries.a: Get GO only from qortal.dev → Downloads, from Q-Share under the name GO 3.0, or from the GO-3.0 releases on Qortal's Gitea; each Gitea release lists the APK's SHA-256 checksum to compare. After that, GO's own updater only installs builds signed with the same key as yours. Never type your seed phrase into an APK from anywhere else.

entries.q: Where can I find older versions of Qortal GO?
entries.a: Every GO 3.0 build is listed in GO 3.0 Updates under Versions on QDN, and each one opens in Q-Share. The Downloads page on qortal.dev also links to older Qortal Go releases on GitHub. Remember that an older build cannot be installed over a newer one.

entries.q: Is Qortal GO finished or still being built?
entries.a: GO 3.0 is young and changes quickly: its versions are still numbered 0.0.x, and new builds come often with fixes and features. A few parts are marked as testing, such as the Qortal Card. Keep GO updated through GO 3.0 Updates, and keep your seed phrase backed up as with any wallet.

entries.q: How do I give feedback or suggest a feature for GO?
entries.a: Join the GO 3.0 group in Q-Chat and tell the team there. GO links to it from Home: in the panel above Qortino, tap + (if the panel shows hotkeys, tap × first; your hotkeys stay saved) and choose Suggest a module, which opens the group's invite. For a wrong Qortino answer, use the report button under that answer instead.

entries.q: What is the public node in Qortal GO?
entries.a: It is the shared gateway node ext-node.qortal.link that GO uses by default, so you can start at once without running Qortal Core yourself. It is quick, but it is shared and run by someone else: it does not take QDN uploads (posts, avatars, apps), and minting, blocking accounts and sending coins other than QORT also need your own node. Big downloads such as Qortino's model can work there but are unreliable, so your own node is highly recommended for them.

entries.q: How do I connect Qortal GO to my own node?
aliases: use own node in qortal go
entries.a:
1. Tap your avatar and choose Node. Before you log in, use Login settings at the bottom right of the Enter Qortal screen.
2. Under Node connection, tap Add private node.
3. Enter a name, the Node URL (your node's address with its API port, 12391 by default) and its API key if it needs one.
4. Tap Save and use. GO switches to that node.

entries.q: How do I switch GO back to the public node?
aliases: go back to public node qortal go
entries.a: Tap your avatar, choose Node, and tap Public node under Node connection (or do the same in Login settings before you log in). Your saved private nodes stay in the list, so one tap switches back to them later.

entries.q: Can GO remember more than one private node?
entries.a: Yes. Saved private nodes keeps a list, each with its own name, URL, port and API key, so you never retype a key. Tap a node to switch to it, or use its buttons to edit or remove it.

entries.q: Do I need an API key to use my node with GO?
entries.a: It depends on how GO reaches the node. A node on the phone's own address (127.0.0.1, such as an SSH tunnel) may work without one. A node on your home network or the internet needs its API key, and GO asks for it when it is missing or wrong. Enter it in the API key field of your saved private node. The public node never asks for a key.

entries.q: Why did GO say my apikey is invalid on the public node?
aliases: go asks api key at login public node
entries.a: On the public node that message came from a busy node's error page, not from a real key problem. GO v0.0.18 fixed it: on the public node GO never asks for a key, so update GO through GO 3.0 Updates. On your own node, the message means the saved key is wrong; enter the node's key again.

entries.q: What can't I do in GO on the public node?
aliases: what needs own node in go
why use my own node with go
entries.a: On the public node you can't publish on QDN (posts with media, avatars, apps), mint, block accounts yourself or send coins other than QORT; those need your own node. Q-Apps and websites also depend on what the public node has stored, so some load slowly, and Qortino's model download is unreliable there, so your own node is highly recommended for it. Reading Q-Apps, chat and QORT payments work.

entries.q: What does Android's back button do in GO?
entries.a: Back closes GO's own windows and panels first, newest first: Settings, Tabs, menus, viewers. With nothing open, it takes you to Home from Apps or Chat, and on Home it sends GO to the background. In a full-screen Q-App it leaves full screen first. The Q-App itself stays open in Tabs; use its own buttons to go back inside it.

entries.q: What does the Public node unavailable window in GO mean?
aliases: use a private node button go
entries.a: GO cannot reach the public node right now, so the Q-App or website you opened can't load. Tap Wait and GO keeps checking (Check now asks at once) and opens the app as soon as the node is back, when the window turns green with "Public node is back". Or tap Use a private node to open node settings.

entries.q: Can GO use my home node when I'm away from home?
aliases: access my node away from home go
entries.a: Yes, if your phone can reach it. One way is a VPN such as Tailscale, using the node's VPN address as your private node. Another is an SSH tunnel that makes the node appear at 127.0.0.1 on the phone. Add that address as a private node, with its API key if it needs one. Never open Core's API port (12391) to the whole internet.

entries.q: Can I browse normal websites in GO?
entries.a: GO shows Qortal websites, the ones published on QDN, in tabs just like Q-Apps; find them with the top bar search. Ordinary web links open in your phone's own browser instead, outside GO.

entries.q: Why does Qortino sometimes say it is not sure?
entries.a: On purpose: Qortino is told never to invent facts, doses, numbers, sources, apps or names. When it isn't sure, it says so and gives the safest established option instead of guessing.

entries.q: How do I create a new account in Qortal GO?
entries.a:
1. On the Enter Qortal screen, tap Create account.
2. Choose a wallet password and type it twice; it protects the account on this phone.
3. Reveal your seedphrase and write it down on paper.
4. Tap Create account, then save the encrypted wallet backup GO offers (it goes to Documents/Qortal Go).
5. Tap Enter GO.
Creating an account is free.

entries.q: How do I import my existing Qortal account into GO?
entries.a:
On the Enter Qortal screen, tap Import account and pick one:
Seedphrase: type it and choose a wallet password for this phone.
Backup file: pick your wallet backup file to keep the account in GO.
Authenticate now: use a backup file this once without saving it.
Check that the address is the one you expect before moving any funds.

entries.q: What does Authenticate now mean when importing in GO?
aliases: go import not saved on device
entries.a: It signs you in with a wallet backup file for this session only: GO uses the file and its password but does not keep the account on the phone. Next time you need the file again. Choose Backup file instead if you want GO to remember the account.

entries.q: What is the wallet password in Qortal GO?
entries.a: It is the password you choose for an account on this phone. GO uses it to encrypt the saved account, and asks for it to unlock, to confirm payments and to reveal keys. It is not your seedphrase, and nobody can reset it. If you forget it, remove the account and import it again with your seedphrase, choosing a new password; a backup file only opens with the password it was saved with.

entries.q: How do I turn on fingerprint unlock in GO?
entries.a:
1. On the Enter Qortal screen, tap Login settings (the slider button at the bottom right).
2. Under Unlock with fingerprint, pick the account.
3. Enter that account's wallet password once.
4. Confirm with your fingerprint.
After that, tap the fingerprint on the unlock screen instead of typing the password.

entries.q: Is fingerprint unlock in GO safe?
aliases: where is my password stored go
entries.a: With fingerprint unlock, GO keeps your wallet password only on this phone, encrypted with a key held in the phone's Android Keystore, and asks for your fingerprint before it uses it. It never leaves the phone and is never uploaded. Any fingerprint enrolled on the phone can unlock GO, so only enrol your own. Sending QORT and Backup Wallet still ask for the typed password. You can turn fingerprint unlock off any time.

entries.q: How do I turn off fingerprint unlock in GO?
entries.a: Open Login settings on the Enter Qortal screen, pick the account under Unlock with fingerprint and tap Remove fingerprint unlock. You then unlock that account with its wallet password.

entries.q: Why doesn't fingerprint unlock work in GO?
entries.a: GO needs a fingerprint sensor that Android reports; without one, Login settings says no sensor was detected. Fingerprint unlock is also set per account, so pick the account first in Login settings. If a scan fails or you cancel it, GO lets you type your password instead.

entries.q: What are Login settings in GO?
entries.a: Login settings is the slider button at the bottom right of the Enter Qortal screen. It holds fingerprint unlock for each saved account, the Node connection (the public node or your private nodes), the startup sound switch, and a Run a Lite Node item that is coming later.

entries.q: How do I switch accounts in GO?
entries.a: Tap your avatar and choose Logout, then pick another account on the Enter Qortal screen. On an unlock screen, Choose another account takes you back to the list. When you reopen GO it starts with the account at the top of the list; long-press an account and drag it to change the order.

entries.q: Can I keep several accounts in Qortal GO?
entries.a: Yes. Every account you create or import (with Save account in GO on) stays in the Enter Qortal list. You can search the list by address, name or note, give an account its own name and a note with the edit button, and long-press an account to move it up or down.

entries.q: How do I remove an account from GO?
entries.a: On the Enter Qortal screen, open the account, tap its edit button and choose Remove in Account details. This only takes it off this phone, with its saved name and avatar: the account and its QORT stay on the blockchain. Make sure you have its seedphrase or backup file first, or you cannot add it back.

entries.q: How do I lock GO without logging out?
entries.a: Tap your avatar and choose Lock now. GO locks at once and asks for your fingerprint or password to come back. You stay signed in: chats and active calls stay connected while it is locked.

entries.q: How does auto-lock work in GO?
entries.a: GO locks itself when you have not used it for a while. Choose the time in Settings → System → Auto-Lock When Idle: Disabled, 10 min, 30 min (the default), 1 hour or 3 hours. Unlock with your fingerprint or password.

entries.q: What is the difference between Lock now and Logout in GO?
entries.a: Lock now keeps you signed in: chats and calls stay connected, and your fingerprint or password brings you back. Logout ends the session: GO's network stops, files received in chat are deleted from GO, and you pick an account again on the Enter Qortal screen. Your saved accounts stay on the phone either way.

entries.q: What happens while GO is locked?
entries.a: The lock covers every GO window, and Q-Apps cannot ask for anything until you unlock: their requests get "GO is locked. Unlock it and try again." A payment link you open while locked waits for the unlock. Chats and active calls stay connected.

entries.q: How do I back up my wallet in GO?
aliases: how do i backup my account
entries.a: On Home, tap Backup Wallet in Quick tools and download the wallet file. It is encrypted with your wallet password, or with a new password you choose for that backup. GO saves it under Documents/Qortal Go. Keep a copy off the phone too, along with your seedphrase written on paper.
