entries.q: Why doesn't my password manager fill in my GO password?
entries.a: On purpose: GO turns autofill off for the wallet password, so password managers are not offered it. Type the password, or turn on fingerprint unlock in Login settings so you don't have to.

entries.q: Why is GO stuck on the Qortal logo when it starts?
entries.a: If GO has trouble starting, it now says "GO is having trouble starting" with a Restart button instead of leaving the logo up. Tap Restart; GO goes back to the fingerprint or password unlock. If it keeps happening, update GO through GO 3.0 Updates.

entries.q: How do I turn off the startup sound in GO?
entries.a: Switch on Disable startup sound in Login settings on the Enter Qortal screen, or Disable Startup Sound in Settings → System after you log in.

entries.q: Do my GO Home and pinned apps sync with Qortal Hub?
entries.a: No, they stay on the phone: hotkeys and Tabs folders are kept in GO for each account, and the Home order for the phone. To copy your Hub's pinned apps into GO once, tap Import Hub dashboard in Tabs; they land in a folder named Hub. GO never writes its folders back, so it can't overwrite Hub's pins.

entries.q: What does the Using public node line on GO's unlock screen mean?
aliases: using my node name login go
entries.a: It tells you which node GO will use when you unlock: Using public node, Using local node, or the name of your private node. To change it, open Login settings → Node connection before you log in.

entries.q: What does the dot on the Qortal logo in GO mean?
entries.a: The dot on the Qortal logo at the top left shows your node: green when it is fully synced, amber while it is still syncing, grey when GO has no sync information. Tap the logo for Core & settings, with the Core version, sync status, block height, peers, minting status and the GO version.

entries.q: Should I change my node's API key after updating GO?
aliases: change node api key after update
old go version api key leak
entries.a: If you used GO with an API-keyed node before v0.0.15, change the node's key once. Older builds could save the key with Q-Trade buy orders, and on mobile data a carrier proxy could see it for a node at 127.0.0.1. Current builds keep the key away from Q-Apps and proxies. Then enter the new key in GO's private node settings.

entries.q: Can I block someone in Qortal GO?
entries.a: Yes, on your own node: open User Search (Quick tools on Home, or Address book in the account menu), look the account up and tap block. Settings → Blocked lists blocked names and addresses with Unblock. Blocking happens on the node, so on the public node it is not available; that node's operator decides who is blocked there.

entries.q: How do I look up another user's account in GO?
entries.a: Tap User Search in Quick tools on Home, or Address book in the account menu, and enter a name or address. GO shows the account's address, public key, level, minting progress and recent payments.

entries.q: What is in GO's account menu?
entries.a: Tap your avatar at the top right. The menu has Notifications, Wallets (opens Q-Wallets), Send QORT, Address book, Minting, Node, GO 3.0 Updates, Lock now and Logout. Qortal Card shows there too if you turn it on in Settings → System. Swipe the menu up or press back to close it.

entries.q: Where are the Settings in Qortal GO?
aliases: where is the settings gear go
entries.a: On Home, tap the gear button on the Account Overview card. Settings opens full screen with the tabs Profile, Security, Blocked and System. Swipe sideways to move between tabs, and press back or the round close button to leave.

entries.q: What is on the Home screen of Qortal GO?
entries.a: Home is a column of windows: Hotkeys and Qortino, Account Overview, Post to Torq, Quick tools, Featured Q-Apps, Status, Wallet Activity, Group Activity and the Torq Feed. You can turn some of them off in Settings → Profile → On Home, and long-press a window's background to move it.

entries.q: How do I rearrange the windows on GO's Home?
entries.a: Long-press the background of any Home window (not a button or link). Every window folds into a short labelled strip; drag the one under your finger up or down, the others make room, and let go. The order is saved on this phone, and Settings → Profile → Reset order puts it back.

entries.q: How do I hide parts of GO's Home screen?
entries.a: Open Settings → Profile and use the switches under On Home: Qortino AI, Featured Q-Apps, Status, Group Activity and the Torq Feed. Turning off Qortino AI keeps your hotkeys. Account Overview, Post to Torq, Quick tools and Wallet Activity always stay.

entries.q: What is Account Overview on GO's Home?
entries.a: It is your account card: avatar, name, online status and address, with buttons to show your receive QR code, copy the address and open Settings (the gear). Tap the name to see the full address, tap the avatar to change it, and tap the status to change it.

entries.q: How do I see my full Qortal address in GO?
aliases: where is my wallet address go
entries.a: On Home, tap your name in Account Overview: GO shows your full address, sized to fit without cutting it off. Tap again to show the name. The copy button next to it copies the address, and Settings → Profile also lists it.

entries.q: Where do I see my QORT balance in GO?
aliases: how much qort do i have go
entries.a: On Home, the Status window shows your QORT Balance at the top. Tap Wallets in the account menu (or Quick tools) to open Q-Wallets, which shows QORT and your other coins.

entries.q: What does the eye button in GO's Settings do?
entries.a: It turns on Privacy Mode, which blurs your name, address, private key and blocked accounts in Settings, so you can share your screen safely. Tap it again to show them.

entries.q: What does Qortal GO (this app) mean in an approval window?
entries.a: It means the request comes from GO itself, not from a Q-App: for example when you publish a post from Home or send a picture in chat, GO asks you to confirm the fee. Check the details as you would for any approval.

entries.q: What is in the Profile tab of GO's Settings?
entries.a: Your current name (with Register name if you have none) and your wallet address, then the On Home switches for Qortino AI, Featured Q-Apps, Status, Group Activity and the Torq Feed, with Reset order for the Home layout. To buy, sell or change a name, it points you to the Names Q-App.

entries.q: How do I change my avatar in GO?
entries.a: On Home, tap your avatar in Account Overview to open Update avatar, choose an image and publish it. An avatar needs a registered Qortal name, costs a small fee, and is published on QDN, so it needs your own node: the public node does not take uploads.

entries.q: How do I set my status to Busy or Offline in GO?
entries.a: On Home, tap the status under your avatar in Account Overview and pick Online, Busy or Offline (Offline makes you appear offline). Idle is set by itself while you are away. With a Hub version that has status sync, your choice follows your account to your other devices.

entries.q: What is in the System tab of GO's Settings?
entries.a: Auto-Lock When Idle, Disable Startup Sound, then the phone options: Widgets screen, Bottom buttons, Immersive mode, Calls, Qortal Card (testing) and Dev Mode, and finally Reduce UI Animations.

entries.q: What is the Getting Started card on GO's Home?
entries.a: New accounts see three steps above Qortino on Home: get your first 2 QORT, register your name, and load your avatar. GO moves on when a step is done and says "All set" at the end; then you can build your workspace there.

entries.q: How do I get my first QORT in GO?
entries.a:
The Getting Started card on Home offers three ways to get your first 2 QORT:
Finish the onboarding on qortal.dev (Go to onboarding).
Ask for 2 QORT in the support chat (Open support chat).
Buy QORT with Q-Trade (Open Q-Trade).
A little QORT pays for fees and for registering your name.

entries.q: What are hotkeys on GO's Home?
entries.a: Hotkeys are six shortcut slots in the window above Qortino on Home. Each holds a Q-App that opens with one tap. They are saved automatically for your account.

entries.q: How do I add or change a hotkey in GO?
entries.a: Tap Add app on an empty slot, or the slider button in the Hotkeys header, to open Select hotkeys. Pick a slot, then search Q-Apps or choose one from Recommended. To empty a slot, use its clear button.

entries.q: Which apps does GO recommend for hotkeys?
entries.a: The Recommended list in Select hotkeys includes Q-Tube, Torq, Q-Blog, Q-Trade and Ear-Bump. For files and mail, search for the stable Q-Share and Q-Mail and put them in a slot. Any other Q-App can be found with the search too.

entries.q: What can I put in the panel above Qortino on GO's Home?
entries.a: Tap + in the empty panel to choose a module: Hotkeys (six app shortcuts), Music player (a small EarBump player with search) or Suggest a module, which opens the GO 3.0 group so you can ask for new ones. The × on a panel clears it; your hotkeys stay saved.

entries.q: How do I use the music player on GO's Home?
entries.a: Choose Music player in the panel above Qortino. Search EarBump for a track or artist, press play, and it drops into the player. Your node prepares the track first, so it can take a moment, longer when few peers have it.

entries.q: What is the Qortino card on GO's Home?
entries.a: Qortino is the character under your hotkeys on Home. Tap him to open Qortino AI, GO's offline helper, and ask anything. To hide him, turn off Qortino AI in Settings → Profile → On Home; your hotkeys stay.

entries.q: How do I post to Torq from GO's Home?
entries.a:
1. In the Post to Torq window, tap Compose.
2. Write your post and add images, GIFs, a poll, a video or files if you like.
3. Tap Publish and confirm the fee.
You need a registered Qortal name, and a node that takes uploads: your own node, since the public node doesn't. When it is published, open latest post shows it in Torq.

entries.q: What can a Torq post from GO's Home include?
aliases: how many images torq post go
entries.a: Formatted text (bold, italic, underline, lists), up to 10 images, up to 4 GIFs, a poll with 2 to 6 choices, one video, and files or audio under 2 GB each. GO keeps the post itself under 5 MB, shrinking images to fit, because Quitter, which shares Torq's data, does not show bigger posts; if it still doesn't fit, it asks you to remove an image.

entries.q: Can I add a poll when I post from GO's Home?
entries.a: Yes. In the Post to Torq composer, tap add poll and type 2 to 6 choices of up to 80 characters; people pick one. Turn on anonymous poll to encrypt the votes: people then see anonymous votes, counts and percentages. Polls only publish on Torq, not Quitter.

entries.q: How do I post a video from GO's Home?
entries.a: Tap add video in the Post to Torq composer and pick a compression: High quality (720p), Medium (480p) or Max (360p, smallest). Give it a title, a category and a thumbnail, because the video is also published for Q-Tube. You can tap Publish while it still compresses; most of the video uploads meanwhile.

entries.q: Why do I need a registered name to post from GO?
aliases: register a qortal name to publish
entries.a: Posts are published on QDN under a registered Qortal name, so the composer asks you to register one first ("Register a Qortal name to publish on Torq"). Register it in Settings → Profile or with Getting Started on Home, then post.

entries.q: How do I switch GO's Home composer between Torq and Quitter?
entries.a: Open the composer with Compose and use the "publish to" switch at its top. Torq is the default, and your choice also sets Home's feed, the Featured tile and the share sheet entry. Quitter takes up to 2 images and no GIFs, polls or files; posts show in both apps either way, since they share the same data.

entries.q: What is the Rev button on GO's Home?
entries.a: With Torq chosen, the Post to Torq window has a Rev button above Compose. It opens Torq's own Rev editor (Revs are Torq's stories) and needs Torq 1.3 or newer. If Torq doesn't take the photo or video, update Torq, then pick it in the Rev editor.

entries.q: Do photos I post from GO show my location?
entries.a: No. GO removes the location and the camera and phone details from photos and videos you post or send. If a picture's format cannot be cleaned, GO refuses it and asks you to save it as JPEG or PNG first.

entries.q: What is the Torq Feed on GO's Home?
entries.a: It shows the newest Torq posts, without replies or reposts. General is the public feed; Following shows people you follow, once you are signed in with a registered name and follow accounts on Torq. Tap the Torq Feed title to open Torq itself.

entries.q: Does GO's Torq Feed hide the people I hid in Torq?
aliases: torq save to qdn hidden go
entries.a: Only if you saved your Torq settings to QDN. GO reads the hidden users list that Torq's Settings → Save to QDN publishes and leaves those people out of the feed. People you hid in Torq without saving to QDN still show in GO.

entries.q: What are the Featured Q-Apps on GO's Home?
entries.a: A tile grid of popular apps: Q-Tube, Torq (Quitter if you chose it), Q-Mail, SubWire, Q-Trade and Q-Chat; tap one to open it. Explore All Q-Apps opens the library. The eye button stops the moving previews (Reduce motion).

entries.q: What does the Status window on GO's Home show?
entries.a: Your QORT balance, how far your node is synced, your minter level, peers, QDN, and the Core and GO versions. Below that it shows the node you are using, with a Change node button, its type and its block height.

entries.q: How do I get back to the Q-Apps library when a Q-App is open in GO?
aliases: back to library from app go
entries.a: Tap the Apps button again: on an open app it shows the library, and on the library it brings back the app you used last. The app stays open in Tabs meanwhile.

entries.q: What are the Quick tools on GO's Home?
entries.a: A row of shortcuts: User Search, Wallets (Q-Wallets), Minting, Backup Wallet, Q-Chat, Mute or Enable Notifications, Apps and QortalLand.

entries.q: What does the Group Activity window on GO's Home show?
entries.a: The latest messages from your groups, right on Home. If you don't need it, turn it off in Settings → Profile → On Home.

entries.q: How do I open the Q-Apps library in GO?
aliases: where is the q-apps library go
entries.a: Tap the Apps button among the round buttons at the bottom, or swipe sideways to Apps. If a Q-App is open, Apps shows that app first; tap Apps again for the library. The library has six tabs: Pinned, Official apps, Community apps, Categories, My apps and + private app, and each remembers where you scrolled.

entries.q: How do I search for a Q-App in GO?
entries.a: Tap the search field in the top bar ("Search Q-Apps or enter qortal://") and type a name. Suggestions show apps and websites, each with an App or Website tag; tap one, or press the keyboard's Go key for the first.

entries.q: What are the buttons in GO's top bar?
entries.a: From left to right: the Qortal logo with a status dot (tap it for Core & settings: node details, Language, Theme and the GO version), the search field for Q-Apps, websites and qortal:// links, Tabs with the number of open tabs, and your avatar for the account menu. While a Q-App is open, tap the search field for its address with Share link, Copy link and Refresh.

entries.q: How do I make qortal.link links open in GO instead of the browser?
entries.a: Let GO open them: in Android Settings → Apps → GO 3.0 → Open by default, turn on the Qortal links GO lists there, the qortal.link gateway and its subdomains such as hub.qortal.link, go.qortal.link and ext-node.qortal.link. GO then turns such a link into the matching qortal:// page.

entries.q: What do Open and Download mean in GO's Q-Apps library?
entries.a: They show what your node has right now. Open means the node already holds the app, so it opens at once. Download means the node still has to fetch it from peers; while it does, the button shows the progress in percent. GO asks the node live for the apps on screen, because the node's own list can be out of date.

entries.q: How are Q-Apps sorted in GO's library?
entries.a: By highest rated, which weighs the stars by how many votes an app has, so a single 5-star vote does not beat many good ones; apps without ratings come last. In Community apps you can sort by alphabetical, newest, oldest, most reviewed or recently updated instead, and filter by category and by installed or not installed.

entries.q: What do the gold stars in GO's Q-Apps library mean?
entries.a: They mark the Featured apps: the 10 best-rated apps of Community apps and of each category, counting only apps with at least 2 votes. The stars show each app's score and how many votes it has. Official apps has its own Featured row too.

entries.q: How do I rate a Q-App in GO?
entries.a: Open the app's page from the library and tap a star under Rate this app. You need a registered name. The first rating of an app creates a poll on the blockchain (a small fee), later ratings vote in it, and you can't give the same rating twice. Changes show after a couple of minutes.

entries.q: What is the Official apps tab in GO's library?
entries.a: It lists Qortal's official Q-Apps, such as Q-Tube, Q-Mail, Q-Trade, Q-Wallets, Q-Blog, Q-Share, Names, Q-Mintership, Q-Search and Q-Support, with a Featured row of the best-rated ones at the top.

entries.q: What is the Community apps tab in GO's library?
entries.a: It holds every other Q-App published on QDN, as a compact list under Community apps (N), the number of apps. A Featured row of the ten best-rated sits on top while no filter is on. Use the category, status and sort filters to narrow the list.

entries.q: How do I browse Q-Apps by category in GO?
entries.a: Open Categories in the library and tap one. Its page lists the category's apps with their own search, and a Featured row when some of them have at least 2 votes. Back returns you to where you were.

entries.q: What does a Q-App's info page in GO show?
entries.a: Tap an app in the library (not its button) to see who published it, About, its rating with Rate this app, and Details: category, service, tags, size, whether it is ready on your node, and when it was published and updated. On phones the page also has Pin to Tabs.

entries.q: How do I pin a Q-App in GO?
entries.a: Tap the pin icon on the app in the library, or Pin to Tabs on its info page. GO adds it to a Library folder in Tabs, which also shows in the library's Pinned tab. Tap the pin again (Unpin from Tabs) to take it out.

entries.q: What is the Pinned tab in GO's library?
entries.a: It is your home screen for apps: your Tabs folders laid out as a grid, the same folders as in the Tabs window. A folder can be small or large; a large one shows its apps so you can tap them directly. Open tabs below lists what is running. Tap the pin on any app in the library to add it here.

entries.q: How do I make and manage folders in GO's Pinned tab?
entries.a: Tap New folder to add one. Long-press a folder for Open, Rename folder, Small or Large folder and Delete folder (GO asks first; open tabs stay open), or hold and drag it to a new place. Inside an open folder, hold an app to move it; drag it off the folder to close the folder, then drop the app on another one.

entries.q: How do I rename a tab or change its address in GO?
entries.a: In the Tabs window, long-press the tab and tap Tab options; in an open folder of the Pinned tab, long-press the app. The options are Rename tab, Change qortal:// address, Restore original name, Remove from folder, and the folders you can move it to (New folder & add makes one).

entries.q: How many Q-Apps can I keep open in GO?
entries.a: Up to 30 tabs of Q-Apps and websites. At 30, GO says "Maximum number of tabs reached. Close one to open another." Your open tabs come back after you restart GO.

entries.q: What is the My apps tab in GO's library?
entries.a: It lists the apps and websites you published under your registered name, with buttons to update them or to publish a new app or website. Publishing needs a registered name and your own node, and each name can have one app and one website.

entries.q: Why doesn't a long press let me move a window on GO's Home?
entries.a: Press on an empty part of the window's background and hold for a moment: buttons, links and anything else you can tap don't start a move. Once every window folds into a short strip, drag yours up or down.

entries.q: Why does a button in GO's Q-Apps library say checking the node?
entries.a: GO is asking your node right now whether it really has that app, because the node's own list can be out of date. It checks only the apps on your screen, a few at a time, so the button turns into Open or Download within moments.

entries.q: Do Q-Apps keep running when GO is in the background?
entries.a: No. Open Q-App tabs pause while GO is in the background, so they don't drain the battery, and they carry on when you come back.

entries.q: How do I reload or share the page of a Q-App in GO?
entries.a: While a Q-App is open, tap its address in the top bar. You get Share link, Copy link and Refresh; the link points to the exact page you are on, such as a single Torq post. The address window closes by itself after you use one.

entries.q: I got my first QORT. Why is Getting Started still showing?
entries.a: It waits for you: once the QORT has arrived it says QORT acquired, and you press Next when you are ready to register your name. After the name and the avatar step, it says All set and the space above Qortino is yours to fill.

entries.q: Can I unlock GO without internet?
entries.a: Yes. Your fingerprint or password unlock happens on the phone, so a node that can't be reached no longer blocks it. Once in, Qortino works offline, while balances, Q-Apps and chat wait for a connection. If you are online and your private node doesn't answer, GO says its URL is invalid; fix the node or switch to the public node.

entries.q: Can a Q-App go full screen in GO?
entries.a: Yes. A Q-App can ask GO to hide its bars and fill the screen, for example for a video or a story. Press Android back to leave full screen; it also ends when you switch to another tab.

entries.q: Why is the Accept button greyed out for a moment in GO's approval window?
aliases: i have read this request go
entries.a: GO keeps Accept disabled for about a second so a stray tap can't approve anything, and for payments and signing it also wants the "I have read this request" tick. If the app sends more requests, they wait in line ("more requests are waiting") instead of replacing the open one. Screenshots are blocked while the window is open.

entries.q: How do I see an app's details from the Tabs window in GO?
entries.a: Long-press the app's card in Tabs. GO shows its description, publisher, rating and qortal:// link with Copy link, and a Tab options button for renaming, changing the address or moving it to a folder.

entries.q: How do I add an open tab to a folder in GO?
entries.a: Long-press the tab in Tabs, tap Tab options and pick a folder, or New folder & add to make one. In the library, the pin icon puts an app in the Library folder.

entries.q: What is the Tabs window in GO?
entries.a: Tabs shows every Q-App and website you have open as cards with a picture of each page, like a browser's tab switcher, together with your folders. Tap a card to switch to it, × to close it, or Close all. The Tabs button in the top bar opens it and shows how many tabs are open.

entries.q: How do I open Tabs in GO?
entries.a: Tap Tabs in the top bar, next to your avatar. On Home, the Q-Apps library and the chat lists you can also pull down from the top of the page: let go past about a third of the way, or flick down, and Tabs stays open.

entries.q: How do I close the Tabs window in GO?
entries.a: Slide it up. On the list of tabs a short swipe scrolls them and a long one closes the window; a swipe on the header, the folder row or the bottom handle closes it at once. Android back closes it too. Tabs always reopens on all tabs, not inside a folder.

entries.q: How do I close a Q-App in GO?
entries.a: Open Tabs and tap × on the app's card, or Close all to close every tab. The library's Pinned tab also lists Open tabs with a close button.

entries.q: Why does Tabs show one card for several windows of the same app?
aliases: same app windows one card go
entries.a: When an app is open in more than one window, Tabs groups them into one card with a small avatar for each window underneath. Tap an avatar to show that window's picture, tap the card to switch to it; × closes only the window shown.

entries.q: Can I open the same Q-App twice in GO?
entries.a: Yes. Tapping an app's icon in a Pinned or Tabs folder opens it again in a new window, even when it is already open. Its card in Tabs still switches to the window that is open.

entries.q: Are the page pictures in GO's Tabs saved anywhere?
aliases: does go save screenshots of apps
entries.a: No. GO takes the picture for each Tabs card itself and keeps it in memory only; it is never written to storage. No picture is taken while a protected screen, such as an approval or your seed phrase, is showing.

entries.q: What does edit mode in GO's Tabs window do?
entries.a: Tap the edit button in Tabs to arrange things: drag apps onto folders, tap × to take an app out, or drag folders to reorder them. Inside a folder, drag apps to reorder them or tap × to remove them. Tap the button again when you are done.

entries.q: What does Import Hub dashboard in GO's Tabs do?
aliases: bring hub pinned apps to phone
entries.a: It reads the pinned apps your Hub saved to QDN for this account and puts them into a folder named Hub in Tabs, replacing that folder if it already exists. It works one way: changes you make in GO don't go back to Hub.

entries.q: What happens when I delete a folder in GO?
entries.a: GO asks first. Deleting removes the folder and the apps saved in it from Tabs and the Pinned tab; tabs that are open stay open.

entries.q: What is the widgets screen in GO?
entries.a: It is a screen to the left of Home (swipe right from Home) for widgets: small Q-Apps made for GO, such as a clock, the weather or news. It is on by default; turn it off in Settings → System → Widgets screen. While it is empty it shows just a round + to add one.

entries.q: How do I add a widget in GO?
entries.a: Swipe right from Home to the widgets screen and tap + (or Add widget while arranging). The list shows widgets published on QDN and who made them; search it and tap one to add it. You can have up to 12 widgets.

entries.q: How do I move, resize or remove a widget in GO?
entries.a: Hold a widget, or an empty spot, to start arranging. Drag a widget to move it; the others make room, and widgets of the same size swap. Drag its corner to resize it. Drop it on Remove at the bottom, or tap ×, to take it away. Tap Done when you are finished.

entries.q: What happens when I tap a widget while arranging the widgets screen?
entries.a: It opens the widget's menu: Open <app> opens the full Q-App in Apps, Reload reloads the widget, and Remove takes it off the screen. Outside arranging, a tap goes to the widget itself.

entries.q: Can a GO widget spend my QORT or post for me?
entries.a: No. Widgets can show things and open apps, but they can't pay, publish, sign, decrypt, save files, send notifications or go full screen. For anything like that a widget can only open its full Q-App, where GO asks you as it does for any app.

entries.q: Where do GO widgets come from?
entries.a: Anyone can publish one: a widget is a Q-App published as an APP with the tag go-widget, or with an identifier starting with go-widget. GO lists every such app from QDN in Add a widget, and nothing runs until you add it.

entries.q: Why don't sideways swipes reach my GO widget?
entries.a: Sideways swipes belong to GO: they move between the widgets screen, Home, Apps and Chat. A long press belongs to GO too, and picks the widget up to arrange it. Taps, typing and scrolling up and down go to the widget.

entries.q: Why does a widget reload when I come back to the widgets screen?
entries.a: To save battery and memory, GO loads widgets the first time you open the widgets screen and unloads them about 3 minutes after you last saw it. They load again when you come back.

entries.q: How do I switch between Home, Apps and Chat in GO?
aliases: switch sections home apps chat go
go bottom buttons home apps chat
entries.a: Tap the round Home, Apps and Chat buttons at the bottom, or swipe sideways: the next section slides in like a page, with its real content, and each section keeps where you had scrolled. Inside a Q-App, swipe along the round buttons instead, since the app keeps its own swipes.

entries.q: What are the round buttons at the bottom of GO?
entries.a: They are GO's three sections, Home, Apps and Chat, shown as round glass buttons with icons. With immersive mode on, Home, Chat and the library scroll on behind them; with it off, and always in a Q-App or website, the page ends above them so they never cover an app's own menu.

entries.q: What is immersive mode in GO?
entries.a: Immersive mode hides the top bar, the bottom buttons and Android's status bar so Q-Apps and websites fill the screen; Home, Chat and the Q-Apps library keep their bars. Choose Off, Auto or Manual in Settings → System → Immersive mode. New installs start on Auto.

entries.q: What is the difference between Off, Auto and Manual immersive mode?
entries.a: Off: the top and bottom bars always show. Auto: in a Q-App the bars slide away when you scroll down and come back when you scroll up. Manual: the bars stay hidden, and a small floating button shows them for a few seconds.

entries.q: How does the floating button in Manual immersive mode work?
entries.a: Tap it to bring the bars back for about 4 seconds; using the bars keeps them out longer, and a tap on the content puts them away. Drag the button along either edge to move it out of the way. It fades when left alone and shows a dot for new chats or bell items.

entries.q: Why does the strip around the camera change colour in GO?
entries.a: With immersive mode on, GO paints the strip around the camera in the page's own background colour, so it blends into each Q-App or website. When a photo or video fills the width, it takes the colour right under the strip, or black, never a colour from the picture.

entries.q: Does immersive mode cover parts of a Q-App?
entries.a: No. Q-Apps and websites are resized to fit, once per change, and never sit under a bar. Content also stays clear of the camera cut-out.

entries.q: Why does Qortino refuse some questions?
entries.a: Qortino won't help with weapons, explosives, poisons or hurting people, or with anything that targets children. It declines in one sentence and offers a safe alternative instead.

entries.q: What does Reduce UI Animations do in GO?
entries.a: Settings → System → Reduce UI Animations cuts down motion throughout GO; leave it off for the normal animated look. On Home, the eye button on Featured Q-Apps stops just its moving previews.

entries.q: How do I switch GO between dark and light theme?
entries.a: Tap the Qortal logo at the top left to open Core & settings, then tap Theme to switch between dark and light. Before you log in, the sun or moon button at the bottom right of the Enter Qortal screen does the same.

entries.q: Why does a GO widget ask to see my account?
entries.a: Some widgets show your own data, so they may ask for your account or your balance the way any Q-App does, and GO asks you first. Widgets may only ask while the widgets screen is showing, and you can decline.

entries.q: Why does GO's top bar look see-through in some Q-Apps?
entries.a: With immersive mode on, the top bar takes the Q-App's own background colour while it shows, so the search field, Tabs and your avatar float on the app. On a light page the controls switch so they stay readable.

entries.q: Does GO write my data to Android's system log?
entries.a: No. Published GO builds are release builds: debug tools can't attach to GO, and it doesn't write debug data to the phone's system log. A problem report only leaves the phone when you copy or save it yourself.

entries.q: Why doesn't GO's Settings have Developer, Help and Reticulum tabs?
entries.a: Those tabs hold desktop Hub options that did nothing on a phone, so GO hides them and keeps Profile, Security, Blocked and System. GO's own phone options, Dev Mode included, are in System.

entries.q: Which GO entries appear in Android's share sheet?
entries.a: For photos and videos: Torq, which opens Home's Post to Torq composer with them, and Torq Rev, which opens Torq's Rev editor with one photo or video. For any file, link or text: GO Groups, GO DMs and GO Self-DM, which put it into a chat. If you chose Quitter on Home, a Quitter entry replaces the Torq ones.

entries.q: How do I change the language in Qortal GO?
entries.a: Tap the Qortal logo at the top left to open Core & settings and tap Language; before you log in, use the globe button at the bottom right of the Enter Qortal screen. GO comes in 12 languages: English, Arabic, German, Spanish, Estonian, Finnish, French, Italian, Japanese, Portuguese, Russian and Chinese.

entries.q: Does GO follow my phone's language?
entries.a: No. GO starts in English and then keeps the language you pick in Core & settings or on the Enter Qortal screen, whatever your phone is set to.

entries.q: How do I update GO if the Updates screen can't reach QDN?
aliases: install new go apk over old
entries.a: Download the newest APK from qortal.dev → Downloads → Android, or from the GO-3.0 releases on Qortal's Gitea, and install it over your GO. It is signed with the same key, so your accounts and chats stay. This works only for a newer version: Android won't put an older one over a newer one.

entries.q: What do New, Installed and Older mean in GO 3.0 Updates?
aliases: some versions could not be loaded
entries.a: In Versions on QDN, Installed marks the build on your phone, New a newer build you can install, and Older a build you can only open in Q-Share. If some versions could not be loaded yet, GO could not fetch their details from QDN; check again later.

entries.q: How do I open a post or load new posts in GO's Torq Feed?
aliases: open post from go home feed
entries.a: Tap a post to open it in Torq. When newer posts arrive, the feed shows a button such as "3 new posts"; tap it to put them at the top. Show more opens up a long post right in the feed.

entries.q: Can a Q-App use my camera, microphone or location in GO?
aliases: can apps track my location go
entries.a: No. GO gives the camera and microphone only to its own screens, the QR scanner and calls, and refuses location to everyone, since GO never uses it.

entries.q: Are my tabs, folders and hotkeys separate for each account in GO?
entries.a: Yes. Tabs folders, hotkeys and the open tabs GO brings back after a restart are kept for each account on this phone, so another account shows its own set. The Home order and screen options such as bottom buttons, immersive mode and widgets apply to the whole phone.

entries.q: Do GO widgets follow my theme and language?
entries.a: GO tells each widget its dark or light theme and its language, and tells it again when you change them, so widgets made for GO can follow along. How a widget looks beyond that is up to its maker.

entries.q: Does GO have widgets for my Android home screen?
aliases: go widget on phone home screen
entries.a: No. GO's widgets live on its own widgets screen inside GO: swipe right from Home to reach them.

entries.q: Why are Qortino's answers usually short?
entries.a: By design: Qortino keeps everyday answers short and gives step-by-step detail for health, safety and survival, or when you ask for it. Ask for more detail and it explains further. It uses metric units, numbered steps for instructions and bullets for lists.

entries.q: Does GO have a guided tour like Qortal Hub?
entries.a: No. The Hub tutorial is only available on desktop. In GO, new accounts get the Getting Started steps on Home instead: get your first 2 QORT, register your name and load your avatar.

entries.q: How do I open QortalLand in GO?
entries.a: Tap QortalLand in Quick tools on Home. QortalLand is Q-Chat's shared social space, where you meet other members, use moods and proximity voice, and challenge people to Chess, Checkers or Qonnect Four.

entries.q: How do I open Qortino in GO?
entries.a: On Home, tap Qortino, the character under your hotkeys. If you don't see him, turn on Qortino AI in Settings → Profile → On Home. The first time, Qortino asks you to assemble his model.

entries.q: How do I download Qortino's model?
entries.a:
1. Open Qortino on Home and tap Assemble Qortino.
2. GO finds the model on QDN, the node fetches each part, and GO saves and checks them on the phone; the progress shows each step.
3. Tap Minimize to use GO meanwhile: the progress shows in GO's notifications and the Android notification bar.
It is a one-time download of about 2.5 GB (GO shows 2.3 GB). Your own node is highly recommended: the public node is not reliable for a download this big.

entries.q: Do I need a private node every time I use Qortino?
aliases: switch back to public node qortino
entries.a: No, not even to download it, but for the download it is highly recommended: the public node is not reliable for a file this big. Once the model is on the phone, Qortino runs offline: it works on any node, or with no internet at all.

entries.q: Does Qortino send my questions anywhere?
entries.a: No. Qortino runs entirely on your phone, with no cloud: your questions and answers are never sent anywhere. The one exception is a report you choose to send with the report button, which goes out as a Q-Mail.

entries.q: How can I check that Qortino's model is genuine?
aliases: where does qortino model come from
entries.a: Qortino's model is Qwen3 4B Instruct 2507 (Apache-2.0 licence), built straight from the official Qwen weights with nothing added and published with Q-Share under the name Qortino AI. It comes in 2 parts because QDN takes at most 2 GB per file. GO checks each part's SHA-256 checksum after download and deletes a part that doesn't match, and anyone can rebuild the parts and compare the checksums.

entries.q: Where are my Qortino chats saved?
entries.a: On your phone only. Tap the history button at the top of Qortino to see your chats: start a New chat, or pin, rename or delete one. Uninstalling GO deletes them too.

entries.q: How do I copy or stop a Qortino answer?
entries.a: While Qortino writes, the send button becomes Stop: tap it to end the answer. Under a finished answer, the copy button copies the whole answer. If an answer was cut short, Continue answer lets Qortino carry on.

entries.q: Can I rely on Qortino in a medical emergency?
entries.a: Use it as a calm helper, not as a doctor. For a life-threatening emergency Qortino first tells you to call emergency services if phones work (112 in Europe, 911 in North America), then gives hands-on first aid steps and the warning signs that need a doctor. It gives no prescription doses, and it can be confidently wrong, so check anything important.

entries.q: Can Qortino look things up on the internet or QDN?
entries.a: No. Qortino answers offline only, from its own model and its curated answers; it does not search QDN or the web, and it never sends you to websites. For anything live, open the Q-App that holds it.

entries.q: What are the links and app cards under some Qortino answers?
entries.a: For Qortal questions, Qortino adds Qortal links and app cards under the answer, each showing the service and who published it, with an Open button that starts that Q-App or website in GO. Answers on other topics don't get them.

entries.q: What happens when I report a Qortino answer?
entries.a: The Teach Qortino window asks what went wrong and how Qortino should answer next time. GO then sends your note, with the question and the answer, as a private Q-Mail to the name Qortino AI (subject "Teaching Qortino AI"). That is a QDN publish, so it costs a small fee and needs your own node. The reports help improve the answers Qortino ships with.

entries.q: Is Qortino available in my language?
entries.a: Qortino's buttons and messages follow GO's language, in all 12 of GO's languages. Its ready-made answers to common Qortal questions are written in English.

entries.q: Does Qortino remember what I said earlier in a chat?
entries.a: Yes, within the same chat: follow-up questions use the conversation so far. In a long chat it drops the oldest turns to make room. Start a New chat from the history button for a fresh topic.

entries.q: Does Qortino cost anything?
entries.a: No. Assembling the model and asking questions are free, with nothing charged per question. The only fee is the small QDN publish fee if you send a report about an answer.

entries.q: What does Reading your question mean in Qortino?
entries.a: Before it writes, Qortino reads your question and the chat so far, and shows how far it has got in percent. A long first question or a long chat takes longest; later questions start faster because it reuses what it already read.

entries.q: What does Fully operational mean in GO's Status window?
entries.a: It means GO reaches your node and the node is synced. Not operational means the node isn't answering or is still syncing; the line below shows how far it has synced, or Node unavailable. Peers counts the node's connections, QDN its data peers, and Node Height its latest block.

entries.q: Why does GO show Unnamed account in my account list?
aliases: name my account in go list
entries.a: The account has no registered name yet, and you haven't given it a label. On the Enter Qortal screen, open it and tap the edit button: in Account details you can give it a name and a note to tell it apart in the list.

entries.q: How do I open a Q-App in GO?
entries.a: Tap Apps for the library and tap Open on an app (Download first if your node doesn't have it yet), search for it in the top bar, or tap a hotkey or a Featured Q-Apps tile on Home. It opens in a tab, and Tabs shows everything you have open.

entries.q: Why does Select hotkeys say Q-Apps unavailable?
aliases: unable to load q-apps right now
entries.a: GO could not load the list of Q-Apps from your node just then. Check the node connection (the dot on the Qortal logo) and open Select hotkeys again. "No Q-Apps match yet" only means your search found nothing; try another app name.

entries.q: Why won't a track play in GO's Home music player?
entries.a: Tracks play from QDN, so your node first gathers the track from peers. "No peers for remaining data" means no peer is sending the rest right now; try again later or pick another track. If playback stalls, press play to retry, and GO rebuilds the stream by itself when a track stalls.

entries.q: Why does GO's Torq Feed say Feed load failed?
entries.a: GO could not load the posts from your node in time. Tap Try Again, or Return to General for the public feed. The Following feed needs a registered name and accounts you follow, so it can stay empty while the General feed works.

entries.q: Can I use GO while Qortino's model downloads?
entries.a: Yes. Tap Minimize: the download carries on, and its progress shows in GO's notifications (the bell) and in the Android notification bar. Tap the Qortino row in the bell to open it again. If GO closes half way, the download carries on after you sign in again.

entries.q: How much RAM does Qortal Core need?
aliases: how much memory for a qortal node
entries.a: Qortal Core's own notes say as little as 4 GB of RAM is acceptable in most cases, and its start script is tuned for machines with 6 GB or more. Core only uses as much memory as it needs, up to a share of the RAM set in start.sh (50% by default). On a machine with less than 6 GB, the script suggests raising that 50 to 75. For a Raspberry Pi, the Qortal wiki recommends the 8 GB model.

entries.q: Is a 4 GB Raspberry Pi enough for a Qortal node?
entries.a: It works, but 8 GB is recommended. The Qortal wiki's Raspberry Pi guide says a 4 GB Pi 4 or Pi 5 will work and recommends the 8 GB model. On a machine with less than 6 GB of RAM, Core's start script suggests letting Java use 75% of the RAM instead of 50%.

entries.q: Should I get a Raspberry Pi 4 or a Pi 5 for a Qortal node?
aliases: best raspberry pi for a qortal node
entries.a: Both work, and the Qortal wiki gives the same advice for each: 8 GB of RAM (4 GB works), a power supply, a case with a fan, and a USB 3.0 SSD of 500 GB or more. The wiki also lists community Qortal OS images for both boards (RaspiPHENIX for the Pi 4, Ra5piPHENIX for the Pi 5). Pick the one you can get and keep running all the time.

entries.q: Do I need a fan on my Raspberry Pi node?
aliases: case with fan for qortal pi
entries.a: Yes. The Qortal wiki lists a case with a fan for every Raspberry Pi node and says the fan is important. The QORTector guide goes further: do not run the device if the fan isn't spinning after you power it on, because the board can overheat.

entries.q: Can I run a Qortal node from a microSD card?
aliases: sd card or ssd for qortal
entries.a: It works, but an SSD is recommended. The Qortal wiki says a 128 GB microSD card will work in a Pi 4 or Pi 5, and recommends a USB 3.0 SSD of 500 GB or more instead. You can write the Qortal OS image straight to the SSD with Balena Etcher and start the Pi from it.

entries.q: What size SSD should I buy for a Qortal node?
aliases: how big an ssd for a qortal node
ssd for raspberry pi qortal node
entries.a: For a Raspberry Pi node the Qortal wiki recommends a USB 3.0 SSD of 500 GB or more, plugged into one of the Pi's blue USB 3.0 ports, and the QORTector comes with a 500 GB SSD. The wiki's general guide gives about 50 GB as the starting need, and says you will likely need more once you use QDN, because your node keeps copies of the sites and apps you open and the names you follow.

entries.q: Why doesn't Wi-Fi work on my QORTector?
entries.a: Set your country first: the QORTector's Wi-Fi and time zone follow its locale, and the default is USA, Pacific time. Run sudo raspi-config, open Localisation Options and set the country (and time zone), then set up Wi-Fi. A network cable is still the recommended connection for a node.

entries.q: Does my router need UPnP for a Qortal node?
aliases: do i need upnp for qortal core
entries.a: It helps but isn't required. If your router has UPnP turned on, a single node gets incoming connections with no setup. Without UPnP, give the node a fixed address on your network (static assignment, usually under the router's DHCP settings) and forward port 12392 (blockchain peers) and 12394 (QDN data peers) to it.

entries.q: Should I put my Qortal node in the router's DMZ?
aliases: dmz instead of port forwarding qortal
is dmz safe for a qortal node
entries.a: No. The Qortal wiki warns never to put a node in the DMZ: it skips the router's firewall checks, so all internet traffic can reach that computer directly, which is a real risk if the node's API is opened up. Use UPnP or normal port forwarding instead.

entries.q: Can I run two Qortal nodes on the same home network?
entries.a: Yes. With UPnP, the first node works as it is; for each extra node, set a different listenPort and listenDataPort in its settings.json (for example 22392 and 22394). Without UPnP, leave the ports alone and forward a different external port to each node's 12392 and 12394. A second node doesn't earn more QORT, but it keeps your account synced and minting if one machine has trouble.

entries.q: Can I run a Qortal node on a limited data plan?
entries.a: It can be hard: the Minter Guide warns that a 24/7 node may use well over 1 TB a month and recommends unlimited plans. To cut usage, the Qortal wiki suggests "maxPeers": 7 in settings.json first, since peers use the most data. For tighter plans you can also turn off relay mode ("relayModeEnabled": false) and, on a minting-only machine, QDN ("qdnEnabled": false), which means no websites or Q-Apps through that node. Stop Core before editing settings.json.

entries.q: Can my Qortal node computer go to sleep?
aliases: does qortal core run while computer sleeps
entries.a: No. Core stops while the computer sleeps, so the node falls out of sync and stops minting. Turn off sleep in the power settings of any machine you use as a node. Hub doesn't need to stay open, but Core must keep running.

entries.q: Does my Qortal node need to run 24/7?
aliases: turn off qortal node at night
entries.a: It's recommended, not required. A node that was off has to catch up on the blocks it missed before you can use it, and it only mints while it's online and synced. There's no other penalty. That's why many people keep a small, low-power machine such as a Raspberry Pi running as their node.

entries.q: How much power does a Raspberry Pi Qortal node use?
entries.a: Very little. The Qortal wiki says a Pi-based node or QORTector uses about 5 W, about the same as leaving a phone charging all day, and far less than most computers. Minting needs no extra power, because Qortal has no mining race.

entries.q: What happens if my Qortal node loses power suddenly?
aliases: qortal database corrupted after power loss
pulled the plug on qortal pi
entries.a: Cutting power while Core is running can damage its database. The Qortal wiki says to always stop Core first, then shut the machine down, and only then switch it off. If the database does get damaged, a bootstrap rebuilds the chain data; your wallet is stored separately. A UPS gives the node time to shut down cleanly in a blackout.

entries.q: How do I shut down a Raspberry Pi Qortal node safely?
entries.a:
Stop Core first, then the Pi:
1. Cancel any open trades in the Trade Portal.
2. In a terminal: cd qortal, then ./stop.sh, and wait for "Qortal ended gracefully".
3. Shut down with sudo shutdown (or restart with sudo reboot).
4. Switch the power off only after the Pi has powered down. The QORTector guide says not to use the power switch to turn it off.

entries.q: Can I run a Qortal node on solar power?
entries.a: Yes, a small node is one of the easier loads to run that way: the Qortal wiki says a Pi-based node draws about 5 W, about like a phone charging. Size the battery for nights and cloudy days, and avoid sudden power loss, because Core should be stopped cleanly or its database can be damaged. The node also still needs a network connection to stay in sync.

entries.q: Can I run a Qortal node without a monitor?
aliases: run qortal node without a screen
entries.a: Yes. A QORTector starts Core in the background on its own, with or without a monitor, and any node can run headless once Core is set to start by itself. You can reach the machine from another computer over SSH or remote desktop (RDP, or VNC on some images), and use Hub on your main computer with the node added under Choose custom node. On a QORTector, plug in HDMI before powering on if you do want a screen.

entries.q: Can I use an old PC as a Qortal node?
entries.a: Usually, yes. Qortal Core runs on any machine with Java 11 or newer, on Linux, Windows or macOS, and its notes say as little as 4 GB of RAM is acceptable in most cases. Give it an SSD with room to grow, turn off sleep, and keep it running. For Windows the Qortal wiki suggests more: a quad-core CPU, 8 GB of RAM and at least 50 GB free for the database.

entries.q: Do minting and non-minting nodes need different hardware?
aliases: minting node vs normal node hardware
does minting need a better computer
entries.a: No. The Qortal wiki says minting and non-minting nodes need the same hardware. A faster machine earns nothing extra; what counts is that the node stays online and synced.

entries.q: Can I run Qortal Core on an Android phone?
aliases: run qortal node on android phone
entries.a: It's possible but not recommended. The Qortal wiki has a Termux guide and warns it is not for the average user: a phone node uses a lot of resources, could damage the phone, and has to stay at home on steady Wi-Fi and power. Qortal GO doesn't run Core itself; it connects to a node, your own or a public one.

entries.q: Can I run a Qortal node on a VPS?
aliases: qortal node on a cloud server
entries.a: Yes. The Qortal wiki has a VPS page with a Linux install: install Java, unzip the qortal.zip release, and start Core as a normal user (its start script refuses to run as root). The settings shipped with Core let any address reach its API (port 12391), so on a VPS keep that port closed in the firewall or turn on apiWhitelist; sensitive calls still need the API key.

entries.q: What hardware does a Qortal gateway node need?
entries.a: Not much: the Qortal wiki's gateway guide says even a Raspberry Pi 4 with 4 GB of RAM can work. What a gateway really needs is a public IP address with ports 80 and 443 forwarded to it (a static IP is preferred; dynamic DNS also works) and unlimited or high-cap data, because everyone who opens a site through it uses your connection. Anything people open through your gateway is stored on your node.

entries.q: Can Qortal Hub run on a Raspberry Pi?
entries.a: Yes. The Qortal Hub release page has a Linux arm64 AppImage next to the x86 Linux, Windows and macOS builds, so it runs on a Pi with a 64-bit OS. Qortal Core runs on the Pi too, since it only needs Java 11 or newer.

entries.q: Which computers can run Qortal Hub?
entries.a: Qortal Hub has builds for 64-bit Windows, macOS, Linux on x86 (AppImage or .deb) and Linux on arm64 (an AppImage, for example for a Raspberry Pi). On an Android phone, use Qortal GO instead.

entries.q: Do I need a 64-bit OS on my Raspberry Pi for Qortal?
entries.a: Use a 64-bit OS. The Qortal OS images on the wiki are full 64-bit (ARM64), which the wiki notes is what lets them support ARRR, and the Hub build for the Pi is an arm64 AppImage.

entries.q: What is inside a QORTector?
entries.a: A QORTector is a ready-made Qortal node on a Raspberry Pi with a custom Qortal OS. The Gen 2 uses a Raspberry Pi 4 with 8 GB of RAM and a 500 GB SSD; the QORTector KB uses a Raspberry Pi 400 keyboard computer with 4 GB of RAM and a 500 GB Samsung T7 SSD. Gen 3 comes with a keyboard and mouse. The first QORTector used an Orange Pi board that couldn't run a full node, and that board was discontinued.

entries.q: Where can I get a QORTector?
entries.a: Pre-built QORTectors are sold on crowetic.com by Crowetic Hardware Development, a third-party company set up by Qortal founders. You can also build your own: the Qortal wiki has the Raspberry Pi guide, community Qortal OS images, and 3D printing files for a case that holds a Pi 4, a Samsung T7 SSD and a 40 mm Noctua fan.

entries.q: What should I do first on a new QORTector?
entries.a:
1. Plug in the monitor (HDMI before power), keyboard, mouse, Ethernet and power.
2. Set your country and time zone under Localisation Options in sudo raspi-config. Do this before changing the password, or you could lock yourself out.
3. Change the default password with passwd.
4. Let Core sync, then add your account and save a backup file.
5. Set up port forwarding if you can.

entries.q: Why should I change the password on a Qortal Pi image?
entries.a: Every QORTector and community Qortal OS image starts with the same default password, and it is printed in the public wiki guides. The images can be reached over SSH or remote desktop, so change it as soon as the device is set up: type passwd in a terminal. On a QORTector, set your locale first.

entries.q: Why does my QORTector show nothing on the monitor?
entries.a: Connect the HDMI cable before you power the device on; the QORTector guide says it won't show a picture otherwise. If you need to unplug HDMI, power the device off first. Core keeps running in the background either way.

entries.q: Why does my Qortal Pi only use 32 GB of my SSD?
aliases: ssd space after flashing qortal image
entries.a: The image's partition is 32 GB or less, so it has to be expanded after flashing. Run sudo raspi-config, choose Advanced Options, then Expand Filesystem, and reboot. After that the node can use the whole drive.

entries.q: Can I keep Qortal's blockchain database on another drive?
entries.a: Yes. Stop Core, then set "repositoryPath" in Core's settings.json to a folder on that drive; by default the database is the db folder next to settings.json. On Windows the wiki's example is "repositoryPath":"D://db". Core finds the database there, or creates one if the folder is empty. QDN data has its own setting, dataPath.

entries.q: Can an older Raspberry Pi run a Qortal node?
entries.a: The Qortal wiki's guides and images cover the Pi 4, the Pi 400 and the Pi 5, with 4 GB of RAM as the working minimum. Older boards aren't covered, and the first QORTector, on a weaker Orange Pi board, couldn't run a full node. A Pi 4 or Pi 5 with 8 GB is the safe choice.

entries.q: Does a Qortal node need a powerful CPU?
aliases: how many cpu cores for qortal
entries.a: No. The Minter Guide asks for at least a dual-core CPU and recommends quad-core or better, and Core runs on Raspberry Pi-class processors. Its start script runs Core at the lowest CPU priority so it doesn't slow your other programs, and no graphics card is needed, since Qortal has no mining.

entries.q: Can a Raspberry Pi 400 run a Qortal node?
entries.a: Yes. The QORTector KB is a Pi 400 with 4 GB of RAM and a 500 GB Samsung T7 SSD. The wiki's torchieMATE image works on it (the newer RaspiPHENIX image is for Pi 4 boards only).

entries.q: Does Qortal GO work on 32-bit phones?
aliases: go app wont install old phone
entries.a: No. GO only contains native code for 64-bit ARM phones (arm64-v8a), plus x86_64 for emulators, because its Reticulum engine and Qortino run as native code. A phone that only runs 32-bit Android can't install it.

entries.q: Does my phone need NFC to use Qortal GO?
aliases: phone with no nfc qortal go
is nfc required for qortal go
entries.a: No. NFC is only used by the optional Qortal Card (testing) feature, and GO installs and works on phones without it. A phone with no NFC simply can't read Qortal cards or tap other GO phones.

entries.q: Which phone should I buy for Qortal GO and Qortino?
aliases: good phone for go and qortino
entries.a: There is no official model list. Look for a recent 64-bit Android phone (Android 8.0 is the minimum, newer is better) with at least 6 GB of RAM so Qortino runs well, and a few GB of free storage for Qortino's model. Add NFC if you want to try Qortal Card. Some brands freeze apps in the background more than others, so check that the phone lets you allow GO in its battery settings.

entries.q: How much free storage does Qortino need?
entries.a: Qortino's model is one download of about 2.3 GB (as GO counts it), saved in two parts. Before it starts, GO checks for that much free space plus about 300 MB spare, so plan for roughly 2.6 GB free. If a try fails partway, parts that already arrived and passed their check are kept and don't count again.

entries.q: How much RAM does Qortino need?
entries.a: 6 GB of RAM or more is recommended. On phones with less, GO still lets you assemble Qortino but warns that answers may be slow and that Android may close it while it runs in the background. The model itself takes about 2.5 GB of memory while it runs, plus about 0.3 GB for its working memory.

entries.q: Why is Qortino slow on my phone?
entries.a: Qortino runs a 4-billion-parameter model on your phone's own processor, so its speed depends on the phone. On a recent mid-range phone with about 8 GB of RAM, GO's tests saw 3 to 5 tokens (word pieces) a second. It is slower on phones with less than 6 GB of RAM, and the first open takes longer because the model has to load into memory.

entries.q: Why does Qortino take a while to start?
entries.a: When it opens, Qortino loads its whole model into the phone's memory ("Waking Qortino up…"); on a mid-range phone that took about 12 to 15 seconds in tests. After that it stays loaded for 90 seconds when you close Qortino (45 seconds once GO is in the background), and its instructions are saved after the first read, so later opens are much quicker.

entries.q: Where does GO keep Qortino's model on my phone?
entries.a: In GO's own app folder on the phone's shared storage, in a folder called Qortino AI (under Android/data, in GO's files folder), with the two model parts in its models folder. If the phone has no shared storage available, GO uses its internal storage instead.

entries.q: Does assembling Qortino delete the old Lite and Standard packs?
entries.a: Yes. The old Lite and Standard packs can't be used any more, so assembling the new model deletes them (up to about 4 GB) and their space counts toward the new one. GO says "Qortino has a new, smarter brain" when it finds an old install.

entries.q: Does Qortino run on my phone's CPU or GPU?
entries.a: On the CPU. Qortino's engine is a CPU-only build of llama.cpp that runs on the phone's fast cores; it doesn't use the graphics chip. Once the model is assembled it needs no internet at all.

entries.q: Does Android backup move Qortal GO to my new phone?
aliases: move qortal go to a new phone
entries.a: No. GO turns off Android's cloud backup and phone-to-phone transfer for all its data, because that data holds wallet files, Reticulum keys and chat history. To move to a new phone, install GO there and restore your account from your backup file or seed phrase, so keep those safe before you reset or give away the old phone.

entries.q: Does Qortal GO work on Android 15 and 16?
entries.a: Yes. GO is built for Android 16 and is tested on it. Android 15 and newer stop some kinds of background service after about 6 hours a day; GO runs its background connection in a way that avoids that cutoff, and on battery (unless Background sync is set to Always) it pauses itself after 6 hours instead. Opening GO reconnects.

entries.q: Which phone brands freeze GO in the background?
aliases: phone brands that freeze qortal go
brands that stop go in the background
phone makers battery managers qortal go
does my phone brand freeze qortal go
entries.a: GO has its own steps for the battery managers of vivo/iQOO, Xiaomi/Redmi/POCO, Samsung, OPPO/realme/OnePlus and Huawei/Honor. Google, GrapheneOS, Motorola, Nokia and other phones get the general Android steps. vivo is the brand GO measured freezing apps when the screen turns off. Menu names can differ a little between models and Android versions.

entries.q: What is the Qortal Card in GO?
aliases: pay with a card in qortal go
entries.a: Qortal Card (testing) lets you pay and take QORT payments by tapping, with a Qortal test card or between two GO phones, over NFC. It is off until you switch it on in Settings > System; then Qortal Card shows in the avatar menu below Notifications, with three tabs: My card, Take payment and Send. Test cards have no PIN yet, so keep only a few QORT on one.

entries.q: How do I turn on Qortal Card in GO?
aliases: where is qortal card in go
entries.a: Open Settings > System and switch on Qortal Card (testing); it is there from GO v0.0.18. Qortal Card then appears in the avatar menu, just below Notifications.

entries.q: Which cards work with GO's Qortal Card?
aliases: cards that work with qortal card
entries.a: Only Qortal test cards: smart cards that carry one of the Qortal Card test applets GO knows. Other cards and tags don't work; GO says "That is not a Qortal Card" or that the card has no Qortal Card applet. You can also skip the card and pay between two GO phones.

entries.q: Can I use any NFC tag or sticker as a Qortal Card?
aliases: nfc tag as a qortal wallet
entries.a: No. A Qortal Card has a chip that keeps its key inside and signs each payment itself, never giving the key out. Ordinary NFC tags, stickers and fobs (such as NTAG or MIFARE chips) can't sign Qortal payments, so they can't work as a wallet. GO answers "That is not a Qortal Card" when you tap one.

entries.q: How do I connect a Qortal card in GO?
aliases: add a card to qortal go
entries.a:
1. Open Qortal Card from the avatar menu and go to My card.
2. Tap Connect a card and hold the card to the back of the phone; keep it still until the phone buzzes.
3. A blank card gets its own new account in the same tap, with a key GO makes from your wallet (never your main key).
If GO can't make that key, for example because the wallet is locked, you can try again or choose Make a new key on the card.

entries.q: What is the difference between Key GO can restore and Key made on the card?
aliases: wallet key vs card key qortal
which key for my qortal card
entries.a: Key GO can restore: GO makes the card's key from your wallet just for that card (never your main account's key), so GO can move the card's QORT back even without the card, and you can save a backup file. Key made on the card: only the card knows it and it never leaves the card, so there is no backup file, and if you lose the card the QORT on it is lost. The restorable key is the recommended choice.

entries.q: Is my main Qortal account key stored on the card?
aliases: does the qortal card hold my wallet
qortal card key and main account
is my seed on the qortal card
entries.a: No. Each card gets its own account and address. With a key GO can restore, GO derives a key for that one card from your wallet; it is never your main account's key, and the card's key can't reveal your main key. Cards you connect belong to the account you are using in GO.

entries.q: How do I top up a Qortal card?
aliases: send qort to my qortal card
entries.a: In Qortal Card > My card, tap Top up on the card. GO opens its own Send QORT screen with the card's address filled in; confirm the amount there. The card's balance updates in about a minute, once the payment is in a block.

entries.q: How do I take a payment with a Qortal card?
aliases: take a payment with a qortal card
entries.a:
1. Open Qortal Card > Take payment and choose Card under Who pays.
2. Enter the amount and tap Charge.
3. The customer holds their card to the back of your phone.
GO checks the card's signature and balance before it sends anything, then shows Paid; the payment confirms in the next block, in about a minute. The fee is paid from the card.

entries.q: Do I need my phone with me to pay with a Qortal card?
aliases: pay with qortal card without phone
does the qortal card need my phone
entries.a: No. When you pay, the shop's GO phone reads your card, the card signs the payment itself, and the shop's phone sends it. You only need your own GO to set the card up, top it up and move QORT back.

entries.q: How do I send QORT to another GO phone by tapping?
aliases: tap to pay phone to phone qortal
entries.a:
1. The person receiving opens Qortal Card > Take payment, chooses GO phone and taps Ask for QORT.
2. You open Qortal Card > Send, tap Tap the other phone, and hold the two phones back to back.
3. GO opens its own Send QORT screen with their address and amount filled in.
Nothing is sent until you confirm there, and their request lasts 2 minutes.

entries.q: How do I receive QORT from another GO phone by tapping?
aliases: get paid by tap qortal go
entries.a:
1. Open Qortal Card > Take payment and choose GO phone under Who pays.
2. Enter an amount if you like (it's optional) and tap Ask for QORT.
3. The other person opens Qortal Card > Send on their GO phone and holds it to the back of yours.
They confirm the payment on their own phone; yours waits and shows Received. The request times out after 2 minutes.

entries.q: What happens if I lose my Qortal card?
aliases: recover qort from a lost card
entries.a: It depends on the card's key. With a key GO can restore, GO can move the card's QORT back to your account without the card, so do that right away (Move back > All). With a key made on the card, only that card can move its QORT, so a lost card means that QORT is lost. Test cards have no PIN yet, so whoever finds one can pay with it.

entries.q: Can someone copy my Qortal card by tapping it?
entries.a: No. The key never leaves the card: over NFC a phone can only read the card's public key and address. Every payment has to be signed by the card itself, and the shop's GO checks that signature before sending. But a test card has no PIN yet, so anyone holding it can make it pay; keep only a few QORT on it.

entries.q: Does the Qortal Card have a PIN or spending limit?
aliases: set a pin on qortal card
entries.a: Not yet. Test cards have no PIN or limit, so anyone holding one can pay with it. PINs and limits need the final card program, which isn't ready yet, so for now keep only a few QORT on a card.

entries.q: How do I move QORT back from a Qortal card to my account?
aliases: withdraw qort from a qortal card
qortal card qort back to wallet
entries.a: In Qortal Card > My card, tap Move back on the card and choose All, Amount or Percent. The fee comes off the card on top, and the form shows what stays on it. A card with a key GO can restore needs no tap; a card with its own key must be held to the phone to sign. Your balance updates in about a minute.

entries.q: Can I back up a Qortal card?
aliases: restore qortal card without the card
entries.a: Yes, if it has a key GO can restore. In the card's More (⋮) menu choose Save backup file and set a password; GO saves a password-protected backup of the card's account to Documents/Qortal Go. It opens in GO or Hub like any Qortal backup file, even without the card. A card that made its own key has no backup file, because that key never leaves the card.

entries.q: Can a Qortal card have its own name and avatar?
aliases: register a name for my qortal card
qortal card shows a name when paying
entries.a: Yes. In the card's More (⋮) menu, Name on chain registers a Qortal name for the card's account, paid from the card (a card with its own key must be held to the phone to sign). Payments from it then show that name, and Card avatar can add a picture; that works for cards with a key GO can restore and needs your own node, because the public node doesn't take uploads. Rename only changes what this phone shows.

entries.q: What does This card already has a key mean in GO?
aliases: qortal card already has a key
card has key error qortal go
go never replaces a card key
entries.a: GO never replaces a key that is already on a card, so no QORT can be stranded at the card's old address. A card that already has a key is read and added as it is instead of being set up again.

entries.q: What does Switch to a key GO can restore do?
aliases: switch to a wallet key qortal card
qortal card gets a new address
entries.a: It turns a card that made its own key into one you can back up. GO first moves the card's QORT back to your account (you hold the card to sign), waits until the old address is empty, then loads a new key made from your wallet with one more tap. The card gets a new address, so don't send anything to the old one. It can't switch if the card has a name on chain, because the name belongs to the old key.

entries.q: What happens to the QORT if I remove a card from GO?
aliases: remove a qortal card from go
entries.a: Removing a card only takes it off GO's list; its QORT stays on the card's account. A card with a key GO can restore shows up again when you connect it. For a card that made its own key, only that card can move the QORT, so keep the card.

entries.q: Where do I hold the Qortal card on my phone?
aliases: where to tap the qortal card
hold the card to the phone qortal
the card moved away too soon
entries.a: Hold it to the back of the phone and keep it still until the phone buzzes. If it slips away mid-read, GO tries again by itself; if it says "The card moved away too soon", tap again and hold it steady. NFC must be on, and GO only listens for a card while a Qortal Card screen is waiting for a tap.

entries.q: Why does GO say NFC is off?
aliases: turn on nfc for qortal go
entries.a: Qortal Card needs the phone's NFC switched on. Tap Turn on NFC in GO to get to Android's NFC setting, switch it on and come back. If GO says the phone has no NFC, it can't read cards or tap other phones.

entries.q: Does taking Qortal card payments cost the shop anything?
aliases: who pays the qortal card fee
entries.a: No. The normal Qortal transaction fee is paid from the customer's card, and GO shows it before you charge. The shop's account only receives the payment; it doesn't sign anything.

entries.q: Can the shop see who paid with a Qortal card?
aliases: who paid with a qortal card
entries.a: The Paid screen shows the card's address, or its name and avatar if the card has a name on chain, and how much QORT is left on the card.

entries.q: What do Try again, Use another card and Send again mean for a card payment?
entries.a: Try again: the card part failed, so the customer taps again for the same amount. Use another card: the card doesn't hold enough QORT for the payment plus fee. Send again: the node didn't take it, and GO resends the very same signed payment, never a second one. If the node sees too little QORT right after a top up, wait for the next block (about a minute) and try again.

entries.q: Can I pay with Q-Assets using a Qortal card?
entries.a: Not yet. GO's Qortal Card screens handle QORT payments only for now.

entries.q: Can I take Qortal card payments without internet?
entries.a: No. The shop's GO phone checks the card's balance on its node and sends the payment through it, so it needs a working connection to a node. The card itself needs no connection.

entries.q: Do both phones need NFC for phone-to-phone payments?
aliases: nfc on both phones qortal go
entries.a: Yes, both need NFC switched on and GO's Qortal Card screens open. The phone that asks for QORT answers a tap only while its request is open (2 minutes) and only while that phone is unlocked.

entries.q: Is there a Qortal NFC bracelet?
entries.a: Not yet. A tap-to-pay bracelet is being developed, but you can't get or use one today. What works now is GO's Qortal Card (testing), with a Qortal test card or between two GO phones.

entries.q: Is an RNode the same as LoRaWAN?
aliases: is lora the same as lorawan
entries.a: No. RNodes use LoRa only as the radio modulation, with no LoRaWAN protocol on top. LoRaWAN is a separate standard for centrally controlled IoT devices; with Reticulum, all the networking is done by Reticulum itself. So you need a plain LoRa radio with RNode firmware, not a LoRaWAN gateway or service.

entries.q: Which LoRa boards can become an RNode?
entries.a: The Reticulum manual lists boards its auto-installer supports: LilyGO T-Beam, T-Beam Supreme, T3S3, LoRa32 (v1.0, v2.0, v2.1), T-Deck and T-Echo; Heltec LoRa32 (v2, v3, v4) and T114; RAK4631-based boards; the openCom XL; and unsigned.io's RNode v2.x. rnodeconf also offers the Seeed XIAO ESP32S3 Wio-SX1262. Most come in versions for different frequency bands, so get the one for the band you will use.

entries.q: How do I turn a LoRa board into an RNode?
aliases: install rnode firmware on a lora board
entries.a:
1. Install Reticulum on a computer with pip install rns; that includes rnodeconf.
2. Connect the supported board by USB.
3. Run rnodeconf --autoinstall and answer its questions about your board and band.
It installs and sets up the RNode firmware. The manual also mentions a web-based flasher, and ready-made RNodes can be bought if you would rather not build one.

entries.q: Is the RNode firmware stable on LoRa development boards?
entries.a: The installer says RNode firmware on boards such as the T-Beam, LoRa32, Heltec, RAK4631, T-Echo and T-Deck, and on homebrew RNodes, should currently be considered experimental: it is supplied as-is and not intended for production or critical use.

entries.q: Which LoRa board should I avoid for an RNode?
entries.a: The RNode installer warns about the LilyGO LoRa32 v1.0: it has a faulty battery charging circuit that can overcharge and damage batteries, so it recommends avoiding that board if at all possible.

entries.q: What frequency band should my RNode use?
entries.a: LoRa boards come in versions for 433 MHz or for 868/915/923 MHz, and a few for 2.4 GHz, so buy the version for the band you will use. Which band and how much power you may use depends on your country: the Reticulum manual warns that radio spectrum is legally controlled, rules vary widely, and knowing them is your responsibility.

entries.q: How far can an RNode reach?
aliases: how far does an rnode reach
entries.a: The Reticulum manual gives no fixed distance; range depends on your settings and setup. Higher spreading factors (up to 12) and coding rates (up to 8) reach further but send more slowly, while 7 and 5 are the fastest; transmit power and bandwidth matter too. For long, fast links between fixed sites the manual suggests Wi-Fi-type radios with high-gain directional antennas, with LoRa RNodes covering wide areas.

entries.q: How fast is a LoRa link with Reticulum?
entries.a: Slow by internet standards: the Reticulum manual describes LoRa links of a few hundred bits per second, and its rnstatus example shows an RNode at about 1.3 kbps. That is enough for text messaging, since setting up an encrypted link costs only 297 bytes and keeping it open about 0.45 bits per second, but big files take a long time.

entries.q: Can I use an RNode with Qortal GO?
aliases: connect a lora radio to qortal go
entries.a: No. GO's Reticulum connects only to Qortal's Reticulum hubs over the internet; it doesn't set up LoRa radios, USB serial devices or Bluetooth RNodes, and it doesn't use local Wi-Fi discovery either. Other Reticulum apps can use RNodes, but chat and calls in GO always go through the Qortal hubs.

entries.q: Can I use an RNode with Qortal Hub?
aliases: add a lora radio to qortal hub
entries.a: Not as a built-in feature: Hub's Reticulum connects through Qortal's hubs over the internet and has no radio settings. Advanced users can switch off Managed Reticulum config in Hub's Reticulum settings and add an RNodeInterface in the Config editor, as the Reticulum manual describes, but Qortal doesn't document this. Hub then stops updating that config for you, so keep its Qortal hub entries in place.

entries.q: Can Qortal voice calls work over LoRa?
aliases: lora too slow for qortal calls
entries.a: Not realistically. Qortal Hub and GO send call audio at about 24 to 32 kbps, while the Reticulum manual describes LoRa links of a few hundred bits per second to around a kilobit. Qortal calls run over the internet, either directly or through Qortal's Reticulum hubs.

entries.q: How do I connect an RNode to my computer?
entries.a: You choose the connection in the RNodeInterface section of Reticulum's config: a USB serial port (for example port = /dev/ttyUSB0), Bluetooth LE (port = ble://, after pairing the RNode with the computer), or Wi-Fi if the RNode supports it (port = tcp:// followed by its address). rnodeconf -p puts an RNode into Bluetooth pairing mode.

entries.q: Can Reticulum use Wi-Fi radios for long links?
entries.a: Yes. Any Wi-Fi hardware that passes bridged Ethernet works with Reticulum's AutoInterface, with no DHCP or other IP setup needed. The manual names Ubiquiti airMAX and LTU radios and MikroTik radios as examples for long, high-capacity links, often used as the backbone between sites while LoRa RNodes cover wide areas for client devices.

entries.q: Do I need a licence to use an RNode?
entries.a: Reticulum is designed to work on licence-free ISM radio bands, which is where RNodes usually run.
