But radio rules vary widely between countries, and the Reticulum manual says it is your responsibility to know and follow the rules where you are. If you transmit on amateur bands under a licence, an RNode can send your callsign at set intervals (id_callsign and id_interval).

entries.q: Can I limit how much my RNode transmits?
entries.a: Yes. In the RNodeInterface config, airtime_limit_short caps transmit time over a window of about 15 seconds and airtime_limit_long over a rolling 60 minutes, both in percent; the manual's example uses 33 and 1.5.

entries.q: What computer should run my RNode at home?
entries.a: Almost anything that runs Python 3. The Reticulum manual's reference setup is an RNode on USB plus any Linux computer, and it calls a Raspberry Pi with a Debian-based OS a good place to start. For a home node it suggests repurposing an old computer, a Raspberry Pi or a supported router that stays on, connected to your Wi-Fi and perhaps an RNode.

entries.q: How should I set up an RNode in a car or other vehicle?
entries.a: The manual's example: give the vehicle an outside LoRa interface set to mode = roaming, an inside Wi-Fi interface for the devices travelling with it, and enable transport. Devices inside can then reach each other and any LoRa nodes in range, and those nodes can reach them. Paths through roaming interfaces expire faster.

entries.q: How do I set up a LoRa node that also has an internet link?
entries.a: Set the interface that connects over the internet to mode = boundary; that is what the Reticulum manual recommends for a node on a LoRa network that also links to a public transport node online. The manual also warns that passing all announce traffic from a fast link onto LoRa wastes its airtime, and the LoRa network won't work well.

entries.q: How do I set up an RNode as a quiet access point for a wide area?
entries.a: Put its interface in mode = access_point. The interface then doesn't send announces on its own and stays quiet until someone uses it, and paths to devices on it expire sooner. The manual gives a radio serving a wide area, where users connect for a while and then leave, as the example.

entries.q: What is the RNode Multi interface for?
entries.a: It is for RNodes with more than one LoRa transceiver, such as the openCom XL with its SX1262 and SX1280 chips. Each radio gets its own sub-interface with its own frequency, bandwidth, power, spreading factor and coding rate; the manual's example pairs a 2.4 GHz high-speed radio with an 865.6 MHz low-speed one.

entries.q: What operating system should I use on a Raspberry Pi node?
aliases: best os for a qortal raspberry pi
entries.a: The Qortal wiki lists trusted community Qortal OS images: RaspiPHENIX for the Pi 4 and Ra5piPHENIX for the Pi 5, both based on Debian 12, usable with a desktop or headless, with remote desktop, SSH and Qortal tools included. You can also use any 64-bit Linux and install Core yourself, since it only needs Java 11 or newer. After flashing an image, expand the filesystem, update the system and get the latest Core as the wiki shows.

entries.q: Can I run Qortal Core in Docker?
entries.a: Yes. Qortal Core's source includes Docker files: copy .env.example to .env and run docker compose up -d --build. The node's data and settings.json live in ./data/qortal, and Java's memory options are in start-arguments.txt there (by default up to 25% of the RAM). Only the container itself may use the API by default, so add other containers to the API whitelist in settings.json if they need it.

entries.q: Do I need a static IP address for a Qortal node?
aliases: public ip for a qortal node
entries.a: Not for a normal node: UPnP or port forwarding is enough. For port forwarding, give the node a fixed address on your home network (static assignment in the router's DHCP settings) so the forward always reaches it. Only a public gateway node prefers a static public IP, and dynamic DNS works there too.

entries.q: Does Qortal Core work over IPv6?
entries.a: Yes, if your operating system supports it. Core's start script runs Java with IPv6 enabled (java.net.preferIPv4Stack=false), and you can add a peer by its IPv6 address in square brackets with the port, for example [address]:12392.

entries.q: What power settings should a Linux node computer use?
entries.a: The Qortal wiki's Ubuntu guide sets, both plugged in and on battery: Suspend when inactive to Never, Lid close action to Do Nothing, and Power button to Ask. That keeps Core running all the time, even with a laptop closed.

entries.q: How do I reach my Raspberry Pi node from another computer?
entries.a: Find the Pi's IP address in your router's list of connected devices (or use its .local hostname), then connect with a remote desktop client such as Microsoft Remote Desktop or Remmina, or over SSH for headless images; some images also have VNC. Log in with the image's user and the password you set. To use Hub with the node, add it under Choose custom node, through an SSH tunnel or the node's API whitelist.

entries.q: Can a QORTector be used as a normal desktop computer?
entries.a: Yes. With a monitor, keyboard and mouse it is a stand-alone desktop, and the wiki says the Gen 2 has served as a full replacement for everyday desktops while using a fraction of the power. The Qortal OS images come with software such as the Chromium browser, VLC and LibreOffice, and the KB model is built into a keyboard.

entries.q: What is the difference between a QORTector and a plain Raspberry Pi?
entries.a: The hardware is a normal Raspberry Pi with an SSD: a Raspberry Pi 4 with a fan for the Gen 2, a Raspberry Pi 400 keyboard computer for the KB. What differs is the software and setup. QORTectors run a custom Qortal OS with kernels tuned for Qortal's cryptography and a threat-mitigation layer, and they start Core by themselves. You can build the same thing yourself with the wiki's Raspberry Pi guide and images.

entries.q: How do I re-image a QORTector?
entries.a:
1. Download the image for your model from the wiki's QORTector page (RaspiPHENIX for the Gen 2, torchieMATE for the KB) and extract it with 7-Zip or Keka.
2. Connect the QORTector's SSD to another computer by its USB cable.
3. Write the .img file to the SSD with Balena Etcher; allow it to write to the large disk.
4. Reconnect the SSD, boot, then expand the filesystem with sudo raspi-config and reboot.

entries.q: Does Qortal Hub support the Qortal Card?
entries.a: No. Qortal Card is a GO feature for Android phones with NFC. A backup file saved from a card with a key GO can restore does open in Hub, like any Qortal backup file.

entries.q: Can I connect more than one Qortal card?
aliases: multiple nfc cards in qortal go
entries.a: Yes. Each card you connect gets its own account and appears in Your cards. GO gives every restorable card its own key and never reuses one, even after a card is removed.

entries.q: Does Qortal Card work on the public node?
entries.a: Yes for paying, topping up, moving QORT back and registering a card's name. Only Card avatar needs your own node, because the public node doesn't take uploads.

entries.q: Can I build a homebrew RNode?
entries.a: Yes. rnodeconf --autoinstall has a Homebrew RNode option for your own board design or a development board paired with a supported radio module: an AVR ATmega1284P, ATmega2560 or ESP32 with an SX1276 or SX1278 transceiver. The installer calls homebrew firmware experimental and not meant for production or critical use.

entries.q: Can one RNode serve all the devices on my home Wi-Fi?
aliases: share one rnode on home wifi
one lora radio whole house reticulum
entries.a: Yes. Put the RNode on one always-on computer, add its interface to that computer's Reticulum config and enable transport there. Other Reticulum devices on your Wi-Fi can then reach the LoRa side with the default AutoInterface setup. Qortal GO doesn't use local Wi-Fi discovery, so it won't use such a gateway.

entries.q: Is the Qortal Card a hardware wallet?
entries.a: Not in the usual sense. A Qortal card is a small separate wallet for spending: it has its own account, its chip signs payments, and it never holds your main account's key. Test cards have no PIN yet, so anyone holding one can pay with it. Keep only a few QORT on a card and your savings in your main account.

entries.q: Can I run a Qortal node with very little storage?
entries.a: Not yet as a full node, which keeps the whole blockchain and needs room to grow. The Qortal wiki describes lite nodes that store no blockchain and ask full nodes for what they need, but they can't mint, and they are still being built. Until they are live, plan a full node around an SSD with plenty of free space.

entries.q: Can I use a regular hard drive for a Qortal node?
aliases: qortal node on a hard drive
entries.a: It isn't recommended. The Minter Guide says solid-state storage (an SSD) is strongly recommended, and the Qortal wiki recommends an SSD for Raspberry Pi nodes. Plan the node around an SSD with plenty of free space and room to grow.

entries.q: Why does GO say that GO phone is not asking for QORT right now?
aliases: that go phone is not asking for qort
not a go phone asking for qort
phone to phone tap error qortal
entries.a: You tapped a GO phone whose request isn't open. On that phone, open Qortal Card > Take payment, choose GO phone and tap Ask for QORT, then tap again within 2 minutes. If GO says it is not a GO phone asking for QORT at all, the other device isn't showing a GO request.

entries.q: Why does GO say the card's signature did not check out?
aliases: card signature did not check out
card did not use the expected key
entries.a: GO checks every signature the card returns, and that it came from the card's expected key, before anything is sent. When a check fails, GO stops and says "Nothing was sent", so no QORT moved. Hold the card still and try the tap again.

entries.q: Why does GO say this card can only make its own key?
aliases: card can only make its own key
test card makes its own key
entries.a: Some test cards carry a test applet that can't take a key from GO, so they can only make a key on the card. That works for paying, but there is no backup file and no switch to a restorable key, and if the card is lost, the QORT on it is lost.

entries.q: Why does Qortal Card ask me to unlock my wallet first?
aliases: unlock your wallet first qortal card
entries.a: To give a card a key GO can restore, GO derives it from your wallet, so the wallet must be unlocked. Unlock GO and tap the card again, or choose Make a new key on the card instead.

entries.q: Is the QORTector open hardware?
entries.a: The Qortal wiki describes it as an open-source, non-proprietary hardware project: it uses standard Raspberry Pi boards, and the Qortal OS images and 3D printing files for the case can be downloaded to build your own. Pre-built units are also sold.

entries.q: How do I set the time zone on a QORTector?
entries.a:
1. Open a terminal and run sudo raspi-config.
2. Choose Localisation Options, then Timezone.
3. Pick your country, then your city or region, and choose Finish.
The default is USA, Pacific time. Do this before you change the password.

entries.q: What can I do in Qortal Hub?
aliases: things to do in qortal hub
entries.a: Qortal Hub is the desktop app for Qortal on Windows, macOS and Linux. In one window you can create or unlock your account, send and receive QORT, chat in Q-Chat groups and direct messages, make voice calls, open Q-Apps and websites from QDN, publish your own apps, and set up and control your own Qortal Core node, including minting.

entries.q: Is Qortal Hub free to use?
aliases: do i pay for qortal hub
entries.a: Yes. Qortal Hub is free, open-source software under the GPL-3.0 licence, and you download it from the Downloads page on qortal.dev. Creating an account costs nothing. You only need a little QORT later for network fees, for example to register a name or join a group.

entries.q: Which Qortal Hub file should I download for my computer?
entries.a: Get Hub from the Downloads page on qortal.dev, which has a button for Windows, Mac and Linux plus a Linux (Script) installer; every release, including older ones, is also on the Releases page of the Qortal-Hub project on GitHub. The files are Qortal-Hub-Setup-win64.exe for Windows, Qortal-Hub-Setup-macOS.dmg for a Mac, Qortal-Hub.AppImage or Qortal-Hub-Setup.deb for a normal 64-bit Linux PC, and Qortal-Hub-arm64.AppImage for 64-bit ARM such as a Raspberry Pi.

entries.q: How do I install Qortal Hub on Windows?
aliases: how to install qortal hub on pc
entries.a:
1. On qortal.dev Downloads, click Windows to get Qortal-Hub-Setup-win64.exe.
2. Open it from your Downloads folder and click Yes when Windows asks to allow changes.
3. Keep the suggested install location unless you have a reason to change it, and click Install.
4. When it finishes, leave Run Qortal Hub ticked and click Finish.
If SmartScreen warns you, choose More info, then Run anyway.

entries.q: How do I install Qortal Hub on a Mac?
aliases: how to install qortal hub on macbook
entries.a:
1. On qortal.dev Downloads, click Mac to get Qortal-Hub-Setup-macOS.dmg.
2. Open the .dmg and drag Qortal Hub into your Applications folder.
3. Eject the installer disk: right-click it on the Desktop and choose Eject.
4. Open Spotlight, type Qortal and choose Qortal Hub. If a popup appears, click Open.
If macOS still blocks it, right-click the app in Finder and choose Open.

entries.q: How do I install Qortal Hub on Linux?
entries.a: You have three choices. The easiest is the Linux (Script) button on qortal.dev Downloads: it copies a command; paste it into a terminal and press Enter, and it sets up Hub and Core for you. Or download Qortal-Hub.AppImage (Qortal-Hub-arm64.AppImage on ARM), allow it to run as a program and start it. On Debian or Ubuntu you can also install Qortal-Hub-Setup.deb.

entries.q: Do I need Qortal Core installed to use Hub?
entries.a: No. Hub can connect to a public node, so you can create an account and look around straight away. Running your own Core is optional but recommended: it gives full decentralized access, faster downloads and keeps your data under your control, and you need it to mint and to publish to QDN, because the public node takes no uploads. Hub can download, install and start Core for you from its Set up Qortal Core window.

entries.q: Do I need to install Python or Java for Qortal Hub?
entries.a: No. Installed Hub releases include everything Hub needs, including its Reticulum chat engine. Java is only for Qortal Core: on Windows Hub runs the official Core installer, and on Linux and macOS, if no Java is found, Hub downloads its own Java 17 into your home folder when it sets up Core. Python and Git are only needed to build Hub from source code.

entries.q: What do I see the first time I open Qortal Hub?
entries.a: After a short logo intro with a startup sound, Hub shows the Enter Qortal screen. There you choose Create account or Import account, and later your saved accounts appear there to unlock. A line below shows which node Hub will use, such as Using public node, with a Connection Mode button next to it. The buttons at the bottom right open Core controls, switch light or dark mode and change the language.

entries.q: Which node does Qortal Hub use when I first install it?
aliases: new hub starts on public node
entries.a: A new Hub starts on the public node, a shared Qortal node run by others, so you can begin without installing anything else. If Qortal Core isn't installed, Hub offers to set it up after you sign in, and when your own node has caught up it shows Local node ready with a Switch to local button. You can change node any time with Connection Mode on the login screen or Change node on Home.

entries.q: Why does Hub show Set up Qortal Core after I sign in?
aliases: set up qortal core popup hub
hub core setup window keeps opening
why hub asks to install core
run your own node locally hub
entries.a: Hub opens it when it can't use a node of your own: you are on the public node and Core isn't installed yet, or you picked Local Node but Core isn't running. The window says you can keep using a public node while Core starts and syncs. Click Download Core and then Start Core to run your own node, or close the window and carry on with the public node.

entries.q: How do I create a new account in Qortal Hub?
aliases: make a qortal account on desktop
entries.a:
1. On the Enter Qortal screen click Create account.
2. Choose a wallet password, type it again, leave Save account in Hub ticked and click Continue.
3. Your seedphrase appears; you can reveal, copy or export it. Click Create account.
4. Click Backup wallet and save the encrypted backup file. Enter Hub only unlocks after that.
5. Click Enter Hub. Everything happens on your computer, with no sign-up server.

entries.q: What is the wallet password in Qortal Hub?
aliases: what password does hub ask for
entries.a: It is the password you choose when you create or import an account. It encrypts the account saved on this computer and your backup file, and Hub asks for it to unlock, to send QORT and to reveal your private key. There is no password reset: if you forget it, import the account again from your seedphrase and choose a new password.

entries.q: Where does Qortal Hub save my backup file?
entries.a: Hub opens your computer's Save dialog, so the backup goes wherever you choose; the suggested name is qortal_backup_ followed by your address and .json. It holds your account encrypted with your wallet password. Keep copies in more than one safe place, such as a USB stick, and remember the password: the file opens only with the password it was saved with.

entries.q: How do I make another backup of my account in Hub?
entries.a: On Home, click Backup Wallet in Quick Tools. Enter your current password, then either keep that password in the exported file or set a new password just for this backup, and click Download wallet file. Hub saves the file wherever you choose.

entries.q: How do I import an existing account into Qortal Hub?
aliases: log in with existing account hub
entries.a: On the Enter Qortal screen click Import account and pick one of three choices: Backup file (drop or select your .json backup to save it in Hub), Seedphrase (type your seedphrase and choose a wallet password for this computer), or Authenticate now (use a backup file once without saving it). Saved accounts then appear on the Enter Qortal screen, ready to unlock.

entries.q: What does Authenticate now do on Hub's Import account screen?
aliases: use backup file without saving hub
entries.a: It signs you in from a backup file without saving the account in Hub. Drop or select the .json file, enter its password, and you are in for this session; nothing is kept on the computer for next time. It is useful on a computer you only use once.

entries.q: How do I unlock my account in Hub?
entries.a: On the Enter Qortal screen, click your saved account, type its wallet password and click Unlock. If you have many accounts, type an address, primary name or note in the filter box to find the right one. Choose another account takes you back to the list.

entries.q: How do I switch accounts in Qortal Hub?
aliases: log in to a different account hub
entries.a: Use the button at the far right of the top bar (Lock or log out), choose Log out and confirm. On the Enter Qortal screen pick another saved account and unlock it with its password. Every account you have created or imported on this computer is listed there; a label and note on each help you tell them apart.

entries.q: How do I add a label or note to a saved account in Hub?
entries.a: On the Enter Qortal screen, use the edit button on the account (Edit account label and note). Fill in Name and an optional Note, then click Save. This label only lives on this computer; it is not a registered Qortal name.

entries.q: How do I remove a saved account from Hub?
entries.a: On the Enter Qortal screen, open the account's edit panel (Edit account label and note) and click Remove. This only deletes the copy saved on this computer; the account itself lives on the blockchain. Make sure you have your backup file or seedphrase first, because without them you can't add it back.

entries.q: What is the difference between Lock and Log out in Qortal Hub?
entries.a: Both are in the menu behind the button at the far right of the top bar (Lock or log out). Lock hides Hub behind a password screen but keeps you signed in, so chats and calls stay connected. Log out ends the session and returns to the Enter Qortal screen after you confirm with Continue to logout.

entries.q: Does Qortal Hub lock itself automatically?
entries.a: Yes, by default after 30 minutes without mouse or keyboard activity. Change it in Account settings (the gear on Home's Account Overview card), System, Auto-Lock When Idle: Disabled, 10 min, 30 min, 1 hour or 3 hours. Unless you choose Disabled, Hub also locks when your computer sleeps or its screen locks.

entries.q: What happens to my calls and chats when Hub is locked?
aliases: does lock end my call hub
entries.a: You stay signed in, so chats and active calls remain connected. Others see your status as Idle (unless you chose Offline), and it switches back when you unlock. An incoming direct call keeps ringing, but its window only appears after you unlock. A screen share you are sending stops when Hub locks.

entries.q: Where does Qortal Hub keep my saved accounts?
aliases: where does hub save my wallet
entries.a: In a file called wallet-storage.json in Hub's qortal-hub data folder: %APPDATA%\qortal-hub on Windows, Library/Application Support/qortal-hub in your home folder on a Mac, and .config/qortal-hub on Linux. The accounts are stored encrypted with their wallet passwords. This is not a backup, so keep your own backup file or seedphrase as well.

entries.q: Hub says my saved account is incomplete or damaged. What now?
aliases: saved account could not be found hub
entries.a: The copy saved on this computer is broken, for example its encrypted seed or password data is missing. The account itself is safe on the blockchain. Choose another account or remove the broken entry, then import the account again from your backup file or seedphrase.

entries.q: Hub says incorrect password when I unlock. What can I do?
aliases: unable to authenticate wrong password hub
entries.a: Check Caps Lock and your keyboard layout, and make sure you picked the right account, since each saved account has its own password. It is the password chosen when that account was created or imported on this computer. If you can't remember it, import the account again from your seedphrase with a new password; a backup file only opens with the password it was saved with.

entries.q: How is the Qortal Hub window laid out?
aliases: where are the menus in qortal hub
entries.a: Across the top is the navigation bar: back and reload buttons, Home or Opened apps, bookmarks, the search box for Q-Apps and qortal:// links, call controls, and on the right Q-Mail, Subscriptions, the notifications bell, your avatar menu and Lock or log out. The main sections, Home, Apps and Q-Chat, are in a sidebar hidden at the left edge: move your mouse onto the small handle there to slide it out. Home is the dashboard you see after signing in.

entries.q: Where is the sidebar in Qortal Hub?
entries.a: It is hidden at the left edge of the window. Hover over the small handle there and the sidebar slides out with Home, Apps and Q-Chat (and Dev Mode if you turned it on), then Info, the language button and the light or dark switch. You can drag the handle up or down to a spot you like. A pink dot on the handle means you have unread chats.

entries.q: What is on the Home dashboard in Qortal Hub?
entries.a: Home has an Account Overview card (your name and address, status and the Account settings gear), Quick Tools, Featured Q-Apps, an Info card with your balance, node and sync status, and Wallet Activity with Send, Receive and Buy. Below sit the Group Activity module and the Quitter Feed module (posts from Torq and Quitter, which share the same data). On the left is the QORTINO workspace, which starts with Getting Started for new accounts.

entries.q: What are the Quick Tools on Hub's Home?
aliases: what are the hub home icons
entries.a: Quick Tools is a pad of eight buttons on Home; hover over one to see its name. They are User Search, Wallets (opens Q-Wallets), Apps, Q-Chat, Backup Wallet, Minting, Mute Notifications (or Enable Notifications) and QortalLand. Minting opens the minting panel, which is mainly useful once you are a minter.

entries.q: What is the QORTINO card on Hub's Home?
aliases: what is qortino on hub home
entries.a: It is a workspace on the left of Home with a guide character called QORTINO. For a new account it shows Getting Started; after that you press + and choose what lives above QORTINO: Hotkeys (six shortcuts to Q-Apps), a Music player for EarBump tracks, or Suggest a module, which opens Q-Mail so you can send the team your idea. It is not the offline AI helper Qortino, which is only in Qortal GO.

entries.q: How do I set up Hotkeys on Hub's Home?
entries.a: In the QORTINO workspace press + and pick Hotkeys. Click an empty slot (+ Add app) or the tune button to open Select hotkeys, search for a Q-App and pick it; the next empty slot is selected for you. There are six slots, saved automatically for your account. Click a filled slot to launch its app; the X in the header empties the workspace again.

entries.q: How do I play EarBump music on Hub's Home?
entries.a: In the QORTINO workspace press + and choose Music player. Click Search, find a track or artist in Search Earbump and pick it to load it into the player, then use play, previous, next and repeat. Tracks come from QDN, so the first play can take a moment while your node fetches it (Preparing on your node...). Music keeps playing when you leave Home and stops when you log out.

entries.q: How do I get started with a new account on Hub's Home?
aliases: what to do first in qortal hub
entries.a:
The QORTINO card on Home shows Getting Started in three steps:
1. Get your 2 QORT.
2. Register your name.
3. Load your avatar.
A step ticks off once it is done on the blockchain; when your QORT arrives it says QORT acquired, and you press Next to go on to your name. Publishing the avatar needs your own node, because the public node takes no uploads. When all three are done the card says All set and offers its workspace modules.

entries.q: How do I get my first 2 QORT in Hub?
aliases: how to get qort in hub
entries.a: In Getting Started on Home, Get your 2 QORT offers three ways: Go to onboarding (the onboarding guide on qortal.dev, which can send 2 QORT after you verify a personal email address), Open support chat (ask for 2 QORT in the Nextcloud support chat), or Open Q-Trade to buy QORT. When the QORT arrives, Hub shows QORT acquired and moves you on to registering a name.

entries.q: Can I skip the Getting Started steps in Hub?
entries.a: There is no skip button, but the steps are only a guide: the rest of Hub works without them. The card switches to its workspace modules once your account holds 2 QORT, has a registered name and has an avatar.

entries.q: What is the guided tour in Qortal Hub?
entries.a: The first time you sign in, in a window at least 1250 pixels wide, Hub offers a short tour: Welcome to Qortal Hub, then Q-Chat, Find Groups, the Qortal Project group, channels, Qortal Land, Direct Messages, message expiry and Q-Apps. Choose Start Tour or Skip for now, and use Back, Next or Skip Tutorial while it runs. If you skip, Hub reminds you that you can restart it from Settings, Help.

entries.q: How do I restart the Hub tutorial?
entries.a: Open Account settings with the gear on Home's Account Overview card, go to Help and click Restart Tutorial under Hub Tutorial. The tour begins after Settings closes and you are back on Home. The button only works when the window is at least 1250 pixels wide; otherwise it says Only available on Desktop.

entries.q: Where do I find my Qortal address in Hub?
aliases: where is my wallet address hub
find my q address in hub
entries.a: On Home, the Account Overview card shows your name, or your address if you have no name. Hover over it to reveal the address, then click it or use the copy button to copy it. Your avatar menu at the top right also shows ADDRESS with a copy button, and the QR button on the card opens Receive QORT with a QR code of the address.

entries.q: How do I change my status in Qortal Hub?
entries.a: Click your avatar at the top right, or the status pill on Home's Account Overview card, and pick Online, Busy or Offline. Offline makes you appear offline: others can't call you and you can't join group voice calls. Hub remembers only Offline for next time; the others reset to Online. Idle is set by itself after 30 minutes without activity and while Hub is locked.

entries.q: What does Privacy Mode do in Hub?
entries.a: Privacy Mode is the eye button at the bottom of the Account settings sidebar. It blurs your name, address, private key and blocked accounts inside Account settings, which helps when you share your screen. It does not blur the rest of Hub, such as Home or the top bar. Hub remembers the choice.

entries.q: How do I look up another user in Qortal Hub?
entries.a: Open User Search from Quick Tools on Home, or click a name in Wallet Activity or a chat user card. Type a name or address and press Enter. You see their avatar and name, level, minting progress, balance, total received and sent, blocks minted, address, public key and recent payments, with Send QORT and Block buttons.

entries.q: What does Block do in Hub's User Search?
aliases: what does blocking do in hub
entries.a: Block adds the person's name to your node's blocked names and their address to its blocked addresses. Blocking an address affects how your node handles their transactions, and blocking a name hides their data across Hub. Unblock reverses it. Blocking needs your own node; on a public node the button is unavailable.

entries.q: How do I see who I blocked in Hub?
entries.a: Open Account settings (the gear on Home's Account Overview card) and choose Blocked. It lists your blocked Names and Addresses, refreshed from your node each time you open it, with an Unblock button on each. If you have blocked nobody it says No blocked accounts yet.

entries.q: Why does Wallet Activity on Hub's Home show only one payment?
entries.a: The card is a quick glance, not a history: it shows only your most recent confirmed QORT payment from the past 7 days, sent or received, or No new wallet activity if there is none. For a longer list, look up your own name or address in User Search (Recent payments) or open Q-Wallets.

entries.q: What are the Featured Q-Apps on Hub's Home?
entries.a: A set of tiles for well-known apps you can open straight from Home: Q-Tube, Quitter (it shares its posts with Torq), Q-Mail, SubWire, Q-Trade and Q-Chat. The wide Q-Tube and Q-Chat tiles show a preview when you hover. Reduce motion stops the moving previews, and Explore All Q-Apps opens the full library.

entries.q: What is the Group Activity module on Hub's Home?
aliases: accept group invite on hub home
entries.a: It is a widget with three tabs: Notifications (recent messages and mentions from your Q-Chat groups), Invites (group invitations to Accept or Ignore) and Requests (join requests for groups you manage, to Approve or Ignore). Discover Groups opens Find Groups, Open in Q-Chat jumps to chat, and Show ignored brings ignored items back.

entries.q: What is the Quitter Feed on Hub's Home?
entries.a: It shows recent posts from Torq and Quitter, which use the same data. General is the public feed; Following shows people you follow and needs a registered name. Click a post to open it in the app; videos only preview there (Preview stays read-only in Hub). A banner tells you when new posts are waiting.

entries.q: How do I hide the Group Activity or Quitter Feed module on Hub's Home?
entries.a: Open Account settings (the gear on the Account Overview card) and choose Modules. Switch off Group Activity, or Quitter Feed (the Torq and Quitter posts module), and it disappears from Home at once; switch it on to bring it back. The other Home cards can't be hidden. When both modules show, Swap position changes their order.

entries.q: What is the What's New window in Hub's Q-Chat?
entries.a: It is a summary of the new Q-Chat in Hub 3: faster Reticulum chat, channels and categories, message expiry, calls, QortalLand and Group Score, with a comparison to the old Q-Chat. It doesn't open by itself; click the version link at the bottom of the Q-Chat group rail, or a What's New? button on Q-Chat's start screens.

entries.q: What is the online count at the top of Hub's Home?
entries.a: The pill next to QORTAL HUB (Online users) counts the accounts that are online on Qortal's Reticulum presence network as seen by your Hub. It changes as people come and go.

entries.q: What does the subscriptions icon in Hub's top bar do?
entries.a: It shows the subscriptions you manage through Q-Apps such as SubWire. A badge counts actions needed, such as a payment that is due; the popover lists Needs action and Active subscriptions with an Open subscriptions button. If you have none yet, it suggests Open SubWire.

entries.q: What does the ongoing transactions icon in Hub mean?
entries.a: It appears in the top bar while Hub is waiting for your transactions to confirm, such as joining a group, registering a name or a reward share. Click it to see each one as awaiting confirmation or success. It goes away once all of them are confirmed, usually after a couple of minutes.

entries.q: What does the Info card on Hub's Home show?
entries.a: It shows your QORT Balance, which node you use (Local node, Public node or a custom node) with its sync percentage, your Minter Level, and Peers, QDN peers, Core version and Hub version. The status light is blue when all is well, amber while syncing and red on a problem. Hover over the card for node details and a Change node button.

entries.q: How do I switch nodes from Hub's Home?
entries.a: Hover over the Info card on Home to expand it, then click Change node next to Using Node. Pick Local Node, Public Node or one of your saved custom nodes, and Hub switches straight away. If it fails you see Could not switch nodes right now.

entries.q: How do I open Q-Chat in Qortal Hub?
entries.a: Click Q-Chat in the left sidebar (hover the handle at the left edge to show it), the Q-Chat button in Quick Tools on Home, or Open Q-Chat on the Featured Q-Chat tile. Q-Chat opens as a tab next to your Q-App tabs, so you can switch between chat and apps.

entries.q: How is Q-Chat laid out in Qortal Hub?
aliases: where are my groups in hub chat
entries.a: On the far left is the rail: the Direct Messages button at the top, your groups below it, and at the bottom Find Groups, Create group, the Group Settings gear and the version link. Pick a group to see its channel list and messages. Its header has Group Call, Group Calendar, Members and Search Chat, and a pill switches between Chat and Enter Qortal Land.

entries.q: What does Hub's Q-Chat show before I join any group?
aliases: welcome to the new improved q-chat hub
entries.a: It says Welcome to the new, improved Q-Chat and that you're not part of any communities yet. Click Find Communities to browse groups, or paste a group invite link into the box (Paste a Group Invite Link...) and click Join. A What's New? button explains the new Q-Chat.

entries.q: How do I join a group from an invite link in Hub?
entries.a: Click the link if someone posted it in chat: Hub shows a preview card with Join for an open group or Apply for a closed one. Or paste it into the Paste a Group Invite Link... box on Q-Chat's start screen and click Join. Joining is a blockchain transaction, so accept the small fee and wait a couple of minutes; a closed group also needs an admin to accept you.

entries.q: How do I share an invite link to my group in Hub?
aliases: invite friends to my group hub
entries.a: In Q-Chat, right-click the group in the rail and choose Copy invite link (About group shows it too). The link looks like qortal://use-group/action-join/groupid- followed by the group's number. Post it in a chat or send it to friends; clicking it shows them a card with Join, or Apply for a closed group.

entries.q: How do I send a message in a Q-Chat channel in Hub?
entries.a: Pick a group in the rail and a channel in its list, type in the box at the bottom (Message channel...) and press Enter. Shift+Enter starts a new line instead. If a channel is read-only you'll see that only admins can post there.

entries.q: How do I make a new line in a Hub chat message without sending it?
entries.a: Press Shift+Enter. If you'd rather Enter never sends, open the Formatting tray under the message box and tick disable enter; then Enter makes a new line and you send with the send button.

entries.q: How do I format text in a Hub chat message?
entries.a: Click Formatting next to the message box to open the formatting tray. It has bold, italic, strikethrough, inline code, bullet and numbered lists, code block, quote, horizontal line and heading, plus undo and redo.

entries.q: How do I reply to a message in Hub's Q-Chat?
aliases: reply to someone in group hub
entries.a: Hover over the message and click Reply. The box shows what you are replying to (Cancel reply removes it); type and send. Replies are grouped under the first message, which then shows how many replies it has.

entries.q: What is a reply discussion in Hub's Q-Chat?
entries.a: When a message gets replies, Hub collects them into a discussion. Click the replies count under the message to open it: you see the initial post and every reply, and can answer there with reply to discussion... Close discussion takes you back to the channel.

entries.q: How do I react to a message in Hub's Q-Chat?
entries.a: Hover over the message and click one of the quick reaction emojis, or add another. Click your reaction again to remove it. Hover over a reaction to see the people who reacted with it.

entries.q: How do I mention someone in Hub's Q-Chat?
aliases: tag a person in chat hub
entries.a: Type @ in the message box and pick from the suggestions, which are sorted into people, channels and special mentions. The person gets a mention alert. Group admins also see @here, which notifies members currently online, and @everyone, which notifies all members.

entries.q: How do I edit a message in Hub's Q-Chat?
entries.a: Hover over your own message and click Edit. Change the text and send; the message shows edited. Its expiry can't be changed while editing.

entries.q: How do I delete a message in Hub's Q-Chat?
entries.a: Hover over your own message and click the red delete button, or press Shift+Delete while the pointer is on it (not while typing). You can only delete your own messages this way. The deletion goes out to the other members' devices too.

entries.q: How do I choose how long my message lasts in Hub's Q-Chat?
aliases: how long do my messages stay hub
entries.a: Use the expiry button next to the message box (set message expiry) before you send. In groups you can pick 1 day, 2 days, 3 days, 1 week or 1 month, but never longer than the channel's own expiry; channel default keeps the channel's setting. Lock one as your preferred expiry to keep using it. A change applies to the messages you send next, not earlier ones.

entries.q: What is a channel's expiry in Hub's Q-Chat?
entries.a: Each channel has an expiry set by its admins when they create or edit it: No Expiry, or 1 day, 2 days, 3 days, 1 week or 1 month. It applies to existing and future messages, and a message can choose a shorter time. The built-in General channel keeps messages for one month, and the Qortal Land channel for 24 hours.

entries.q: How do I search messages in Hub's Q-Chat?
entries.a: Click Search Chat in the group's header. Type at least 2 characters or choose a filter: from: (a person), in: (this channel or all channels), has: (attachment or link), date: (before and after) and sort: (newest, oldest or relevant). Click a result to jump to it.

entries.q: How do I send a picture in Hub's Q-Chat?
entries.a: Click Add attachment (+) by the message box and choose the image, paste it, or drag it onto the chat (Drop to Attach). Hub compresses pictures to WebP before sending, and turns GIFs into small animated WebP files, showing the progress while it works. Images travel peer to peer over Reticulum.

entries.q: How do I send a file in a Q-Chat group in Hub?
entries.a: Click Add attachment (+) by the message box, or drag the file onto the chat, and send. Others see a file card and click it to download, then Open file. Files are shared peer to peer over Reticulum, so they need Reticulum chat turned on and come from members who have them.

entries.q: How do I view, copy or save a picture in Hub's Q-Chat?
entries.a: Click the picture to open the image viewer. There you can zoom in and out, copy image to the clipboard or download image to save it, and close the viewer when done.

entries.q: What are link previews in Hub's Q-Chat?
aliases: qortal link card in hub chat
entries.a: When someone posts a qortal:// link to a Q-Tube video, a Quitter or Torq post or a SubWire publication, Q-Chat shows a preview card that opens the right Q-App. Group invite links and calendar event links get their own cards too.

entries.q: How do I mark a group as read in Hub?
entries.a: Right-click the group in the Q-Chat rail and choose Mark as read, or Mark all as read for every group. Inside a channel, jump to latest takes you to the newest message. Reading on one of your devices also clears the unread state on your other devices.

entries.q: How do I hide someone in a Q-Chat group in Hub?
entries.a: Click their name or avatar to open the user card and choose hide user, then hide for 1 hour, hide for 24 hours or hide until unhidden. Hidden people stay out of that group's Reticulum chat for you. Hidden users in the group's right-click menu lists them, with unhide.

entries.q: What is the difference between hiding and blocking someone in Hub?
aliases: hide or block someone in hub
entries.a: Hiding is local to one group's Q-Chat: the person's messages stay out of that group for you, for 1 hour, 24 hours or until you unhide them. Blocking works on your node: it blocks their name for QDN data and social features and their address for transactions, everywhere in Hub, until you unblock. Blocking needs your own node.

entries.q: How do I change the chat text size in Hub?
entries.a: In Q-Chat, click the Group Settings gear at the bottom of the rail, open Accessibility and choose Text size. The desktop Hub offers Default, Medium and High; it changes Reticulum messages, channel labels and the members list. (Qortal GO has its own text size setting with Small, Default and Large.)

entries.q: How do I highlight my own messages in Hub's Q-Chat?
entries.a: In Q-Chat, click the Group Settings gear at the bottom of the rail, open Accessibility, Messages, and turn on Highlight my messages. Your messages then get a faint background.

entries.q: What is the Threads setting in Hub's Q-Chat?
entries.a: Under Group Settings, Legacy, Threads shows the old Threads and Admin buttons in the Q-Chat header. The setting warns that Threads will be removed in an upcoming release, so move anything important from a thread to a channel or another safe place before updating.

entries.q: How do I turn Q-Chat mention notifications on or off in Hub?
entries.a: In Q-Chat, click the Group Settings gear, open Notifications, Mentions, and switch Mention notifications. The same switch is in the bell's Notification settings, Hub tab. Mentions are the only group chat messages that create Hub notifications.

entries.q: Why doesn't Hub notify me about every new group message?
entries.a: By design: in Reticulum Q-Chat only mentions create Hub notifications; ordinary unread messages show as unread dots and counts in Q-Chat instead. Direct messages from friends also raise a desktop alert while Hub is in the background.

entries.q: How do I start a direct message in Hub?
entries.a: In Q-Chat, click Direct Messages at the top of the rail, then New chat, and enter the person's Qortal name or address. You can also click someone's name in a group and choose message on their user card.

entries.q: What is Saved Messages in Hub?
entries.a: Saved Messages is a private chat with yourself, always first in your Direct Messages list. Use it for notes, links or files you want to keep handy. Like other DMs it reaches all your devices signed in with the same account.

entries.q: How long do direct messages last in Hub?
aliases: hub direct messages expire one month
how long are dms kept hub
entries.a: Direct messages expire after 1 month by default. Before sending, you can pick a shorter time with the expiry button: 1, 2 or 3 days, or 1 week. The change applies to the messages you send next, not to ones already sent.

entries.q: How do I send a file in a Hub direct message?
entries.a: In the DM, attach the file and send it (Transfer file with Reticulum). Your Hub sends an offer, and the other person downloads the file straight from your computer over Reticulum, so stay online until they have it. Offers expire after 2 hours; if one expires, send it again.

entries.q: What does Add friend do in a Hub DM?
aliases: why add friend before calling hub
entries.a: Add friend, at the top of a direct chat, marks the person as your friend. Voice calls between you only work once both of you have added each other; the chat shows a note such as Calls unlock when they add you back. Friends' DMs can also raise desktop alerts when Hub is in the background. Remove friend undoes it.

entries.q: How do I add an event to my group's calendar in Hub?
entries.a: Group admins open Group Calendar in the group's header and click Add event. Give it a title and description, pick all day or timed with start, end and time zone, choose whether it repeats, and add a location, link, cover image or reminder. Members see the events, and Share copies an event link to post in chat.

entries.q: What cover image can I use for a group calendar event in Hub?
entries.a: Use a JPEG, PNG or WebP image under 25 MB. The cover has a 16:9 shape, and 1200 x 675 pixels is the recommended size. Hub lets you crop and zoom it, then compresses it before saving.

entries.q: How do I make a voice call in Qortal Hub?
entries.a: Open a direct chat with the person in Q-Chat and click Start voice call in the chat header. It only works when you have both added each other as friends, the other person is online, and your Hub has a healthy P2P connection. They get an Incoming voice call window and can Accept or Decline.

entries.q: Why is the call button greyed out in a Hub DM?
aliases: why cant i call in hub
hub call not working friend offline
entries.a: Hover over it to see why. Add this user as a friend before calling means you haven't added them yet, and calls also need them to add you back. Contact is offline means they aren't on the network right now. P2P health is bad means your Hub has no stable Reticulum peers yet, so wait a moment or check the Info panel.

entries.q: How do I answer a call in Qortal Hub?
entries.a: When someone calls, Hub rings and shows an Incoming voice call window with their name and two buttons: Accept and Decline. It appears wherever you are in Hub. If Hub is locked, the call keeps ringing and the window shows after you unlock.

entries.q: What can I do during a voice call in Hub?
entries.a: The call controls sit in Hub's top bar so you can keep using Hub. You can mute or unmute your microphone, mute call audio (or Hear call audio), open call audio settings to pick your microphone and speaker, share your screen in a one-to-one call, and Hang up.

entries.q: How do I choose my microphone or speaker for calls in Hub?
entries.a: During a call, open call audio settings in the call controls. Pick a microphone and a speaker from the lists; System microphone and System speaker follow your computer's default devices. If the lists are empty Hub shows could not list devices, so check that your computer can see the device.

entries.q: How do I share my screen in a Hub call?
entries.a: In a one-to-one call, click Share your screen in the call controls. Choose what to share (a screen or one application window); only that is visible to the other person, sent directly through the encrypted WebRTC call. Click Stop sharing to end it. The other person sees View shared screen.

entries.q: Why can't I share my screen in a Hub call?
entries.a: Screen sharing needs a direct WebRTC connection, so it isn't offered while the call runs over the Reticulum fallback (Screen sharing requires a direct WebRTC call). The other person's app may also not support it yet. Screen sharing is only for one-to-one calls, not group calls, and it stops if your Hub locks.

entries.q: What does the call history in a Hub DM show?
entries.a: Calls appear in the direct chat as rows: voice call for an answered one, missed voice call, declined voice call, cancelled voice call or no answer. A missed call also shows in the notifications bell as Missed voice call from the caller.

entries.q: What do the call failure messages in Hub mean?
aliases: not a friend call declined hub
entries.a: The other person declined the call means they pressed Decline. The call ended, their microphone may be unavailable means their side could not start audio. Call declined, they do not have you as a friend means you must be on each other's friends list. voice call failed means the connection could not be made; try again in a moment.

entries.q: How do I start or join a group voice call in Hub?
entries.a: Open the group in Q-Chat and click Group Call in its header. If a call is already going, you join it; otherwise you start it, and other members can join. While you are in it the button reads Leave Call, and the group shows Voice call in progress in the rail.

entries.q: How many people can join a group call in Hub?
aliases: how many in group call hub
entries.a: Hub 3 allows up to 15 people in a group voice call (Q-Call); Hub's README still calls group calls beta. When it is full, others see This call is full with the limit. The group rail shows how many are in the call next to the limit.

entries.q: Why can't I join a group voice call in Hub?
aliases: only group members can join this call
entries.a: The message tells you why: Only group members can join this call; finish your other call first (you can be in one call at a time); Switch your status to online to join (Offline status blocks group calls); Group voice calls need a healthier P2P connection; or Reticulum is not ready yet. Fix that and press Group Call again.

entries.q: What do the Q-Call controls in Hub's top bar do?
entries.a: During a group call, the Q-Call pill in the top bar shows the participants and lets you Mute or Unmute, Mute call audio or Hear call audio, Expand call to the full call view, or Leave call. From the full view, Minimize to sidebar shrinks it again so you can keep chatting.

entries.q: Is there text chat inside a Hub group call?
entries.a: Not yet: the call view says Text chat for group calls is not available yet. Keep chatting in the group's channels while the call runs; minimize the call to see them.

entries.q: How do I copy call diagnostics in Hub?
entries.a: In the group call view, use Copy diagnostics JSON to clipboard or Export call diagnostics (JSON download). It describes the call's connections and audio; share it only with someone you trust who is helping you fix the call.

entries.q: Which of my computers rings when I'm signed in on two with Hub?
aliases: call rings on all devices hub
entries.a: A direct call rings on every device where your account is online. The first one you answer on takes the call, and the others are told to stop ringing. In a group call your account can be active from one device at a time.

entries.q: Does a voice call in Hub reveal my IP address?
aliases: does the other person see my ip hub
entries.a: It can. Since Hub 3.0.1, calls send audio over WebRTC when the two computers can connect directly, and fall back to Reticulum when they can't. A direct WebRTC connection means the two computers exchange network addresses, so the other person's app can learn your IP address. The call itself is encrypted.

entries.q: What is QortalLand in Qortal Hub?
entries.a: QortalLand is a shared social world inside Q-Chat groups. Each group has its own space, where members walk around as avatars, show moods, talk to people nearby with proximity voice and play Chess, Checkers or Qonnect Four. It is new and still growing.

entries.q: How do I enter QortalLand in Hub?
aliases: return to chat from qortal land hub
entries.a: Open a group in Q-Chat and click the Enter Qortal Land pill, or use QortalLand in Quick Tools on Home, which takes you into your top group. You must be a member of at least one Q-Chat group and have Reticulum on. Click Return to Chat to go back.

entries.q: How do I play a game with someone in Hub's QortalLand?
entries.a: Click another member's avatar, press Play games and pick Qonnect Four, Checkers or Chess. They get an invitation to Accept or Decline, and the game opens in its own window. You can't invite someone who is set to Do Not Disturb or already in a game.

entries.q: How do I use proximity voice in Hub's QortalLand?
entries.a: Open the Proximity voice control and click Enable voice to talk with players near your avatar; it lists who is nearby and who is speaking. You can mute your microphone, change the volume, choose a microphone, and mute a single player. Move away from people and you stop hearing each other.

entries.q: How do I open a Q-App in Qortal Hub?
aliases: start an app in qortal hub
entries.a: Click Apps in the left sidebar to reach the Apps Dashboard, then click a pinned app, or type its name in the search box (Search apps or enter qortal:// link) and pick it. Explore opens the full Q-Apps library. The app opens in a tab, and its files download from QDN the first time.

entries.q: What is the Apps Dashboard in Hub?
entries.a: It is the page you get from Apps in the sidebar, like a new tab page. It has a search box for apps and qortal:// links, a Home button, an Explore button that opens the Q-Apps library, and your pinned apps, which you can drag into the order you like.

entries.q: How do I search for a Q-App from Hub's top bar?
aliases: search q-apps or enter qortal hub
entries.a: Click the search box in the top bar (Search Q-Apps or enter qortal://), type part of an app's name and press Enter: Hub opens the Q-Apps library with that search. Text that starts with qortal:// opens that link in a new tab instead.

entries.q: How do I pin a Q-App in Hub?
aliases: keep app on hub apps dashboard
entries.a: Open the app's page in the library and click Pin to dashboard, or click the pin button in the top bar while the app is open in a tab. Pinned apps appear on the Apps Dashboard.

entries.q: How do I unpin or reorder apps on Hub's Apps Dashboard?
entries.a: Drag a pinned app to a new place to change the order. To remove one, right-click it and choose Unpin app, or use Unpin from dashboard on its library page. These changes stay on this computer until you save them with Pinned Q-App backup.

entries.q: Which apps does Hub pin by default?
entries.a: Hub starts with its official apps pinned: Q-Blog, Q-Mail, Q-Trade, Q-Tube, Q-Wallets, Quitter (it shares its data with Torq), Names, Q-Assets, Q-Follow, Q-Fund, Q-Manager, Q-Mintership, Q-Node, Q-Search, Q-Share, Q-Shop and Q-Support. Like every Q-App, they load from QDN when you open them.

entries.q: How do I keep my pinned apps the same on another computer?
aliases: save pinned apps to qdn hub
entries.a: Open Account settings (the gear on Home's Account Overview card), System, Pinned Q-App backup, and click the save button. Save to QDN publishes your pinned apps as encrypted settings for a small fee; it needs a registered name and your own node, because the public node takes no uploads. On another computer, revert to QDN loads them. You can also export the list to a file and import it there.

entries.q: What is in Hub's Q-Apps library?
entries.a: Open it with Explore on the Apps Dashboard or Explore All Q-Apps on Home. Its tabs are Official Apps (with a featured row), Community Apps, Categories, My Apps (what you published) and + Private App. Each app has a card you click for its details page.

entries.q: How do I filter and sort apps in Hub's library?
entries.a: Use the search box at the top of the library, then the filters: Category, and Status (All, Installed or Not installed). Sort by can be Alphabetical, Newest, Oldest, Highest rated, Most reviewed or Recently updated.

entries.q: What do Installed and Not installed mean in Hub's library?
entries.a: Installed (ready) means the app's files are already on the node you use, so it opens straight away. Not installed means they still have to come from QDN: the app's page then shows Download instead of Open, and clicking it opens the app while your node fetches it.

entries.q: What does an app's page in Hub's library show?
entries.a: Click an app's card to see About, by @developer, its category, service, size, status, when it was published and updated, its tags, and its ratings. Buttons let you Open or Download it, Pin to dashboard and rate this app.

entries.q: How do I rate a Q-App in Hub?
entries.a: Open the app's page in the library and choose 1 to 5 stars under rate this app. You need a registered name, and the rating is saved on the blockchain as a poll vote, so you approve a small fee. It can take a couple of minutes for your rating to show.

entries.q: How many Q-Apps can I have open at once in Hub?
aliases: maximum number of tabs reached hub
entries.a: Up to 10 app tabs. When you try to open more, Hub says Maximum number of tabs reached. Close one to open another.

entries.q: How do I switch between open Q-Apps in Hub?
aliases: return to my open apps hub
entries.a: Open apps sit in tabs in the Apps view; click a tab to switch, or close it. From Home, the Opened apps button at the left of the top bar takes you back to your tabs; in Apps the same button turns into Home. Q-Chat opens as one of these tabs.

entries.q: Why does Hub ask me before closing an app tab?
aliases: are you sure you want to close this tab hub
entries.a: That app has locked its tab, usually because closing it now could lose work such as a publish in progress. Hub shows Close Tab Confirmation, sometimes with the app's own reason; choose Close Tab to close anyway or Cancel to keep it. An app has to ask your permission before it can lock its tab.

entries.q: How do I reload a Q-App or go back inside it in Hub?
entries.a: Use the buttons at the left of the top bar while the app's tab is open: the back arrow goes back inside the app when it has history, and Reload page reloads the app.

entries.q: How do I copy the link of the app page I'm viewing in Hub?
aliases: copy qortal link of app hub
share link to app page hub
qortal link of current page hub
entries.a: While an app is open, the top-bar search box shows its qortal:// link. Click the copy link button next to it; Hub says link copied to clipboard. Anyone with Hub or Qortal GO can open that link.

entries.q: How do I bookmark a Q-App page in Hub?
entries.a: With the app open, click the bookmark button in the top bar and choose Add bookmark, give it a name and a folder, and save. Hub saves the app location without its query parameters. You can also add any Qortal link by hand, such as qortal://APP/Name/path. Bookmarks are kept per account on this computer.

entries.q: How do I organise bookmarks into folders in Hub?
entries.a: In the Bookmarks menu, use Create folder (or New folder) and give it a Folder name. Bookmarks and folders can be edited, moved, renamed or removed. Deleting a folder doesn't delete its bookmarks; they move to the top level.

entries.q: What is + Private App in Hub's library?
entries.a: It lets you use or publish Q-Apps that only the members of a private (closed) group can open. Access app opens one shared with a group you belong to; Publish app lets a group admin publish an app encrypted for that group.

entries.q: How do I open a private Q-App shared in my group?
entries.a: In the library, click + Private App and stay on Access app. Choose the private group, then the publisher's name and the app's identifier (ask whoever shared it), and click Access. Hub downloads and decrypts it with the group's key and opens it in a tab.

entries.q: How do I publish a private Q-App to my group in Hub?
aliases: share app with group only hub
entries.a: You must be an admin of the group and use your own node for publishing. In the library, click + Private App, then Publish app. Select your Qortal name and the group, enter an identifier, choose the app's .zip file (up to 50 MB), give it an app name and a logo, and click Publish. Hub encrypts it for the group's members.

entries.q: What does Refetch apps and websites list do in Hub?
entries.a: It reloads the list of apps and websites from your node. Use it when an app you expect, such as one just published, doesn't show in the library yet; new publishes can take a few minutes to reach the network.

entries.q: Can a Q-App send me notifications in Hub?
entries.a: Yes, if you allow it. The first time an app asks, Hub shows its name with allow this app to send you Hub notifications? and the buttons allow and don't allow. Allowed apps show alerts in the bell and, unless muted, as desktop notifications.

entries.q: How do I stop one Q-App's notifications in Hub?
entries.a: Click the notifications bell, then the gear (Notification settings), and open the Q-Apps tab. For that app, turn on Disable OS push to stop desktop alerts but keep them in the bell, or click Revoke to take away its permission completely.

entries.q: What happens when a Q-App asks me to approve something in Hub?
entries.a: Hub shows a window naming the app and what it wants to do, such as publish to QDN, send coins, join a group or send a chat message, with any fee. Read it carefully and click Accept or Decline. Some requests have a box such as always authenticate automatically, which lets that app skip the question next time.

entries.q: How do I open Settings in Qortal Hub?
entries.a: Go to Home and click the gear next to your name on the Account Overview card (Account settings). The settings window has tabs on the left: Profile, Security, Blocked, Developer, System, Modules, Help and Reticulum. Close it with the X, Esc or a click outside.

entries.q: What can I change in Hub's System settings?
aliases: what is in hub system settings
entries.a: System holds the app-wide switches: Reticulum group chat, Attachment storage and Community call support (when Reticulum is on), Filter Developer Logs, Auto-Lock When Idle, Reduce App Notifications, When closing the window, Disable Startup Sound, Reduce UI Animations and Pinned Q-App backup.

entries.q: How do I choose what closing the Hub window does?
entries.a: In Account settings, System, use When closing the window: Always ask (the default), Minimize to tray (Minimize to dock on a Mac) or Quit completely. With Always ask, closing shows a Close Qortal Hub window with Minimize to Tray, Quit Completely and Cancel.

entries.q: How do I fully close Qortal Hub so it stops running?
entries.a: Right-click the Qortal Hub icon in the system tray and choose Quit App, then confirm with Quit; on a Mac the icon is in the Dock. You can also pick Quit Completely when Hub asks on closing, or set When closing the window to Quit completely. Quitting Hub doesn't stop Qortal Core, which runs as its own program.

entries.q: Where is Hub's tray icon and what does it do?
entries.a: On Windows and Linux, Hub puts an icon in the system tray; on a Mac it uses the Dock instead. The tray menu has Show App, which brings the window back, and Quit App. Its tooltip also tells you how many unread Q-Chat mentions you have.

entries.q: What does the number on Hub's app icon mean?
entries.a: It is the number of unread Q-Chat mentions. The tray icon's tooltip says the same, for example 1 unread mention. Read the mentions in Q-Chat and the number goes away.

entries.q: How do I turn off Hub's startup sound?
entries.a: Open Account settings, System, and switch on Disable Startup Sound. Reduce UI Animations also skips the intro sound.

entries.q: How do I reduce animations in Qortal Hub?
entries.a: Open Account settings, System, and switch on Reduce UI Animations. Hub then turns off most motion, including the logo intro. On Home, the Featured Q-Apps card also has its own Reduce motion switch for the moving previews.

entries.q: What is Filter Developer Logs in Hub's settings?
entries.a: It is a switch in System settings, on by default, that keeps Hub's log free of the very detailed technical lines while still recording warnings and errors. Leave it on unless a developer asks you for full logs.

entries.q: How do I mute all desktop notifications from Hub?
entries.a: Click Mute Notifications in Quick Tools on Home, or switch on Reduce App Notifications in Account settings, System; both are the same setting. Desktop alerts stop, but notifications still appear inside Hub in the bell. Click Enable Notifications to turn them back on.

entries.q: What does the notifications bell in Hub show?
entries.a: The bell in the top bar lists Q-App notifications such as new Q-Mail, and with Reticulum on, your Q-Chat mentions, missed calls and calendar reminders. Click an item to open it; closing the panel marks everything as seen, and items older than three days drop off. Payments don't appear there; see Wallet Activity on Home.

entries.q: What desktop notifications does Qortal Hub send?
entries.a: Hub can alert you to a payment you received (New payment received; click to open Wallets), notifications from Q-Apps you allowed, including Q-Mail, mentions in Q-Chat, direct messages from friends while Hub is in the background, and calendar reminders. They close by themselves after about 10 seconds, and clicking one brings Hub to the front.

entries.q: How do I switch Qortal Hub between light and dark mode?
entries.a: Use the sun or moon button at the bottom of the left sidebar, or the theme button at the bottom right of the login screen. Hub starts in dark mode and remembers your choice.

entries.q: Can I make my own colour theme in Hub?
entries.a: Not in Hub 3.0.3: custom themes are switched off, and the Theme Manager says Custom themes are currently disabled. You can choose light or dark mode.

entries.q: How do I change the language in Qortal Hub?
entries.a: Click the globe button with the language code (such as EN) in the left sidebar, or the language button at the bottom right of the login screen, and pick a language. Hub switches at once and remembers it. It doesn't follow your computer's language, so pick it yourself.

entries.q: Which languages does Qortal Hub support?
entries.a: Twelve: English, Arabic, German, Spanish, Estonian, Finnish, French, Italian, Japanese, Portuguese, Russian and Chinese. A few small texts, such as the lock screen and the close-window question, are still only in English.

entries.q: How does Qortal Hub update itself?
entries.a: Hub checks the official releases when it starts and once a day. When a new version is out it downloads it in the background, shows a desktop notification, and installs it when you quit Hub, so the next start runs the new version. You can also download the latest release from qortal.dev and install it over the old one.

entries.q: How do I see which version of Qortal Hub I have?
entries.a: Hover over Info in the left sidebar: the Core information panel ends with UI version, which is Hub's version. Home's Info card shows it as Hub, and the link at the bottom of the Q-Chat group rail shows the version too.

entries.q: Can I run two Qortal Hub windows at the same time?
entries.a: Yes. Each time you start Hub while it is already running, a new instance opens, up to 10. Every instance has its own window and profile, so you can unlock a different account in each, while they share your saved accounts, the app settings and one Reticulum connection.

entries.q: Why did a second Hub open instead of the one in my tray?
aliases: new hub window instead of tray
entries.a: Starting Hub again while it is hidden in the tray launches a new instance rather than showing the hidden one. To get the first one back, use Show App in the tray menu (or click the Dock icon on a Mac), and close the extra one.

entries.q: How do I reveal my private key in Hub?
entries.a: Open Account settings and go to Security. Type your wallet password, click Decrypt, then Copy key if you need it. Hub warns you never to share it: anyone who has it could control the wallet and its funds. The key is hidden again when Settings closes; only reveal it to recover or move your wallet.

entries.q: What is in the Profile tab of Hub's settings?
entries.a: Profile shows your Current name (or No name registered, with a Register name link) and your Wallet address. Buying, selling or changing names is done in the Names Q-App, which the tab points you to.

entries.q: What is the menu button at the top left of Hub's window?
entries.a: The menu button in Hub's title bar opens the standard application menu with File (the app menu on a Mac), View and Edit. Zoom and full screen are in View. Hub's own settings are not there; they are under the gear on Home.

entries.q: How do I create, rename or remove a channel in Hub?
entries.a: As a group admin, right-click the group in the rail (or use the channel list) and choose Create channel: enter a channel name, pick the type (Open, Read-only or Admin), set its expiry and click Create channel. Right-click a channel for Channel Settings to rename it or change who can post, or Remove Channel, which asks you to type delete because it can't be undone.

entries.q: What do the markers in Hub's channel list mean?
entries.a: A channel can show an unread mention marker (with a count when there are several), an Unread reply marker when someone answered you, or a plain unread messages marker. A small timer-style icon means the channel's messages are deleted automatically after its expiry time; hover over any marker for its meaning.

entries.q: How do I see a group's members in Hub?
aliases: who is in this group hub
entries.a: Click Members in the group's header to open the members panel (click it again, Hide Members, to close it). Members are sorted into Admins, Lounge, Park, Members and Offline, and you can collapse each section. Click a member to open their user card.

entries.q: What do Lounge and Park mean in Hub's members list?
entries.a: They are places in the group's QortalLand: Lounge lists members who are in the lounge right now and Park those in the park. Members online in Q-Chat but not in QortalLand are under Members, and the rest under Offline.

entries.q: How do I block someone by name or address in Hub?
aliases: add name to block list hub
block someone in direct messages hub
entries.a: In Q-Chat's Direct Messages list, use the blocked users button (it shows only when you use your own node). Type the Qortal name or address and choose Block. Blocking an address affects how your node handles their transactions; blocking a name hides their data across Hub. You can also block from User Search.

entries.q: How do I get a reminder for a group event in Hub?
entries.a: Each event has a Reminder: None, At start, 10 minutes before, 30 minutes before, 1 hour before or 1 day before. When it is due, Hub puts Reminder: and the event's title in the notifications bell, and shows a desktop alert if you aren't looking at Hub.

entries.q: How do I share a group calendar event in Hub?
entries.a: Open the event in Group Calendar and click Share to copy its link. Paste it in a chat: Hub turns it into a preview card that opens the right group and event. People who aren't members of that group are asked to join it, or request to join, before they can see the event.

entries.q: Who can add or change events in a group's calendar in Hub?
entries.a: Only the group's admins and owner. They see Add event, and on an event Edit event and Delete event; deleting removes every occurrence of a repeating event and can't be undone. Other members can view the events and share their links.

entries.q: Hub says I need at least 4 QORT to send a message. Why?
aliases: you need at least 4 qort to send a message hub
cant send message low balance hub
entries.a: That rule only applies to the old (legacy) Q-Chat, which Hub uses when Reticulum is turned off. With Reticulum on, Hub doesn't check your balance before you chat. Turn Reticulum back on in Account settings, Reticulum (and Reticulum group chat under System), or hold at least 4 QORT.

entries.q: What happened to General Chat in Qortal Hub?
aliases: where is general chat in hub
entries.a: The old Hub-wide General Chat was removed in Hub 0.6.0. Today each Q-Chat group has its own built-in General channel instead, whose messages last one month. For a big public place to talk, join the Qortal Project group.

entries.q: What is new in Qortal Hub 3?
entries.a: Hub 3.0, released in August 2026, rebuilt Q-Chat on Reticulum: live chat with channels and categories, replies and reactions, attachments, message expiry and search; faster direct messages with Saved Messages; one-to-one calls with screen sharing and group calls for up to 15 people; group calendars; link previews; QortalLand; and Find Groups with Group Score. Qortal identities, groups and admin roles stay at its core.

entries.q: What changed in Hub 3.0.1, 3.0.2 and 3.0.3?
entries.a: 3.0.1 fixed memory leaks and message relaying, added the user status picker, and started sending call audio over WebRTC with Reticulum as fallback. 3.0.2 cut CPU use during chat history repairs. 3.0.3 (August 2026) added the guided first-run tour, a more prominent Q-Chat card on Home, faster group history sync and an opt-in Community transport setting.

entries.q: What came with Qortal Hub 2.0?
entries.a: Hub 2.0 (June 2026) brought a redesign of Hub, Q-App notifications, online presence, and beta versions of group calls, calls with friends in direct messages and file transfers in direct messages. Hub 2.0.1 added the option to edit the Reticulum config by hand.

entries.q: Where do files I save from a Q-App go in Hub?
aliases: would you like to download hub
entries.a: When a Q-App wants to save a file, Hub first asks would you like to download: with the file's name. Accept, and your computer's Save dialog opens so you choose the folder and name. Nothing is saved without that approval.

entries.q: Can I build Qortal Hub from source code?
entries.a: Yes. You need Node.js, plus Python 3.9 or newer and Git for the Reticulum parts. In the project folder run npm install, npm run build and npx cap sync @capacitor-community/electron, then in the electron folder npm install and npm run electron:start to start it, or npm run electron:make-local to make a package. Released installers already include everything, so most people never need this.

entries.q: Can I change how my avatar looks in Hub's QortalLand?
entries.a: Yes. In QortalLand click Customize to open the Character panel. Pick a character skin (Original, Nova, Luna, Aqua, Amber or Frost) and choose options for hair, face and clothes.

entries.q: What do AFK and DND mean in Hub's QortalLand?
entries.a: They are status tags shown over a player's avatar: AFK means away from the keyboard and DND means Do Not Disturb. You can't invite a player who is set to Do Not Disturb, or one already in a game, to play.

entries.q: Where do I see my QORT balance in Hub?
aliases: how much qort do i have hub
entries.a: Click your avatar at the top right: the menu shows BALANCE with your QORT. Home's Info card shows QORT Balance too, and the Send QORT window shows your Balance before you send. For other coins, open Q-Wallets.

entries.q: Can I see my seedphrase again later in Hub?
entries.a: No. Hub shows the seedphrase only while you create the account. Later, Account settings, Security can reveal your private key, and your backup file with its password also restores the account. If you never saved the seedphrase, keep at least one backup file in a safe place.

entries.q: What does a user card show in Hub's Q-Chat?
aliases: click a name in chat hub
entries.a: Click someone's name or avatar in a chat or the members list. The card shows their name, avatar, minter level, QORT balance and Qortal address (with copy address), and buttons to message them, send QORT, view profile in User Search, or hide user in this group.

entries.q: What are Official Apps and Community Apps in Hub's library?
entries.a: Official Apps is the curated list Hub ships with, such as Q-Mail, Q-Tube, Q-Trade, Q-Wallets, Q-Share, Names and Q-Mintership, with a featured row at the top. Community Apps lists the other apps and websites people have published on QDN. Both open the same way; check an app's details and ratings before you trust it with approvals.

entries.q: How do I browse Q-Apps by category in Hub?
entries.a: Open the Q-Apps library and click the Categories tab. Pick a category card to see its apps, and use Sort by to order them, for example by Highest rated or Newest.

entries.q: How do I open a QDN website in Hub?
entries.a: Type its link into the search box at the top, such as qortal://WEBSITE/Name, and press Enter; a link with just a name, like qortal://Name, opens that name's website. It opens in a tab like a Q-App. Websites from your own name and others also appear in the Q-Apps library.

entries.q: Can others see when I'm typing in Hub's Q-Chat?
entries.a: Yes. Hub shows a typing indicator to the others in a direct chat or channel while you write, and you see theirs. There is no switch to turn it off.

entries.q: Can I edit, delete or react to direct messages in Hub?
entries.a: Yes, just as in groups: hover over a message to react, Reply, Edit your own message or delete it. Edits and deletions reach the other person and all of your own devices.

entries.q: Where are Qortal Hub's log files?
entries.a: Hub writes a log called qortalHub.log in a logs folder inside its app data folder, and starts a new file when it reaches about 10 MB. Filter Developer Logs in System settings keeps the very detailed lines out while still recording warnings and errors. If someone helps you with a problem, the log is useful; never share your seedphrase, backup file or password with it.

entries.q: Can I put an emoji in a channel name in Hub?
entries.a: Yes. When you create a channel or open its Channel Settings, use the emoji button next to the channel name to pick an emoji and add it to the name.

entries.q: How do I reorder channels and categories in Hub?
entries.a: Group admins drag a channel or a whole category to a new place in the channel list. Anyone can collapse or expand a category by clicking its heading, and drag the edge of the channel list (Resize channel list) to make it wider or narrower.

entries.q: Can a calendar event repeat in Hub?
entries.a: Yes. Under Repeats choose Does not repeat, Daily, Weekly, Monthly or Yearly, and optionally a Repeat until date, which must be on or after the start date. Deleting a repeating event removes all its occurrences.

entries.q: Which time zone does a Hub calendar event use?
