entries.a: The event's own Time zone, chosen when it is created (Event times use this time zone). Hub also shows the time converted to your time, so members in other countries see when it starts for them. All day events have no start and end time.

entries.q: A file in Hub's chat says Not downloaded. What do I do?
entries.a: Click the file to download it from the members who have it; when it is done, click Open file to open it with your computer's default app. If it says Download failed, click Try again, since no one holding the file may have been online. If your computer can't open it, Hub says The operating system could not open this file.

entries.q: How long can a Q-Chat message be in Hub?
entries.a: Up to 4000 bytes per message, which is about 4000 plain letters; emoji and many other scripts use more than one byte each. Near the limit Hub shows a counter (your message size is of N bytes out of a maximum of 4000), and a longer message won't send. Split long text into several messages.

entries.q: Why does Hub make the pictures I send in chat smaller?
aliases: why are my photos smaller hub
entries.a: So they travel quickly peer to peer over Reticulum. Hub converts pictures to WebP and scales them to at most 1200 pixels wide before sending, and turns GIFs into small animated WebP files of about 500 KB, showing a progress note while it works. To share an original file, send it as a file attachment instead.

entries.q: Hub says You cannot write in this channel. Why?
aliases: you cannot write in this channel hub
entries.a: The channel is limited by its admins. A Read-only channel says Only admins can post. Everyone can read, and an Admin channel is only for admins and the group owner. Post in another channel of the group, or ask an admin if you think you should be able to write there.

entries.q: Why do my friends show in Hub's Direct Messages list?
aliases: person in dms i never messaged hub
entries.a: Hub lists the people you have added as friends in Direct Messages even before you have chatted, so you can message or call them quickly. Saved Messages always comes first, and other chats follow with the most recent at the top.

entries.q: What happens if I start a new call while I'm already in one in Hub?
aliases: join call while in call hub
entries.a: Hub keeps you in one call at a time. When you start or join another, it warns that you are already in a call and that continuing will fully drop it before connecting the new one. Choose Drop and continue to switch, or cancel to stay where you are.

entries.q: Why didn't the guided tour start in Hub?
aliases: tour only available on desktop hub
start tour window too small hub
entries.a: The tour needs a Hub window at least 1250 pixels wide, so make the window bigger or maximise it. It also runs only once per computer: after you skip or finish it, start it again from Account settings, Help, Restart Tutorial.

entries.q: Why is Getting Started still asking for my 2 QORT in Hub?
aliases: qort arrived but not ticked hub
entries.a: The step ticks off once your balance is at least 2 QORT, or your recent confirmed payments add up to 2 QORT. A payment takes a minute or two to confirm before it counts. When it shows QORT acquired, press Next to go on to registering your name.

entries.q: What does the node line on Hub's login screen mean?
entries.a: It tells you which node Hub will use when you unlock: Using local node (with a green dot), Using public node, or Using followed by the name of a custom node. Click Connection Mode next to it to switch.

entries.q: Why can't I enter QortalLand from Hub's Home?
aliases: enable reticulum to enter qortalland hub
join a q-chat group to enter qortalland hub
qortal land button not working hub
entries.a: Hub tells you what is missing: Enable Reticulum to enter QortalLand means Reticulum is switched off (turn it on in Account settings, Reticulum), and Join a Q-Chat group to enter QortalLand means you aren't in any group yet. Join a group in Q-Chat, then try again.

entries.q: What happens to Hub when my computer goes to sleep?
entries.a: Unless Auto-Lock When Idle is set to Disabled, Hub locks when the computer goes to sleep or its screen locks, so you unlock it with your password afterwards. When the computer wakes up, Hub reconnects to Reticulum by itself.

entries.q: What happens when I click a web link in Hub's Q-Chat?
aliases: open website link from chat hub
entries.a: Ordinary web links (http, https or www) open in your computer's normal web browser, outside Hub. qortal:// links open inside Hub as an app, website or preview card. Be careful with links from people you don't know.

entries.q: How do I copy a message's text in Hub's Q-Chat?
entries.a: Right-click the message. The menu has quick reactions at the top, then Copy Message, Reply Message, and for your own messages Edit Message and Delete Message. Copy Message puts its text on the clipboard.

entries.q: How do I jump to the newest or unread messages in a Hub channel?
entries.a: When you have scrolled up, use jump to latest (or scroll to bottom) to return to the newest message. If unread messages are waiting, Hub says unread messages below and offers scroll to Unread Messages; a New messages line marks where they start.

entries.q: What is the Welcome back screen in Hub's Q-Chat?
entries.a: It is what Q-Chat shows when no group is selected: Welcome back, with Here's what you've missed while you were away and your groups with their new messages and mentions (View all servers shows the rest). If nothing is new it says You're all caught up. Browse Communities and What's New? buttons sit below.

entries.q: Can I message someone who has no registered name in Hub?
entries.a: Yes. In Direct Messages, click New chat and enter their Qortal address instead of a name. Without a name they show by their address, so double-check you typed it right.

entries.q: What can I do when I click another player in Hub's QortalLand?
entries.a: A panel opens with fun effects to send (Buzz, Love, Devil, Angel, Rain and Sunshine), Send QORT, Call followed by their name for a voice call, and Play games for Qonnect Four, Checkers or Chess. Calls and games aren't offered while the player is set to Do Not Disturb, or is already in a call or a game.

entries.q: Are Hub's settings shared between my accounts?
aliases: do settings follow my account hub
entries.a: Some are. Close-window behaviour, Auto-Lock, the startup sound, the Reticulum switches, Community call support and the attachment storage limit apply to every account on this computer. Reduce App Notifications, mention notifications and your Home hotkeys are saved per account. Animations, Dev Mode, Home modules and Privacy Mode are kept by each Hub window on this computer.

entries.q: What if the public node is down when I use Hub?
entries.a: If Hub can't reach the public node, it opens Set up Qortal Core with Public nodes are currently unavailable and suggests keeping the window open while your own Core starts and syncs. Start Core there, or switch to a custom node you trust, and try again later.

entries.q: Will Qortal Hub run on my Linux distribution?
entries.a: Most likely, on 64-bit x86 or ARM. The AppImage builds are made on Debian 11 so they also run on older systems, and AppImages need the FUSE 2 library, which the qortal.dev install script adds for you. On Debian or Ubuntu you can use the .deb package instead.

entries.q: Does Qortal Hub open qortal://pay payment links?
entries.a: Not in Hub 3.0.3: its code has no handling for qortal://pay links or payment QR codes, which are Qortal GO features. In Hub, open Send QORT (your avatar menu or Send on Home's Wallet Activity) and type or paste the address or registered name and the amount.

entries.q: How do I vote on a poll in Hub's chat?
entries.a: Click show poll on the poll card in the message, pick an option and click vote. Hub asks you to accept a VOTE_ON_POLL transaction with its small fee, and reminds you that polls are public. You can vote once; the results update after the network confirms it.

entries.q: Hub says my backup file doesn't contain a valid account. Why?
aliases: this backup file does not contain a valid account
entries.a: The file you dropped isn't a Qortal account backup, or it is damaged. Pick the .json file whose name starts with qortal_backup_ followed by your address. If Hub instead says These accounts are already stored on this device, the account was imported before and is already in your list.

entries.q: Is there a do not disturb mode in Qortal Hub?
entries.a: Not as such. Setting your status to Busy only shows others a red dot; it doesn't silence anything. To stop desktop alerts, click Mute Notifications in Quick Tools on Home (alerts still collect in the bell), and to stop calls reaching you, set your status to Offline.

entries.q: When did Qortal Hub first come out?
entries.a: The first test versions of Qortal Hub were published in late 2024. Version 1.0.0 followed in March 2026, Hub 2.0 in June 2026 with calls and presence, and Hub 3.0 in August 2026 with the new Reticulum Q-Chat.

entries.q: What does the Q-Manager button in a Hub group do?
entries.a: It opens the Q-Manager app in a panel beside the chat, set to the group you are viewing, so you can use it without leaving Q-Chat. Click the button again, or the X on the panel, to close it.

entries.q: Why does Hub show Unnamed account in my account list?
aliases: account has no name hub login
why is my account unnamed hub
entries.a: The account has no registered name yet and you haven't given it a label on this computer. Use the edit button on it (Edit account label and note) to add a Name and a Note, or register a Qortal name, which then shows as its primary name.

entries.q: How do I change my wallet password in Hub?
entries.a:
Hub has no change-password button, but you can do this:
1. On Home, click Backup Wallet in Quick Tools, enter your current password, untick keeping the current password, type the new one and save the file.
2. Check the new file opens, for example with Import account, Authenticate now.
3. Remove the saved account (Edit account label and note, Remove).
4. Import account, Backup file: pick the new file and unlock with the new password.
Older backup files still open with the old password.

entries.q: Why don't I get desktop alerts for some direct messages in Hub?
entries.a: Hub raises a desktop alert for a direct message only when it comes from someone on your friends list, is still unread, and Hub is hidden or not the active window. Add the person as a friend if you want their messages to alert you. Mentions in groups alert you separately.

entries.q: What keyboard shortcuts does Hub's Q-Chat have?
entries.a: Enter sends and Shift+Enter starts a new line (unless you tick disable enter in the Formatting tray). Type @ to mention someone. Pointing at your own message and pressing Shift+Delete deletes it. In Hub's settings window, Esc closes it.

entries.q: Why does Hub's Home look different in a small window?
entries.a: Home arranges its cards in three columns when the window is at least 1250 pixels wide. In a narrower window the cards stack instead, and the guided tour waits until the window is wide enough. Maximise Hub to get the full layout.

entries.q: What is in Q-Chat's Group Settings in Hub?
entries.a: Despite the name, the Group Settings gear at the bottom of the Q-Chat rail holds settings for all of Q-Chat: Accessibility (Text size and Messages, with Highlight my messages), Notifications (Mentions) and Legacy (Threads). Settings for one group, such as its channels, are in that group's right-click menu instead.

entries.q: What is in the avatar menu at the top right of Hub?
entries.a: Click your avatar to see your name (or no primary name) and Authenticated account, the STATUS choices Online, Busy and Offline, your QORT BALANCE, your ADDRESS with a copy button, and a Send QORT button. The button to its right is Lock or log out.

entries.q: Is minting on Qortal the same as mining?
entries.a: No. Qortal has no mining. Blocks are made by minting: approved accounts run a full node, and every online minter shares each block's reward by level instead of one winner taking it. There are no mining rigs and no race for power, and better hardware earns nothing extra.

entries.q: Is minting the same as staking?
aliases: do i stake qort to mint
entries.a: No. Staking pays whoever locks up the most coins. Qortal minting has no coin-holding requirement and doesn't pay by balance: rewards depend on your minting level and on staying online. There is nothing to stake and nothing to lock up.

entries.q: Do I need to hold a lot of QORT to mint?
aliases: does my qort balance affect minting
entries.a: No. Minting doesn't reward you for the QORT you hold, and you don't lock any up. What counts is being approved into the MINTER group and keeping your node online with your minting key. You only need a little QORT for fees, such as 0.01 QORT to join the MINTER group.

entries.q: What is a minter?
entries.a: A minter is an account in the MINTER group whose full node helps produce blocks. Minters keep a node online with their minting key, and in return share each block's reward by level. Minting rights come through a nomination and Minter Admin approval; they can't be bought.

entries.q: What is the MINTER group?
aliases: what is the minter group for
entries.a: The MINTER group is the on-chain group whose members are allowed to mint; its group ID is 694. Joining it through an approved invite is what makes you a minter. Its invites, removals and admin changes only take effect with group approval from its Minter Admins.

entries.q: What is Mintership?
entries.a: Mintership is the system that decides how accounts get and keep minting rights on Qortal. It replaced sponsorship: community-elected Minter Admins approve new minters by on-chain group approval, and today level 5+ minters nominate the candidates. The wiki explains the name as mentorship plus minting.

entries.q: What does a minting node actually do?
aliases: what does my node do when minting
what happens when my node mints
entries.a: Your node stays synced with the chain and, using your minting key, signs an online signature in each minting submission window to prove it is a live minter. Those signatures decide who shares the block rewards. Nodes of level 5+ minters can also sign new blocks. It all runs automatically while Qortal Core is running.

entries.q: Is minting automatic once it is set up?
aliases: do i have to do anything to keep minting
entries.a: Yes. Once your minting key is on your node, Qortal Core submits your minting signatures by itself. Your part is to keep the node running, synced and up to date. You only need to open Qortal Hub to check or change something.

entries.q: Do I need to keep Qortal Hub open to mint?
aliases: does closing qortal hub stop minting
logged out of hub still minting
entries.a: No. Minting is done by Qortal Core, the node itself, not by the Hub window. Minting continues while Core keeps running and stays synced, so you can close Hub and open it only when you need to manage things.

entries.q: Why is minting good for the Qortal network?
entries.a: More independent minters running full nodes around the world make the network more resilient and harder to censor. Rewards are spread across all online minters instead of going to the biggest holder or fastest machine. Minters also build up levels, which give long-term contributors more weight in Qortal's polls.

entries.q: Is minting about making money?
entries.a: Not mainly. The Minter Guide describes minting as supporting the network and its infrastructure, not extracting profit, and calls Qortal sovereignty-driven rather than money-driven. Nominators and Minter Admins look for people who share those values, and a nomination focused on earning QORT is a weak one.

entries.q: Should I focus on minting as a new Qortal user?
entries.a: Not yet. The Welcome to Qortal app advises new users to explore the network, learn how it works and build real participation first. Minting is a long-term goal for people who want to support the infrastructure, and getting nominated rests on that track record anyway.

entries.q: Is there KYC to become a minter?
aliases: do i need id to mint
entries.a: No. Qortal has no KYC: no ID, email or phone number. Instead, Minter Admins look at your on-chain activity to judge whether you are a real, unique person who takes part in Qortal, which is why publishing and visible participation matter.

entries.q: Does the block signer get extra QORT?
aliases: who gets the block reward minting
do i earn more for signing blocks
entries.a: No. On Qortal the minter who signs a block earns nothing extra. Rewards are shared among all online minters by level tier, so minters don't compete with each other. Signing just moves the chain forward.

entries.q: Who can sign new blocks on Qortal?
entries.a: Only minters at level 5 or higher sign blocks; level 5 is when nodes start submitting blocks by default. Higher levels are more likely to be the signer, which makes attacks that need many blocks in a row very unlikely. Signing earns no extra reward.

entries.q: What is MemPoW?
entries.a: MemPoW is Qortal's memory-based proof of work. Each minting signature must carry a MemPoW result, computed at a fixed difficulty with about 1 MB of RAM, so it doesn't max out the CPU. Its job is to limit how many minting keys one computer can run, ideally two. Q-Chat also uses it against spam.

entries.q: Why can a node only have two minting keys?
entries.a: Because of MemPoW: every minting signature needs a memory-based proof of work, and one computer can only compute about two in each minting window. That stops one machine from running many minting accounts. Qortal Hub follows the same limit and won't start minting on a node that already has two minting keys.

entries.q: How does Qortal know a minter is really online?
entries.a: Every minting node signs an online signature with its minting key, plus a MemPoW result, and submits it inside the minting window. All nodes check these, so a node can't pretend to be online. Only minters whose valid signatures are in get credit and rewards for that round.

entries.q: What does online minter mean?
entries.a: An online minter is one whose node is synced, has its minting key assigned and is submitting valid minting signatures. Only online minters are paid, and each tier's share is split among the online minters in it. The Minter Guide's home page shows how many are online now.

entries.q: How many minters does Qortal have?
entries.a: The number changes all the time. The Minter Guide's home page shows live counts of active minters (members of the MINTER group) and of minters online now, and Q-Mintership's Stats page shows online minters by level. In Hub, the Minting panel shows how many minters are in your own tier.

entries.q: What do I need before I can be nominated for minting?
aliases: what do i need to mint
what i need for a minting nomination
entries.a:
The Minter Guide lists four things:
1. A Qortal account with a registered name.
2. A full node, synced and online.
3. A real track record of using Qortal over a reasonable period.
4. A level 5+ minter willing to nominate you.

entries.q: Do I need a registered name to become a minter?
aliases: does a nominee need a registered name
entries.a: For nomination, yes. Qortal Core itself doesn't check for a name when minting, but the Minter Guide lists a registered name as the first requirement, and Q-Mintership won't publish a nomination for an account without one: 'Nominee must have a registered Qortal name.' A name also lets you publish on QDN, the best evidence of real participation.

entries.q: Do I need my own node before I'm nominated?
aliases: run a node to get nominated
entries.a: Yes. You need a full node that stays synced and online: a desktop install, a dedicated machine, a VPS or a QORTector. That node is what will mint once you have a minting key, and the Minter Guide's sample nominations mention candidates who already ran a synced node for months.

entries.q: How can I prepare to be nominated?
entries.a:
The Minter Guide suggests:
1. Use the network visibly: publish on QDN, use Q-Mail, Q-Chat and Q-Trade.
2. Get to know people in Q-Chat and the community.
3. Contribute: build, create content, help newcomers, translate, report issues.
4. Learn how Qortal and minting work.
5. Let a level 5+ minter who knows your work nominate you.

entries.q: What activity do Minter Admins value most?
aliases: what counts as track record minting
prove i'm a real user minting
entries.a:
The Minter Guide ranks it from least to most useful:
1. Viewing content: not visible on chain, so it proves nothing.
2. Joining groups and chatting: good, but chat leaves little lasting proof.
3. Publishing data on Q-Share, Torq, Q-Tube, websites and so on: the strongest, because publishes don't expire.
Quality counts more than quantity.

entries.q: Does chatting in Q-Chat count toward a nomination?
aliases: is chatting enough to be nominated
entries.a: It helps people get to know you, but it is weak evidence: chat messages expire (from a day to a month, depending on the channel), so they leave little lasting proof. Publishing on QDN is the strongest signal, so pair chatting with things you publish.

entries.q: Can I become a minter without coding skills?
entries.a: Yes. Nominators look for real participation, not code. You can publish files on Q-Share, videos on Q-Tube or posts on Torq, help newcomers, or build a website by drag and drop with Qortal Web Builder (qortal://APP/QWB). The Minter Guide's examples include non-developers who were strong candidates.

entries.q: How long should I use Qortal before seeking a nomination?
aliases: when to look for a nominator
how long to wait to mint
entries.a: There is no fixed time. The Minter Guide says to use Qortal genuinely for a decent stretch first, and the wiki's earlier guidance was at least about a month of activity. Its sample nominations describe candidates active for many months. What matters is a real track record someone can verify.

entries.q: How do I find someone to nominate me?
entries.a: Nominations are strongest from someone who knows you or has seen your work, so get to know people in Q-Chat and the wider community. Nominators choose community members they think would make good minters. The wiki also mentions the Q-Mintership Forum as one place to meet a nominator.

entries.q: Can a Minter Admin nominate someone?
entries.a: Yes, if their account is level 5 or higher. Q-Mintership's Create Nomination only works for a MINTER member or Minter Admin at level 5+, and being a Minter Admin doesn't skip the level rule. The decision then rests with the Minter Admins' votes and approvals as usual, and nobody can nominate themselves.

entries.q: What happens after I'm nominated?
entries.a: In Q-Mintership, a poll is attached to your nomination card, and the community and Minter Admins comment and vote. When about 40% of the Minter Admins have voted yes, an admin creates your MINTER group invite, which then needs approvals from about 40% of the admins. Once it is active, your card shows INVITED and a Join MINTER Group button; join, then start minting from Hub.

entries.q: What are the two 40% thresholds in Q-Mintership?
entries.a:
There are two separate steps:
1. Poll: about 40% of the Minter Admins vote yes on the nomination card, which unlocks the admin action buttons.
2. Approval: an admin creates the GROUP_INVITE, and it only becomes active when about 40% of the Minter Admins sign it with GROUP_APPROVAL.
The Minter Guide's home page shows how many votes that is today.

entries.q: What is GROUP_APPROVAL in Mintership?
entries.a: GROUP_APPROVAL is Qortal's group-decision transaction, a kind of multi-signature. For the MINTER group, invites, removals and admin changes only take effect once enough Minter Admins have signed with GROUP_APPROVAL, about 40% of them. No single admin can grant or remove minting rights alone.

entries.q: How do I accept my MINTER group invite?
entries.a: Once enough Minter Admins have approved it, your nomination card in Q-Mintership shows INVITED and a Join MINTER Group button; press it to send a JOIN_GROUP transaction (0.01 QORT). The invite also appears in Hub's group invites, where Join works too. When it confirms, you are in the MINTER group.

entries.q: How much QORT do I need to join the MINTER group?
aliases: qort needed to join minter group
entries.a: Joining is a JOIN_GROUP transaction, which costs 0.01 QORT and has to come from your confirmed balance. If your balance is empty, ask your nominator or someone you know on Qortal to send you a little.

entries.q: How long does the nomination process take?
aliases: how long to get approved as a minter
how long until i can mint
entries.a: It depends on how quickly the Minter Admins review, vote and approve; there is no fixed time. Once an admin creates your MINTER invite, the admins have the group's approval window of 10,080 blocks, about a week or more, to approve it before it expires. Check your card on the Minter Board for its status.

entries.q: What happens if my nomination runs out of time?
entries.a: If the MINTER invite doesn't get enough approvals within its approval window of 10,080 blocks, it expires. Your account and level stay exactly as they were, and you can be nominated again; re-nominations are normal. The same goes after a rejection.

entries.q: Can more than one person support a nomination?
entries.a: There is one nomination card per person: Q-Mintership blocks a second card for someone who already has one ('Duplicate nominations are blocked'). Others show their support by voting Yes on the card's poll and by commenting, and the wiki notes that more community support helps the Minter Admins decide faster.

entries.q: What should a good nomination include?
aliases: what to put in a nomination
entries.a:
The Minter Guide suggests five parts:
1. Who: their registered name and a one-line introduction.
2. Relationship: how you know them or their work.
3. Contributions: apps, content, community help, time active.
4. Evidence: qortal:// links anyone can check.
5. Why mint: how it fits Qortal's values.

entries.q: What makes a nomination weak?
aliases: what not to write in a nomination
entries.a: A generic one-liner like 'good person, please approve', claims nobody can check, nominating a stranger as a favour, focusing on earning QORT, or a brand-new account with no history. A nominator who disappears after publishing also hurts. Minter Admins need something they can verify.

entries.q: How do I nominate someone in Q-Mintership?
aliases: how to nominate someone for minting
entries.a:
You need a level 5+ account:
1. Open Q-Mintership (qortal://APP/Q-Mintership) and sign in.
2. Go to the Minter Board and press Create Nomination.
3. Fill in the nominee's name or address, a short summary, your statement and qortal:// links.
4. Press Publish and confirm in Hub.
A poll is attached and the card is open for votes.

entries.q: Who can't be nominated for minting?
entries.a: Q-Mintership blocks nominating yourself, anyone already in the MINTER group or a Minter Admin, anyone without a registered name, and anyone who already has a nomination card from another nominator; vote and comment on that card instead.

entries.q: Can I edit my nomination after publishing it?
entries.a: Yes. In Q-Mintership, open the nomination form again for the same nominee: it loads your card and the button becomes Update Nomination. Only the card's original publisher can update it, and if its poll is missing, a new one is created.

entries.q: Should I tell someone before I nominate them?
entries.a: Yes. The Minter Guide suggests giving the candidate a heads-up so they are ready to join the MINTER group once approved: they need a little QORT for the joining fee, a synced node, and to watch their card for the Join MINTER Group button.

entries.q: What links should I add to a nomination?
aliases: what to link in a nomination
entries.a: Add qortal:// links to things anyone can check: the person's Q-Apps or websites, Q-Tube videos, Q-Share files, Torq posts and their registered name. Minter Admins do open the linked content and value quality over quantity. Q-Mintership's form has a Links (qortal://...) section, with Add Another Link for more.

entries.q: Is there a template for writing a nomination?
entries.a: Yes. The Minter Guide (qortal://WEBSITE/Q-Minter) has a Great Nomination Examples page with a template: how you know them, what they've contributed, why they should mint, and evidence links. It also shows strong and weak example nominations side by side.

entries.q: Why should I only nominate people I know?
entries.a: A nomination is a vouch, and your reputation is attached to it. The Minter Guide asks nominators not to nominate strangers as a favour or inflate claims: Minter Admins verify what they can, and a weak or wrong nomination reflects on the nominator too. Nomination sources are tracked, so abuse can be spotted.

entries.q: Do nominators earn anything for nominating?
entries.a: No. The block reward has no share for nominators, just as sponsors under the old system earned nothing extra. A nomination is a vouch that puts your reputation behind someone. Q-Mintership keeps statistics on nominators' results, and its developers have talked about a 'best nominator' award.

entries.q: What is the Minter Board?
entries.a: The Minter Board is the public board in Q-Mintership where level 5+ minters publish nomination cards. The community and Minter Admins discuss and vote on each card there, and each card shows its poll results and the state of the person's MINTER invite.

entries.q: What is the Admin Board in Q-Mintership?
entries.a: The Admin Board is an encrypted board only Minter Admins can read. They publish cards about a minter or a topic there and discuss and vote on them privately. Once about 40% of the admins vote yes on a card about a minter, Create KICK Tx and Create BAN Tx buttons appear, and a removal then needs the other admins' approvals.

entries.q: What is the MAM board in Q-Mintership?
aliases: propose a new minter admin board
entries.a: The MAM board (called the AR Board in the code) is where proposals to add or remove Minter Admins are made and reviewed, separate from nominations. It also lists the current Minter Admins. Changes proposed there still need group approval from the existing Minter Admins.

entries.q: What is the Q-Mintership Forum?
entries.a: It is the discussion area inside Q-Mintership, with public rooms for general and minter-focused talk, a private admin room, replies and attachments. The wiki mentions it as one place to look for a nominator.

entries.q: Can anyone vote on a nomination?
entries.a: Anyone can vote Yes or No on a card's poll, but Q-Mintership only counts votes from minters and Minter Admins in its totals; other votes show only in the poll details. Admin and minter votes are counted separately, and only the Minter Admins' votes and approvals decide.

entries.q: How much does my vote count on a nomination poll?
aliases: does my level affect my vote
entries.a: In Q-Mintership, each voter's weight is their blocks minted, so long-time minters count for more. The card shows Admin Yes and No, Minter Yes and No, and the totals. The Minter Admins' votes are what unlock the next step.

entries.q: Can Minter Admins change their vote on a nomination?
entries.a: Yes. The Minter Guide notes that Minter Admins can change their first vote as they review the activity on a card. The invite is only created once about 40% of the admins' votes are yes, and it then needs their separate approvals.

entries.q: What is the Q-Mintership+ app?
entries.a: Q-Mintership+ is a pre-release test version: a community rewrite of Q-Mintership from the Q-Apps+ suite, with a simpler on-chain approval flow and an account Explorer. For nominating, voting and joining the MINTER group, use the published Q-Mintership (qortal://APP/Q-Mintership).

entries.q: What is the difference between Q-Mintership and Q-Mintership+?
entries.a: Q-Mintership is the published app to use: nomination cards on the Minter Board with a poll, then an admin-made invite that the Minter Admins approve. Q-Mintership+ is a pre-release test version that drops the poll and lets admins approve or reject on chain directly. Its nominations are separate records that don't appear on Q-Mintership's Minter Board.

entries.q: Is Q-Mintership+ official?
entries.a: No. Q-Mintership (qortal://APP/Q-Mintership) is the published app to use. Q-Mintership+ is a pre-release test version from the Q-Apps+ suite, being tested with the community and offered to Q-Mintership's developers as a pull request.

entries.q: Do Q-Mintership+ nominations show in Q-Mintership?
aliases: q-mintership+ nominations in the original app
nomination not showing on minter board
entries.a: No. Q-Mintership+ is a pre-release test version and stores its nominations as its own records, so Q-Mintership's Minter Board doesn't list them. To nominate someone, use Q-Mintership, where the community and the Minter Admins look for nomination cards.

entries.q: How do I see my nomination's progress?
entries.a: Open Q-Mintership's Minter Board and find your card. It shows the poll results (Admin Yes and No, Minter Yes and No), the invite status, such as INVITE PENDING APPROVAL or INVITED, and how many admins have approved the invite so far. The Minter Board's own steps say to check back often.

entries.q: Can Minter Admins reject a nomination?
entries.a: Yes, by voting No on the card's poll: if yes votes from about 40% of the Minter Admins never come, no MINTER invite is created. Once an invite exists, it only becomes active if enough admins approve it within its approval window; otherwise it expires. You can be nominated again later.

entries.q: What happens when enough Minter Admins approve?
entries.a: Core applies it by itself at the threshold, and the invite becomes active: your card shows INVITED with a Join MINTER Group button. Press it to send JOIN_GROUP (0.01 QORT); if your account already had a join request open, Core adds you at once. Then you can start minting from Hub.

entries.q: I sent a MINTER join request before; what happens to it?
entries.a: A join request can't be withdrawn. It stays open until a nomination of you is approved, which then makes you a member at once, or until the Minter Admins remove it by group approval. You don't need to send another one.

entries.q: Can Q-Mintership notify me about my nomination?
entries.a: Yes. On the Minter Board, Notification Settings lets you turn on Minter Board notifications, say whether you're willing to get them by Q-Chat or Q-Mail, and join the notifications group; saving settings needs a registered name. Each card also has a bell for that card's alerts, and Enable Hub notifications gives push alerts in Hub for nomination updates.

entries.q: Can I share a link to a nomination?
entries.a: Yes. Each nomination card in Q-Mintership has a Link button (Copy link in list mode) that copies a share link to that card, so you can send it to the nominee or post it in Q-Chat.

entries.q: Can I comment on a nomination?
entries.a: Yes. On a Q-Mintership card, press Comments to open the thread and Post Comment to add yours; you can also reply, and edit your own. Each comment is a small QDN publish under your registered name, with the usual small fee. Minters, admins and the nominee use comments to explain their views.

entries.q: What is the Explorer in Q-Mintership+?
entries.a: It is part of Q-Mintership+, a pre-release test version: a read-only tool to look up accounts, names and transactions. In the published Q-Mintership, tap any name to open its Account Inspector, with its level, blocks minted, MINTER group status, transactions and older sponsorship details.

entries.q: Why can the number of approvals needed change?
aliases: why did the minter threshold change
entries.a: Because the target is about 40% of the MINTER group's admins, and Core recounts the admins every block. When a Minter Admin is added or removed, the number needed for every waiting invite or removal can rise or fall, even for ones that already have approvals.

entries.q: How do I become a Minter Admin?
aliases: apply to be a minter admin
entries.a: There is no application form and no minimum level; it is earned. Any existing minter can be proposed: a proposal card goes on Q-Mintership's Minter Admin Management board (Propose a Minter for Admin Position), admins and minters vote, and the promotion only takes effect with group approval from the existing Minter Admins.

entries.q: How are Minter Admins removed?
entries.a: The same way: a demotion card for the admin goes on Q-Mintership's MAM board, admins and minters vote, and once about 40% of the admins support it, the removal is proposed on chain and only takes effect when enough Minter Admins approve it. A demoted admin stays a MINTER member.

entries.q: What do Minter Admins look for in a nomination?
aliases: what admins check in a nomination
entries.a: They are trying to answer one question: is this a real, unique person who actually takes part in Qortal? They look at the candidate's on-chain activity and published content, the nominator's relationship to them, and community comments. Returning minters are also checked for signs of having run more than one minting account.

entries.q: Can one Minter Admin approve a minter alone?
entries.a: No. A MINTER group invite only becomes active when about 40% of the Minter Admins have signed it with GROUP_APPROVAL. No single admin can invite, or remove, anyone alone, and every step is on chain for anyone to check.

entries.q: Where can I see the list of Minter Admins?
entries.a: The current list is always in Q-Mintership, whose MAM board lists the admins. The Welcome to Qortal app's Minting page also shows the current admins of the MINTER group, fetched live, with a Q-Mail button on each.

entries.q: How do I contact a Minter Admin?
entries.a: Open the Welcome to Qortal app's Minting (Introduction) page, find Meet the Minter Admins, and use the Q-Mail button on an admin's card. Q-Mail messages don't disappear, so the admin can read and reply whenever they are online.

entries.q: Why are Minter Admins paid?
entries.a: Minter Admin is a paid role because it carries real responsibility over who can mint. The pay comes from the block reward: the Minter Admins' share is split evenly among the individual admins, and each one only receives it while actively minting.

entries.q: Do Dev Admins have to mint to get their reward share?
aliases: dev admin share of block reward
entries.a: No. Minter Admins must be actively minting to receive their share, but Dev Admins have no minting requirement: they contribute through development work on Qortal instead. A Dev Admin who stops contributing can be removed from the group.

entries.q: What is the difference between Minter Admins and Dev Admins?
aliases: who approves core updates vs minters
entries.a: Minter Admins decide who can mint: they approve and remove members of the MINTER group. Dev Admins decide what code the network runs: they approve Qortal Core auto-updates. Both act by quorum with GROUP_APPROVAL, and both share the block reward slice that founders used to get.

entries.q: Can Minter Admins kick or ban a minter?
entries.a: Yes, with group approval. Minter Admins discuss it on the encrypted Admin Board; once about 40% of them vote yes on a card about a minter, an admin can create a KICK or BAN transaction, which only takes effect when enough Minter Admins approve it. A Minter Admin must lose the admin role first, and kicked members keep their level.

entries.q: Why would someone be removed from the MINTER group?
entries.a: The guides give two main reasons: running more than one minting account, in which case all related accounts are removed, and looking like you were active only to get approved and then went silent, no longer looking like a unique contributing user. A removal needs the same quorum of Minter Admins as an approval.

entries.q: What if I was removed from MINTER by mistake?
entries.a: The Minter Guide says a mistaken removal can be put right: the account can be re-invited to the MINTER group, again by Minter Admin group approval. Contact the Minter Admins, for example by Q-Mail, and explain.

entries.q: Do I lose my level if I'm removed from MINTER?
aliases: does leaving minter reset my level
entries.a: No. Your level comes from your blocks minted, which stay on chain: kicked members keep their level. They just can't mint again until a new nomination of them is approved.

entries.q: Can I leave the MINTER group?
entries.a: Yes, you can leave it like any other group. You keep your level, but you no longer mint. To come back you need a new nomination, which nominators choose to make, and Minter Admin approval again.

entries.q: What happens if I'm banned from MINTER?
aliases: how long is a minter ban
entries.a: You can't join the MINTER group while the ban lasts, and Q-Mintership marks your card BANNED FROM MINTER GROUP. Before you can join again, the Minter Admins would have to lift the ban, again by group approval; after that you can be nominated again.

entries.q: Is a new minter still reviewed after joining?
entries.a: Yes. Approval isn't the last review: Minter Admins keep watching activity in the MINTER group. Minting rights are for people who use and support Qortal, not a one-time ticket to farm rewards, so going silent after approval, or signs of multiple minting accounts, can lead to removal.

entries.q: Will I be removed if my minting node is offline for a while?
aliases: minting paused will i be removed
entries.a: The guides don't list node downtime as a reason for removal. Being offline costs you the rewards and level progress for that time, and your blocks minted stay on chain. Removals are about things like multiple minting accounts, or being active only to get approved and then going silent.

entries.q: Who owns the MINTER group?
entries.a: The null account, an address nobody controls. The MINTER group was transferred to it, so it is listed as an admin but can't vote or sign. No single person owns the group, and decisions come only from the Minter Admins' group approval.

entries.q: Can the 40% approval threshold be changed?
entries.a: Not with today's Qortal Core. Changing the MINTER group's approval percentage would need an UPDATE_GROUP from the group's owner, and the owner is the null account, which nobody can sign for. So no app can change it; it would need a Core change first.

entries.q: Are Minter Admins elected?
aliases: how were the first minter admins chosen
entries.a: Yes. The first group of Minter Admins was voted in by the community at large. Since then, admins are added and removed by proposals that the existing Minter Admins approve with GROUP_APPROVAL. More MINTER groups, with their own Minter Admins, are expected as the network grows.

entries.q: Why can't I comment on a nomination?
aliases: need a name to comment mintership
on the block list can't comment
entries.a: Comments are small QDN publishes under your registered name, so you need to be signed in to Hub or GO with a name, and a little QORT for the fee. Q-Mintership's admins also keep a comment block list: a name on it gets 'You are on the block list and cannot publish comments.'

entries.q: Why doesn't my vote count in a nomination's totals?
aliases: my vote not counted on a nomination
why is my nomination vote not shown
entries.a: Anyone can vote on a card's poll, but Q-Mintership only counts minters and Minter Admins in its Minter and Admin totals; other votes appear only in the poll details, marked as User. That is by design: only the Minter Admins' support moves a nomination forward.

entries.q: Why can't I propose a nomination?
entries.a: Q-Mintership only lets a MINTER member or Minter Admin at level 5 or higher publish a nomination ('You have to be a level 5 or above Minter to nominate a user'), signed in inside Hub or GO with a registered name. The nominee also needs a registered name and can't be you, an existing minter or admin, or someone who already has a card.

entries.q: I pressed Join MINTER Group but I'm not a member yet, what do I do?
aliases: joined minter but not a member
join minter group button did nothing
entries.a: Give it a block or two and refresh: the JOIN_GROUP transaction has to confirm on chain first. Check that you have 0.01 QORT of confirmed balance for the fee, and that your card said INVITED, meaning the invite was fully approved and not still pending.

entries.q: How do I open the Minter Guide?
entries.a: Open qortal://WEBSITE/Q-Minter in Qortal Hub or GO. It is also linked from the Q-Minter and The History of Minting buttons in Q-Mintership, and from the 'Minting requires a private node' window, which has an Open Q-Minter guide button.

entries.q: What is in the Minter Guide?
entries.a: It has: Qortal Minting Overview, History of Qortal Minting, Becoming a Minter, The Nomination Process, Publishing a Nomination, Great Nomination Examples, Minter Admins, Full Minting Explainer, Best Practices, Nodes & Hardware, and a Glossary. Its home page also shows live network stats.

entries.q: Does the Minter Guide show live numbers?
entries.a: Yes. Its home page reads the network and shows active minters, minters online now, the block reward, the number of Minter Admins and about how many votes approval needs, plus a chart of each tier's share with an estimate of QORT per minter per 1,000 blocks. If it can't reach the network, it shows the last known values.

entries.q: Is the Minter Guide official?
entries.a: It is a community education guide, published on QDN as Q-Minter. It describes the live nomination system, but warns that exact thresholds, counts and screens can change, and asks readers to check against qortal.org, qortal.dev, the Qortal wiki and Q-Mintership itself.

entries.q: How do I start minting after joining the MINTER group?
aliases: how to start minting in hub
entries.a:
In Qortal Hub, connected to your own synced node:
1. On Home, open Quick tools and press Minting.
2. Check the panel says the account is ready for the next minting step.
3. Press Start minting and confirm the transaction.
4. Wait while Hub confirms your reward share (it can take a minute or two); it then adds your minting key to the node.
The panel then shows Minting active.

entries.q: Where is the Minting button in Qortal Hub?
entries.a: On Hub's Home, the Quick tools window has a Minting button with a sprout icon; it opens the minting panel. In Qortal GO you can also tap your avatar at the top and choose Minting.

entries.q: What does the Start minting button do?
aliases: what happens when i press start minting
entries.a: It sets up your minting key in one go. If your account has no self reward share yet, Hub sends a REWARD_SHARE transaction to create one, waits for it to confirm, then reads its private key, your minting key, and adds it to your node. If the reward share already exists, Hub just adds the key to the node.

entries.q: How long does Start minting take?
entries.a: Usually a minute or two. Hub says confirming the reward share on chain can take up to 90 seconds; it checks every 30 seconds and gives up after about 10 minutes with 'timeout waiting for reward share confirmation'. If that happens, make sure your node is synced and press Start minting again.

entries.q: Why is the Start minting button greyed out?
entries.a:
Hub disables it while:
- your node is still syncing,
- the node already has two minting keys (remove one first), or
- it is still checking your reward-share status.
If you see Visit Q-Mintership instead, your account isn't in the MINTER group yet.

entries.q: What do the minting states in Hub's minting panel mean?
entries.a:
Synchronizing: the node is still syncing, so minting can't begin yet.
Minting active: this account, or the selected key, is set to mint on this node.
Not minting: the account isn't in the minter group yet, or the node already has several minting keys, or the account is ready for the next step, Start minting.

entries.q: Hub says only 2 minting keys are allowed per node, what do I do?
aliases: too many minting keys on node
remove a minting key to add another
entries.a: Your node already holds two minting keys, the most one node can run. Open the minting panel, find Node minting accounts, and press Remove minting account on the one you no longer need. Then press Start minting for your account.

entries.q: How do I remove a minting account from my node?
entries.a: In Hub, open the minting panel (Home, Quick tools, Minting). Under Node minting accounts, press Remove minting account on that account. This only changes your node: the account, its level and its reward share stay as they are, so you can add it again later with Start minting.

entries.q: What is a reward share on Qortal?
entries.a: A reward share is a key pair that stands for a minting relationship between accounts, not for an account itself. Its private key is the minting key a node uses. A self-share, with your own account on both sides, gives your own minting key; old sponsorship keys were reward shares from a sponsor to a new account.

entries.q: Is my minting key the same as my private key?
aliases: is the minting key my seed phrase
entries.a: No. Your minting key is the private key of your reward share, a separate key pair made for minting, not your account's own private key or seed phrase. It lets a node mint for your account. Keep it private anyway, and keep your account backup safe; the minting key can't restore your account.

entries.q: Is it safe to share my minting key?
aliases: someone asked for my minting key
entries.a: No. The Minter Guide says never to share your minting key publicly, and never to share your backup file or password with anyone. The Qortal team will never message you asking for them. Be wary of anyone offering to 'speed up' or 'sell' minting.

entries.q: Can I buy minting rights or a minting account?
entries.a: No. Minting rights can't be bought: they come from a nomination and Minter Admin approval, and each person may have only one minting account. In the past some people self-sponsored extra accounts and sold them; that is what the current system is built to stop, and linked accounts get removed. Be very wary of anyone selling or 'speeding up' minting rights.

entries.q: Can I mint on the public node?
entries.a: No. Minting needs your own node; the public node is shared. Hub and GO only open the minting panel when connected to a node you run, and on the public node they show 'Minting requires a private node' with a button to open the Q-Minter guide. Minting keys can only be assigned on a node you fully control.

entries.q: Can I create my minting key before I'm in the MINTER group?
aliases: minting key not in minter group
entries.a: No. Qortal Core only accepts a reward share, the transaction that creates your minting key, from an account that is allowed to mint, which means a MINTER group member. That is why Hub's minting panel shows Visit Q-Mintership instead of Start minting until you have joined.

entries.q: Can I mint through a gateway node?
aliases: cannot view minting details on the gateway
entries.a: No. Hub shows 'cannot view minting details on the gateway' and won't open the minting panel there. Minting needs Hub or GO connected to your own full node.

entries.q: Does my node need to be fully synced to mint?
entries.a: Yes. Your node must be caught up to the current block height to mint, and Hub won't start minting while it is still syncing: 'The node is still syncing, so minting cannot begin yet.' A node that falls behind stops earning until it catches up.

entries.q: Why is my reward share taking so long to confirm?
aliases: reward share waiting for payout block
entries.a: Qortal Core doesn't confirm reward-share transactions in the 25 blocks before each 1,000-block payout, or in the payout block itself, so one sent just then waits until that stretch has passed, roughly half an hour. If Hub gives up meanwhile, wait for it to confirm, then press Start minting again: Hub finds the confirmed reward share and just adds the key.

entries.q: Do I lose my blocks minted if my node goes offline?
aliases: do i have to run 7200 blocks straight
does my level drop if i stop minting
entries.a: No. Your blocks minted are recorded on chain and never reset, so you don't have to run 7,200 blocks in a row to reach Level 1. While your node is offline you simply don't earn or gain credit; once it is back and synced, you carry on from where you were.

entries.q: Can I mint with the same account on two nodes?
aliases: same minting key on two nodes
do more nodes earn more qort
entries.a: Yes. The wiki and the Minter Guide both say one minting account can mint on several nodes at once, which keeps you minting if one node goes down. It doesn't earn more: you still get one share. The rule is that it must be the same single minting account on all of them.

entries.q: How do I move minting to a new computer?
aliases: move minting to a new node
entries.a:
1. Install Qortal on the new machine and let the node fully sync.
2. Log in to Hub there with the same account.
3. Open Minting and press Start minting: Hub finds your existing reward share and just adds the key to the new node.
4. On the old node, remove the minting account if you're retiring it, or keep both running for redundancy.

entries.q: My node stopped minting after a reinstall, how do I fix it?
entries.a: Add your minting key to the node again. In Hub, open Minting and press Start minting: if your reward share already exists on chain, Hub just puts the key back on the node, with no new transaction. Then check that Node minting accounts lists your account and the panel shows Minting active.

entries.q: What is Q-Node and do I need it for minting?
entries.a: Q-Node (qortal://APP/Q-Node) is a Q-App for managing your node, including its minting accounts. The Minter Guide calls it the more manual way. Most people can simply use Hub's Minting panel and Start minting, which creates your minting key and adds it to the node for you.

entries.q: How do I add a minting key with Q-Node?
entries.a: Open Q-Node while connected to your own node and choose Add minting account; if it asks for the minting key, paste the 44-character key. Q-Node then lists the node's minting accounts and their minting status. Hub's Start minting does all of this for you, including making the key.

entries.q: Do I need Qortal Hub to mint?
aliases: do i need hub for minting
mint with qortal core and no hub
entries.a: The minting itself is done by Qortal Core, your full node. Hub is the easy way to set it up: its Minting panel creates your minting key and adds it to the node, and Q-Node is a more manual option. Once the key is on the node, Core keeps minting without Hub open.

entries.q: What does (minting) next to my sync status mean?
entries.a: Hub's sync status says whether your node is synchronized and whether it is minting, for example 'Synchronized (100%) (minting)'. '(not minting)' means the node isn't minting right now, for example because no minting key is on it yet or it is still syncing.

entries.q: Why does Hub say this account is not yet part of the minter group?
aliases: not yet part of the minter group
you are not part of the minter group
entries.a: Your account isn't a member of the MINTER group, so it can't mint yet. That takes a nomination and Minter Admin approval in Q-Mintership, then joining the group. The panel's Visit Q-Mintership button opens the app; if you were just approved, press Join MINTER Group on your card first.

entries.q: What does the Hub minting panel show?
aliases: what is in the minting panel
entries.a: The 'Manage your minting' panel shows your wallet and minter profile, your level with the blocks and estimated days to the next level, the next step (with Start minting or Visit Q-Mintership), the node's minting accounts, your current status, and blockchain statistics and rewards info for reference.

entries.q: How does Hub estimate my minting reward?
aliases: how much will i earn per day minting
entries.a: It takes the current block reward, your tier's percentage and the number of minters online in your tier: block reward × tier % ÷ minters in the tier gives the estimated reward per block, and multiplying by the average blocks per day gives the estimate per day. The real figure moves as minters come and go.

entries.q: What are the blockchain statistics in Hub's minting panel?
entries.a: They are reference figures for the network: the average Qortal block time, measured over the last 1,440 blocks, the average blocks per day, and the average QORT created per day (blocks per day × block reward). Hub uses them for its reward and time-to-level estimates.

entries.q: Can I view stats for another minting account on my node?
entries.a: Yes. In the minting panel, tap an account under Node minting accounts; it gets a Viewing stats badge, and the profile, level progress and rewards info then show that key's figures.

entries.q: Where can I see my minting level?
aliases: how many blocks have i minted
entries.a: Home's Status window, in Hub and GO, shows Minter Level as dots; in Hub, hovering over it shows a bar with your blocks minted against the next level's total. The minting panel shows your level, the blocks still needed and the estimated days. User Search shows any account's level and minting progress.

entries.q: What do the dots next to Minter Level mean?
entries.a: They show your minting level: one filled dot per level, out of nine dots. In Hub, hover over them to switch to a level bar with your blocks minted against what the next level needs. If you're not in the MINTER group, the row shows Apply instead, which opens Q-Mintership.

entries.q: Can I see another person's minting level?
entries.a: Yes. Hub's User Search shows an account's level and a Minting progress section with its blocks minted against the next level and an estimate of the days to get there. In Q-Mintership, tapping a name opens its Account Inspector, with its level, blocks minted and MINTER group status.

entries.q: What does Minting for ~N days mean in Hub?
aliases: with 24/7 minting you will reach level
entries.a: It is Hub's estimate of how many days of 24/7 minting you still need to reach the next level. Hub works it out from the blocks you still need, rounded up to the next 1,000-block payout, and the current average blocks per day, so it shifts when block times change or your node is offline.

entries.q: What does blocks to next level mean in Hub?
entries.a: It is how many more blocks you need before your next level shows. Hub counts the blocks between your blocks minted and the next level's total, then rounds up to the next 1,000-block payout, because credit arrives in batches of 1,000.

entries.q: Which reward tier am I in?
entries.a: Tiers pair the levels: Tier 1 is levels 1 and 2, Tier 2 levels 3 and 4, Tier 3 levels 5 and 6, Tier 4 levels 7 and 8, and Tier 5 levels 9 and 10. Level 0 isn't in a tier and earns nothing yet. Hub's minting panel shows your current tier.

entries.q: Do more minters in my tier mean less QORT for me?
aliases: why rewards drop with more minters
entries.a: Yes. Your tier's percentage of each block is split evenly among the minters online in that tier, so more online minters means a smaller slice each, and fewer means a bigger one. Climbing into a higher tier raises your share.

entries.q: Why didn't my rewards go up when I levelled up?
aliases: rewards the same after level up
no increase after new minting level
entries.a: Rewards are paid by tier, and each tier covers two levels. Going from level 1 to 2, 3 to 4, 5 to 6 and so on keeps you in the same tier, so your share stays the same. Your share rises when you reach the next odd level: 3, 5, 7 or 9.

entries.q: Why do my minting rewards change from day to day?
aliases: why did my minting rewards drop
entries.a: Several things move: how many minters are online in your tier, since the share is split among them; the transaction fees in each payout period, which are part of the reward; and the block reward itself, which steps down over time. How many blocks come per day also changes your daily total.

entries.q: How often are minting rewards paid?
aliases: how often do minters get paid
entries.a: In batches. Every 1,000th block is a payout block: it pays the block rewards and fees of the previous 1,000 blocks to the minters that were online just before it, in the 25 blocks leading up to the payout. This has been the method since Qortal Core 4.4.0 (block 1,508,000, December 2023). At about one block a minute, that is one payout roughly every 17 hours.

entries.q: What happens to rewards when a top tier has fewer than 30 minters?
entries.a: For the two top tiers, levels 7–8 and 9–10, Qortal Core needs 30 or more online minters before paying the tier on its own. With fewer, its minters and its share move down and join the tier below; for example, if fewer than 30 minters at levels 7–8 are online, levels 5 to 8 share 45% together, as Hub's panel shows. A tier with nobody online pays its share to the admins instead.

entries.q: Does Level 0 still mint?
entries.a: Yes. From the moment you're in MINTER with your key on the node, your node mints and counts blocks, but rewards only start at Level 1, after 7,200 blocks minted. That first stretch, about a week, is a waiting period before your first payout.

entries.q: Why do I still show Level 0 after 7,200 blocks?
entries.a: Because blocks are credited in batches of 1,000. The 7,200 needed for Level 1 hasn't changed, but in practice Level 1 shows after about 8,000 to 9,000 blocks of online time. Wait until Hub actually shows Level 1 rather than going by the raw counter.

entries.q: Why is my minting level not going up?
aliases: level stuck at the same number
entries.a:
Check these:
1. Credit arrives every 1,000 blocks, so the counter jumps in steps.
2. Your node must be online, synced and minting; offline time doesn't count.
3. Your minting key must be on the node: the panel should say Minting active.
4. Higher levels simply take far more blocks.

entries.q: What is blocksMinted?
entries.a: blocksMinted is the running total of blocks your account has helped mint. It is recorded on chain, never resets, and decides your level. It grows in steps of 1,000 because credit is paid in batches.

entries.q: How many blocks minted does each level need?
entries.a:
Total blocks minted needed:
Level 1: 7,200
Level 2: 72,000
Level 3: 201,600
Level 4: 374,400
Level 5: 618,400
Level 6: 964,000
Level 7: 1,482,400
Level 8: 2,173,600
Level 9: 3,037,600
Level 10: 4,074,400

entries.q: How many blocks does it take to go from one level to the next?
How long does each minting level take?
aliases: how long to reach each level
how long does it take to reach a level
how long to reach the next minting level
how long are the minting levels
when do i reach each level
entries.a:
Rough times of 24/7 minting from the start, at about one block a minute:
Level 1: about a week
Level 2: about 50 days
Level 3: about 4.5 months
Level 4: about 8.5 months
Level 5: about 14 months
Level 6: about 22 months
Level 7: about 2.8 years
Level 8: about 4.1 years
Level 9: about 5.8 years
Level 10: close to 8 years
Slower blocks or downtime add to these; Hub's minting panel shows your own estimate.

entries.q: What does reaching Level 1 change?
entries.a: From Level 1 you start sharing block rewards, in Tier 1: levels 1 and 2 share 6% of each block among their online minters. Your blocks minted keep counting toward the next levels, and your level gives you weight in Qortal's polls. Nothing else is needed; just keep your node online.

entries.q: What does Level 5 unlock?
entries.a: At Level 5 you can nominate new minters in Q-Mintership, your node can sign blocks (nodes submit blocks by default from level 5), and you move into Tier 3, where levels 5 and 6 share 19% of each block.

entries.q: Is there a level above 10?
entries.a: No. Level 10 is the highest level, at 4,074,400 blocks minted, about 8 years of minting. The wiki says a level 10 account's influence is meant to keep growing after that, but ever more slowly, so lower levels can come close to it; that part hasn't been built yet.

entries.q: What is a minting penalty?
entries.a: It is a large negative number of blocks minted that Core recorded on some accounts, which holds them at level 0. Core's self-sponsorship check, run over the whole chain in December 2022 and February 2024, set it for patterns from the sponsorship days, such as sponsored accounts passing rewards to the same few accounts or sponsorships given out in bulk. The chain doesn't record which pattern matched.

entries.q: What is blocksMintedAdjustment?
entries.a: It is an extra blocks-minted credit some accounts got at Genesis for forging the old QORA chain while it was considered dead. Since block 2,206,300, Qortal Core no longer counts it toward an account's level: only blocks actually minted on Qortal count, less any minting penalty.

entries.q: How did sponsorship work?
entries.a: From 2020 to 2024, a level 5+ account or a founder created a 0% reward-share key, the sponsorship key, for a newcomer. The newcomer added it to their node and minted through level 0, about 7,200 online blocks, until reaching Level 1, then made their own minting key. Sponsors earned nothing extra for it.

entries.q: What was the Mintership era?
entries.a: From 2024 to 2025, sponsorship gave way to Mintership: candidates published their own card on the Minter Board in Q-Mintership, the community and Minter Admins voted, and once about 40% of admins approved, the account was invited into the MINTER group. It made approval a transparent, quorum-based decision on chain.

entries.q: Why can't candidates publish their own Minter Card anymore?
entries.a: Self-created cards were abused: some people published low-quality, AI-generated content, pretending to be genuine community members to get into the MINTER group. Nominations add a web of trust: an established level 5+ minter puts their reputation behind a real person they know, which raises quality and removes fake self-submissions.

entries.q: How did the first minters start at Genesis?
entries.a: They didn't need a sponsor. QORA Forgers, accounts that forged QORA blocks after block 500,000 to keep that chain alive, became Qortal minters at levels 1 to 5 depending on how much they had forged. QORTector buyers and founders could also mint from the start.

entries.q: Why did Qortal remove Proof of Stake?
entries.a: QORA, Qortal's predecessor, used Proof of Stake, which lets money buy influence, the opposite of Qortal's aims. When the project was rebuilt from scratch, PoS was removed entirely in favour of minting, and Qortal launched at Genesis on 29 June 2020 with no pre-mine.

entries.q: What was the self-sponsorship problem?
entries.a: Under sponsorship, some level 5+ accounts created extra accounts and sponsored them themselves, then kept them minting from the same machine or sold them. The answers were MemPoW, which limits a computer to about two minting keys, Core's self-sponsorship checks with penalties, and finally replacing sponsorship with Minter Admin approval.

entries.q: What does Q-Mintership cost to use?
aliases: fee to vote on a nomination
entries.a: Reading is free. Each action is a small transaction with Qortal's usual fee of about 0.01 QORT: publishing a nomination card and its poll, voting, commenting, and joining the MINTER group.

entries.q: Does my node need to be online the whole time to get minting credit?
aliases: blocks minted didn't go up after payout
why no minting credit for this batch
entries.a: Credit and rewards are paid per 1,000-block batch, and Qortal Core records online minters only in the 25 blocks just before each payout block. If your node is offline or out of sync during that stretch, you miss that whole batch, even if it was online most of the time before. Staying online all the time is the simple way never to miss one.

entries.q: What is the difference between a node and a minter?
entries.a: A node is any computer running Qortal Core, fully synced with the network. A minter is an account that has been approved into the MINTER group and has its minting key on a node. Anyone can run a node; only MINTER members' nodes mint and earn block rewards, and one minting account can run on several nodes.

entries.q: What hardware does the Minter Guide recommend for minting?
entries.a: Minimum: a dual-core CPU, 4 GB RAM, an SSD with comfortable free space and stable broadband. Recommended: quad-core or better, 8 GB+ RAM, a larger SSD, a wired connection with port forwarding, and 24/7 uptime with a UPS. Uptime matters more than power; check the Qortal wiki for current disk needs.

entries.q: How much internet data does a minting node use?
entries.a: A lot. Community reports put an active 24/7 node at around 1.5 TB per month, though it varies with peers, syncing and traffic. Many home plans cap at about 1 TB, so an unlimited plan is strongly recommended; otherwise consider a VPS with uncapped bandwidth, or watch your usage.

entries.q: Is it worth running a node before I can mint?
aliases: node before i can mint worth it
does a node earn without minting
should i run a node if not a minter
entries.a: Yes, if you can. A node that isn't minting earns no QORT, but every extra healthy node helps Qortal's peers and QDN, and you need your own synced node anyway once you are approved. The Minter Guide's sample nominations mention candidates who already ran a synced node for months.

entries.q: Should my minting node use Wi-Fi or a cable?
entries.a: A cable if you can. The Minter Guide recommends a wired connection over Wi-Fi for stability, plus port forwarding or UPnP so your node reaches more peers and stays synced.

entries.q: How do I keep my minting node reliable?
entries.a:
From the Minter Guide's checklist:
1. Keep the node running 24/7.
2. Have stable power and internet; a UPS helps.
3. Keep Qortal Core on the latest official release.
4. Check the node stays synced with the network.
5. Bootstrap if it falls badly out of sync.
6. Set up port forwarding or UPnP.

entries.q: What should I do if my minting node falls out of sync?
entries.a: While it is behind, it can't mint. If it is only a little behind, let it catch up. If it is badly out of sync, the Minter Guide suggests bootstrapping the database to catch up quickly; the Qortal wiki has a bootstrap guide. Once synced, check the minting panel shows Minting active.

entries.q: Why does Qortal need Minter Admins?
entries.a: Because Qortal has no KYC, someone has to judge whether a new minter is a real, unique person, so that nobody can run many minting accounts. Minter Admins are that human layer: instead of one sponsor deciding, a quorum of community-elected admins must agree on chain, and their approvals and removals are open for anyone to check.

entries.q: Can family members each have a minting account?
aliases: one minting account per person family
entries.a: The rule is one minting account per person, so each real person can have their own, with their own nomination and track record. What isn't allowed is one person running several minting accounts; Minter Admins judge each account on whether it looks like a real, unique person.

entries.q: I'm a returning minter, what do Minter Admins check?
entries.a: The Minter Guide says that for returning minters, admins also look for signs of self-sponsorship, that is, of having run more than one minting account in the past. Keep to a single minting account. Former members keep their level and can be nominated again.

entries.q: What values do Qortal minters share?
entries.a: The Minter Guide describes minters as people who value decentralization, individual sovereignty and supporting the network: Qortal is sovereignty-driven, not money-driven. Showing those values in how you take part helps your nomination.

entries.q: What should a nominator do after publishing a nomination?
entries.a: Stay engaged: share the candidate's story in the community, answer questions on the card, and be available to vouch when the Minter Admins review it. The Minter Guide says an engaged nominator makes a real difference, and disappearing after publishing weakens a nomination.

entries.q: Can I see how a minter was approved?
aliases: check how a minter was approved
entries.a: Yes. Nomination cards, polls, invites and approvals are recorded on the Qortal blockchain or QDN, so anyone can check how a given minter was approved. In Q-Mintership, a card's poll details list who voted, and its invite section lists the GROUP_APPROVAL transactions behind it.

entries.q: How much QORT can I earn by minting?
aliases: how much qort minting per month
entries.a: There is no fixed amount. Each block's reward is split by level tier, and your tier's share is divided among the minters online in it, so earnings depend on the current block reward, your level and how many others share your tier. Level 0 earns nothing. Hub's minting panel shows an estimate per block and per day, and the Minter Guide's chart estimates QORT per minter per 1,000 blocks.

entries.q: How long until I get my first minting reward?
aliases: when do i start earning from minting
when will i get qort from minting
how soon do minters get paid
entries.a: Rewards start once you reach Level 1, which takes about a week of online minting; Level 1 usually shows after 8,000 to 9,000 blocks because credit comes in batches. After that you are paid at each 1,000-block payout, roughly every 17 hours at about one block a minute.

entries.q: What happens to a tier's share if nobody in it is online?
aliases: where does an empty tier's reward go
entries.a: Since Qortal Core 4.7.0, any part of the block reward not paid to online minters in a tier or to the QORA transition goes to the admins: half to the Minter Admins who are minting, and the rest to the Dev Admins. That is why the never-filled level 9–10 tier's 32% goes to them.

entries.q: Have the tier percentages always been the same?
entries.a: No. Until block 1,010,000 the tiers shared 5%, 10%, 15%, 20% and 25%, and QORA holders got 20%. From block 1,010,000 the tiers moved to today's 6%, 13%, 19%, 26% and 32%, and the QORA share dropped to 1%.

entries.q: What changed for minting in Qortal Core 4.7.0?
entries.a: From block 2,012,800, the founder reward tier was removed and founder accounts became like any other. The rewards that went to founders, plus the share of any tier without online minters (so far the whole level 9–10 tier), now go to the Minter Admins and Dev Admins, split 50/50.

entries.q: Why can't my nomination be decided right away?
entries.a: Group approvals have a minimum delay: after a MINTER invite is created, Qortal Core can't decide it for a few blocks, whatever the count. After that, once enough Minter Admins have approved, Core applies it in its next decision block, and the nominee can join.

entries.q: What happens to an approved MINTER invite that's never used?
entries.a: It stays stored until the person joins, or until the Minter Admins cancel it, which needs their group approval like any other MINTER decision. There is no rush, but the nominee does need to press Join MINTER Group to become a member.

entries.q: How do I sort or filter cards on the Minter Board?
entries.a: Use Display settings at the top of the Minter Board: switch between Card Grid and List Mode, sort by date, nominee name, publisher name, newest comments, or least or most votes, and choose which cards to show, from the last day up to 90 days (45 by default) or all. Tick Show Existing Minter Cards (History) to include older cards.

entries.q: Can I still see the old Minter Cards from before nominations?
entries.a: Yes. In Q-Mintership, tick Show Existing Minter Cards (History) in the Minter Board's display settings to include older cards, and set Show cards from to Show All.

entries.q: Why can't I see a nomination card on the Minter Board?
entries.a: Check the Minter Board's display settings: by default it only shows cards from the last 45 days, so set Show cards from to Show All, and tick Show Existing Minter Cards (History) for older ones. Press Refresh after a new publish, since a card can take a little while to appear.

entries.q: Can the community vote on removals and new Minter Admins?
aliases: vote on a new minter admin
community vote on a minter ban
entries.a: Partly. Removals are handled on the encrypted Admin Board, which only Minter Admins can read. Proposals to add or remove Minter Admins are cards on the MAM board, with a poll where minters' votes show next to the admins'; only the Minter Admins' support and group approval decide.

entries.q: Is there more than one MINTER group?
entries.a: Today there is one: Qortal Core only lets members of the MINTER group, group 694, mint. The Minter Guide and the wiki say more MINTER groups, each with its own Minter Admins, are expected as the network grows.

entries.q: How can I check whether an account is a minter?
aliases: is someone in the minter group
entries.a: In Q-Mintership, tap the account's name to open its Account Inspector, which shows its MINTER group status, level and blocks minted; a nomination card also says EXISTING MINTER once the person is in. For your own account, Hub's minting panel says whether it is part of the minter group, and Home's Minter Level shows dots only for members.

entries.q: Can I nominate someone by their address?
entries.a: You can type a name or an address in Q-Mintership's Nominee Name or Address field, but it has to lead to a registered name: 'Nominee must have a registered Qortal name. Enter a valid name, or an address that has a registered name.' The card then uses that name.

entries.q: Can I nominate more than one person?
aliases: how many people can i nominate
entries.a: Yes. Each nomination card is about one person, and each person can only have one card. The wiki expects nominations to be made thoughtfully, and each nominator's record is tracked, so quality matters more than numbers.

entries.q: Is my nomination public?
entries.a: Yes. The Minter Board, its cards, polls and comments are public, and the invite and approvals are on chain. Only the Admin Board, where Minter Admins discuss decisions, is encrypted to them.

entries.q: Can I see who voted on a nomination?
aliases: see voters on a minter card
entries.a: Yes. On a Q-Mintership card, Display Poll Details shows Yes and No vote details: each voter's name, whether they are an admin, a minter or a user, and their weight in blocks minted. The invite section also lists the admins' GROUP_APPROVAL transactions.

entries.q: What should I do while my nomination is open?
entries.a:
1. Keep a little QORT; joining costs 0.01.
2. Have your node installed, synced and running.
3. Read and answer comments on your card, and keep taking part in Qortal.
4. Check your card on the Minter Board often.
5. When it says INVITED, press Join MINTER Group.

entries.q: Can I speed up my nomination?
entries.a: Not directly; the Minter Admins review in their own time. What helps is a clear, honest nomination with links to things you've published, plus community support and thoughtful comments, which the wiki says help admins decide faster. Never pay anyone who offers to 'speed up' minting rights.

entries.q: How do I know when I've been approved as a minter?
aliases: approved as a minter how to know
am i in the minter group
