entries.a: First tap Authenticate on the website itself: only then can the embedded apps share the session. If an app inside the page still can't sign in, that is often a Hub limit for apps inside other pages. Use Open in Qortal on the app's tile to open it in its own tab.

entries.q: Can I turn off live clock-in sharing in POS+?
entries.a: Yes. In Settings, Shifts, turn off "Share clock-ins live" if you'd rather not approve a publish for every clock-in. Hours are then published with the day close instead, so the owner's Live now list won't show them until then.

entries.q: What does Clear saved copies do in POS+?
entries.a: Settings, This device, Clear saved copies removes the store data POS+ cached on that device, so it loads fresh from QDN next time. Unpublished sales are never touched by it, so today's sales stay until you close the day.

entries.q: Can I use POS+ on a phone or tablet?
entries.a: Yes. POS+ runs inside Qortal GO on Android phones and tablets as well as in Qortal Hub on a computer, with layouts for each. Each device keeps its own sales draft for its location until you close the day there, so set Settings, This device, Location on every device you sell from.

entries.q: Which places get the most detailed forecast in Q-Weather?
entries.a: Hour-by-hour high-resolution regional models cover the USA (including Alaska, Hawaii and Puerto Rico), Canada, Iceland, the UK and Ireland, the Nordic and Baltic countries, Poland and much of Europe, and coarser regional data covers Europe, North Africa and the Middle East. Everywhere else, and after the first two to three days, the forecast is ECMWF up to 15 days. Tap the model name on the map to see which model covers which hours for your place; How Q-Weather works lists the models in the forecast your node has.

entries.q: Does Q-Weather track my location?
entries.a: No. Q-Weather talks only to your own Qortal node: it never contacts an outside server, needs no account and doesn't track you. You add your places yourself, by search or on the map, and your places and settings stay on your device.

entries.q: How do I share a place from Q-Weather?
entries.a: Open the place's ⋮ menu. Share copies a link to that place's forecast, and the same menu has Rename, Edit place, Delete place and Show in GO widgets.

entries.q: How do I message someone on ThankQ?
entries.a: Open their listing or profile and tap Send Message, write it and Send. ThankQ sends it as a Q-Chat direct message and as a Q-Mail, so the person sees it even if they don't open ThankQ. Requests you send are announced to the other person the same way.

entries.q: Where do I see my bookings on ThankQ?
entries.a: Requests lists Incoming and Outgoing requests with their status, and a badge shows new incoming ones; while ThankQ is open it also pops up "New incoming request from" the guest. Your Profile has a calendar marking check-in and booked days, with your upcoming bookings under it.

entries.q: How do I comment on a place in World Map?
entries.a: Open the place, go to Comments, write your comment and tap Post, then confirm in Hub. The comment is published to QDN under your name, so you need a registered name, and anyone viewing the place can read it.

entries.q: Can I use World Map on my phone?
entries.a: Yes. In Qortal GO, World Map has tabs for Map, My POI's, My Lists, Discover and Profile. To set a place, tap the map once or drag the red pin, and long-press a community score to see how it is worked out.

entries.q: Can I buy from several shops at once on Q-Shops?
entries.a: Yes. Your Q-Shops cart groups items by shop, and shipping and store-asset totals are worked out per shop at checkout. You pay each shop separately with Pay this shop, approving each payment in Hub.

entries.q: How do shop owners see orders made in Q-Shops?
entries.a: Sign in with the name that publishes the shop, open the account menu and choose Open Manage Sales for that name, then Refresh from QDN. It lists checkouts made in the Q-Shops app, read from buyers' encrypted receipts. Orders placed on your own website show in its Q-Shop block's Merchant tab instead.

entries.q: How do I change the theme of my QWB website?
entries.a: In QWB's Settings, pick the site Theme for the published page, Light or Dark. Single blocks can also have their own look under Block appearance in their Options. Publish the site again for visitors to see the change.

entries.q: How do I add a photo album to my QWB website?
entries.a: Add the Albums block and pick your photos. QWB publishes them to QDN in one batch, so Hub asks you once rather than for every picture. Choose a layout (grid, masonry, hero or carousel); visitors can open pictures in a lightbox, and the carousel has arrows, dots and swiping.

entries.q: What if Qortal Web Builder can't connect to my wallet?
entries.a: QWB can only sign in when opened inside Qortal Hub or GO, for example from the Apps list or qortal://APP/QWB, not as a file in a normal browser. Wait a second after it opens and tap Connect again. If it still fails, update Hub, and use Run bridge diagnostics to copy details for support.

entries.q: How do I add a poster to my title on Subscreen?
entries.a: On the Publish page or in Edit, drop an image or tap to choose one: JPG, PNG or WebP up to 10 MB, ideally vertical 2:3, and crop it to the poster shape. It shows on posters in Subscreen and as the thumbnail in Q-Tube. Without one, the first snapshot of the video is used.

entries.q: Is Subscreen the same as Q-Tube?
entries.a: No, but they share data. Subscreen shows the Movies and Series from Q-Tube's format, and what you publish in Subscreen is published in Q-Tube's format under your name, so it appears in both, with the same comment thread. Subscreen adds things for films and shows: ratings out of 10, cast & crew, collections, bookmarks lists and tips.

entries.q: How does Q-Drive encrypt my files?
entries.a: Each file, its name and type, and your folder list are encrypted on your device with AES-256-GCM before anything is published, so nodes that store them see encrypted data only. Nothing private goes into the public QDN details such as titles or tags. Qortal's own encryption layer keeps nothing secret by itself; all of Q-Drive's privacy comes from this encryption on your device.

entries.q: What happens to my Q-Drive if I lose my Qortal account?
entries.a: Your drive key is encrypted to your Qortal account, so only that account, and people you shared files with, can open your files. Restore the same account from your seed phrase on any device and your drive opens again. If the seed phrase is lost, nobody can recover the account or the drive; this can't be undone, so keep your seed phrase backed up offline.

entries.q: Do I need a registered name for Q-MEME or GIFs?
entries.a: Yes, to publish or like. Both apps save your memes, GIFs and likes to QDN under your registered name, so without one they ask you to register a name in Hub or GO first. Browsing, saving and copying work without a name.

entries.q: Does the person I share with need Q-Drive?
aliases: q-drive share to someone without drive
entries.a: They need a Qortal account with a registered name, because you share by typing their name, and they open the files in Q-Drive inside Hub or GO. They don't need a drive of their own: Shared with me works without one, and seeing what was shared costs them nothing. If they don't use Qortal apps at all, Q-Mail with the file attached (up to 40 MB) is the other way.

entries.q: Is there a storage limit in Q-Drive?
entries.a: QDN has no quota, so Q-Drive shows no bar. Its storage meter just lists your files and their size, the trash on its own line, and the encrypted size on QDN. The limits are per file (2000 MB, or 500 MB on a public node) and the 0.01 QORT fee for each publish. Your files also need nodes that keep them, ideally your own.

entries.q: Why can't I open a Q-Drive share link?
entries.a: Check the message Q-Drive shows. "Only the person it was shared with can open it" or "Not for this account" means you are signed in with another account or name. "This share was stopped" means the sender stopped it. "Fetching from peers…" or "Not found on your node yet" means it hasn't reached your node: wait and retry. Also check that the whole link was copied; Q-Drive links look like qortal://APP/Q-Drive/s/…

entries.q: Why can't I select my name in Subscreen?
entries.a: Subscreen can't use names that contain #, ?, / or % yet. If your name has one of these, pick another of your names in the account menu, or register a plain name in Hub, to rate, comment and publish.

entries.q: Can buyers leave reviews in a QWB Q-Shop?
entries.a: Yes. Each product's detail window has a Reviews tab, but a review can only be written after a purchase of that product recorded in the buyer's browser from checkout. That keeps reviews to people who actually bought.

entries.q: Does Help Host Map Tiles in World Map make my node host the map?
aliases: world map help host map tiles
entries.a: Help Host Map Tiles lets you pick the map data publishers, and World Map saves your choice as a list on your node. Your node stores a name's data for others when you follow that name, so to be sure you help, also follow those publisher names on your own node. Hosting needs your own node; a public node doesn't host for you.

entries.q: How do I contribute map tiles to World Map?
aliases: world map contribute to map quality
entries.a: Tap Contribute to Map Quality to open Publish Tiles. Pick the name to publish under and choose PNG, JPG or WebP tile files: each identifier comes from the file name or path, such as 12-2207-1297.png or tiles/12/2207/1297.png. Tiles you already published are skipped, and the rest go out as QDN images in one batch you approve in Hub.

entries.q: How do I suggest a meetup with someone on ThankQ?
entries.a: Open their meetup post and tap Suggest a Meetup. Pick the kind (coffee, walk, chat, dinner, local tour, hike, co-work or event), roughly when, and write a message, then Send Suggestion. ThankQ publishes it and tells them by Q-Chat and Q-Mail, and it shows in their Requests, Incoming.

entries.q: What does Hide Incomplete Listings do on ThankQ?
entries.a: Some listings on QDN are missing details, for example a publish that didn't finish, and ThankQ shows them as incomplete cards asking the host to republish. Tick Hide Incomplete Listings in Explore to leave those out and see only complete listings.

entries.q: What is the POS app on Qortal?
entries.a: The Q-App named POS is an old test version that is no longer worked on. The point-of-sale app to use is POS+, a separate Q-App: search for POS+ in the Apps list of Hub or GO.

entries.q: Can I get back a file I deleted forever in Q-Drive?
entries.a: Often, yes, because Delete forever only takes the file off your drive and its encrypted data stays on QDN. Open Settings, Storage, Find missing files and ask it to show files deleted earlier; adding one back puts it in your drive again as a change you save. It only works while nodes still have that file's data.

entries.q: Why didn't my Singularity score save?
entries.a: Check the message under the game. You need a registered name, at least one minted block, and a run that beats your verified best. If you declined in Hub, or the publish timed out, look for Hub's approval prompt and tap Save verified score again. A saved score can take a moment to show on the leaderboard while it reaches your node.

entries.q: Is Q-Shops the same as the Q-Shop app?
entries.a: No. Q-Shops gathers the stores that people build with the Q-Shop block of Qortal Web Builder, reading the catalogs their websites publish. The Q-Shop Q-App is a separate shop app with its own stores, so its shops don't appear in Q-Shops.

entries.q: How do I edit, remove or share my place on World Map?
entries.a: Open your own place on the map: its popup has Comments, Edit, Remove and Copy / chat. Edit opens the same form as Add POI. Remove marks the place as deleted so World Map stops showing it, although earlier versions stay on QDN. Copy / chat copies the place's title, region and coordinates, and can also send them as a chat message to a Qortal address you type.

entries.q: Why can't I find my website on Qortal Web?
aliases: qwb site not on qortal web
entries.a: Give the network a little while after you publish: Qortal Web reads the index file your site publishes, and other nodes need to fetch it. A group-only site shows only to signed-in members of that group. Sites published with older QWB versions may need Publish Website once more, so the index carries what newer Qortal Web expects.

entries.q: How do people visit my QWB website?
entries.a: Share its link, qortal://WEBSITE/<your name>, which QWB shows after publishing. Visitors open it in Qortal Hub or Qortal GO; it won't open in an ordinary web browser. A Global site is also listed in the Qortal Web Q-App, where people can find it by search.

entries.q: Does ThankQ show listings on a map?
entries.a: Yes. Explore shows listings beside a map with pins coloured by kind: available host, full host, meetup and event travel. Listings need coordinates, or a city and country ThankQ can place, to appear as pins. You can also show ThankQ's pins inside the World Map Q-App.

entries.q: What are the + versions of Qortal apps, like Q-Mail+?
aliases: what does the + mean in q-share+
entries.a: The + apps (the Q-Apps+ suite) are pre-release test versions of official Q-Apps, published as Q-Mail+, Q-Share+, Q-Shop+ and Q-Mintership+ so the community can try new designs before they reach the stable apps. For everyday use, open the stable app without the +: Q-Mail, Q-Share, Q-Shop or Q-Mintership. The + apps read and write the same QDN data, so your mail, shares and orders show up in both. Q-Share 2.0 and Q-Mail 4.0 began as Q-Share+ and Q-Mail+.

entries.q: How do I open a + app like Q-Share+?
aliases: how to start a plus app
entries.a: The + apps are pre-release test versions, so for everyday use open the stable app instead, such as qortal://APP/Q-Share or qortal://APP/Q-Mail. To try a + app, search its name in the Apps section of Hub or GO, or type its link with the plus sign itself, for example qortal://APP/Q-Share+. The encoded form %2B can open a blank tab.

entries.q: Which + apps like Q-Mail+ can I use right now?
aliases: list of plus apps on qdn
entries.a: As of November 2026, Q-Mail+, Q-Share+, Q-Shop+ and Q-Mintership+ are published on QDN as pre-release test versions. Names+, Q-Tube+, Q-Node+, Q-Trade+, Q-Support+, Q-Fund+ and the Q-Apps+ launcher are still being built. For everyday use choose the stable apps without the +, which work with the same data.

entries.q: Can I change the theme in Q-Mail or Q-Share?
entries.a: Yes. Q-Mail (since 4.0) and Q-Share (since 2.0) have four themes: Hub 3.0 (the default), the app's classic look (Q-Mail Classic or Q-Share Classic), Black and White. They follow Qortal Hub's light and dark switch. Pick one in the app's Settings → Appearance.

entries.q: Can I save my Q-Share settings and restore them on another device?
entries.a: Yes. Q-Share's Settings → Sync has Save to QDN, which publishes your settings and theme as a small document under your name, and Restore, which loads them on another device. Saving is a normal QDN publish: Hub asks you to confirm and the usual small fee applies. If Restore finds nothing yet, wait a minute for it to reach that node. In Q-Mail, the published mail state can carry your theme and text size (Settings → Sync).

entries.q: Do Q-Mail and Q-Share work on a phone in Qortal GO?
entries.a: Yes. Q-Mail (since 4.0) and Q-Share (since 2.0) are built for phones and GO. Q-Mail shows one pane at a time, with large touch targets, sheets, Send above the keyboard, press-and-hold menus, and Back or a swipe to close what is on top. Q-Share has a bottom bar, a Share button, filters in a bottom sheet, pull-to-refresh, and full-screen Share and Edit forms with Publish above the keyboard.

entries.q: What is the Q-Apps+ launcher app?
entries.a: Q-Apps+ is a pre-release launcher being built to show all the + test apps in one place, with search, favourites and a page per app linking to its stable original. It only reads from QDN; it publishes nothing and spends nothing. As of November 2026 it has not been published, so find Q-Apps in the Apps section of Hub or GO.

entries.q: What are the qortal:// links for the official Q-Apps?
entries.a: Type any of these in the Hub or GO search bar: qortal://APP/Q-Tube, qortal://APP/Q-Mail, qortal://APP/Q-Share, qortal://APP/Q-Shop, qortal://APP/Q-Fund, qortal://APP/Q-Support, qortal://APP/Q-Trade, qortal://APP/Names, qortal://APP/Q-Node, qortal://APP/Q-Mintership, qortal://APP/Q-Blog, qortal://APP/Q-Assets, qortal://APP/Ear-Bump, qortal://APP/Q-Search, qortal://APP/SubWire, qortal://APP/Subscriptions, qortal://APP/Q-Charts and qortal://APP/Welcome to Qortal.

entries.q: How do I open Q-Mail?
entries.a: Open Q-Mail from the Apps section in Qortal Hub or Qortal GO, or type qortal://APP/Q-Mail in the search bar. Q-Mail asks Hub to sign you in; accept it, because mail is read and sent under your registered Qortal name.

entries.q: How do I send a Q-Mail?
aliases: send mail to a qortal name
entries.a:
1. Open Q-Mail and press Compose (the floating button on a phone).
2. In To, type the recipient's registered Qortal name and pick it from the suggestions; Q-Mail checks every name before sending.
3. Add a subject, write your message and attach files if you like.
4. Press Send (Ctrl or Cmd+Enter on a computer) and approve the publish in Hub.
The mail is encrypted to the recipient and published on QDN under your name.

entries.q: Do I need a registered name to use Q-Mail?
aliases: can i use q-mail with no name
entries.a: Yes. Q-Mail sends mail from one Qortal name to another: you need a registered name to send, and the recipient must have one too. Each mail is encrypted with the recipient's public key, which Q-Mail finds through their name; if it says a name has no public key yet, mail to that name can't be encrypted, so it can't be sent.

entries.q: Is Q-Mail encrypted?
entries.a: Yes, the contents are. The subject, text and attachments are encrypted to each recipient's public key before they are published on QDN, so only the people it was sent to, and you as the sender, can read them. What isn't hidden is that a mail exists: it is a public QDN record under your name, and its identifier holds the start of the recipient's name.

entries.q: Can people see who I send Q-Mail to?
aliases: q-mail privacy who sent to whom
entries.a: Partly. The message itself is encrypted, but each mail is a public QDN record under your name, and its identifier contains the first 20 characters of the recipient's name and the last 6 characters of their address. So anyone browsing QDN can see that you mailed that name, and when. To keep the recipient's name off the record, send to an alias inbox they gave you (Send to alias); the record then shows the alias instead.

entries.q: What is an alias in Q-Mail?
entries.a: An alias is an extra inbox label that isn't a registered name. With Send to alias, the mail goes to the alias inbox the recipient told you about instead of their name inbox, so the public QDN record shows the alias rather than their name. It is still encrypted to the recipient and you are still the sender. Cc and Bcc copies aren't sent with an alias. Aliases you watch are listed under Aliases in the mailbox list.

entries.q: How do I reply from an alias inbox in Q-Mail?
entries.a: A reply from an alias inbox goes out under an alias of your own, so the other person keeps writing to that alias. Q-Mail asks for it, and it must differ from the inbox's alias. If you choose the same alias as the person you are writing to, Q-Mail warns that this can give away who you are and asks before sending.

entries.q: What do Cc and Bcc do in Q-Mail?
entries.a: Cc: each Cc name gets its own encrypted copy, and everyone who gets the mail can see the Cc names. Bcc: each Bcc name also gets its own encrypted copy and isn't listed in the mail, but every copy is a public QDN record under your name, labelled with that name and sharing one send id with the other copies, so Bcc is not fully hidden. Reply all fills the Cc row for you.

entries.q: How big can Q-Mail attachments be?
entries.a: Each file can be up to 40 MB in a normal mail, and up to 25 MB in a group thread message. Every file needs a file extension, such as .pdf or .png. Attachments are encrypted like the message, and each one is published as its own resource, so it adds its own small fee.

entries.q: How do I attach and open files in Q-Mail?
entries.a: To attach, press Attach files in the composer or drop files on it; attached files show as tiles you can tap to preview before sending. To open, look for the paperclip on a message in the list: its files open or save from there without opening the mail. Images, text, audio, video and PDFs open inside Q-Mail (PDFs in Hub's own reader), with Download to save them.

entries.q: What does it cost to send a Q-Mail?
entries.a: Q-Mail itself charges nothing. Each mail is a QDN publish with the normal small network fee (about 0.01 QORT), and each attachment, Cc copy and Bcc copy is a publish of its own with its own fee. Hub shows the request and asks you to confirm before anything is sent.

entries.q: How do I reply to or forward a Q-Mail?
entries.a: Open the message and press Reply, Reply all or Forward, or right-click it in the list (press and hold on a phone). A reply goes out from the name the mail was sent to, and Forward sends the original attachments along. The message you are answering shows above the editor for context, but it isn't copied into your reply; the reply links back to it instead.

entries.q: What does Show earlier do in Q-Mail?
entries.a: Replies in Q-Mail 4 link to the messages before them instead of copying them. In an open message, Show earlier loads those messages from QDN five at a time, newest first, and Show older goes further back, to the start of the conversation. A message that was deleted, wasn't sent to you, or isn't on your node yet says so, and you can retry the last.

entries.q: Why does an older Q-Mail show replies without the earlier messages?
aliases: q-mail history not shown old version
entries.a: Since Q-Mail 4.0, a reply carries links to the last 10 earlier messages instead of copies of them, which keeps every reply under about 2 KB. Older versions of Q-Mail can't follow those links, so they show the reply on its own. Open it in the current Q-Mail and press Show earlier.

entries.q: What are group threads in Q-Mail?
entries.a: Group threads are mail conversations for a Qortal group you belong to, listed under Threads by group. The messages are encrypted to every group member who has a public key, but a thread's title is public. You can start threads and reply to posts, with unread marks. If you don't use them, turn off Settings → Mail → Show group threads, which also makes Q-Mail load faster.

entries.q: How does Q-Mail work when I have several names?
entries.a: Q-Mail gathers the mail for all your names. Each name appears under Inbox (and under Aliases and Sent), so you can open one name's mail, fold the list away with its arrow, or hide a name with Hide from the list. A reply goes out from the name the mail was sent to. When writing, the From field lists your names with avatars, with search when you have more than 15, and Settings → Account sets the active mailbox.

entries.q: How do I archive or mark a Q-Mail as unread?
entries.a: Open the message and press Archive or Mark unread, or right-click it in the list (press and hold on a phone) for Archive, Mark as read or unread and Select. Archiving from a list shows Undo. Archived mail goes to Archived, and Move to inbox brings it back. Read and archive marks survive a reload and can be published with your mail state for your other devices.

entries.q: How do I search my Q-Mail?
entries.a: Use the search bar above the message list (or press / on a computer). It looks through the inbox, Archived, Sent and alias inboxes by name and subject, and through message bodies too when you ask it to. Results keep appearing while Q-Mail decrypts your mail.

entries.q: What is Publish Q-Mail State?
entries.a: Your read and unread marks, archive and some settings are kept on this device. Publish Q-Mail State (in the mailbox list, or Settings → Sync → Publish mail state now) saves them to QDN as one document encrypted to you, which costs one QDN publish. On another device Q-Mail offers to load that state once per sign-in, or loads it by itself if you turn on Always fetch and apply published mail state.

entries.q: Does Q-Mail keep drafts?
entries.a: Yes. Unsent messages are kept in the Drafts mailbox on this device, shown like the inbox with the recipient, subject and the start of the text. Drafts are not published, so they don't appear on your other devices. Discarding a message deletes its draft too.

entries.q: Can I delete a Q-Mail I sent?
entries.a: In Sent you can delete a message you sent. Q-Mail does it by publishing a replacement over it, because QDN can't erase a publish; Hub asks you to confirm. It can't undo the fact that the mail was sent, and the recipient may already have read it, so treat sent mail as permanent.

entries.q: How do I add a signature to my Q-Mail?
entries.a: Go to Settings → Mail and set a mail footer, either one for all your names or one per name. It is added to new mail and, if you choose, to replies and forwards.

entries.q: Why are some names crossed out in Q-Mail?
entries.a: Q-Mail crosses out names that contain hidden characters, as Qortal Hub does. Such names are often made to look exactly like someone else's name. Check the name carefully before you reply, send anything or follow a request in that mail.

entries.q: How do I block someone in Q-Mail?
entries.a: Q-Mail hides mail from names on your Qortal block list, the list your node keeps for Hub and other Q-Apps. Settings → Mail → Blocked names → Manage shows that list and lets you unblock names. To hide a name only from Q-Mail's list of your own inboxes, use Hide from the list instead.

entries.q: Does Q-Mail have keyboard shortcuts?
entries.a: Yes, on screens 600 px and wider: c compose, r reply, a reply all, f forward, e archive, u mark unread, j and k next and previous, Enter or o open, / search, Esc close, and g then i, s, t or a for Inbox, Sent, Threads or Aliases. Press ? to see the list.

entries.q: How long does new Q-Mail take to show up?
aliases: when does q-mail show new mail
entries.a: While Q-Mail is open it checks for new mail regularly, and new mail shows within about 2 minutes. Checking pauses while the tab is hidden and resumes when you come back. Unread counts show in the mailboxes, the bottom bar and the window title.

entries.q: What is the difference between Q-Mail and Q-Mail+?
entries.a: Q-Mail+ is the pre-release test version of Q-Mail, where new changes are tried before they reach the stable app; use Q-Mail for everyday mail. Q-Mail 4.0 (October 2026) is the redesign that was first tested as Q-Mail+, so the two look almost the same today. Both read and write exactly the same mail, so mail sent from either opens in the other and nothing is lost if you try Q-Mail+. Each keeps its own settings, such as the theme.

entries.q: How do I open Q-Mail with the recipient already filled in?
entries.a: Use a link of the form qortal://APP/Q-Mail/to/<name>, for example qortal://APP/Q-Mail/to/Alice, in a chat, a post or a Qortal website. Opening it starts Q-Mail's composer with that name in To.

entries.q: How do I change the text size in Q-Mail?
entries.a: Open Settings → Appearance in Q-Mail and choose Text size: Small, Medium or Large. The same section has the theme picker.

entries.q: How do I open Q-Share?
entries.a: Open Q-Share from the Apps section in Qortal Hub or Qortal GO, or type qortal://APP/Q-Share in the search bar. Anyone can browse shares and download files. To share files or comment, sign in with a registered Qortal name.

entries.q: How do I share files with Q-Share?
aliases: q-share how to share files step by step
entries.a:
1. Sign in with your registered name and press Share (the floating Share button on a phone).
2. Drag files in or tap to choose them.
3. Give the share a title, pick a category and write a description.
4. Press Publish and confirm in Hub. Each file is published with its own small fee, and you see progress for every file.
The share then shows under Latest shares and in My shares.

entries.q: How many files and how big can a Q-Share share be?
aliases: how many files in one share
entries.a: In Q-Share a share holds up to 10 files, and each file can be up to 2 GB. For more files, publish several shares; a collection can keep them together.

entries.q: What does sharing files on Q-Share cost?
entries.a: Q-Share takes no fee of its own. Each file is one QDN publish with the normal small network fee, plus one more publish for the share's details, so a share of 5 files is 6 publishes. Hub shows the request and asks you to confirm before anything is published.

entries.q: How do I download files from Q-Share?
entries.a: Open the share and press Fetch all files, or Download on one file. Your node first fetches the file from peers that hold it; when it's ready, press Save to keep it on your device. Save all as .zip saves every file in one zip (up to 150 MB). The Downloads list shows progress, a Save button on each ready file, and Clear finished.

entries.q: Why does a Q-Share file say it is not available?
aliases: q-share not found on the network
entries.a: Q-Share files come from other nodes that hold them. Not available on your node right now or Not found on the network means your node can't get the file from any peer at the moment, usually because no node that holds it is online or reachable. Try again later. Publisher is blocked means that name is on your block list.

entries.q: Can I preview files in Q-Share before downloading?
entries.a: Yes. A share page shows images (tap for a bigger view) and text files, opens PDFs in Hub's own reader, and plays audio and video with Play audio or Play video once the file is on your node. Settings → Content → Preview images automatically shows images up to 5 MB without a tap; turn it off to save data on a slow node.

entries.q: How do I edit a share I published on Q-Share?
entries.a: Open your share and press Edit share. Change the title, category, description or files, then publish; Hub asks you to confirm the update and its fee. Only the name that published a share can edit it.

entries.q: Can I delete a share on Q-Share?
entries.a: No. QDN can't erase a publish, and Q-Share has no delete for shares: you can edit a share, but it stays on QDN under your name. So share only files you are happy to keep public.

entries.q: Is Q-Share private?
aliases: who can see my q-share files
entries.a: No. Q-Share is for public file sharing: anyone on Qortal can find your share, open it and download its files, and nodes that follow your name keep copies. Don't put anything private in it. To send a file to one person privately, attach it to a Q-Mail, which encrypts it for the recipient.

entries.q: What are collections in Q-Share?
entries.a: A collection is a named list of shares, yours or anyone's, like a reading list or playlist. On a share page press Add to collection to save it to one of your collections or start a new one. The Collections page has Mine and All, and each name's profile shows its collections. A collection is a small document published under your name, so making or changing one is a publish with the usual small fee.

entries.q: How do I delete a collection in Q-Share?
entries.a: Open the collection and press Delete. QDN keeps every publish, so a collection can't be erased: Q-Share republishes it with all its items removed and the title kept, so it leaves All and stays under Mine as empty until you fill it again.

entries.q: What is the Following feed in Q-Share?
entries.a: Following on Home lists the newest shares from names you follow. Follow a publisher from their profile. Following a name also makes your node download and host everything that name publishes; the Follow button's tooltip shows how big that is. You can hide the Following chip in Settings → Content.

entries.q: How do I find my own shares in Q-Share?
aliases: where are my own shares q-share
entries.a: On Home turn on My shares. If you have several names, pick one of them or All my names. Your profile page, opened from your name, also lists your Shares and Collections.

entries.q: How do I search or filter Q-Share?
entries.a: Use the filters on Home (a Filters sheet on a phone): search by title, filter by publisher (names are suggested as you type), pick a category, and sort Newest first or Oldest first. Reset filters clears them all, and the small x in a field clears that field. Settings → Content → Default sort sets how Home opens.

entries.q: What categories does Q-Share use?
entries.a: The main categories are Software, Gaming, Audio, Video, Image, Document, Book and Other, most with sub-categories: for example Audio has Music (with genres), Podcast and Audiobook, and Software has OS, Application, Source Code and Plugin. Pick them when you share so people can filter for your files.

entries.q: How do I comment on a share in Q-Share?
entries.a: Open the share, write in Your comment below it and press Submit comment. You can reply to other comments and edit your own. You need to be signed in with a registered name, and each comment is a small public QDN publish.

entries.q: How do I share a link to a Q-Share share?
entries.a: On the share page press Copy link. It copies a qortal:// link like qortal://APP/Q-Share/share/<name>/<id>, which opens the share in Hub or GO when someone taps it in a chat, mail or post.

entries.q: How do I hide someone's shares in Q-Share?
entries.a: Go to Settings → Content → Hidden names and add the names (separate several with commas); their shares leave your lists in Q-Share only. Names on your Qortal block list are hidden from every list too, and Blocked names in Settings manages that list.

entries.q: What changed in Q-Share 2.0?
entries.a: Q-Share 2.0 (October 2026) is a redesign of Q-Share that keeps the same shares, files and comments. It adds four themes, a phone layout, filters and sort, My shares and a Following feed, previews for images, text, audio, video and PDFs, Save all as .zip, collections, a publish flow whose retries never pay twice, and Settings with sync to QDN.

entries.q: What is the difference between Q-Share and Q-Share+?
entries.a: Q-Share+ is the pre-release test version of Q-Share, where the next changes are tried first; use Q-Share for everyday sharing. Q-Share 2.0 began as Q-Share+, and the test version now also tries extras such as notifications, shares of up to 300 files, folders and covers in collections, and playlists. Both use the same shares, files and comments. If you try it: collections given folders or covers in Q-Share+ show only their top-level shares in Q-Share, and saving them there can drop those extras.

entries.q: How do I see everything one person has shared on Q-Share?
entries.a: Tap the publisher's name to open their profile, which has Shares and Collections tabs and a Follow button. You can also open it with qortal://APP/Q-Share/channel/<name>.

entries.q: Why can't I see my new share in Q-Share yet?
aliases: published but not in my shares
entries.a: Hub publishes one resource at a time, so a share with several files takes a while; keep the tab open until it finishes. If it isn't in My shares yet, it may still be publishing in Hub, so check again before you publish it again, because every retry costs new fees. Q-Share's Retry checks QDN for what has landed and waits for Hub's answer, so it never pays twice.

entries.q: How do I open Q-Tube?
entries.a: Open Q-Tube from the Apps section in Qortal Hub or Qortal GO, or type qortal://APP/Q-Tube in the search bar. You can watch without signing in; sign in with a registered name to publish, comment, like or send super likes.

entries.q: How do I watch a video on Q-Tube?
entries.a: Tap a video's thumbnail. Q-Tube starts fetching it to your node from the peers that hold it, shows the progress, and plays it once enough has arrived. Videos you start are added to Watched Videos, and the thumbnail shows how far you got.

entries.q: Why does a Q-Tube video take a while to start?
entries.a: Q-Tube videos aren't on a company server: your node has to fetch each video from other nodes that hold it, and the first start waits for that download. Videos from names with many followers come faster, because more nodes host them. If a video doesn't move at all, no node with it may be online right now; try again later.

entries.q: Do I need a registered name to use Q-Tube?
aliases: do i need qort for q-tube
entries.a: Not to watch: anyone can browse and play videos. You need to be signed in with a registered name to publish videos and playlists, comment, like or dislike, send super likes, and see notifications; the Publish button only appears once you are.

entries.q: How do I upload a video to Q-Tube?
entries.a:
1. Sign in with your registered name and press Publish (the + on a small screen), then Video.
2. Drag your video files in or click to choose them.
3. For each video add a title, a description, a category and sub-category, and a cover image.
4. Optionally add the videos to a new or existing playlist.
5. Publish and confirm in Hub; the publish has the usual small QDN fee.

entries.q: What video formats does Q-Tube support?
entries.a: Q-Tube lists these as supported: containers MP4 (preferred), M4V, OGG, WEBM and WAV; audio codecs Opus (preferred), MP3, FLAC, PCM and Vorbis; video codecs AV1 (preferred), VP8, VP9 and H.264. Other codecs can cause problems with the picture or the sound.

entries.q: How big can a Q-Tube video be?
entries.a: Each video file can be up to 2 GB. Bigger files take longer to publish and longer for viewers to fetch from other nodes, so compressing a long video first helps.

entries.q: Can I upload several videos at once on Q-Tube?
entries.a: Yes. Drop several files into the video publish window. Helpful options: Populate Titles by filename, All videos use the same Cover Image, and Populate all descriptions by Title. At the end you can put them all into a new or existing playlist.

entries.q: How do I make a playlist on Q-Tube?
entries.a: Press Publish, then Playlist, give it a title and description, and add videos to it; you can search them by title in all videos or just your own. You can also add videos to a playlist while publishing them. Open a playlist you own to edit it, remove videos or delete it.

entries.q: What is the difference between subscribe and follow in Q-Tube?
entries.a: Subscribe adds a name's videos to the Subscriptions tab on Q-Tube's Home page; it does not download anything to your node. Follow makes your node download and host everything that name publishes, which helps their videos load faster for everyone; the Follow button shows how big that is first.

entries.q: Do my Q-Tube subscriptions and bookmarks sync to other devices?
entries.a: No. Q-Tube keeps your subscriptions, bookmarks and watch history in this app's storage on this device, for the account you're signed in with. They are not published, so another device or a cleared browser starts empty.

entries.q: What is a super like on Q-Tube?
entries.a: A super like sends QORT to a video's creator with a message, and the message is shown before the normal comments. The minimum is 1 QORT. Press super like under the video, enter the amount and your message, publish and confirm in Hub. Each super like is checked against the payment before it is displayed, and the QORT you send can't be taken back.

entries.q: How do I comment on a Q-Tube video?
entries.a: Sign in with your registered name, write in the comment box under the video and submit it. You can reply to other comments and view or hide replies. Each comment is a small public QDN publish.

entries.q: How do I like or dislike a Q-Tube video?
entries.a: Use the thumbs up or thumbs down under the video; press it again to take it back. You need a registered name, and each like or dislike is a small QDN publish under your name.

entries.q: How do I bookmark videos on Q-Tube?
entries.a: Use bookmark video (or bookmark playlist) on a video or playlist. Open Bookmarks in the side menu to see all bookmarked videos, sort them into bookmark lists, and group lists in folders.

entries.q: Where is my watch history on Q-Tube?
aliases: find a video i watched qtube
entries.a: Open Watched Videos in the side menu. It lists the videos you started, newest first, up to the last 200, and is kept on this device only.

entries.q: Does Q-Tube remember where I stopped watching?
aliases: start where i left off qtube
entries.a: Yes, for a while. Q-Tube saves how far you got in each video on this device for 7 days and resumes from there; the thumbnail shows it as a progress bar.

entries.q: How do I download a Q-Tube video to my device?
entries.a: Use the download button on the video page: start download: click here fetches the video to your node, then ready to save: click here saves it as a file on your device.

entries.q: How do I share a Q-Tube video?
entries.a: Use copy link video on the video page and choose what to copy: the link, the title, the description, or several. The link is a qortal:// link that opens the video in Q-Tube for anyone using Hub or GO.

entries.q: How do I find videos on Q-Tube?
entries.a: Use the search at the top. Filters let you show videos, playlists or all, sort by most recent, and narrow by category, sub-category or a User's Name (Exact). Reset clears the filters.

entries.q: What categories does Q-Tube have?
entries.a: Q-Tube's categories include Movies, Series, Music, Education, Lifestyle, Gaming, Technology, Sports, News & Politics, Cooking & Food, Animation, Science, Health & Wellness, DIY & Crafts, Kids & Family, Comedy, Travel & Adventure, Art & Design, Nature & Environment, Business & Finance, Personal Development, Religion, History, Anime, Cartoons, Qortal, Paranormal, Spirituality, Privacy and Other. Movies, Series, Education and Anime have sub-categories.

entries.q: How do I edit my Q-Tube video?
entries.a: Find your video in the list or on your channel and press edit video properties (the pencil). Change the title, description, category or cover image, then press update video and confirm the publish in Hub.

entries.q: Can I delete my Q-Tube video?
entries.a: Yes: on your own video press delete video (delete playlist for a playlist) and confirm in Hub. Because QDN can't erase anything, Q-Tube publishes a tiny delete marker in its place, so it disappears from the app; people who already downloaded it may still have a copy.

entries.q: How do I block a channel in Q-Tube?
entries.a: Press block user content on one of their videos. Q-Tube then hides that name's videos, and you can unblock it later from blocked names in your account menu.

entries.q: What is Your Channel in Q-Tube?
entries.a: Your Channel, in the side menu, is your page on Q-Tube: your videos and playlists, plus a channel description. Use add channel description to write one, publish it, and edit or delete it later. Everyone else's name opens their channel the same way.

entries.q: What does index video do in Q-Tube?
entries.a: Index video opens the Index Manager, where you publish search terms for a video so it can be found by searches such as Q-Search. Each index is a small publish with a fee. Extra indices keep your fees lower but count for less in search results.

entries.q: What notifications does Q-Tube show?
entries.a: When you are signed in, the bell in Q-Tube's top bar lists super likes on your videos, saying who sent them; tap one to open the video. It shows no new notifications when there are none.

entries.q: Where can I watch videos that explain Qortal?
entries.a: Watch the On Qortal channel on Q-Tube: it has explanatory videos about the network, Q-Apps and how to get started. Open it with qortal://APP/Q-Tube/channel/On Qortal/videos. The Welcome to Qortal app also points to it.

entries.q: What does it cost to use Q-Tube?
entries.a: Watching is free. Anything you publish is a QDN publish with the usual small network fee: a video, a playlist, a comment, a like and an index each count. A super like also sends the QORT you choose to the creator.

entries.q: Is there a Q-Tube+?
entries.a: Q-Tube+ is a pre-release version being built in the Q-Apps+ suite, using the same videos, playlists and channels as Q-Tube. As of November 2026 it hasn't been published, so use Q-Tube.

entries.q: What is Q-Shop?
entries.a: Q-Shop is Qortal's shop app (qortal://APP/Q-Shop): sellers open a shop and list products, and buyers pay the seller directly in QORT or Pirate Chain (ARRR), with no platform fee and no one in the middle. Orders are encrypted for the buyer and the seller. Q-Shops is a different app: a marketplace of shops made with Qortal Web Builder.

entries.q: How do I buy something on Q-Shop?
aliases: buy a product in q-shop app
entries.a:
1. Open a shop and press Add to Cart on the products you want.
2. Open My Cart and choose the coin to pay with.
3. Fill in the Delivery Information.
4. Confirm the purchase: Hub asks you to approve the payment, then to publish your order.
You pay the seller directly. The seller gets your order as an encrypted Q-Mail, and it shows under My Orders.

entries.q: What coins can I pay with on Q-Shop?
entries.a: QORT, and Pirate Chain (ARRR) when the shop accepts it: each shop chooses its Supported Coins, and the shop's page shows them. You pay from your wallet in Hub.

entries.q: Is buying on Q-Shop safe?
aliases: can i trust a q-shop seller
entries.a: There is no one in the middle: you pay the seller directly, there is no escrow or support desk, and a payment you send can't be taken back. Before buying, read the shop's reviews and its Average Review, ask the seller anything unclear by Q-Mail, and start with a small order at a shop you don't know.

entries.q: Can I get a refund on Q-Shop?
entries.a: Only from the seller. Q-Shop can't reverse a payment, so a refund is something the seller sends you. Write to the seller by Q-Mail first, because most problems are a mix-up. A seller who refunds can set the order's status to Refunded, and your review tells other buyers how it went.

entries.q: Where do I see my Q-Shop orders?
entries.a: Open My Orders from your account menu in Q-Shop. Each order shows its status as the seller sets it: Received, Shipped or Refunded. For anything else, write to the seller by Q-Mail.

entries.q: I paid on Q-Shop but my order isn't there. What should I do?
entries.a: Don't pay again. Q-Shop sends your payment first and publishes the order after it, so if it said Order failed to be placed, the seller has your payment but no order. Write to the seller by Q-Mail with what you ordered and when you paid.

entries.q: Are Q-Shop orders private?
entries.a: Your order, with your delivery details, is published encrypted so only you and the seller can read it, and the order Q-Mail the seller gets is encrypted too. Payments are ordinary blockchain transactions, which anyone can see.

entries.q: How do I open my own shop on Q-Shop?
entries.a: Sign in with your registered name and press Create Shop. Fill in the shop's name, description, location, where it ships and its Supported Coins (if you take Pirate Chain, import or enter your ARRR address), then publish and confirm in Hub. Then accept the second request, which creates the shop's data container; Q-Shop says this step is obligatory. If that step fails, press Retry Publishing.

entries.q: How do I add products to my Q-Shop?
entries.a: Open your shop's Product Manager and press Add Another Product. Give it a title, a description and pictures, choose Physical or Digital, set the Price in QORT (and Price in ARRR if you take it), a category and its status (Available, Out of stock or Retired), then press Save Products and confirm in Hub.

entries.q: How do I get paid as a Q-Shop seller?
entries.a: Buyers pay you directly: QORT to your Qortal address and ARRR to the ARRR address in your shop's details. Each new order reaches you as an encrypted Q-Mail (You have sold a product for your shop!) and in your shop's Orders, with the buyer's delivery details.

entries.q: How do I mark a Q-Shop order as shipped?
entries.a: In your shop's Product Manager, open the order under Orders, set its Order Status (Received, Shipped or Refunded), add a note if you like, and press Update Status. Hub asks you to confirm the small publish.

entries.q: How do reviews work on Q-Shop?
entries.a: You can review a shop only after you have ordered from it: press Add Review, give it a title and write your review. Each shop shows its Average Review, so you can see how others found it before you buy.

entries.q: What is the difference between Q-Shop and Q-Shop+?
entries.a: Q-Shop+ is a pre-release test version of a redesigned Q-Shop; for everyday buying and selling use Q-Shop. It reads and writes the same shops, products, orders and reviews, so a shop made in either shows in both. The test version tries things such as search across shops, a step-by-step checkout, auctions, variants, delivery prices and discount codes, and these may still change. Payments and orders made in it are real, the same as in Q-Shop.

entries.q: How do I take a product off my Q-Shop?
entries.a: Open Product Manager, edit the product, set its Product Status to Out of stock or Retired, then press Save Products and confirm in Hub; buyers then can't add it to their cart. Q-Shop has no delete, because QDN can't erase what you published.

entries.q: How do I contact a seller on Q-Shop?
entries.a: Q-Shop works with Q-Mail: write to the shop owner's registered name in Q-Mail, which encrypts your message to them. The seller's name is on the shop's page, and the Q-Mail item in Q-Shop's account menu opens Q-Mail.

entries.q: What is Q-Fund?
entries.a: Q-Fund is Qortal's crowdfunding Q-App (qortal://APP/Q-Fund). Someone starts a campaign with a goal in QORT and an end date, and people donate QORT to it, with no middleman and no platform fee. If the goal is met by the deadline the donations go to the creator; otherwise the funds are returned. Campaigns, updates and comments are published on QDN.

entries.q: How do I donate to a Q-Fund campaign?
entries.a: Open the campaign, press Back this project (or Donate Now), enter how much QORT to give and confirm the payment in Hub. The QORT goes to the campaign's AT, a small program on the chain that holds the funds until the deadline. You can't donate while a campaign is still being deployed or after it has ended.

entries.q: How do I start a Q-Fund campaign?
entries.a: Sign in with your registered name and press Start a Q-Fund. Fill in the title, a few words about it, the full description, a cover image and any attachments, the Goal Amount (QORT), and an end date 2 to 30 days away. Publishing deploys the campaign's AT on the chain, with 0.2 QORT sent to it, plus the usual publish fees; Hub asks you to confirm.

entries.q: What happens if a Q-Fund doesn't reach its goal?
entries.a: The donations only go to the creator if the goal is reached by the deadline. If it isn't, the funds are returned instead of going to the creator. When the campaign ends, its page says Q-Fund Goal Achieved or Q-Fund Goal Not Achieved.

entries.q: How long can a Q-Fund campaign run?
entries.a: Between 2 and 30 days: you pick the end date when you create the campaign. The campaign page shows the Estimated Time Remaining until it ends.

entries.q: How do I post an update on my Q-Fund campaign?
entries.a: Open your campaign and press Add an update. Give it a title, write the update and add files if needed, then publish. Donors and visitors see the latest updates from the campaign owner on its page, and you can edit an update later.

entries.q: Can I see who donated to a Q-Fund campaign?
entries.a: Yes. Show list of donors on the campaign opens the Donor Details. Donations are ordinary QORT payments to the campaign's AT, so they are public on the chain.

entries.q: What does Q-Fund has been modified after its creation mean?
entries.a: Q-Fund shows this when a campaign's details were edited after it was created. Read the campaign again before you donate, and check its updates and comments.

entries.q: Can I review a Q-Fund owner?
entries.a: Yes. Use Add Review on a campaign to review its owner, with a title and your text. The page shows the owner's Average Review, so you can check others' experience before donating.

entries.q: Is there a Q-Fund+ or Q-Support+?
entries.a: Both are pre-release versions still being built in the Q-Apps+ suite, reading the same campaigns and issues as Q-Fund and Q-Support. As of November 2026 neither has been published, so use Q-Fund and Q-Support.

entries.q: What is Q-Support?
entries.a: Q-Support (qortal://APP/Q-Support) is where you report issues to the Qortal developers or to Q-App developers: bug reports, feature requests and tech support questions about Qortal Core, Hub, GO, Q-Apps and websites. An issue can carry a bounty or a link to a Q-Fund to reward whoever solves it.

entries.q: How do I report a bug or request a feature in Q-Support?
entries.a:
1. Sign in with your registered name and press Open an Issue.
2. Write the Title of Issue and the Description of Issue.
3. Pick what it is about (Core, Qortal Hub, Qortal Go, Q-Apps/Websites with the app's name, and others) and its type (Bug Report, Feature Request, Tech Support or Other).
4. Add links, a source-code link or files if they help, and an optional bounty.
5. Publish and confirm in Hub.

entries.q: Does Q-Support charge a fee to post an issue?
entries.a: Yes. When you publish an issue, Q-Support asks you to agree to a small fee for its further development; the box is ticked by default and shows the amount. Issues whose fee was paid show a mark in the list. Each publish also has the normal QDN fee.

entries.q: What is a bounty in Q-Support?
entries.a: A bounty is a reward offered for solving an issue. When you open an issue you can enter a Bounty Amount in QORT or another coin (BTC, LTC, DOGE, DGB, RVN or ARRR), or a link to a Q-Fund that raises money for it. An issue linked to a Q-Fund has Donate to Crowdfund, which sends QORT to that campaign.

entries.q: How do I find issues in Q-Support?
entries.a: Use the search box and the sort options: Sort by Newest, Oldest, Bounty or User. You can narrow the list by category, or by a User's Name (Exact) to see one person's issues.

entries.q: What do the statuses in Q-Support mean?
entries.a: Each issue has a status, Open, In Progress, Complete or Closed, chosen by its publisher and changed with Update Issue as the work goes on. Comments under the issue hold the discussion.

entries.q: What features does the Q-Node app have?
entries.a: Q-Node (qortal://APP/Q-Node) manages your own Qortal node from Hub. It shows a dashboard of widgets (sync status, block height, Core version, node uptime, minting status, connected peers and QDN data peers), the peer lists, and the node's minting accounts, and it has admin actions: restart, stop, bootstrap and force sync. It replaces the old Node Management screen.

entries.q: Why doesn't Q-Node work on the public node?
entries.a: Q-Node's actions are admin commands for your own node, and Hub refuses them while you're connected to a public node. Switch Hub to your local node, or a custom node of your own, and open Q-Node again.

entries.q: How do I add a peer in Q-Node?
entries.a: In the connected peers list press add new peer and type the peer's hostname, IPv4 or IPv6 address, adding :port if needed. Remove takes a peer off the list. QDN data peers are added and removed the same way in their own list. Hub asks you to approve each change.

entries.q: How do I restart or stop my node from Q-Node?
entries.a: Use Q-Node's admin actions and approve each in Hub. Restart can take up to 5 minutes. Stop shuts the node down, and you have to start it again yourself. Bootstrap rebuilds the node's chain from a bootstrap download and can take up to 10 minutes to begin.

entries.q: What does force sync do in Q-Node?
entries.a: Force sync, on a peer in Q-Node's peer list, tells your node to sync its chain from that peer; Q-Node shows starting sync with peer and the address. Choose a peer whose last height matches the rest of the network.

entries.q: Is there a Q-Node+?
entries.a: Q-Node+ is a pre-release version still being built in the Q-Apps+ suite, with the same node controls as Q-Node. As of November 2026 it hasn't been published, so use Q-Node.

entries.q: What is the Q-Trade app?
entries.a: Q-Trade (qortal://APP/Q-Trade) is the Q-App for buying and selling QORT for other coins (LTC, BTC, DOGE, DGB, RVN and ARRR) directly with other users, through Qortal's on-chain trade system. It shows open sell orders, your buy and sell history, recent trades and stuck orders. Its makers add no fees of their own.

entries.q: How do I buy QORT in Q-Trade?
aliases: q-trade how to buy qort step by step
entries.a:
1. Choose the coin you will pay with and make sure your wallet for that coin in Hub has enough.
2. In Open Market Sell Orders, select the orders you want and press BUY.
3. Confirm in Hub, and keep Q-Trade open until it answers.
4. Follow it under My Pending Orders until it completes.
Another buyer can take the same order first; a trade that doesn't go through is refunded.

entries.q: How do I sell QORT in Q-Trade?
entries.a: Open Sell QORT, press New Sell Order, enter the QORT amount and your price in the other coin, and press Create sell order, then confirm in Hub. Your order shows in the market until someone buys it or you cancel it. Selling needs your own node: managing sell orders isn't possible on a public (gateway) node.

entries.q: How do I cancel a sell order in Q-Trade?
entries.a: Find the order under your sell orders and press Cancel sell order, then confirm in Hub. Orders that got stuck are listed under Stuck orders, each with Cancel sell. It can take a couple of minutes for the change to show across the network.

entries.q: Where is my trade history in Q-Trade?
entries.a: Open Trade History for My Buy History, My Sell History and Historic Trades (the most recent 20). After you submit a buy, Q-Trade offers Download record or Save Record; keep it in case a trade gets stuck.

entries.q: Why does Q-Trade send me to Q-Wallets?
entries.a: Q-Trade shows your QORT and other-coin balances, but sending a foreign coin is done in Q-Wallets: press Send, then Open Q-Wallets, which opens that coin's wallet in a new tab. Receive shows the address to fund the wallet you trade with.

entries.q: Is there a Q-Trade+?
entries.a: Q-Trade+ is a pre-release version still being built in the Q-Apps+ suite, with the same orders and fees as Q-Trade and the trading logic kept as it is. As of November 2026 it hasn't been published, so use Q-Trade.

entries.q: What is Q-Assets?
entries.a: Q-Assets (qortal://APP/Q-Assets) is the app for Qortal's native assets: issue an asset, look up its details and holders, trade it for QORT, track portfolios and read issuers' news. Assets are tokens on Qortal's own chain, checked by Qortal Core just like QORT, and trades settle peer-to-peer with no custodian.

entries.q: How are Q-Assets different from QORT?
entries.a: QORT is created by consensus: it began at the genesis block with no coins and is minted into existence by Qortal's minters. Every other asset is created by a user who issues it, so its supply is decided by that one issuer. Both are validated on chain in the same way. Q-Assets suggests using assets as stock-like ownership proofs, group ownership or distributions.

entries.q: How do I find assets in Q-Assets?
entries.a: Open the Asset Explorer to browse and filter assets. Assets with fewer than four completed QORT trades are hidden by default, except your own holdings, assets you issued and assets less than seven days old; turn on Show low-volume assets to see them all. New assets carry a NEW badge, their issuer's details and a caution notice.

entries.q: How do I trade an asset in Q-Assets?
entries.a: Open the asset's market. The order book lists what buyers offer and sellers ask, priced in QORT; click a price level to prefill your order. Enter the quantity and price, press Place BUY or Place SELL and confirm in Hub. Q-Assets uses limit orders only, has no exchange fee (just the network fee), and shows your open orders in the My Orders strip, where you can cancel them.

entries.q: Does placing an order in Q-Assets mean my trade went through?
aliases: my asset order did not buy
entries.a: No. Placing an order puts it on the order book; it fills only when matching orders meet it, all at once or bit by bit. A new order shows as confirming until the network confirms it, and My Orders shows what quantity remains. You can cancel what hasn't filled.

entries.q: How do I issue my own asset in Q-Assets?
entries.a: Open Issue Asset and fill in the Asset Name, a description, the total supply and whether it is divisible, then optionally a primary group (recommended) and whether it is private, which needs a private group. Confirm in Hub: the whole supply is created in your account at once. You can then publish a Genesis Publication that describes the asset for holders.

entries.q: What does divisible mean for a Q-Asset?
entries.a: A divisible asset can be held and traded in fractions. An indivisible one comes in whole units only, so Q-Assets asks for whole numbers when you trade it. You choose this when you issue the asset.

entries.q: What is a private asset in Q-Assets?
entries.a: A private asset is tied to a private group the issuer chooses: Q-Assets shows its details only to members of that group. Converting an asset to private asks you to pick the group and confirm.

entries.q: What does Asset Data show in Q-Assets?
entries.a: Asset Data gathers what the chain knows about an asset: ownership, the original issuance, supply, divisibility, spending flags, on-chain metadata, holders and confirmed transactions. Holders tells the current owner apart from the original issuer.

entries.q: What does circulating supply mean in Q-Assets?
aliases: how much of an asset is out
entries.a: Q-Assets counts as circulating only what is out of the owner's hands: it leaves out the current owner's own balance and the unsold part of their sell orders, so listing tokens for sale doesn't make them circulate. If balances or orders can't be checked, it shows the figure as unavailable.

entries.q: What is Xqlore in Q-Assets?
entries.a: Xqlore is Q-Assets' explorer for the Qortal network: search names and open their profiles, see an account's activity and trading history, and look at network trading and long-term statistics. It reads what it shows from the node you are connected to.

entries.q: What is Q-Deck in Q-Assets?
entries.a: Q-Deck is the project area in Q-Assets: group boards and projects with tasks, assets linked to a project, and shared schedules. Tasks can receive paid upvotes and bounties to support them.

entries.q: How do I get Q-Assets notifications?
entries.a: Q-Assets offers to register Qortal Hub alerts for its announcements and asset news; accept Hub's permission when it asks. Issuers can also send notifications and an encrypted Q-Mail to their asset's primary group members.

entries.q: Can I get an asset back if I send it to the wrong address?
entries.a: No. An asset transfer, like a QORT payment, can't be reversed. Q-Assets warns about the Qortal Null Account in particular: it has no owner and no private key, so anything sent there can never be recovered. Check the recipient before you confirm.

entries.q: What is Q-Charts?
entries.a: Q-Charts (qortal://APP/Q-Charts) draws charts of past QORT trades against LTC, BTC, DOGE, DGB, RVN and ARRR, built from the trade data on the chain, with daily candles and a moving average over ranges from 1 month to 3 years. Hover a candle to see its volume. Its History view shows the merged trade history with the top buyer and seller.

entries.q: Why is Q-Charts slow the first time?
entries.a: The first time, Q-Charts pulls all trade data from the chain and saves it in a cache in your browser, which takes a while. After that it only fetches newer trades: press Fetch Newer Trades when it says the cached data may be outdated. Clear Cache starts over.

entries.q: What is Q-Search?
entries.a: Q-Search (qortal://APP/Q-Search) is a search engine for Qortal. Type words into Search Qortal and it lists the qortal:// links people have indexed under those words, each with its title, description, app and path. Tap a result to open it in a new tab.

entries.q: Why doesn't Q-Search find my content?
entries.a: Q-Search only finds links someone has indexed with search terms. Index your content with an Index button: on any Q-Search result, or in apps such as Q-Tube (index video). In the Index Manager, add your search terms and a title and description for the link, then publish.

entries.q: What is the Index Manager in Q-Apps?
entries.a: The Index Manager, opened from Index buttons in Q-Search, Q-Tube and other apps, publishes search terms for a qortal:// link (Create new index, Publish index) and an optional title and description (Add metadata). It suggests Recommended Indices and asks you to keep terms short. Each index is a small publish; extra indices for the same link cost less but count for less in search results.

entries.q: What is the Stats Board in Q-Mintership?
entries.a: The Stats Board in the original Q-Mintership shows nomination statistics, including Nominator Stats with a leaderboard of nominations by nominator. Cards published before June 2026, before the nominator method, count as legacy activity and are left out of the leaderboard.

entries.q: What is the account details explorer in Q-Mintership?
entries.a: The original Q-Mintership has a User Account Details Explorer: for any account it shows an overview, past transactions and older sponsorship statistics, so the community and Minter Admins can review a candidate more easily.

entries.q: What can I find in the Welcome to Qortal app?
entries.a: Welcome to Qortal (qortal://APP/Welcome to Qortal) is a guide for newcomers: what Qortal is and why it is different, getting started with Hub, account security, nodes, an introduction to minting, the mobile app, building on Qortal, community help, a FAQ and a glossary. It also has a Q-App catalog and live network stats.

entries.q: What is Q-Blog?
entries.a: Q-Blog (qortal://APP/Q-Blog) is Qortal's blogging app. You create a blog under your registered name and publish posts on QDN that mix text with images, videos, audio, files and polls. Readers can comment, bookmark posts and blogs, subscribe to blogs and tip a writer.

entries.q: How do I create a blog on Q-Blog?
entries.a: Sign in with your registered name, open the account menu and choose Create new blog. Give it a title, a Blog Id (it forms the blog's link, shown under Url Preview), a description, a category and tags, then publish and confirm in Hub. My Blogs lists the blogs you own.

entries.q: How do I write a post on Q-Blog?
entries.a: Open your blog and press Create Post. Pick the Minimal Editor for plain writing, or the Builder Editor to lay out text, images, video, audio, files and polls in blocks; switching editor type deletes what you've written so far. Add the post title and description, then publish and confirm in Hub.

entries.q: What is Wiki Mode on Q-Blog?
entries.a: Wiki Mode lets other names write and edit posts in your blog. Turn on Enable Wiki Mode when you create or edit the blog. Leave the Editor Whitelist empty to let any name take part except those in the Editor Blacklist, or list names in the whitelist to allow only them (comma-separated). You, the owner, can always edit.

entries.q: How do I add a poll to a Q-Blog post?
entries.a: Create the poll under My Polls with Create new poll: a poll name, a description and the options (Add option for more), then Create Poll. Embed it in a post with Add a poll in the editor. Readers vote right in the post.

entries.q: How do I tip a writer on Q-Blog?
entries.a: Press Support on the writer's blog or post, choose the coin (QORT, BTC, LTC, DOGE, DGB, RVN or ARRR) and the amount, then press Send Coin and confirm the payment in Hub. It goes straight to the author from your Hub wallet, and a sent payment can't be undone.

entries.q: How do I follow and save blogs on Q-Blog?
entries.a: Press Subscribe on a blog to follow it; Subscriptions in the account menu lists the blogs you follow. Save bookmark keeps a post or blog under Bookmarks, where you can give each bookmark a folder name, for example Research, to keep them organised.

entries.q: Can I comment on Q-Blog posts?
entries.a: Yes, with a registered name: write in Your comment under the post and submit it, or reply to another comment. A comment must be under 200 characters, and each one is a small public QDN publish.

entries.q: What is Ear-Bump?
entries.a: Ear-Bump (qortal://APP/Ear-Bump) is a music app on Qortal: upload songs and playlists under your name, listen to what others publish, like songs and playlists, and search the library. Songs are published on QDN as audio, so they play from the nodes that hold them.

entries.q: How do I upload a song to Ear-Bump?
entries.a: Sign in with your registered name, press Add Song, choose the song file and a cover image, and enter the song title and author; every field is required. Publish and confirm in Hub, and Ear-Bump says Song created! when it's done.

entries.q: How do I make a playlist on Ear-Bump?
entries.a: Press Add Playlist, give it a title, a description and an image (all required), add songs, and press Save Playlist. Your playlists then appear under My Playlists in Your Library.

entries.q: How do I find music on Ear-Bump?
entries.a: Use Search (What do you want to listen to?), browse Newest songs and Playlists, or press Discover a Playlist (Shuffle) for a random one. Your Library keeps My Songs, My Playlists, Liked Songs and Liked Playlists.

entries.q: What can I publish on SubWire?
entries.a: SubWire (qortal://APP/SubWire) publishes two kinds of posts: essays, which are text articles with rich formatting, images and embeds, and episodes, which are podcast or video posts with an audio or video file (MP3, WAV, MP4, MOV or AVI) and a cover image. Each can be public or only for your subscribers.

entries.q: How do I write an article on SubWire?
entries.a: Sign in with a registered name and press Write, then choose an essay or an episode. Add a title, an optional subtitle, a category, a cover image and your text or media, choose public or subscribers-only under Publishing Options, and publish. Save Draft keeps unfinished work under Your Drafts.

entries.q: How do subscriber-only articles work on SubWire?
entries.a: Attach a private group you own to your SubWire profile as its subscription group. You can then publish articles encrypted so only members of that group can read them. By default the title, subtitle and cover image stay public so people can discover the article; turn on Also encrypt title, subtitle & cover image to hide everything.

entries.q: How do I charge for my SubWire articles?
entries.a: SubWire's subscriber content uses a private group with a subscription set up for it. Create a private group, set up a QORT subscription for it (the Subscriptions app does this), then attach that group to your SubWire profile. People who subscribe and are let into the group can read your subscribers-only articles.

entries.q: How do I set up my SubWire profile?
entries.a: Open your profile and press Edit Profile to add a bio, a cover image and, if you like, a subscription group for subscriber-only content. Your profile is your author page, listing your publications.

entries.q: Can I announce my SubWire article on Torq?
entries.a: Yes. After you publish, SubWire asks Share on Quitter? and lets you edit a short post announcing the article before posting it. Torq reads the same posts as Quitter, so the announcement shows in Torq feeds too.

entries.q: How do I find writers on SubWire?
entries.a: Use Explore to discover publications and authors, or search for users by name. Your Home feed shows articles from the authors you follow.

entries.q: Why can't I read a SubWire article?
entries.a: If it is a subscribers-only article, you need to be a member of the author's subscription group. If you are a member and it still won't open, wait for the group keys to sync and try again. Article Not Found means it may have been deleted or the link is wrong.

entries.q: What is the Subscriptions app?
entries.a: Subscriptions (qortal://APP/Subscriptions) lets the owner of a private Qortal group sell access to it for QORT. Subscribers pay on a billing interval, the owner accepts them into the group, and they can then read the group's encrypted content. Home has Subscriptions I'm in, Subscriptions I manage and Create subscription.

entries.q: How do I create a subscription for my group?
entries.a:
1. Open Subscriptions and press Create subscription.
2. Choose a private group you own (create one first if you have none).
3. Set the pricing rules: Price (QORT, at least 1, up to 2 decimals), Billing Interval (Daily or Monthly, 30 days) and a Grace Period.
4. Add the details and what subscribers get, one perk per line.
5. Press Publish & create and confirm in Hub.

entries.q: How do I subscribe to a group in the Subscriptions app?
entries.a: Open the subscription's page and press Pay subscription, then confirm the payment in Hub. Next, join the group and publish your subscription record on chain when asked; it links your payment to the subscription. The manager then approves your join request and re-encrypts the group keys, after which you can read the group's encrypted content.

entries.q: I paid a subscription but have no access yet. Why?
aliases: cant see group content after paying
entries.a: Access needs two steps from the subscription's manager: approving your join request, and re-encrypting the group keys so they include you. That usually happens when they review new subscribers, and you get access by yourself once it's done. Meanwhile the page shows Pending Approval or Waiting for Access.

entries.q: What happens if I don't pay my subscription on time?
entries.a: Each subscription has a billing interval and a grace period after a payment is due. When it's due, Subscriptions says your payment is due and asks you to pay to keep access. A manager can remove members whose payment is overdue, and the app shows you the reason.

entries.q: How do I leave a subscription?
entries.a: Press Leave Group on the subscription and confirm. Leaving the group ends the subscription: you lose access to the group's content and perks. This can't be undone; to get access back you would need to subscribe again.

entries.q: How do I accept new subscribers in the Subscriptions app?
entries.a: Open your subscription under Subscriptions I manage and use Review & Accept Requests; only people who paid and published their subscription record can be invited. After accepting, wait about 2.5 minutes while the network processes it, keeping the window open, then press Re-encrypt Keys so the new members can read the group's encrypted content.

entries.q: Can I pause or change my subscription in the Subscriptions app?
entries.a: Yes. Edit the subscription's details and save; changing the price creates a new pricing version. To pause it, set Subscription Status to not accepting new subscribers: nobody new can subscribe or pay, existing members keep their access, and you can re-enable it later.

entries.q: How do I see who has paid in the Subscriptions app?
entries.a: Open the subscription under Subscriptions I manage. Its members list shows each member's Last paid, Amount paid, Pricing version, when their subscription ends and the payment transaction. Unpaid only shows just the members who haven't paid.

entries.q: How do I select several Q-Mails at once?
entries.a: Choose Select from a message's menu (right-click, or press and hold on a phone), or tick the box at the top of the inbox for Select all. A bar then appears with actions for the selected mail, such as Mark as read or unread and Archive, with Undo after archiving. A sender's group has its own menu to read, archive or select all its messages.

entries.q: How do I hide one of my names from the Q-Mail list?
entries.a: Right-click the name under Inbox (or press and hold it) and choose Hide from the list; it folds away at once, with Undo, and its mail stays in the Inbox. Settings → Mail can hide names too, lists the hidden ones to show them again, and has Hide names with nothing in the inbox for names whose mail is all archived.

entries.q: How do I make the Q-Mail panes wider or narrower?
entries.a: On a computer, drag the borders between the mailboxes, the message list and the open message to set their widths; Q-Mail remembers them. With no message open, the list uses the whole width. On a phone it shows one pane at a time.

entries.q: What does This message could not be shown mean in Q-Mail?
aliases: q-mail message could not be shown
entries.a: Q-Mail shows it in place of a broken message, for example one with an impossible date or a subject that isn't text, so the rest of your mail keeps working. An earlier message in a conversation that can't be shown says so in its own place.

entries.q: Can I open qortal:// links from inside a Q-Mail?
entries.a: Yes. qortal:// links in a mail open through Hub, so a group join link asks Hub to join that group and an app link opens the app. Treat links from people you don't know with care, as with any message.

entries.q: How do I watch an alias inbox in Q-Mail?
entries.a: Open Aliases, type the alias under Add alias and press Add Alias; mail sent to that alias then shows in its inbox. Alias Scan (Start alias scan, then Scan more) looks through older Q-Mail for alias mail you can open and carries on where the last run stopped. Each alias can also have a reply alias for your answers.

entries.q: How do I close a message on my phone in Q-Mail?
entries.a: Press Back, or swipe right from the left: it closes what is on top, such as an open message, the composer, an attachment preview, a dialog or Settings. A round arrow follows your finger and fills in when letting go will close it. The mailboxes menu closes with a swipe left.

entries.q: How do I switch between list and grid view in Q-Share?
entries.a: Use the List/Grid switch above the lists on Home, profiles and collections, or set it in Settings → Appearance.

entries.q: What does Load stats do in Q-Share settings?
entries.a: Settings → Network → Load stats counts every share on QDN, page by page, and shows how many shares there are and how many publishers made them. It only runs when you press it, because counting everything takes a while; Recount runs it again.

entries.q: How do I remove a share from a Q-Share collection?
entries.a: Open the collection and press Remove on the share. That republishes the collection, which is one small publish, and Hub asks you to confirm.

entries.q: Can I sell digital products on Q-Shop?
entries.a: Yes. When you add a product in Product Manager, choose Digital as its Product Type instead of Physical.

entries.q: What are promotions in Q-Assets?
