entries.a: Promotions let you pay, in QORT or an accepted asset, to promote content in Q-Assets' community feed for seven-day periods; holding Q-Assets can add bonus value to a promotion. Payments are checked before a promotion shows, and admins can block promotions.

entries.q: What are asset publications in Q-Assets?
entries.a: Issuers can publish pages about their assets on QDN: a Genesis Publication describing the asset, and Asset News for later updates, shown in Q-Assets' feeds next to the app's own announcements. Readers open them from the asset's page or with View News Publication on Q-Assets.

entries.q: How does a + app like Q-Share+ become the official version?
entries.a: Each + app goes through four stages: it is built in the Q-Apps+ project, published under its + name on QDN as a pre-release testground, tested with the community with fixes released as 1.0.x versions, and then offered to the original app as a pull request for its maintainers. Until that happens the stable app is the one to use. Q-Share 2.0 and Q-Mail 4.0 went all the way.

entries.q: Can I delete a SubWire article?
entries.a: Yes: on your own article choose Delete and confirm. SubWire warns that this can't be undone.

entries.q: Does opening a Q-Mail mark it as read?
aliases: why is my q-mail still bold
entries.a: Yes. Opening a message in your inbox or an alias inbox marks it read, and a sender's group stops being bold once all its messages are read. Read marks stay after a reload on this device; publish your mail state to carry them to another device.

entries.q: Which less common file types does Q-Share handle?
entries.a: Subtitle files (.srt, .vtt) and checksum files (.md5, .sha…) preview as text, audiobooks (.m4b) and WebM audio (.weba) play, and comic books (.cbz, .cbr) are listed as documents to download. Other files can always be downloaded and saved.

entries.q: How do I open someone's Q-Tube channel?
aliases: see all videos from a name q-tube
entries.a: Tap the creator's name on any of their videos, or open qortal://APP/Q-Tube/channel/<name>. The channel lists their videos and playlists, with their channel description. Subscribe and Follow sit beside the creator's name on each video.

entries.q: How does Q-Shop show prices in ARRR?
entries.a: If a shop accepts Pirate Chain and you choose ARRR as the coin, Q-Shop shows the rate it uses as 1 QORT = … ARRR, worked out from the latest trades on Qortal's trade system. If it can't get a rate, it goes back to QORT.

entries.q: What is an asset's primary group in Q-Assets?
entries.a: When you issue an asset you can pick a Qortal group as its primary group; Q-Assets calls it optional but recommended. The issuer can then send notifications and an encrypted Q-Mail to that group's members, and a private asset must use a private group.

entries.q: Can I edit my Q-Fund campaign after creating it?
entries.a: Yes, the owner can open the campaign with Update Crowdfund and publish changed details. Q-Fund then warns visitors that the Q-Fund has been modified after its creation, so explain what changed in an update.

entries.q: Can I comment on a Q-Fund campaign?
entries.a: Yes. Each campaign has Comments: write yours and submit it, and use Load More Comments to see older ones. You need a registered name, and each comment is a small public publish.

entries.q: Can I edit my Q-Support issue?
entries.a: Yes. Open your issue and use Update Issue to change its text, category, status or bounty, then Publish Edit and confirm in Hub; Publish Edit with Fee also pays Q-Support's development fee.

entries.q: What does the Q-Node peer list show?
entries.a: For each peer your node is connected to, Q-Node shows its address, the direction of the connection, the handshake status, the peer's last block height, its Core version and how long it has been connected, with actions such as remove and force sync. The QDN data peers have a list of their own.

entries.q: Does the Welcome to Qortal app show live network numbers?
entries.a: Yes. Its home page shows Live network stats: the block height, the number of MINTER group members and the network peers, refreshed while it's open. If it can't reach a node, it shows the last known values instead.

entries.q: What Hub alerts does the original Q-Mintership send?
entries.a: Since version 3.0.7, after you allow it, Q-Mintership can send Qortal Hub alerts: a forum reply to your post, an Admin Board or AR Board card that names you, a reply to your comment, and nomination comments, votes, invites and joins on the Minter Board for the nominator, the nominee and Minter Admins.

entries.q: How do I add links to my Q-Blog's menu bar?
entries.a: Open Manage your custom navbar links from your blog's editing tools, add each link with its Nav Item name, and press Save Navbar; Remove Navbar takes the bar away again.

entries.q: How do I block someone on Q-Blog?
entries.a: Use Block user content on their post to hide what they publish. Blocked Names in the account menu lists them, and Manage blocked names lets you unblock.

entries.q: Where can I see recent super likes on Q-Tube?
entries.a: The filters panel on Q-Tube's Home has a Recent Super Likes list with the latest super likes across Q-Tube; tap one to open its video. On a video's page, its own super likes and their messages show above the normal comments.

entries.q: Why can't I open a web link in a Q-Share description?
entries.a: Qortal Hub can't open ordinary web, email or phone links from inside a Q-App. In a share's description Q-Share offers to copy such a link instead (Copy web link), so you can paste it into your browser. qortal:// links in descriptions open normally in Hub or GO.

entries.q: Is QDN data stored on the blockchain?
aliases: is qdn data on the blockchain
qdn on chain or off chain
does qdn put files in blocks
are qdn files on the blockchain
entries.a: Mostly not. Each publish is a small transaction on the blockchain that records your name, the service, the identifier and a SHA-256 hash of the data. The files themselves are kept off-chain, on the disks of the Qortal nodes that host them. Only very small data, up to 239 bytes, fits inside the transaction itself.

entries.q: What is a QDN resource?
aliases: what is a resource on qortal
what counts as a qdn resource
what is a resource on qdn
entries.a: A resource is one published item on QDN. It can be a few characters of text, one file, or a whole folder of files such as a website. Each resource is found by three things: the publisher's registered name, a service (the type of content, such as VIDEO or WEBSITE) and an optional identifier. Publishing again to the same three replaces it.

entries.q: What is a service on QDN?
aliases: what does service mean on qdn
entries.a: A service is the type of content a resource holds, such as IMAGE, VIDEO, AUDIO, DOCUMENT, FILE, JSON, WEBSITE or APP. Each service has its own rules: some take one file, some a whole folder, and some have a size limit (IMAGE 10 MB, THUMBNAIL 500 KB, JSON 25 KB, APP 50 MB). Apps read the service to know how to show your data, so pick the one that fits.

entries.q: How many services does QDN have?
aliases: how many services are on qdn
entries.a: Qortal Core has over 40 public services and 10 private ones, whose names end in _PRIVATE. Most people meet only a few: IMAGE, THUMBNAIL, VIDEO, AUDIO, FILE, DOCUMENT, JSON, WEBSITE and APP. The others are used by particular Q-Apps, for example STORE and PRODUCT for shops or BLOG_POST for blogs.

entries.q: Which QDN service should I use for my file?
aliases: which service for a video qdn
what service do i choose on qdn
qdn service for a zip file
best service to publish a file qdn
which qdn service for my file
what service should i use on qdn
entries.a:
Photos: IMAGE (up to 10 MB). Small pictures and avatars: THUMBNAIL (500 KB).
Videos: VIDEO. Music and other sound: AUDIO.
PDFs and text documents: DOCUMENT. Any other file, such as a zip: FILE.
Small structured data: JSON (25 KB).
A website: WEBSITE. A Q-App: APP (50 MB).
Most of the time the Q-App you publish with, such as Q-Tube or Q-Share, picks the service for you.

entries.q: What is the difference between single-file and multi-file QDN services?
aliases: single file vs multi file qdn
can i publish a folder on qdn
entries.a: Most services hold exactly one file or piece of data, such as one IMAGE, one VIDEO or one JSON text, and Qortal Core refuses more. A few can hold a whole folder: WEBSITE, APP, FILES, GIF_REPOSITORY, GAME, BLOG, DATABASE, SNAPSHOT and GIT_REPOSITORY. To read one file out of a multi-file resource, an app has to give that file's path inside it.

entries.q: What is an ARBITRARY transaction on Qortal?
entries.a: It is the blockchain transaction type behind every QDN publish. It carries your name, the service, the identifier, a hash of the data (or the data itself when it is tiny) and the fee, and it is signed by your account. Nodes read these transactions to know what exists on QDN and which version of each resource is the newest.

entries.q: Where does my node keep QDN files?
aliases: where are qdn files on disk
where are qdn files stored on my computer
entries.a: Qortal Core keeps QDN files in a folder called data inside its own folder, apart from the blockchain database in the db folder. Temporary files and the built copies of apps and websites sit under data/_temp. You can move the store with the dataPath setting in Core's settings.json.

entries.q: How does QDN stop someone from changing my files?
aliases: can someone change my qdn files
can my qdn files be changed by someone
can someone edit my qdn website
entries.a: Every publish is signed by your account and records SHA-256 hashes on the blockchain: one for the data and one for a small file that lists the hash of every piece. Nodes check every piece they receive against those hashes and refuse any that don't match. Only the account that owns the name can publish a new version, so nobody else can replace your files.

entries.q: Can anyone see what I publish on QDN?
aliases: who can see my qdn files
can people see what i upload on qortal
can everyone see my qdn uploads
is what i publish on qdn public
entries.a: Yes, when you use a public service: anyone whose node can fetch it can open it. The record of the publish, meaning your name, the service, the identifier, the size and the time, is also on the public blockchain. For things only some people should read, use a private service (its name ends in _PRIVATE), which is encrypted for the people you choose. Even then, the record that you published something stays public.

entries.q: Which nodes store a QDN resource?
aliases: which nodes keep my qdn files
where is my qdn content hosted
entries.a: First the node you published from, which keeps the original copy. Then every node that follows your name downloads your publishes on its own. With the default settings, any node that opens a resource also keeps a copy and shares it with others. The more nodes hold it, the faster it loads and the safer it is.

entries.q: Does my node host things I only looked at?
aliases: does viewing qdn content host it
my node keeps what i open
does my node host what i view
do i host what i open on qdn
do i host videos i watch
entries.a: Yes, with the default storage policy, FOLLOWED_OR_VIEWED. When you open a website, app, video or file, your node downloads it, keeps it and can serve it to other people. It stays until your node needs the space or you block that name. A node set to the FOLLOWED policy keeps only names it follows.

entries.q: What QDN storage policies can a node use?
entries.a:
FOLLOWED_OR_VIEWED (the default): keeps names you follow and anything you open.
FOLLOWED: keeps only names you follow; other things you open are removed later.
VIEWED: keeps what you open but downloads nothing in advance.
ALL: tries to download and keep everything published.
NONE: keeps nothing.
Data from blocked names is never kept, whatever the policy.

entries.q: How do I change my node's QDN storage policy?
aliases: stop my node hosting viewed data
how to change qdn storage policy
entries.a: Close Qortal Core, open its settings.json and add a line such as "storagePolicy": "FOLLOWED", then start Core again. The value must be spelled exactly: FOLLOWED_OR_VIEWED, FOLLOWED, VIEWED, ALL or NONE. Core reports an error for any other value.

entries.q: How do I limit how much disk space QDN uses?
aliases: set a maximum for qdn data
entries.a: Set maxStorageCapacity in Qortal Core's settings.json to the most bytes QDN may use, for example 100000000000 for about 100 GB, and restart Core. Without it, Core counts the drive's free space plus the QDN data it already holds as its limit. It stops fetching new data at 80% of the limit and starts removing data at 90%.

entries.q: What happens when my node's QDN storage is full?
aliases: node disk full of qdn data
what does my node delete when full
entries.a: At 80% of its storage limit, your node stops fetching new QDN data in the background. At 90%, it deletes small batches of chunks at random, so that not every node drops the same pieces. It never deletes the original copies of files you uploaded from that node. The limit is the drive's free space plus the QDN data already stored, or maxStorageCapacity if you set a lower one.

entries.q: Will my node delete my own uploads to save space?
aliases: are my published files deleted when full
does my node keep my own data
does my node delete my uploads
are my own qdn files kept
own uploads safe when storage full
entries.a: No. When you publish, your node marks those files as the original copy, and the space cleanup skips them, because they may be the only copy on the network. Older versions are still removed after you publish a newer one. Keep your own backup of anything important anyway.

entries.q: Does following a name download everything they publish?
aliases: how much space does following take
following a name downloads all their content
how much does following a name download
entries.a: Yes. Your node downloads all of that name's QDN content and keeps fetching new publishes as they appear. Some names hold many gigabytes, so check first: in Q-Share, the Follow button's tooltip shows the name's current download size and number of files. Following helps the creator too, because the more nodes follow a name, the faster its content loads for everyone.

entries.q: Which apps have a Follow button for QDN names?
aliases: where do i follow a name
how do i follow a name on qdn
how to follow a publisher qdn
entries.a: Q-Apps such as Q-Share and Q-Tube show a Follow button next to a publisher. It adds the name to your node's followedNames list, which tells Qortal Core to host that name's data, and both apps use the same list. Following someone on Torq is a different, social follow: Torq publishes it to QDN so it shows in your feed.

entries.q: Where are my QDN follows stored?
aliases: are qortal follows on the blockchain
do follows move to another node
entries.a: Hosting follows, the ones made with the Follow button in apps like Q-Share and Q-Tube, are kept on your node, not on the blockchain and not in your account. Qortal Core keeps them in a small file in its lists folder. So every account that uses that node shares the same follows, and they don't come with you to another node or to the public node.

entries.q: Can I follow names while I'm on the public node?
aliases: follow button not working in go
follow names on the public node
entries.a: No. Follows are saved on the node itself, and Hub and GO refuse list changes on a public node, so Follow buttons in Q-Apps don't work there. Connect to your own node to follow names and host their data.

entries.q: What happens to hosted data when I unfollow a name?
entries.a: Your node stops downloading that name's new publishes. With the default FOLLOWED_OR_VIEWED policy, what it already holds stays until storage cleanup needs the space. With the FOLLOWED policy, the cleanup removes that name's data on one of its next passes.

entries.q: Does following a name for hosting cost QORT?
aliases: do i pay to follow on qdn
does following a name cost qort
entries.a: No. A hosting follow, made with the Follow button in apps such as Q-Share or Q-Tube, is a setting on your own node, not a blockchain transaction, so there is no fee. It costs disk space and bandwidth instead, because your node downloads and serves that name's content. A Torq follow is different: Torq publishes it, so it costs the normal publish fee.

entries.q: Does the public node keep QDN data for me?
aliases: why are apps slow on the public node
does the public node keep my data
apps reload slowly on public node
entries.a: Not for long. The public node serves many people and drops apps and files within hours, so the first open after a while often has to fetch everything from peers again. Your own node keeps what you open and follow, so it loads much faster the next time.

entries.q: What is relay mode on QDN?
aliases: does my node relay qdn data
entries.a: Relay mode lets your node pass QDN requests and chunks between other peers, even for data it doesn't host. Relayed chunks go into a temporary relay cache, not into your hosted data. It is on by default (relayModeEnabled in settings.json) and helps data reach nodes that can't connect to each other directly.

entries.q: How does my node find a QDN file?
aliases: where does my node get qdn data
how does my node get qdn files
entries.a: It asks its connected data peers which of them hold the resource's chunks. When one does, your node can connect to it directly and download the chunks, checking each against its hash. If there is no direct path, requests can be relayed through other nodes. Content with many hosts arrives fastest.

entries.q: What are QDN data peers?
aliases: what does qdn data peers mean
entries.a: Since Qortal Core 6, QDN has its own peer connections, separate from the ones used for blocks. Data peers are the nodes yours is connected to for swapping QDN files. Hub and GO show how many under "QDN (data) peers" in the core information panel. With few data peers, QDN content can be slow to load.

entries.q: Does my node need an open port to share QDN data?
aliases: do i need port forwarding to host qdn
entries.a: It helps, but it isn't required. QDN uses its own data port, 12394, and Qortal Core tries to open it on your router by UPnP when it starts. Nodes that others can't reach directly, publishers included, can still get and share data through relays via better-connected nodes.

entries.q: Can I turn off QDN on my node?
entries.a: Yes. Set "qdnEnabled": false in Qortal Core's settings.json and restart Core. The node then stores, serves and publishes no QDN data, so Q-Apps, websites and files won't load through it. The blockchain side keeps working.

entries.q: Can I move my QDN data to another drive?
aliases: move qdn data to another drive
store qdn on an external disk
entries.a: Yes. Close Qortal Core, move its data folder to the new drive, set "dataPath" in settings.json to the folder's new full path, and start Core again. If you point dataPath at an empty folder instead, your node starts with no QDN data and downloads what it hosts again.

entries.q: Does every node know about every QDN resource?
aliases: does my node know all qdn data
does every node have every qdn resource
do all nodes know all qdn content
entries.a: Every synced node knows that each resource exists, because every publish is a transaction in the blockchain. Over time, nodes also fetch each resource's small metadata file with its title, description and tags. The files themselves are downloaded only for names a node follows, things it opens, or everything if its policy is ALL.

entries.q: Why can I see a QDN resource in search but not open it?
aliases: resource in search but wont open
qdn file listed but not loading
search shows a video that cant play
found on qdn but not available
qdn resource found in search but wont open
entries.a: Search results come from the blockchain record of each publish, which every node has. The files are separate: they must come from a node that still holds them. If no node hosting it is online and reachable, your node keeps asking and shows "Waiting for data from peers..." until one appears.

entries.q: Why are titles missing on some QDN items?
aliases: why no titles on qdn items
why blank titles in app list
entries.a: Titles, descriptions and tags live in a small metadata file published with the data. Until your node has fetched that file, apps can show only the name and identifier. Nodes fetch metadata in the background, so titles usually fill in later; a public node may lack them for older items.

entries.q: What is a QDN metadata file?
aliases: what is the qdn metadata file
entries.a: It is a small JSON file published with most resources. It holds the title, description, tags and category, the list of chunk hashes, the file names inside the resource and its MIME type. Its hash is stored in the publish transaction, so it can't be changed afterwards.

entries.q: How long can a QDN title, description and tags be?
entries.a: Title: up to 80 bytes, which is 80 plain letters; accented letters and other scripts use more than one byte each. Description: up to 240 bytes. Tags: up to 5, each at most 20 characters. Qortal Core cuts a title or description that is too long, and drops a tag that is too long rather than shortening it.

entries.q: What categories can a QDN resource have?
entries.a: A resource can carry one optional category from Qortal Core's list of about 50, such as Art and Design, Books and Reference, Cryptocurrency and Blockchain, Entertainment, Gaming, Music, News, Self-Sufficiency and Homesteading, Software, Tools, Video, Other and Uncategorized. Hub's publish form and the Q-Apps library use these categories to sort apps and websites.

entries.q: What is a QDN chunk?
aliases: what is a chunk on qortal
how big is a qdn chunk
entries.a: A chunk is a piece of a published file. Before upload, Qortal Core compresses and encrypts the data, then cuts it into chunks of 512 KB, each with its own hash. Nodes share a file chunk by chunk and check every piece. Data small enough to fit in one chunk is kept whole.

entries.q: Why does a QDN loading page show 0 / 2 files?
entries.a: Until your node has a resource's metadata file, which lists its chunks, it can only count two things: that file and the data. So it shows 0 / 2 while it looks for peers. Once the metadata arrives, the real count appears, such as 3 / 14. If it stays at 0 / 2 for a long time, no reachable node is sending that resource right now.

entries.q: Is public QDN data encrypted?
aliases: are my public qdn files encrypted
is public data on qdn encrypted
entries.a: In a way. Qortal Core encrypts every upload with a fresh random key before cutting it into chunks, and the chunks stay encrypted on every node that stores them. But for public services that key is part of the public transaction, so any node can open the data, and your node keeps an unencrypted built copy of apps and sites you opened recently, for speed. To keep something private, use a _PRIVATE service, which your app encrypts for chosen people before upload.

entries.q: Can a node operator read private QDN data they host?
aliases: can nodes read private qdn data
private qdn files readable by host
can node operators read private qdn data
can the host read my private qdn files
can a node see my private files
entries.a: No. Data in a _PRIVATE service is encrypted by the app on your device before it reaches any node, using the public keys of the people allowed to read it. Hosting nodes store and pass on only that encrypted form. Only someone holding one of the matching private keys can decrypt it.

entries.q: What is the VIDEO service on QDN?
entries.a: VIDEO holds one video file. It has no size limit of its own, so the general limit of 2 GiB per publish applies. Q-Tube, for example, publishes each video as a VIDEO resource plus a DOCUMENT that describes it, with identifiers starting qtube_vid_. VIDEO_PRIVATE is the encrypted version for chosen viewers.

entries.q: Why must my node download a whole video before it plays?
aliases: why does a qdn video download before playing
entries.a: QDN stores a video zipped, encrypted and cut into chunks, so your node needs every chunk before it can put the file back together. Q-Tube and similar apps show a percentage while your node gathers them. Videos that many nodes host arrive faster, and once your node holds a video, it starts at once the next time.

entries.q: What is the AUDIO service on QDN?
entries.a: AUDIO holds one sound file, such as a song or a recording. Like VIDEO, it has no size limit of its own beyond the general 2 GiB per publish. Q-Apps such as Q-Mail, Q-Fund and Q-Shop use it for audio, and AUDIO_PRIVATE is the encrypted version.

entries.q: What is the difference between AUDIO, VOICE and PODCAST on QDN?
entries.a: All three hold one sound file. AUDIO and PODCAST have no size limit of their own beyond the general 2 GiB per publish. VOICE is meant for voice recordings and is capped at 10 MB, as is its encrypted twin VOICE_PRIVATE.

entries.q: What are the QCHAT services on QDN?
entries.a: They are services set aside for files shared in Q-Chat: QCHAT_IMAGE (up to 500 KB), QCHAT_ATTACHMENT (up to 1 MB), and QCHAT_AUDIO and QCHAT_VOICE (up to 10 MB each). QCHAT_ATTACHMENT_PRIVATE (1 MB) is the encrypted form. QCHAT_ATTACHMENT takes only zip, pdf, txt, odt, ods, doc, docx, xls, xlsx, ppt and pptx files.

entries.q: What is the ATTACHMENT service on QDN?
aliases: file attached to a mail qdn
entries.a: ATTACHMENT holds one file attached to something else, such as a mail, and is capped at 50 MB. ATTACHMENT_PRIVATE is the encrypted form with the same cap. Q-Mail uses it for mail attachments, so only the recipients can open them.

entries.q: What is the FILES service on QDN?
aliases: publish several files as one qdn
entries.a: FILES holds a bundle of several files, or a folder, as one resource, unlike FILE, which takes a single file. It has no size limit of its own beyond the general 2 GiB per publish. To get one file out of the bundle, an app asks for that file's path inside it.

entries.q: What is DOCUMENT_PRIVATE used for?
entries.a: DOCUMENT_PRIVATE holds one encrypted document. Hub and GO use it for things only certain people may read: a private group's secret key, encrypted for each member, and your saved settings and pinned apps, encrypted for yourself. Q-Mail keeps its saved mail state in it too. Its service number is 801, and it has no size limit of its own beyond the general 2 GiB.

entries.q: What are BLOG and BLOG_POST on QDN?
entries.a: BLOG_POST holds one post, and BLOG can hold a whole blog as a folder of files. Blogging apps use them, and so do others: Q-Mintership, for example, publishes its forum messages as BLOG_POST. Neither has a size limit of its own beyond the general 2 GiB.

entries.q: What is the COMMENT service on QDN?
entries.a: COMMENT holds one comment of up to 500 KB, published under the commenter's name. It differs from BLOG_COMMENT, which blogging apps use for comments on posts (also 500 KB), and from CHAIN_COMMENT, which is tiny (239 bytes) and kept fully on-chain.

entries.q: What is the PLAYLIST service on QDN?
entries.a: PLAYLIST holds one list that groups other resources, such as the videos of a series. Q-Tube uses it for playlists, with identifiers starting qtube_playlist_. The videos themselves are separate VIDEO publishes.

entries.q: What are STORE and PRODUCT on QDN?
entries.a: They are services for shops. Q-Shop publishes a shop as a STORE resource and its items as PRODUCT resources under the seller's name, and keeps other shop data in DOCUMENT and DOCUMENT_PRIVATE. OFFER and COUPON also exist for shop offers and coupons.

entries.q: What other services does QDN have?
entries.a: Besides the common ones, Qortal Core also has PLUGIN, EXTENSION, ITEM, DATABASE, SNAPSHOT, GIT_REPOSITORY, METADATA, ARBITRARY_DATA and CHAIN_DATA (239 bytes, kept on-chain). They are for more specialised uses. DATABASE, SNAPSHOT, GIT_REPOSITORY and ARBITRARY_DATA can hold folders; the others hold one file.

entries.q: What is CHAIN_DATA on QDN?
aliases: tiny data on the blockchain qortal
entries.a: CHAIN_DATA holds a tiny piece of data, up to 239 bytes, stored entirely inside the blockchain transaction, like CHAIN_COMMENT. Because nothing has to be fetched from peers, every synced node has it at once.

entries.q: Why does Qortal Core reject my publish for the service I chose?
aliases: why was my qdn publish rejected
entries.a: Each service checks what you send. Core refuses data over the service's size limit, a folder sent to a single-file service, JSON that isn't valid, a website without an index file, a GIF collection with anything other than .gif files, and encrypted data in a public service or plain data in a private one. Choose the service that matches your content.

entries.q: What is the maximum size of one QDN publish?
entries.a: 2 GiB, measured after Qortal Core zips and encrypts the data; Hub and GO refuse files over about 2 GB. That limit covers services with no smaller cap of their own, such as VIDEO, AUDIO, FILE and DOCUMENT. Hub's own publish form takes website zips up to 400 MB and app zips up to 50 MB.

entries.q: How do I publish a file bigger than 2 GB on QDN?
aliases: split a large file for qdn
upload a huge file to qdn
entries.a: Split it into parts of 2 GB or less and publish each part as its own resource, with identifiers that show the order. Whoever downloads them joins the parts again afterwards. GO's offline helper Qortino is published this way, in two parts, because QDN takes at most 2 GiB per file.

entries.q: Why can't I publish from GO on the public node?
aliases: cant publish on the public node
go publish fails on public node
public node does not take uploads
why cant i post media from go
entries.a: Publishing means uploading the file to a node, and the public node GO uses by default refuses uploads without its API key, which only its operator has. So QDN publishes from GO, such as posts with media, avatars or Q-App uploads, need your own node or a private node you have the API key for. You can switch nodes in GO's node settings.

entries.q: What does "Your node needs its API key to publish" mean?
aliases: your node needs its api key to publish
node needs api key to publish
entries.a: Qortal Core only accepts uploads from apps that send its API key. GO shows this message when your node refused a publish for that reason. Tap Open node settings in the publish window and enter your node's API key; Core keeps it in the apikey.txt file in its folder.

entries.q: What do I need before I can publish on QDN?
aliases: what do i need to publish qdn
what do i need to publish on qdn
entries.a:
A registered name, since every resource sits under a name you own.
A little QORT for the fee, about 0.01 QORT per publish.
A node that takes your uploads: your own node, or a private node you have the API key for.
Free disk space on that node, a bit more than twice the file's size.
The content in the right form for its service, for example a zip with index.html for a website.

entries.q: How much does it cost to publish on QDN?
aliases: how much to publish a video on qortal
entries.a: About 0.01 QORT per publish, the network's standard transaction fee. It is the same for a short text and a large video, because only a small record goes on the blockchain; nodes store the file itself. Each resource is its own publish, so an app that publishes five files charges five fees, and every update costs one more. The approval window always shows the exact fee.

entries.q: Does a bigger file cost more to publish on QDN?
aliases: is the qdn fee based on size
does qdn fee depend on file size
entries.a: No. The fee depends on the size of the transaction, not the file, and a publish transaction is always small because it holds only a hash of the data. So a 1 GB video costs the same fee as a short note. What a big file costs is upload time and disk space on the nodes that host it.

entries.q: Do I pay again when I update a QDN resource?
aliases: pay again to update my website
do i pay to update on qdn
entries.a: Yes. An update is a new publish to the same name, service and identifier, so it is a new transaction with the usual fee of about 0.01 QORT. Changing only the title or description is a new publish too. So is deleting, which really means publishing a replacement.

entries.q: Can I publish to QDN under someone else's name?
aliases: use someone elses name on qdn
which name does my publish use
entries.a: No. Qortal Core accepts a publish only when the account signing it owns the name it uses. If you own several names, you can use any of them, and the approval window shows which name the resource goes under.

entries.q: What happens step by step when I publish on QDN?
aliases: what happens when i publish on qdn
how does publishing on qdn work
how a publish reaches the network
entries.a:
1. The app sends your file to your node, in parts if it is large.
2. Qortal Core zips it, encrypts it and cuts it into 512 KB chunks, each with a hash.
3. Hub or GO signs the publish transaction with your key, and your node broadcasts it.
4. Other nodes add the record to their index. Those that follow your name, or open the resource, fetch the chunks and pass them on.

entries.q: How long until others can see what I published on QDN?
aliases: how long until my upload appears
my new publish is not visible
how long until my publish shows
when do others see my qdn publish
when will others see my website
entries.a: Usually a few minutes. Your publish is a transaction that has to reach other nodes, and then those nodes fetch the files from yours or another host. Hub asks you to wait a couple of minutes for the network to pick up the change. Keep your node online meanwhile, since at first it may hold the only copy.

entries.q: Why should I keep my node online after publishing?
aliases: publish then turn off my pc
qdn first copy only on my node
my upload is unavailable after shutdown
keep my node on after publishing
entries.a: Right after a publish, your node may be the only one holding the files. If it goes offline before other nodes have fetched them, nobody can load the resource until it comes back. Once followers and viewers hold copies, the content no longer depends on your node.

entries.q: What does GO's Publishing to QDN window show?
aliases: what is the publish bubble in go
minimize a qdn upload in go
publishing to qdn window in go
use another app while go publishes
entries.a: When a Q-App publishes a big file (5 MB or more), or a publish takes over 8 seconds, GO shows its own Publishing to QDN window. It shows each file's progress, the speed and the time left. You can minimize it into a small bubble and keep using the app; tap the bubble to see it again. It tells you when everything is published, or why a publish failed.

entries.q: What do Processing and Retrying mean while publishing to QDN?
aliases: your node did not answer trying again
entries.a: Processing means every part of the file is on your node, and the node is putting it together and preparing the transaction for signing. Retrying means your node did not answer, so GO tries again shortly. If the node refuses a publish outright, for example for a missing API key, it stops at once and says why.

entries.q: What should I do if a QDN publish timed out?
aliases: qdn publish timed out what now
entries.a: First check whether it went through: look for the resource in the app, or wait a few minutes and search again. Publishing again straight away can publish it twice and charge the fee twice. If it really isn't there, publish again.

entries.q: Why does publishing say "Not enough space on your hard drive"?
aliases: not enough space on your hard drive
disk space to publish on qdn
how much free space to publish
entries.a: Before a big upload, Hub and GO ask the node whether it has room. Qortal Core wants a little more than twice the file's size free, because it holds the uploaded parts and the joined, processed file at the same time. Free up space on the node's drive, or publish from a node with more room.

entries.q: Does QDN compress my files?
entries.a: Yes. Qortal Core zips everything it stores off-chain before encrypting it and cutting it into chunks. Tiny data that fits fully on-chain is stored without compression.

entries.q: Can I publish the same file twice on QDN?
aliases: publish the same file twice qdn
two copies of a file on qdn
republish same file with new identifier
entries.a: Yes, as two separate resources with different identifiers, names or services. Each is its own publish with its own fee, and nodes store each copy separately. Publishing again to the same name, service and identifier doesn't add a copy: it replaces the old version.

entries.q: What does the QDN publish approval window show?
aliases: allow this app to publish to qdn
what am i approving when publishing
entries.a: It asks "allow this app to publish to QDN?" and shows the service, the identifier, the name the resource goes under and the fee. For several files at once it lists each one with the total fee. It also says when the data will be encrypted, and if the app adds a fee of its own, you must tick "accept app fee" before you can approve.

entries.q: What is an app fee on a QDN publish?
aliases: why does an app charge an extra fee
entries.a: Some Q-Apps ask for a small payment to an address they name, along with a publish. The approval window then shows the app fee on top of the publish fee, and you must tick "accept app fee" to go ahead. The payment is sent after the publish succeeds; if it fails, you are told the publish went through but the app fee was not sent.

entries.q: Can a Q-App publish to QDN without asking me?
entries.a: Normally no: Hub and GO show an approval window for every publish, with its service, name and fee. An app can ask for session permissions, and if you accept them ("I trust this app and understand these permissions will auto-execute"), some actions, publishing included, can run without asking for the rest of that session. Accept that only for apps you trust.

entries.q: Why did only some of my files publish to QDN?
aliases: some resources have failed to publish
only some of my files published
entries.a: When an app publishes several files at once, each is its own publish, so some can fail while others succeed. GO's publish window then says "Some files did not publish" and marks each file. Retry only the failed ones, and check first that they really are missing, so you don't pay twice.

entries.q: Why can't I publish right after registering a name?
aliases: publish right after registering a name
registered name not found when publishing
entries.a: The name you publish under must already be registered on the blockchain, and a new registration only counts once it is in a block. Until then, a publish fails with "Name not found". Wait a minute or two and try again, and check that the publish uses a name your account owns, spelled exactly.

entries.q: Why does a publish say my QORT balance is insufficient?
aliases: need qort for the qdn fee
entries.a: Every publish needs its fee, about 0.01 QORT, in your balance, and a multi-file publish needs one fee per file plus any app fee. Hub and GO check this before they ask for approval. Add QORT to your account and try again.

entries.q: Does updating a QDN resource upload the whole file again?
aliases: update only the changed files qdn
does qdn upload the whole zip again
does an update upload everything again
entries.a: Yes. Every update is a complete new version: you send the whole file, or the whole website or app zip, again. Qortal Core doesn't upload only the changed parts, and other nodes then fetch the new version in full.

entries.q: What happens to the old version after I update a QDN resource?
aliases: old version after a qdn update
what happens to replaced qdn files
what happens to old versions on qdn
entries.a: Nodes serve only the newest version. Once a node sees your newer publish, it deletes the older version's files in its next cleanup and stops fetching them. The blockchain still keeps the record of each earlier publish, with its time, size and hash, but the old files fade from the network.

entries.q: Can I get an old version back after updating on QDN?
aliases: restore an old version on qdn
get back the previous version of my website
entries.a: Not from QDN in the usual way, because nodes delete the files of replaced versions. To roll back, publish the old files again to the same name, service and identifier, which costs the normal fee. So keep your own copy of everything you publish.

entries.q: Can I delete something I published on QDN?
aliases: can i delete my website on qdn
how do i delete something on qdn
entries.a: Not completely. You can replace it: publish a new version to the same name, service and identifier, such as a short delete marker, and apps then show it as deleted. Nodes drop the old files during cleanup, but the record of your earlier publish stays on the blockchain, and anyone who saved a copy keeps it. The replacement costs the normal fee.

entries.q: Why does an app say a QDN item was deleted by its publisher?
aliases: what does D mean on qdn
entries.a: The publisher replaced the item with a delete marker, for example the single letter D, at the same name, service and identifier. Apps such as Q-Share and Torq read that as deleted and hide the item. The earlier publish is still recorded on the blockchain, but nodes stop serving its old files.

entries.q: Can someone else delete my QDN content?
aliases: can someone delete my qdn files
can my content be removed from qdn
who can take down qdn data
can my qdn content be deleted by others
can someone censor my qdn content
entries.a: No. Only the account that owns the name can publish a replacement. A node operator can remove copies from their own node or block your name there, but that only changes what their node holds and shows. Your content stays available from every other node that hosts it.

entries.q: Can I remove QDN data from my own node?
aliases: delete hosted data from my node
free space from qdn hosted data
clear qdn data on my node
remove qdn data from my node
delete a local copy of qdn data
entries.a: Yes. A Q-App that manages hosted data can remove copies your node holds; the Qortal wiki points to the Host-Monitor-Plus Q-App for viewing and managing what your node shares. Hub and GO ask "allow this app to delete N hosted resources?" first. Blocking a name also removes its data from your node. This only affects your node, other nodes keep their copies, and it isn't possible on a public node.

entries.q: What is hosted data on Qortal?
aliases: which qdn files does my node store
entries.a: Hosted data is the QDN content your node currently stores and serves to others: your own uploads, the names you follow and things you opened. A Q-App can show you the list, but Hub and GO ask "allow this app to get a list of your hosted data?" first, and it doesn't work on a public node.

entries.q: Does QDN data expire?
aliases: is there an expiry date on qdn
how long does qdn keep files
entries.a: No, there is no expiry date. A resource stays available as long as at least one reachable node holds it. Copies disappear only when a node runs short of space, its storage policy doesn't keep that data, its operator blocks the name, or the publisher replaces the resource.

entries.q: Why does a Q-App or website open faster the second time?
aliases: why is a q-app slow again after a week
why is a q-app faster the second time
qdn site opens faster second time
app opens quicker after first time
entries.a: After the first open, your node keeps the chunks and a ready-built copy of the app or website, so the next visit is quick. That built copy expires after 7 days, and the next visit rebuilds it from the chunks your node still holds, which takes a moment. If the chunks are gone too, the node fetches them from peers again.

entries.q: What happens to my QDN content if I stop running my node?
aliases: stop running my node qdn content
turn off my node what happens to my website
shut down node lose qdn data
qdn data when my pc is off
entries.a: Whatever other nodes host stays available from them: the followers of your name and people who opened your content. Anything that only your node held can't be loaded until your node comes back. Your publishes stay recorded on the blockchain, and when your node returns, it serves its original copies again.

entries.q: What happens to my QDN content if I lose my seed phrase?
aliases: lost my account what happens to my website
can i update qdn after losing my seed
private qdn data with a lost key
qdn content after losing seed phrase
entries.a: Your public content stays on QDN as long as nodes host it, but you can no longer update or replace it, because only the account that owns the name can publish. Private data encrypted for your account can't be decrypted by anyone, you included. This can't be undone, so keep your seed phrase backed up safely.

entries.q: How do I keep my QDN content available for the long term?
aliases: my qdn content disappeared how to restore
entries.a: Keep a node online that holds your publishes, and follow your own name on a second node if you can. Ask people who value your content to follow your name, since every follower adds a copy. Keep the original files too: if your content ever vanishes from QDN, publish them again to the same name, service and identifier.

entries.q: What happens when I block a name's QDN data?
aliases: what does blocking a name do
entries.a: Your node stops downloading and serving that name's QDN content, even if you follow the name, and with the default storage policy it also deletes what it already holds. Pages from that name then say the name is blocked so content cannot be served. Other people's nodes are not affected, and you can unblock the name later.

entries.q: Is content on QDN moderated?
aliases: can bad content be published on qdn
entries.a: There is no central moderator. Anyone who owns a registered name can publish; Qortal Core checks only that the publisher owns the name and that the data fits the service's rules. Each node operator decides what their node stores and serves and can block names, and some Q-Apps let you hide publishers you don't want to see. So your own node and its block list are how you choose what you see and host.

entries.q: Can I publish anonymously on QDN?
aliases: is my qdn publish linked to me
who can see i published this
entries.a: Not fully. Every publish is signed by your account and sits under a registered name, so it is linked to that name and its address on the public blockchain for good. You can use a name that doesn't reveal who you are, but everything published under it stays linked to that name and account.

entries.q: Does blocking a name remove its content for everyone?
aliases: does blocking remove content for everyone
does blocking a name affect everyone
does my block affect other users
entries.a: No. Blocking changes only your own node: it stops fetching, holding and showing that name's data. Every other node decides for itself. That is how QDN avoids a central switch that could remove content for everyone.

entries.q: What is the difference between blocking a name and blocking an address?
aliases: block txs vs block qdn data
blocking an address vs a name
difference between blocking a name and an address
entries.a: Blocking a name is about QDN: your node stops fetching and showing that name's published data. Blocking an address is about transactions: your node stops processing things such as chat messages from that address. Hub and GO let you block either one or both.

entries.q: Can I unblock a name and get its QDN content back?
entries.a: Yes. Remove the name from your blocked list, and your node fetches and serves that name's data again, following your storage policy. Anything your node deleted while the name was blocked has to be downloaded again, from nodes that still host it.

entries.q: Can I see the history of a QDN resource?
aliases: list all versions of a qdn resource
see previous publishes of a resource
entries.a: Partly. Every publish to a resource is a transaction kept on the blockchain, so the times, sizes and hashes of all its versions stay on record, and search tools can list them. The files of older versions, though, are deleted by nodes once a newer version exists.

entries.q: What do QDN resource statuses mean?
entries.a:
Published: it exists, but your node hasn't downloaded it yet.
Downloading: your node is fetching its chunks from peers.
Downloaded: all files are on your node, not built yet.
Building: your node is putting the files together.
Ready: built and ready to open.
Missing data: your node couldn't get all the files yet; try again later.
Not published: no such resource exists.
Blocked: the name is on your node's block list.

entries.q: What does the Published status mean on QDN?
entries.a: Your node knows the resource exists, from its publish on the blockchain, but hasn't downloaded any of its files yet. Opening it, or following the name, makes your node start fetching it. In the Q-Apps library, such apps show a Download button instead of Open.

entries.q: How do I search for content on QDN?
aliases: how to find files on qortal
look for videos and files on qdn
entries.a: There is no single search engine. Each Q-App searches your node's index for its own kind of content: Q-Tube for videos, Q-Share for files, the Q-Apps library for apps and websites. The index comes from the publish records every node has, so a result can show up even when its files aren't available right now.

entries.q: What does "Building resource..." mean on a QDN loading page?
entries.a: Your node has every file of the resource and is building it: joining the chunks, decrypting them and unpacking the result so it can be shown. "Files downloaded, preparing..." is the step just before. It is usually quick, large apps and websites take longer, and the page reloads by itself when it's ready.

entries.q: What does "Unable to Load. Please try again later." mean?
aliases: unable to load please try again later
resource could not be loaded after multiple attempts
app failed to load on qortal
unable to load please try again
entries.a: The loading page tried to build the resource 10 times without success and stopped, saying "The resource could not be loaded after multiple attempts." Usually some chunks were still missing or the build failed. Wait a while, then reload the page or open the app again.

entries.q: What does "peers available" mean on a QDN loading page?
aliases: how many peers have this file
entries.a: While your node downloads a resource, the loading page shows how many peers are taking part in that transfer. More peers usually means a faster download. If no count shows, your node hasn't found anyone with the data yet.

entries.q: Is QDN part of Qortal Core?
aliases: do i need extra software for qdn
entries.a: Yes. Qortal Core, the node software, runs both the blockchain and QDN, so there is nothing extra to install. Since Core 6, QDN traffic runs on its own connections and port, 12394, next to the blockchain's peers. Hub and GO talk to Core to show and publish QDN content.

entries.q: Why does a Q-App take long to open the first time?
aliases: why is the app loading so long
q-app takes long to open first time
why is the first open of a q-app slow
entries.a: The first time, your node has to find the app on other nodes, download every chunk and build it before it can show anything. After that the app sits on your node, so it opens much faster, unless your node later removes it to free space. On a public node this first wait happens more often, because it drops apps within hours.

entries.q: What is the difference between Downloaded and Ready on QDN?
entries.a: Downloaded means every file of the resource is on your node, but it hasn't been built yet. Ready means it has been built, joined, decrypted and unpacked into a copy that can be shown at once. A Downloaded resource becomes Ready the next time it is opened, after a short build.

entries.q: What does Gathering from QDN mean in GO?
aliases: looking for the file on qdn
entries.a: When you save a QDN file in GO, it first shows "Looking for the file on QDN...", then "Gathering from QDN" with a percentage and a count of chunks while your node collects them from peers. After that the file downloads from your node to the phone and is saved. A count that doesn't move means no peer is sending the file right now.

entries.q: How do I publish a website in Qortal Hub?
aliases: upload my website to qortal hub
steps to publish a website on qdn
how to publish a website in hub
entries.a:
1. Build the site as plain files with index.html at the top level, then zip the files themselves, not the folder around them.
2. In Hub, open the Q-Apps library and go to the My apps tab.
3. Choose publish website, pick your name, and add a title, description, category and tags.
4. Select the zip, press Publish and approve the fee.
5. Wait a few minutes for the network to pick it up.
You need your own node, a registered name and a little QORT.

entries.q: What must a QDN website zip contain?
aliases: how to zip my website for qortal
what goes in a website zip
entries.a: An index file at the top level of the zip: index.html, index.htm, default.html, default.htm, home.html or home.htm. Qortal Core rejects a website without one. Zip the files themselves rather than the folder that holds them, keep links between files relative, and remember that file names are case-sensitive.

entries.q: What is the address of my QDN website?
aliases: how do people open my website
entries.a: It is qortal://WEBSITE/ followed by your registered name, for example qortal://WEBSITE/QortalDemo. A page inside it adds its path, as in qortal://WEBSITE/QortalDemo/about.html. People open it by entering the link in the search bar of Hub or GO, or by tapping it in a chat.

entries.q: How big can a website be on QDN?
aliases: how big can my qortal site be
entries.a: Hub's website form takes a zip of up to 400 MB, and Qortal Core allows up to 2 GiB per publish. Smaller is better, though: every visitor's node has to fetch the whole site before showing it.

entries.q: How do I update my website on QDN?
aliases: how to update my website on qdn
publish a new version of my website
entries.a: Change your files, zip them again with index.html at the top, and publish them as a website under the same name; in Hub's My apps tab, use update on your published website. The new version replaces the old one for everyone within a few minutes. The whole zip is uploaded again, and the usual fee applies.

entries.q: Do I need to keep my computer on for my QDN website to stay up?
aliases: keep computer on for qdn website
website offline when my node is off
does my qortal site need my pc running
keep my computer on for my website
does my website need my node online
entries.a: Only while your node holds the only copy. Once others follow your name or have opened your site, their nodes serve it too, even while yours is off. Keeping your node online, or asking a friend to follow your name, keeps the site reachable in quiet times.

entries.q: Can people without Qortal see my QDN website?
aliases: view a qdn website in a normal browser
share my qdn site with non qortal users
can people without qortal see my website
entries.a: Only through a gateway: a Qortal node whose operator has turned on Qortal Core's gateway mode serves QDN websites to ordinary web browsers. Gateway mode is off by default. Otherwise visitors need Qortal Hub or Qortal GO.

entries.q: Can I use my own domain name for a QDN website?
aliases: custom domain for a qdn website
my own domain for a qortal site
entries.a: Yes, with a node you run. Point the domain at that node with DNS A or CNAME records, then turn on Qortal Core's domain map in settings.json: "domainMapEnabled": true and a domainMap list of domain and name pairs. The node then serves that name's website for the domain, on port 80 by default. The site itself still lives on QDN under your name.

entries.q: Can my QDN website link to other QDN sites and images?
aliases: show an image from another name qdn
entries.a: Yes, with qortal:// links. qortal://WEBSITE/QortalDemo opens another site's home page, and qortal://WEBSITE/QortalDemo/page.html one of its pages. You can also use a qortal:// link as an image source, for example qortal://THUMBNAIL/QortalDemo/qortal_avatar for that name's avatar. Hub and GO open such links inside Qortal.

entries.q: How do people find my QDN website?
aliases: where can people see my qortal website
list my website in the q-apps library
where do qdn websites show up
entries.a: The Q-Apps library in Hub and GO lists every name's main app and website, with the title, description and category you gave when publishing. You can also share your site's link, qortal://WEBSITE/ followed by your name. Sites made with Qortal Web Builder can also be listed in the Qortal Web app.

entries.q: Can I publish a website from Qortal GO?
aliases: publish site on my phone qortal
publish a website on my phone
entries.a: Yes, if GO is connected to your own node or to a private node you have the API key for: the My apps tab in GO's Q-Apps library has the same publish website form as Hub. On the public node it doesn't work, because the public node doesn't take uploads.

entries.q: Why does my website still show the old version after an update?
aliases: old version of my site after publish
entries.a: Each node switches to the new version only after it has received your new publish and fetched the new files, which usually takes a few minutes. Until then it may still show the copy it already built. Wait a little and reload; if you see Not Found or a loading page instead, the new version is still on its way.

entries.q: What are the parts of a qortal:// link?
aliases: how is a qortal link built
entries.a: qortal://SERVICE/name/identifier/path. SERVICE is the type, such as WEBSITE, APP or THUMBNAIL; name is the publisher's registered name; identifier picks one resource when a name has several; path is a page or file inside it. The identifier and path can be left out, as in qortal://APP/Q-Tube, and the word default stands for no identifier.

entries.q: How do I open a qortal:// link in Qortal Hub?
aliases: open a qortal link in hub
paste a qortal link in hub
how to use a qortal:// link
how to open a qortal link on pc
enter a qortal link on desktop
entries.a: Type or paste it into the search bar at the top of Hub, which says "Search Q-Apps or enter qortal://", and press Enter. qortal:// links in Q-Chat messages and inside Q-Apps open with a click. Either way the resource opens in Hub's apps view.

entries.q: How do I open a qortal:// link in Qortal GO?
aliases: open a qortal link in go
paste a qortal link in go
how to open a qortal link on phone
tap a qortal link to open go
entries.a: Tap it in a chat message or an app, or paste it into GO's top search bar, which says "Search apps or enter qortal:// link", and choose Open as Qortal link. On Android, tapping a qortal:// link in another app, such as a browser or a messenger, opens GO as well.

entries.q: Can I share a qortal:// link with people outside Qortal?
aliases: share a qortal link outside qortal
send a qortal link to a friend
does a qortal link work in a browser
entries.a: You can send it anywhere, but it opens only for people who have Qortal Hub or Qortal GO. On Android, a tapped qortal:// link opens GO directly. Web links on the qortal.link gateway hosts can open in GO too (Android may ask which app to use), and GO turns them into the same qortal:// link.

entries.q: Why does my qortal:// link to a + app open a blank tab?
aliases: qortal link plus sign blank tab
app name with a plus in a link
entries.a: Write app names that contain a plus, such as POS+, with the plus itself: qortal://APP/POS+. Written as %2B, Hub opens a blank tab, because it doesn't decode the app name. Spaces and special characters later in the link should be encoded, a space as %20, the way Hub's own copy link does it.

entries.q: What does default mean in a qortal:// link?
entries.a: default stands for no identifier. So qortal://WEBSITE/QortalDemo/default is the same as qortal://WEBSITE/QortalDemo, the name's main website. It helps when you add a path and want it clear that there is no identifier, as in qortal://WEBSITE/QortalDemo/default/page.html.

entries.q: Can a qortal:// link point to an image or a single file?
entries.a: Yes. Any resource can be linked: qortal://THUMBNAIL/QortalDemo/qortal_avatar points to that name's avatar, and a link with IMAGE, VIDEO, FILE or DOCUMENT plus the name and identifier points to that item. Websites can use the same links as image sources, so pictures load straight from QDN.

entries.q: What other kinds of qortal:// links are there?
entries.a: Besides links to resources, Hub and GO understand group links such as qortal://use-group/action-join/groupid-<number>, which offer to join that group, and qortal://use-embed/ links, which show a poll, image or file inside a chat message. GO also opens payment links such as qortal://pay?recipient=<name or address>&amount=5, with the Send screen filled in for you to confirm; Hub 3.0.3 doesn't open payment links.

entries.q: What is a qortal://use-embed link?
entries.a: It is a link that Hub and GO show as an embedded item in a chat message: a poll, an image or an attachment stored on QDN. Apps create it and copy it for you to paste. For an encrypted image or file, the link itself carries the decryption key, so anyone who gets the link can open the item.

entries.q: Can a qortal:// link take my QORT?
aliases: can a qortal link steal qort
tapping a payment link on qortal
entries.a: Not by itself. A qortal:// link only opens a resource, an app or a filled-in form. A payment link opens the Send screen with the recipient and amount filled in, and nothing is sent until you confirm. Check the details first, because a sent payment can't be undone.

entries.q: Can I link to a page inside a Q-App?
aliases: link to a page inside a q-app
share a page of a q-app
qortal link to a page in an app
entries.a: Yes. Add the path after the app name, as in qortal://APP/Torq/post/ followed by the post's identifier; the app opens on that page if it supports such links. Many apps' own Copy link buttons build these links for you.

entries.q: Do I get paid for hosting QDN data?
entries.a: No. Hosting QDN data is voluntary: your node keeps what you follow and open, and shares it, without payment. Qortal Core has no data market yet; QORT is earned by minting, not by hosting.

entries.q: Why does my node use bandwidth when I'm not doing anything?
aliases: why does my node use bandwidth
entries.a: Your node works in the background: it downloads new publishes from names you follow, fetches small metadata files for QDN items, sends chunks to other nodes that ask for data you host, and relays data for others. To cut this down, follow fewer names, set a storage limit, or change the storage policy.

entries.q: How do I publish something private on QDN?
aliases: publish a private file on qdn
entries.a: Use a Q-App that offers private or encrypted publishing, such as Q-Mail for mail. The app encrypts the data on your device for the people you choose and publishes it to a _PRIVATE service, such as FILE_PRIVATE or DOCUMENT_PRIVATE. The approval window shows that the data is encrypted. The publish itself, with your name and the identifier, is still public.

entries.q: Who can open a private QDN resource?
aliases: who can decrypt a private qdn file
who can read private qdn data
who can open private qdn data
entries.a: Only the people it was encrypted for, and you, because Hub and GO always add your own key. The app encrypts the data with a fresh random key and then locks that key separately for each chosen person's public key, so each of them can open it with their own private key. Everyone else, hosting nodes included, sees only scrambled data.

entries.q: Can I encrypt QDN data for several people at once?
aliases: share an encrypted file with many people
private file for several people qdn
entries.a: Yes. An app can give several public keys when it encrypts, and each of those people can then open the same resource. Q-Mail does this for group threads and Bcc copies, encrypting to every recipient's key.

entries.q: Can I keep private files on QDN that only I can open?
aliases: store my own files privately on qdn
private files only i can open
entries.a: Yes. An app can encrypt data for your own key alone and publish it to a _PRIVATE service, so only your account can decrypt it. Hub and GO do this when you save your pinned apps to QDN, and Q-Mail when it saves its mail state. Others can still see that the resource exists, just not what's in it.

entries.q: Are private QDN resources hosted like public ones?
aliases: do followers store my private qdn data
entries.a: Yes. Nodes that follow the publisher or open the resource store and share its chunks the same way. The data is encrypted, so the hosting nodes can't read it; only the chosen recipients can.

entries.q: What is group-encrypted data on QDN?
aliases: who can read group encrypted data
entries.a: It is data encrypted with a private group's shared key, so any member can open it and outsiders can't. The group's admins publish that key, the group secret key, encrypted for each member, as a DOCUMENT_PRIVATE resource on QDN. Hub and GO use it for a private group's Threads, and for its chat only when Reticulum chat is turned off; private Q-Apps are shared with a group this way too.

entries.q: Why does a QDN item show an old created date after I updated it?
aliases: why does my update show the old date
entries.a: QDN keeps two times for each resource: created, from its very first publish, and updated, from the newest one. An update changes only the updated time, so apps that sort by created date keep showing your item where it first appeared.

entries.q: Why do QDN identifiers look like random strings?
aliases: why is the identifier so long
entries.a: Apps usually build identifiers from a short app prefix plus a random part, such as qshare_file_ followed by the title and a random code, so every item gets its own address and the app can find its own data by the prefix. Some apps, like those built on qapp-core, also turn words into hashed identifiers for privacy.

entries.q: Can I change the identifier of something I published?
aliases: move a resource to a new identifier
entries.a: No. The identifier is part of the resource's address. To use a new one, publish the content again under the new identifier, which makes a separate resource with its own fee, and if you want the old one gone, replace it with a delete marker.

entries.q: Can I move QDN content to a different name?
aliases: move qdn content to another name
transfer my files to a new name
change the name of my published content
move qdn content to a different name
qdn content to a new name
entries.a: Not directly. Content belongs to the name it was published under. You can publish it again under another name you own, as new resources with their own fees, or transfer the whole name, which moves control of everything published under it.

entries.q: Why does a QDN loading page reload by itself?
aliases: retrieving content from the qortal data network
entries.a: The loading page checks the resource's status every few seconds while your node downloads and builds it. As soon as the status is Ready, the page reloads itself and the app or site appears in its place.

entries.q: Why does a Q-App open on one node but not on another?
aliases: app works on pc not on phone
q-app loads on my node not the public node
different nodes have different qdn data
app opens in hub but not in go
q-app opens on one node not another
app works on one node only
entries.a: Each node holds different QDN data, depending on what it follows, what its users have opened and how full it is. Your own node may already have an app that a public node dropped, or the other way round. If an app won't load on one node, wait while it fetches from peers, or try it from your own node.

entries.q: Why does my QDN publish take so long?
aliases: why is uploading taking so long
why is my publish so slow
entries.a: Three steps take time: uploading the file to your node, the node zipping, encrypting and chunking it, and then other nodes fetching it. A big file over a slow link to your node can take many minutes, and GO's publish window shows the speed and the time left. Let it finish before you close the app.

entries.q: Can I see who hosts my QDN content?
aliases: see who follows my name for hosting
how many nodes have my files
list of nodes hosting my data
who is seeding my qdn data
entries.a: Not by name. Hosting follows are private settings on each node, so there is no public list of who hosts your content. While a resource downloads, the loading page shows how many peers are sending it, which gives a rough idea. Torq follows, which are published, are a different thing.

entries.q: What are the private QDN services and their size limits?
entries.a: QCHAT_ATTACHMENT_PRIVATE 1 MB, ATTACHMENT_PRIVATE 50 MB, FILE_PRIVATE, IMAGE_PRIVATE 10 MB, VIDEO_PRIVATE, AUDIO_PRIVATE, VOICE_PRIVATE 10 MB, DOCUMENT_PRIVATE, MAIL_PRIVATE 5 MB and MESSAGE_PRIVATE 1 MB. Those without a figure have no cap of their own beyond the general 2 GiB per publish. All of them accept only data the app has encrypted.

entries.q: What files can a GIF_REPOSITORY contain?
aliases: publish a gif collection on qdn
what is allowed in a gif repository
why was my gif collection rejected
entries.a: Only .gif files, at least one, with no folders inside, up to 25 MB in total. Qortal Core refuses a GIF collection that holds anything else.

entries.q: What does Build failed mean on QDN?
aliases: build failed please try again later
entries.a: Your node had the files but couldn't put the resource together, for example because some data didn't check out. The status says "Build failed. Please try again later". Wait a while, then open it again.

entries.q: Does QDN data make the blockchain bigger?
aliases: are files added to the chain
does qdn make the chain bigger
entries.a: Only a little. Each publish adds one small transaction with the name, service, identifier and hashes, but the files themselves stay off-chain on the nodes that host them. How much QDN data a node stores depends on what it follows and opens, not on everything ever published.

entries.q: Does my phone store QDN data?
aliases: does go store qdn data on my phone
is my phone a qdn node
does my phone host qdn data
entries.a: Not as a node. GO doesn't run Qortal Core, so it doesn't host QDN data for others; it shows what the node it is connected to fetches. GO keeps only a few things itself, such as the files of your widgets and the files you choose to save.

entries.q: Why is my Qortal data folder so big?
aliases: why is qortal using so much disk
why is my data folder large
entries.a: It holds the QDN data your node hosts: everything from names you follow, what you and others using that node have opened, the original copies of your own publishes, and built copies of apps and websites. Following big publishers, or the ALL policy, makes it grow fast. Set maxStorageCapacity to cap it, or follow fewer names.

entries.q: Can I delete my node's data folder to free space?
aliases: remove qdn data to free space
is it safe to delete the data folder
can i delete the data folder
wipe qdn data on my node
entries.a: You can, with Qortal Core stopped, but you lose all the QDN data it held, including the original copies of what you published from it, which may be the only ones on the network. Your node then downloads the names you follow again. To keep usage down safely, set maxStorageCapacity instead.

entries.q: Does bootstrapping my node delete my QDN data?
aliases: does bootstrap remove my hosted files
entries.a: No. A bootstrap replaces the blockchain database in the db folder. The QDN files in the data folder stay where they are.

entries.q: Can I copy files straight out of my node's data folder?
aliases: open files in the qortal data folder
where are the real files in qdn data
entries.a: Not usefully. The data folder holds QDN data as compressed, encrypted chunks, filed by transaction and hash, not as the original files. To get a file back, download or save it through a Q-App, Hub or GO.

entries.q: Does QDN have folders?
aliases: can i make folders on qdn
folders in the qortal data network
entries.a: Not in the way a disk does. Every item is just a name, a service and an identifier, and apps group items by giving their identifiers a shared start, such as qshare_file_. Only multi-file services like WEBSITE, APP and FILES hold real folders, inside one resource.

entries.q: Can one Q-App read data published by another?
aliases: does an app own my qdn data
can a q-app read another apps data
entries.a: Yes. Public QDN data belongs to the name that published it, not to an app, so any app can read it if it knows the service and identifiers used. That's how Torq shows the same posts as Quitter.

entries.q: What happens to my data if a Q-App stops being available?
aliases: q-app disappeared what about my data
app gone what happens to my files
q-app no longer works data lost
my data if an app is removed
entries.a: Your data stays: it is published under your name, not inside the app, and lasts as long as nodes host it. Any app that understands the same services and identifiers can still read it. The app itself is a QDN resource too, so it comes back if a node still hosts it or its publisher publishes it again.

entries.q: Do Q-Apps update automatically?
entries.a: Yes. A Q-App is a QDN resource, so when its publisher publishes a new version, nodes switch to it, and you get it the next time the app loads. There is no install step, and only the owner of the app's name can publish an update.

entries.q: What are lists on a Qortal node?
entries.a: Lists are small files your node keeps for its own settings, such as followedNames for the names it hosts and blockedNames for the names it blocks. Q-Apps can read and change them with your approval. They live only on that node, in Core's lists folder, and a public node doesn't let apps use them.

entries.q: Why does an app ask to access my list?
aliases: allow this app to access the list
why does q-share ask for my list
app wants to access my list
always allow lists to be retrieved
entries.a: Lists such as followedNames and blockedNames are kept on your node, and Hub and GO ask before an app reads or changes one: "allow this app to access the list?". Q-Share asks, for example, to show your Following feed or to follow a name. For apps you trust, you can tick "always allow lists to be retrieved automatically".

entries.q: How do I know my QDN publish worked?
aliases: how to verify a publish on qortal
entries.a: Hub says it was successfully published, and GO's publish window shows Published to QDN. Then give it a few minutes and look for it in the app you used, or open its qortal:// link: if it loads, it's on QDN. A Not Found page soon after publishing usually means the network hasn't caught up yet.

entries.q: Why doesn't my app or website show in the Q-Apps library yet?
aliases: my app is not in the q-apps library
website not showing in the library
library not updated with my new app
my website not in q-apps library
app not showing in library yet
entries.a: The library lists each name's main app and website, the ones published without an identifier, and Hub and GO refresh that list about every 20 minutes. Give it some time after publishing. A resource published with an identifier doesn't appear there at all.

entries.q: Is there a limit on how much I can publish on QDN?
aliases: how much can i upload to qdn
how much can i publish on qdn
entries.a: There is no quota per name or account. Each publish has its own size limit, 2 GiB at most, and costs a fee, and your content takes up space on every node that hosts it.

entries.q: Can I publish under my name from two devices?
aliases: same name on hub and go
publish from two devices same name
which publish wins with two devices
entries.a: Yes. Any device signed in to the account that owns the name can publish under it, from Hub or from GO with a node that takes uploads. If both publish to the same name, service and identifier, the newer publish wins.

entries.q: Should my node use the ALL storage policy?
aliases: should i use the ALL policy
should i host everything on qdn
entries.a: Only with plenty of disk space and bandwidth. ALL makes your node download and keep everything published on QDN by every name, which adds copies for everyone but fills storage quickly; Core still stops fetching at 80% of its limit. For most nodes, the default FOLLOWED_OR_VIEWED, plus following the names you care about, is enough.

entries.q: Can I use QDN as cloud storage for my files?
aliases: use qdn as an online drive
entries.a: Partly. You can publish files, encrypted for yourself if you like, and reach them through any node that holds them. But QDN keeps a file only while some node hosts it, and the record of every publish is public, so it isn't a backup service: keep your own copies too.

entries.q: Do I need to run Qortal Core to use QDN?
aliases: browse qdn on the public node
do i need my own node to publish
do i need qortal core for qdn
use qdn on the public node
entries.a: Not to look around: Hub and GO can use a public node to open Q-Apps, websites and files. To publish, follow or block names, or host data, you need a node you control: Qortal Core on your own computer, or a private node you have the API key for.

entries.q: Why can't my syncing node see new QDN content?
aliases: syncing node cant open new apps
new publishes not found on my node
node behind and qdn content missing
entries.a: Your node learns what exists on QDN from the blockchain, so until it has synced up to now, it doesn't know about the newest publishes and shows them as Not Found. It also waits until it has enough up-to-date peers before fetching QDN data. Let the sync finish, then try again.

entries.q: How do I know a QDN item really comes from who it says?
aliases: is this qdn content really from them
fake qdn content with the same title
is qdn content really from the publisher
can someone fake my qdn content
entries.a: Look at the registered name it was published under: only the owner of that name can publish there. Anyone can copy a title, an identifier, or text that claims to come from someone else, but only under their own name. Good apps show the publisher's name from the publish itself, not from what the content claims.

entries.q: Can my QDN website load images or fonts from other websites?
aliases: load web fonts on a qdn site
outside web content in a qdn site
why dont external images load on my qdn site
entries.a: No. In Hub and GO, QDN websites and Q-Apps can load only what comes through the node, so images, fonts or scripts from ordinary web servers don't load. Put everything the site needs inside its zip, or load it from QDN with qortal:// links.

entries.q: Does each node keep whole QDN files or just pieces?
aliases: do nodes store whole qdn files
nodes keep whole files or pieces
entries.a: A node that hosts a resource normally keeps all of its chunks, so it can serve the whole thing. When a node runs short of space, it deletes chunks at random, so some nodes end up holding only parts.
