entries.a: No. GO never opens or installs an app package it receives or downloads, and you should not install one from a stranger either: it could be anything, including a fake GO made to steal your seedphrase. Update GO only through GO 3.0 Updates, which installs only builds signed with GO's own key.

entries.q: Someone promises to double my QORT if I send some first. Is it real?
aliases: send qort to get more back
pay a fee to unlock my qort
get my qort back from a scammer
entries.a: No, it is a scam. Once you send QORT nobody can reverse it, and the promised return never comes. The same goes for anyone saying you must pay to unlock, release or withdraw your QORT: QORT in your account is always yours to send, and the only cost is the small network fee GO shows you.

entries.q: Can someone recover my lost account for a fee?
aliases: recover lost qortal account for a fee
entries.a: No. Without the seedphrase, or the backup file and its password, nobody can get into a Qortal account: not developers, not admins, not any "recovery service". People who offer this for a fee, or ask for whatever parts of your wallet you still have, are scammers.

entries.q: Is it safe to let someone help me by sharing my screen or controlling my device?
aliases: share my screen with a helper
entries.a: Be very careful. Someone who can see or control your screen while GO is unlocked can read whatever you open and tap Accept for you. Never open your seedphrase, private key or backup screens while sharing. Real helpers can guide you with words; if they insist on remote control or on seeing those screens, stop.

entries.q: How do I know a payment to me really arrived?
entries.a: Check your own wallet, not a screenshot. Your balance, and Wallet Activity on Home with its Transaction history, show what really arrived. A screenshot or message is easy to fake. A real payment confirms in the next block, about a minute later.

entries.q: Someone says my account will be closed or frozen unless I act now. Is that real?
entries.a: No. Nobody can close, freeze or delete a Qortal account: it is your keys, it lives on the blockchain, and no company is in charge of it. Messages that rush you to act, pay or "verify" are a pressure trick. Ignore them and never share your secrets.

entries.q: Do I need to approve anything to receive QORT?
aliases: app asks approval to receive a payment
entries.a: No. To receive QORT you only give your address or name; the sender signs the payment and it arrives on its own. If someone says you must accept a request, sign something or pay a fee to receive money, it is a trick to get you to approve a payment out of your account.

entries.q: Can a chat message hack my account?
entries.a: Reading a message does not give anyone your keys. GO cleans message content before showing it, does not load pictures from outside servers, and refuses links that point back into GO. The real dangers are links to fake sites, files you choose to install, and people talking you into approving requests or sharing secrets.

entries.q: What are the warning signs of a Qortal scam?
aliases: how to spot a scam on qortal

entries.q: Is a Q-App that looks like an official one always genuine?
entries.a: No. Anyone can publish an app under their own name, and a copy can look exactly like the original. What tells them apart is the publisher's name, which GO shows on the app and in Requested by when it asks for something. Open well-known apps from the Official apps tab in GO's library or from links you trust, and be wary of a familiar app under an unfamiliar name.

entries.q: Is it safe to share my screen while I use Qortal?
aliases: screen sharing with my wallet open
is it safe to share my screen
entries.a: Yes, if you keep your secrets off the screen. Never open your seedphrase, private key, backup or password screens while sharing, recording or streaming: anyone watching, or anyone who sees the video later, could take your account. In GO those screens show up black in recordings and shares, but on a computer Hub cannot hide them. The eye button in Settings (Privacy Mode) blurs your address and key there.

entries.q: Does the desktop Hub block screenshots of my seedphrase or private key?
entries.a: No. The protection that turns sensitive screens black in screenshots and recordings is only in the Android app. On a computer, anything Hub shows, including a revealed seedphrase or private key, can be captured by screenshots, screen recorders and screen sharing. Show those only when nobody, and no recording, can see your screen.

entries.q: Can my phone's assistant or other apps read GO's sensitive screens?
entries.a: GO blocks assistant screen reading, screenshots, recordings and the recent-apps picture on its sensitive screens: unlock and lock, seedphrase, private key and backup screens, and payment and approval windows. It also hides its content from services that are not accessibility tools. Chats and Q-Apps are not covered, so treat what you show there as visible.

entries.q: Who can read my direct messages in GO?
aliases: can qortal developers read my messages
can the node read my messages
can a group admin read my dms
entries.a: Only you and the person you are writing to. In GO and Hub 3.0, direct messages travel over Reticulum, encrypted between your devices, and they are not written to the blockchain. Qortal developers, node operators and the hubs that pass traffic along cannot read them. The messages are kept on the devices in the conversation, so keep your phone locked.

entries.q: Can anyone read the messages in a public group?
aliases: who can read public group chat
can strangers read my group messages
entries.a: Yes. Anyone can join an open (public) group and read what is posted there, so treat it like speaking in a public square. Closed groups, shown with a lock in Find groups, only let in members an admin accepts, and their chat is for members. Never post private details, or anything about your seedphrase or backup, in a public group.

entries.q: Can a Q-App send my data to outside servers?
aliases: can apps phone home on qortal
entries.a: Not in GO. Q-Apps there are limited to your node: what an app loads, fetches and connects to stays on the node, and it cannot open other apps on your phone. So it cannot quietly report to an outside server. It can still publish or send messages, but only through approval windows you see or permissions you granted, so read what you accept.

entries.q: Will my keyboard remember my seedphrase?
aliases: does my keyboard save the seed words
entries.a: GO turns off keyboard suggestions and learning in the seedphrase field, so a keyboard that follows that setting does not store the words. A keyboard app that ignores it, or sends what you type online, could still see them, so use a keyboard you trust when you restore an account.

entries.q: Is Qortal anonymous?
aliases: can people find out who i am on qortal
how to stay private on qortal
entries.a:
Not fully. Your account needs no ID, but everything on the chain is public and tied to your address and name. To stay more private:
- Use separate accounts for things you want kept apart.
- Pick a name that does not reveal who you are, and leave personal details out of posts.
- Use Private (Reticulum only) calls so callers cannot see your IP address.
- Run your own node, so no one else's node sees what you ask for.

entries.q: Do Qortal Hub and GO collect my personal data?
aliases: does go send my data anywhere
entries.a: No. The Qortal privacy policy for Hub and GO says they do not collect or send personal data to outside servers; your wallet and permission settings stay on your device. What you do on the network, such as payments and publishes, is still public on the blockchain.

entries.q: Is it safe to use GO on the public node?
aliases: is the public node safe to use
can the public node steal my qort
entries.a: For everyday use, yes. GO signs on your phone and sends the public node only the signed transaction, so the node never gets your Qortal private key and cannot move your QORT. GO also refuses to send it any foreign coin's private key. The trade-off is that someone else runs it: it sees what your phone asks for, decides what it blocks, and some things need your own node.

entries.q: What can the public node's operator see?
aliases: what does the public node see
can the node see what i do
entries.a: Whatever your phone asks it for: lookups of your address and balance, the Q-Apps, sites and data you open, and the transactions you send through it, which are public on the chain anyway. Like any server, it also sees your IP address. It does not see your private key or seedphrase. With your own node, all of this stays at home.

entries.q: Why is my own node better for privacy?
aliases: private node vs public node privacy
why run my own node for privacy
entries.a: Your requests go to a machine you control instead of someone else's; Hub sums it up as "Your data stays local". You also decide who is blocked, foreign coin keys go only to your own node when you trade or send them, and you can mint. The public node is quicker to start with, but it is shared and run by someone else.

entries.q: Why must I keep my node's API key secret?
aliases: what can someone do with my api key
entries.a: The API key unlocks your node's admin controls. With it, a program that can reach the node can stop, restart or bootstrap it, change its peers, and add or remove minting accounts. Treat it like a password: never post it or give it to a stranger, and never open the node's API port to the internet. If it may have leaked, replace it with a new key and enter that in GO.

entries.q: Is it safe to reach my node over plain HTTP or public Wi-Fi?
aliases: connect go to my node on cafe wifi
entries.a: Not on public Wi-Fi. Over plain HTTP, everything between GO and the node, including the API key, can be read by others on that network; on your own home Wi-Fi it is a common setup. Away from home, reach your node through Tailscale or an SSH tunnel. GO also refuses to send coin private keys over plain HTTP (except to the phone itself or over Tailscale) and downloads updates only over HTTPS or from a node on the phone.

entries.q: What should I do right after I create my account?
aliases: first steps after creating a wallet
just created my account what now
entries.a:
1. Save the backup file and copy it off the phone, for example to a USB stick.
2. Write the 14-word seedphrase on paper and keep it offline.
3. Keep your wallet password somewhere safe, apart from the file.
4. Write down your address, so you can check a restore later.
5. Turn on fingerprint unlock if you like, and leave Auto-Lock When Idle on.
Do this before you receive QORT or register a name.

entries.q: How can my family get to my QORT if something happens to me?
aliases: if i die what happens to my qort
entries.a: Only through the same keys you use: nobody, Qortal included, can hand your account to your family. One way is to give a trusted person a copy of your backup file (it is encrypted, so it is safe for them to hold), and keep the password or the seedphrase where they can reach it when needed, for example with your will. Add a short note on how to restore it in GO or Hub.

entries.q: Why should I keep GO and Hub up to date?
entries.a: Updates bring security fixes as well as features. GO v0.0.15, for example, was a security and privacy release: it closed a flaw that could let outside code run as GO, added screen protection and kept location data out of shared photos. Update GO through the GO 3.0 Updates screen. Hub updates itself: it checks the official releases when it starts and once a day, downloads a new version in the background and installs it when you quit.

entries.q: What should I do if I think my account was hacked?
entries.a:
1. Open Wallet Activity on Home, Transaction history, and see where the QORT went and when.
2. Think whether you accepted a payment in a Q-App: accepted approvals go through.
3. Check you are in the right account: a mistyped seedphrase opens a different, empty one.
4. If you did not send it, assume your seedphrase, private key or backup file and password leaked: create a new account, back it up and move what is left at once.
Nobody can reverse a sent payment.

entries.q: What does "could not confirm the public key" mean?
aliases: could not confirm the public key
public key could not be confirmed
entries.a: Before GO encrypts something for a person, it checks that the public key the node gave it really belongs to that address. If it does not match, GO stops and nothing is encrypted or sent, so a wrong or tampered key cannot be used to read what you meant for them. Try again later, or from another node.

entries.q: Why does my seedphrase read like a strange sentence?
aliases: seed phrase words make no sense
why seedphrase looks like a sentence
entries.a: GO picks 14 random words to fit a fixed pattern of word types, such as adverb, verb, noun and adjective, so the phrase reads like an odd sentence. That makes it easier to write down and read back, but the words themselves are random, so it will not make sense. Copy it exactly as shown.

entries.q: What does "the node address could not be checked, so your private key was not sent" mean?
aliases: node address could not be checked
blocked node address could not be checked
entries.a: Before a coin's private key leaves the phone, GO reads the node's address to check it is allowed: not a public node, and encrypted or local. This time it could not read the address, so it played safe and sent nothing. Check the node URL in your node settings and try again.

entries.q: Should I send a small test payment first?
entries.a: For a large payment to a new address, it is a good habit: send a small amount, ask the person to confirm it arrived (or check it yourself for your own cold wallet), then send the rest. Payments cannot be reversed, and GO shows the full address in its confirmation, so compare that too. A test costs one extra small fee.

entries.q: Does Qortal have two-factor authentication?
entries.a: Not in the usual sense: there is no login server to send codes from. Your protection is your keys. The wallet password locks the copy on each device and your backup file, GO adds fingerprint unlock and Auto-Lock When Idle, and every payment needs your password or your Accept in an approval window.

entries.q: Can I use fingerprint unlock in Qortal Hub on my computer?
entries.a: No. Fingerprint unlock is only in the Android app; on the desktop Hub you unlock with your wallet password. Hub can still lock itself when idle, so set Auto-Lock When Idle in its settings.

entries.q: Is it safe to hand someone my phone while GO is unlocked?
aliases: lend my phone with go open
hand phone to a friend go unlocked
entries.a: Lock GO first: tap your avatar, then Lock now. While GO is unlocked, whoever holds the phone can read your chats and tap Accept on Q-App requests, including payments. Send QORT still asks for your password, but approvals do not. Chats and calls stay connected while GO is locked.

entries.q: What should I check when a Q-App asks to add an admin, kick or ban someone?
aliases: allow this app to add user as an admin
allow this app to kick from the group
allow this app to ban from the group
entries.a: Check the name shown and the group. Making someone an admin gives them power over the group's members, so a wrong name there is a real risk; kick and ban remove a member. Each is a transaction with a fee, so accept only changes you meant to make, in an app you trust.

entries.q: What should I check when a Q-App asks me to vote on a poll?
aliases: you are being requested to vote on the poll below
entries.a: Check the poll name and the option shown, because that is the vote your account casts. Votes on Qortal polls are public, so anyone can see how your account voted. A vote is a transaction with a small fee, so only accept polls you meant to vote in.

entries.q: Can a Q-App or the node see the other accounts saved in GO?
aliases: other wallets saved in go private
entries.a: A Q-App only ever deals with the account you are logged into, and only learns it when you authenticate. GO also stopped sending the node every saved address at once for the account list. Still, if you use two accounts from the same phone and node, that node sees requests for both.

entries.q: How is my backup file encrypted?
aliases: what encryption does the qortal wallet use
entries.a: Your password is run through a deliberately slow key step (SHA-512 and bcrypt, with a random salt), and the result encrypts your account key with AES. A separate check value (the wallet integrity check) tells GO whether the password is right and the file undamaged. The slow step makes each password guess costly, but a short password can still be guessed, so use a long one.

entries.q: What if I lose my backup file?
entries.a:
1. If you have your seedphrase, you are fine: it restores the account on its own.
2. If the account is still saved in GO or Hub and you know its password, save a fresh backup now: Home, Quick tools, Backup Wallet.
3. If neither is true, the account cannot be recovered, and nobody can do it for you.

entries.q: Is my wallet password my private key?
aliases: is my password the private key
entries.a: No. Your private key is a long secret GO makes from your seedphrase. Your wallet password only locks the copy of that key saved on your device and in your backup file. Changing the password changes the lock, not the key, and the password on its own is no use without the device or the file.

entries.q: Are the files and pictures I send in chat encrypted?
aliases: who can see files i send in chat
entries.a: Yes, on the way. In GO and Hub 3.0 they go from device to device over encrypted Reticulum links, not through a server, so nobody in between can read them. In a DM only you and the other person get them; in a group, every member can. The receiving phone keeps them in GO's private storage until they are saved or the person logs out.

entries.q: I forgot my wallet password. What can I do?
entries.a:
Nobody can reset it, but you may still get back in:
- With your seedphrase: on the account's unlock screen tap the pencil (Account details), Remove, then Import account, Seedphrase, and choose a new password. Do this only with your seedphrase written down and checked.
- With a backup file: it opens only with the password it was saved with, so try each one you might have used.
- With fingerprint unlock on: GO may still open, but sending QORT and Backup Wallet need the typed password.
Without the seedphrase or a working password, the account is lost.

entries.q: What do balance and wallet transaction requests from a Q-App share?
aliases: allow this app to fetch your balance
allow this app to retrieve your wallet transactions
always allow balance to be retrieved automatically
entries.a: A balance request shows the app how much of one coin you hold; a wallet transactions request shows it that wallet's payment history. Neither lets it spend anything. The always allow box makes that read automatic for that app and coin, so tick it only for apps you trust with that information. ARRR has no always box: GO asks while the app is open and warns you, because your ARRR seed has to go to your node.

entries.q: Why do Q-Apps keep asking me to approve things?
aliases: why do q-apps ask for approval
why must i accept q-app requests
what is a q-app approval window
entries.a: Because a Q-App cannot use your account on its own. Whenever it wants to do something as you, such as pay, publish, post a chat message or read your wallet, GO or Hub shows an approval window and waits for your Accept. That is your protection: read each one, accept what you started, and decline anything you did not expect.

entries.q: How do I keep my account safe in Qortal Hub on my computer?
aliases: keep my wallet safe on desktop
entries.a:
- Set Auto-Lock When Idle in Hub's settings, and lock Hub when you step away.
- Keep backup copies on USB sticks too, not only on that computer.
- Remember Hub cannot hide your seedphrase or private key from screenshots or screen sharing.
- Download Hub and Core only from official sources.
- Read every approval window before you accept.

entries.q: Do GO's diagnostics or logs contain my password or seedphrase?
aliases: is it safe to send go diagnostics
entries.a: No. GO never stores your seedphrase words, and the unlock timings in its diagnostics keep no passwords or addresses. Copy diagnostics also swaps addresses, names, IDs and IP addresses for stand-ins before you share it. Even so, never paste your seedphrase or password into a report or chat yourself.

entries.q: What is Torq?
entries.a: Torq is the social Q-App on Qortal: posts, replies, reposts, likes, follows, photos, videos, GIFs, polls and Revs (short photo and video stories). It runs inside Qortal Hub on a computer and Qortal GO on Android. There is no central server: what you post is stored on QDN under your registered name. Torq reads and writes the same data as Quitter, so Quitter accounts, posts and follows carry over.

entries.q: How is Torq related to Quitter?
aliases: is torq the same as quitter
entries.a: Torq is built from Quitter and uses the same QDN data, so it is not a new network. A post made in Torq is a Quitter post, and a follow in Torq is a Quitter follow. Torq adds what Quitter was missing: a composer that works on phones, real paragraphs, up to 10 photos, GIFs, polls, playable embeds, bookmarks, SuperLikes and Revs. People still on Quitter keep seeing your text, photos, videos and links.

entries.q: Do my Quitter posts and follows carry over to Torq?
entries.a: Yes. Torq keeps Quitter's identity on QDN, so your old Quitter posts, replies, likes, followers and the people you follow all show in Torq straight away. There is nothing to import or move. Open Torq signed in with the same Qortal name you used on Quitter.

entries.q: Do I need a new account for Torq?
entries.a: No. Torq has no sign-up or password of its own. It uses the Qortal account you are signed into in Hub or GO, and your registered name is your Torq identity. Your profile, posts and follows belong to that name.

entries.q: Do I need a registered name to use Torq?
aliases: cant post on torq no name
entries.a: You need a registered Qortal name to post, reply, like, follow, vote or bookmark, because everything you do is published under that name. Without one you can still open Torq and read public posts. Register a name in Hub or GO first; it costs a small amount of QORT.

entries.q: Can Quitter users see my Torq posts?
entries.a: Yes. Torq posts are Quitter posts, so Quitter shows your text, photos, videos and links. Quitter can't show GIFs, attached files or polls, and it shows only the first four photos. Posts with any of those carry a qortal://APP/Torq/post link so Quitter readers can open the full post in Torq.

entries.q: Why does my Torq post show a Torq link when viewed on Quitter?
aliases: extra link at end of torq post
why link in my torq post
entries.a: When a post has something Quitter can't display (GIFs, files, a poll, or more than four photos), Torq adds a qortal://APP/Torq/post link to it. People on Quitter tap it to open the whole post in Torq. Inside Torq that link stays hidden, so Torq readers never see it.

entries.q: How do I open Torq?
entries.a: In Qortal GO, open Apps and search for Torq, or tap the Torq logo on the Post to Torq window on Home. In Qortal Hub, open the Q-Apps library and search for Torq. You can also open the link qortal://APP/Torq from anywhere in Hub or GO. There is nothing to install.

entries.q: Can I use Torq in a normal web browser?
entries.a: No. Torq is a Q-App, not a website. It runs inside Qortal Hub or Qortal GO, which fetch it from QDN and sign your posts with your Qortal account. In a normal browser it can't publish or read your account.

entries.q: Can I use Torq on my phone?
entries.a: Yes, in Qortal GO on Android. Torq is laid out for phones: round buttons in the bottom-right corner open the side bar and the composer, you swipe pages away to go back, and Revs fill the screen. GO's Home can also post to Torq and show a Torq Feed without opening the app.

entries.q: Does it cost anything to use Torq?
entries.a: Reading is free. Every post, reply, repost, like, follow and vote is a small publish on QDN, so it needs a small QORT fee, which Hub or GO shows when it asks you to approve. Fees go to Qortal's minters, not to Torq. A SuperLike also sends the QORT amount you choose to the author.

entries.q: Why does Torq ask me to approve every like and post?
entries.a: Each post, reply, like and follow is published on QDN under your name, and only you can sign that, so Hub or GO shows an approval with its fee first. Revs are the exception: double-tap likes and quick reactions wait on your device and are saved together with one approval when you close the Revs.

entries.q: Where are my Torq posts stored?
entries.a: On QDN, Qortal's data network, under your registered name. There is no Torq server: the nodes that hold the data serve it to everyone. Photos are stored inside the post itself, while videos and files are published as their own QDN resources next to it.

entries.q: Can anyone delete or censor my Torq posts?
aliases: can someone remove my torq post
entries.a: There is no company or server behind Torq that can remove your posts or suspend you. Only the owner of a name can change or delete what is published under it. Other people can hide you in their own Torq, and a node owner can block your name on their node, but that only changes what they see.

entries.q: Why is it called Torq?
entries.a: From torque: force applied away from the centre. Torq's slogan is "Force, applied off-center", meaning a social network where no one sits in the middle deciding what rises or sinks. With Revs hidden, tap the slogan next to the Torq logo to read its manifesto.

entries.q: How do I see which version of Torq I have?
entries.a: Open Settings in Torq and scroll to the bottom. The last row shows Torq and its version number; tap it to read the changelog, newest release first.

entries.q: How do I update Torq?
entries.a: There is nothing to install or update by hand. Torq is a Q-App on QDN, so when a new version is published, opening Torq again loads it. If Torq was open during an update and a part of it can't load, it says so and offers Reload. Settings shows the version you are running.

entries.q: How do I get started on Torq?
entries.a:
1. Sign in to Hub or GO with an account that has a registered name.
2. Open Torq, go to your profile and tap the pencil to add a short bio.
3. Find people in Discover and tap Follow.
4. Write your first post (on a computer in the box at the top of Home, on a phone with the round post button), tap Post and approve it.

entries.q: How do I set up my Torq profile?
entries.a: Open your profile in Torq and tap the pencil (Edit Profile). Write a bio of up to 200 characters, tap Save Profile and approve the publish. Paragraph breaks in your bio are kept. Your picture is your Qortal name's avatar, which you set in Hub or GO, not in Torq.

entries.q: How do I change my profile picture on Torq?
entries.a: Torq shows the avatar of your Qortal name, the same picture every Q-App uses. Change it in Qortal Hub or GO with change avatar; it needs a registered name and a small publish fee. Torq shows the new picture once the publish has gone through.

entries.q: Can I use more than one name on Torq?
entries.a: Yes. If your account has several registered names, choose one with the name switcher at the top of Torq's Settings (on a phone it is also at the top of the side bar). Torq then posts, likes and follows as that name. The names you used last stay at the top, and switching keeps you on the page you were on.

entries.q: How do I follow someone on Torq?
entries.a: Open their profile and tap Follow, then approve the publish. You can also choose Follow @name in the menu on one of their posts. Their posts then show in your Following feed. To stop, open their profile and tap Unfollow.

entries.q: How do I find people to follow on Torq?
entries.a: Open Discover. Creators ranks people by Most followers, Most posts, Most liked, Most discussed or Most reposted; Users searches by name; Hashtags finds topics. When your Following feed is empty, Torq also offers to find people to follow.

entries.q: What is the difference between Everything and Following on Torq?
entries.a: Everything shows public posts from everyone, newest first. Following shows the people you follow, with their replies and reposts. With Subscriptions turned on in Settings, the tab is called Following & Subs and also includes subscription posts you can read. On a phone, swipe sideways to switch between them.

entries.q: Why is my Following feed empty on Torq?
entries.a: Following only shows people you follow, so it stays empty until you follow someone, or while they haven't posted. Follow a few people from Discover; an empty Following feed also offers to find people. A new follow takes a minute or two to reach the network.

entries.q: Does Torq use an algorithm to choose what I see?
entries.a: No. Home lists posts newest first: Everything has everyone's public posts and Following has the people you follow. Nothing is boosted and no reach is for sale. Discover's Creators lists are plain counts, such as most followers or most liked.

entries.q: How do I write a post on Torq?
entries.a: On a computer, type in the What's happening? box at the top of Home. On a phone, tap the round post button in the bottom-right corner. Add text and, if you like, photos, a video, GIFs, a poll or files, then tap Post and approve the publish in Hub or GO.

entries.q: How do I make paragraphs in a Torq post?
entries.a: Press Enter. Torq's composer puts a real paragraph gap where you press Enter, and the gap is kept when the post is shown, on phones too. The phone keyboard stays steady while you type.

entries.q: Can I use bold, italics or lists in a Torq post?
entries.a: Yes. Tap the Text formatting button in the composer to show the bar: Bold, Italic, Underline, Bullet list, Dash list and Numbered list. On a computer the usual shortcuts work, such as Ctrl+B. Formatting is kept in text under a link card too.

entries.q: How many photos can I add to a Torq post?
entries.a: Up to 10 photos per post, in JPEG, PNG or WebP. Before posting you can change their order by dragging them or with the arrows. Quitter readers see only the first four, so a post with more carries a Torq link for them.

entries.q: Why did Torq make my photos smaller?
entries.a: Quitter leaves out any post of 5 MB or more, so Torq keeps every post under that size. Photos are saved as WebP (or JPEG where WebP isn't available) at up to 1920 pixels wide, and if the post is still too big, the largest photos are shrunk further until it fits.

entries.q: What is the size limit for a Torq post?
entries.a: Torq doesn't count characters; the limit is size. The whole post, photos and poll pictures included, must stay under 5 MB, because Quitter leaves out anything bigger. Torq shrinks photos to fit. Videos and files are published separately, so they don't count toward the 5 MB.

entries.q: How do I add a video to a Torq post?
entries.a: Tap the video button in the composer and choose a file; a post holds one video. Torq then asks for Q-Tube video data: a title, a category, an optional description, and a thumbnail picked from the video or your own picture. Then post as usual.

entries.q: Which video formats work on Torq?
entries.a: Use MP4 or MOV with H.264 video, or WebM with VP9. When you add a video, Torq checks it and refuses ones Hub can't play, such as MKV, AVI, WMV or HEVC (H.265), and says why. Save or export the video as MP4 with H.264 and add it again.

entries.q: Will my Torq video show up on Q-Tube?
entries.a: Yes, if the post is public. A video you upload with a public Torq post is published as a Q-Tube video, with the title, category and thumbnail you gave it. Videos in subscription posts stay private. Deleting the Torq post also deletes the videos and files you uploaded with it.

entries.q: How do I show a video as a Q-Tube card on Torq?
entries.a: After you add or link a video, choose Video card or Just the video right on it in the composer. The card shows the title, your channel, the description, likes and SuperLikes. Torq remembers your choice for the next video. Videos in subscription posts always show as the player.

entries.q: How do I add a GIF to a Torq post?
entries.a: Tap the GIF button in the composer. The picker shows GIFs from the community GIFs Q-App: search, tap a tag, or pick from Most used, and Library opens the GIFs Q-App. A post can hold up to 4 GIFs; pasting a GIFs link attaches one too. Quitter can't show GIFs, so its readers get a Torq link.

entries.q: How do I make a poll on Torq?
entries.a: Tap the poll button in the composer and type your question as the post text. Add 2 to 6 choices, up to 80 characters each, with a photo if you like. Below them you can turn on Anon Poll, set Who can vote, Results by and Poll length. Then tap Post.

entries.q: What is an Anon Poll on Torq?
entries.a: An Anon Poll encrypts each vote, so people see anonymous votes, counts and percentages, but not who picked what. Turn on the Anon Poll switch while making the poll. The poll type can't be changed after it is posted.

entries.q: How do I limit who can vote in a Torq poll?
entries.a: Under Who can vote, limit the poll to members of one of your public groups, to accounts at a minting level or above, or both. Votes from anyone else aren't counted. The poll shows who can vote and tells others why they can't. These rules can't be changed after posting.

entries.q: What does Results by Minter weight mean in a Torq poll?
entries.a: With Results by set to Minter weight, each vote counts by the number of blocks its voter has minted, as in Qortal's own polls. The default, Votes, counts each vote once. You pick it while making the poll, and it can't be changed after posting.

entries.q: How do I set when a Torq poll closes?
entries.a: Tap Poll length while making the poll. It starts as No end; pick a quick length, or a day, hour and minute for it to close. The end can be from 5 minutes to 30 days away, and the poll then shows how long is left.

entries.q: Can I change my vote in a Torq poll?
entries.a: Yes, while the poll is open: tap another choice and your vote moves. The poll reminds you with "Tap another choice to change your vote". Each vote is a small publish, so Hub or GO asks you to approve it.

entries.q: How do I see who voted in a Torq poll?
entries.a: Hover over a choice in Hub, or long-press it on a phone, to see the voters' avatars. In an Anon Poll the votes are encrypted, so only the counts and percentages show.

entries.q: Why can't I vote in a Torq poll?
entries.a: Voting needs a registered name, and the poll may have closed. A poll can also be limited by Who can vote to members of a group or to a minting level; the poll then says who can vote and why you can't, and other votes show as not counted.

entries.q: How do I attach a file or music to a Torq post?
entries.a: Tap Add attachment (the paperclip) and choose Publish Files. Pick documents, audio, zips or other files, each under 2 GB; you can give each a title and a thumbnail. They are published to QDN with the post, the way Q-Share does it. In the post, audio plays and PDFs open in a preview; Quitter readers get a Torq link.

entries.q: What does Add from QDN do in Torq?
entries.a: It attaches a file that is already published on QDN instead of uploading it again. Under Add attachment, choose Add from QDN and paste a Q-Share link, a qortal:// file link, a Web Builder folder link, or the identifier of a published file.

entries.q: Which links turn into cards in Torq?
aliases: post a qapp link in torq
entries.a: Paste a supported link and Torq shows a card or player: Q-Tube videos, Subscreen titles, Subwire articles, Q-Chat group invites, Q-Apps and websites (deep links too), Torq or Quitter posts, GIFs, Q-Shop items, and links to Q-Share, Q-Blog, Q-Mail, Q-Fund, Q-Assets, Q-Podcasts and Q-Music. The post still carries the plain qortal:// link for Quitter.

entries.q: How do I remove a link card but keep the link in Torq?
entries.a: While writing, tap the X on the card. That removes the card and leaves the link in your text. You can also write under a card, with bold, italics and lists kept.

entries.q: Can I change the order of link cards in a Torq post?
entries.a: Yes. With two or more link cards, use the arrows above each card, or drag it by its handle on a computer. There is also a place to type between each pair of cards. Moving a card leaves your text where it is, and the post shows the cards in the order of their links.

entries.q: How do I mention someone in a Torq post?
entries.a: Type @ and start the name; Torq suggests names, people you follow first. Pick one to add the mention. The person sees it in Torq's Notifications under Mentions, and gets a Hub or GO alert if they allowed Torq notifications.

entries.q: How do hashtags work on Torq?
entries.a: Write # and a word, such as #qortal, in a post or a Rev caption. Tap a hashtag to search it, or use Discover's Hashtags tab, which suggests tags as you type. A hashtag search finds posts, replies, and Revs with that tag in their captions.

entries.q: How do I see trending hashtags on Torq?
entries.a: Turn on Trending in Torq's Settings, under Content. Trending hashtags then show on Home and in What's happening. It stays off until you turn it on. Hashtags on Revs count toward trending too.

entries.q: How do I quote a post on Torq?
entries.a: Copy the post's link with its share button and paste it into a new post or reply. Torq shows it as a quoted card with its pictures, music and files, and you write your own words with it. If your post is only that link, Torq publishes it as a plain repost instead.

entries.q: How do I repost on Torq?
aliases: share post to my followers torq
why can't i repost on torq
entries.a: Tap the repost button (two arrows) under the post and confirm Repost. It goes to your followers and your profile. Tap it again to Unrepost. You can't repost your own posts, repost the same post twice, or repost subscription posts.

entries.q: How do I edit a post on Torq?
entries.a: Open the menu (the three dots) on your post, choose Edit, make your changes and post again. Torq republishes it in place, so its link, likes and replies stay, and its link cards are kept. Reposts can't be edited.

entries.q: Can people see the old version after I edit a Torq post?
entries.a: No. QDN keeps only the latest version, so the old wording is gone. If a reader turns on Edited posts in Settings, a quiet Edited mark shows next to the date; opening it shows when the post was published and edited, and the current text.

entries.q: How do I delete a post on Torq?
entries.a: Open the menu (the three dots) on your post, choose Delete and confirm. Videos and files you uploaded with it are deleted too. This can't be undone. Treat public posts as permanent anyway: others may have seen or saved them already.

entries.q: How do I pin a post to my Torq profile?
entries.a: Open the menu on one of your own posts and choose Pin to profile; it then sits at the top of your profile. You have one pin, so pinning another post replaces it, and Unpin from profile removes it. Replies and subscription posts can't be pinned, and the option isn't offered on a public node.

entries.q: What happens to a post I close before sending on Torq?
entries.a: It waits as a draft: text and formatting, photos, videos, files, a poll or a quoted post. A small orange Draft tab sits on the Post button, or on the reply button of the post you were answering; open it to carry on. Drafts last until Torq is closed or reloaded. The X in the post box throws a draft away.

entries.q: How do I add emoji to a Torq post?
entries.a: Tap the emoji button in the composer and pick one; it goes where your cursor is. If the full emoji list can't download, common emoji stay on offer and Try again fetches the list again.

entries.q: How do I reply to a post on Torq?
entries.a: Tap the reply button under the post, or open the post and use the Post your reply... box. Write your reply, add photos or other media if you like, tap Post and approve it. To answer a reply, use Reply to @name under it.

entries.q: How do I see replies to replies on Torq?
entries.a: Open the post: its thread shows replies and replies to replies, and the reply count includes them all. If Expand reply threads is off in Settings, only the first line of replies shows and deeper ones open with Show replies.

entries.q: Can I edit or delete my reply on Torq?
entries.a: Yes. Your own replies have the same menu as your posts, with Edit and Delete. Editing republishes the reply in place; deleting can't be undone.

entries.q: Why doesn't my new post show up on Torq right away?
entries.a: A publish takes a minute or two to reach the network, so other people, and your other devices, see it a little later. Torq shows your own post at once and keeps looking for late replies, likes and reposts. If it isn't there after a few minutes, check that you approved the publish in Hub or GO.

entries.q: How do I like a post on Torq?
entries.a: Tap the heart under the post and approve the publish; the heart fills once it's approved. Tap it again to unlike. You can't like your own posts, but on your own post the heart shows who liked it.

entries.q: How do I see who liked or reposted a Torq post?
entries.a: In Hub, hover over the like, repost or reply count. On a phone, tap the count. A list of names opens over the post without leaving it; on a phone, drag it down to close.

entries.q: Are my likes and follows public on Torq?
aliases: can people see my likes torq
entries.a: Yes. Likes and follows are small public documents published under your name. Anyone can see them, and profiles list them in the Likes, Followers and Following tabs. Unlike subscription posts, they aren't encrypted.

entries.q: How do I share a link to a Torq post?
entries.a: Tap the share button under the post. Torq copies a qortal://APP/Torq/post/... link to your clipboard; paste it into a chat, a post or another Q-App. Anyone with Hub or GO can open it, and a link to a reply opens the conversation at that reply.

entries.q: How do I open a Torq link someone sent me?
entries.a: Tap it inside Qortal Hub or GO, for example in Q-Chat. A post link looks like qortal://APP/Torq/post/name/identifier and a profile link like qortal://APP/Torq/user/name. Old Quitter post links work in Torq too.

entries.q: How do I load new posts on Torq?
entries.a: Torq checks for new posts while you read. When some arrive, a New posts notice with the posters' avatars appears at the top of the feed; tap it to show them and jump to the top. It works on Everything and Following.

entries.q: How do I view or save a photo from a Torq post?
aliases: tap to see full image torq
save a picture from a torq post
entries.a: Tap the photo to open it full screen. Pinch, or use two fingers on a touchpad, to zoom; swipe through a set; and tap Save image to keep a copy; Hub may ask where to save it. Very tall pictures show their middle in the feed with Tap to see full image.

entries.q: Can I keep a video loading while I scroll on Torq?
aliases: keep fetching in the side panel
entries.a: Yes. A video that is still fetching has a Keep fetching in the side panel button. Tap it and keep scrolling; PDFs, images, audio and other files can do the same. The side panel tells you when one is ready, and you open it from there.

entries.q: Can I watch Q-Tube videos inside Torq?
entries.a: Yes. A Q-Tube link in a post plays in the feed, or shows as a Q-Tube card with the title, channel, description and length. From the card you can like the video, send it a Q-Tube SuperLike with an optional message, or tap Watch on Q-Tube. Hover the like or SuperLike button to see who sent them.

entries.q: Can I read Subwire articles in Torq?
entries.a: Yes. A Subwire article link opens inside Torq, with its video or audio. You can like the article, see who liked it, or open it in Subwire.

entries.q: How do group invite links work in Torq?
entries.a: A Q-Chat group link (qortal://use-group/action-join/groupid-...) in a post shows as a group invite card. Tap Join group: an open group joins you at once, and a closed group sends a request, shown as Pending.

entries.q: How do Q-Shop links show in Torq?
entries.a: Shops, products, collections and names for sale shared from Q-Shop show as cards. A product shows its picture, title and QORT price first (with a sale or auction if there is one), a shop shows its logo, rating and what it accepts, and the card opens the app it names.

entries.q: Can I rate a Subscreen title from Torq?
entries.a: Yes. A Subscreen link shows a card with the poster, genres and average rating, and plays or previews the playlist. You can rate the title from 1 to 10 without leaving Torq.

entries.q: What is a SuperLike on Torq?
entries.a: A SuperLike sends QORT straight to the author of a post or reply, with an emoji and an optional message, the way Q-Tube's SuperLikes work. A SuperLiked post gets a gold edge and a row of its SuperLikers' avatars, each wearing their emoji. SuperLikes are Torq-only; Quitter doesn't show them.

entries.q: How do I send a SuperLike on Torq?
aliases: how do i superlike a post
entries.a:
1. Like the post: a small gold SuperLike button springs up beside the like count.
2. Tap it and pick an emoji (the heart by default), an amount (1, 5, 10, 25 or any whole QORT) and a message if you like.
3. Approve the payment to the author, then the SuperLike. It shows on the post as soon as the payment is approved.

entries.q: Can I get a SuperLike payment back on Torq?
entries.a: No. A SuperLike is a real QORT payment to the author, and sent QORT can't be taken back, so check the amount before you approve. If you approve the payment but decline the second approval (the SuperLike itself), the payment isn't lost: tap the SuperLike button again and Finish SuperLike publishes it without paying twice.

entries.q: Why doesn't my SuperLike count on Torq?
entries.a: A SuperLike only counts once its payment checks out on chain: at least 1 QORT, from your address to the author's, within ten minutes of the SuperLike, and each payment counts once. This keeps SuperLikes from being faked. If you declined the second approval, tap the SuperLike button again and use Finish SuperLike.

entries.q: Where can I see SuperLiked posts on Torq?
entries.a: Open Discover and choose SuperLiked: posts people sent QORT to, the most recently SuperLiked first. On a post, hover over a SuperLiker's avatar (tap it on a phone) to see what they sent and their messages. When someone SuperLikes your post, a gold notification shows under Likes.

entries.q: Is a SuperLike message public on Torq?
entries.a: Yes. The message, up to 280 characters, is also posted as your public reply in the same approval, marked in gold with the emoji and amount. People can reply to it and like it. SuperLikes aren't offered on subscription posts.

entries.q: How do I search on Torq?
entries.a: Open Discover, type in the search box and press Search. Users finds people by name, Hashtags finds tags and suggests them as you type, Creators ranks active people, and SuperLiked lists SuperLiked posts. The X clears the search.

entries.q: What does the Creators tab in Torq's Discover show?
entries.a: Creators ranks people by Most followers, Most posts, Most liked, Most discussed (most replies) or Most reposted. Pick a ranking to see who leads it, and tap a name to open the profile.

entries.q: How do notifications work on Torq?
entries.a: Open Notifications from Torq's left panel (on a phone, the side bar). The tabs are All, Followers, Unfollowed, Mentions, Replies and Likes, covering posts and Revs; All also shows new posts from people you follow. A reply notification opens on that reply. On a phone, pull down to refresh. Torq also shows a popup and plays a sound for new ones.

entries.q: How do I get Torq alerts in Hub or GO?
entries.a: When you open Torq, Hub or GO asks whether it may send notifications; allow it. On a computer, if you said no, Torq's left panel shows Enable Hub notifications to ask again. You are then alerted about mentions in posts and Revs, replies to your posts and Revs, SuperLikes, and new posts from people you follow. Likes and follows show only on Torq's Notifications page.

entries.q: Why does a Torq alert open Quitter?
entries.a: Torq's alerts for posts still carry Quitter's link and picture. Qortal GO 3.0 v0.0.18 and newer fix this on its side: Torq alerts show Torq's avatar and open Torq, so update GO if yours still opens Quitter. In Hub such an alert may open in Quitter, which shows the same post.

entries.q: What is the Unfollowed tab in Torq notifications?
entries.a: It lists people who stopped following you, with the time it happened. Unfollows come from Qortal itself, so they match on every device and include older ones. Followers shows only people who followed you, and blocking someone doesn't count as an unfollow.

entries.q: How do I turn off Torq's notification sound or popups?
entries.a: Open Torq's Settings, Notifications. Turn off Notification Alerts for the popups and Notification Sound for the sound; tap test sound to hear it first. Both are on until you change them. Hub's and GO's own alerts for Torq are set in Hub or GO.

entries.q: How do I bookmark a post on Torq?
entries.a: Open the menu (the three dots) on the post and choose Add to Bookmarks. Saved posts are on the Bookmarks page, under All or in a folder. Choose Remove from Bookmarks to take one off.

entries.q: How do I sort Torq bookmarks into folders?
entries.a: On the Bookmarks page, tap New folder and name it; each folder has its own colour. On a bookmarked post, the folder mark beside its menu moves it into a folder or back to Unfiled. A folder's menu has Rename and Delete folder. On a phone, swipe sideways to move between folders.

entries.q: How do I get my Torq bookmarks on another device?
entries.a: Bookmarks are kept on the device where you made them. On the Bookmarks page, tap Save to QDN to publish your folders and bookmarks; it shows Unsaved while there are changes. On the other device, open Bookmarks and tap Fetch from QDN.

entries.q: Are my Torq bookmarks private?
aliases: can others see my bookmarks torq
can people see my bookmarks torq
entries.a: Only until you save them to QDN. Save to QDN publishes your bookmarks as a plain, unencrypted document under your name, which anyone could read. Bookmarks you never save stay on that device only.

entries.q: What are the tabs on a Torq profile?
entries.a: Posts, Revs, Replies, Likes, Followers and Following. A profile that offers a subscription also has Sub Posts, and the Revs tab goes away while Revs are hidden. On a phone, swipe sideways to move between tabs; they scroll when they don't fit.

entries.q: How do I see who someone follows on Torq?
entries.a: Open their profile. The header shows how many followers they have and how many they follow, and the Followers and Following tabs list the names. Tap a name to open that profile.

entries.q: How do links in a Torq bio work?
entries.a: A qortal:// link in a bio opens in a new tab, and a website or Q-App link shows as a small card with its icon and title. A normal web link (one starting with https) is copied instead, so you can paste it into a web browser.

entries.q: How do I see a profile picture full size on Torq?
entries.a: Tap the avatar on someone's profile page to open it full screen. If the avatar has a gold ring, tapping it plays their Revs instead; inside a Rev, tap the avatar to see it full size.

entries.q: How do I hide someone on Torq?
entries.a: Open the menu on one of their posts and choose Hide @name, or add the name under Hidden users in Settings. Their posts and Revs leave your feeds, in Torq only. You still see their likes and their replies on your posts. You can hide up to 100 users.

entries.q: What is the difference between hiding and blocking on Torq?
entries.a: Hiding works in Torq only: their posts leave your feeds, nothing is published, and they aren't blocked across Qortal. Blocking adds the name to the Qortal block list on your node, so it applies beyond Torq too, and you won't see their posts or profile.

entries.q: How do I block someone on Torq?
entries.a: Open the menu on their post and choose Block @name, or tap Block on their profile. Unblock from their profile, or from Settings, Blocked Users. Blocking uses your own node's block list, so these options don't appear on a public node.

entries.q: How do I hide posts with certain words on Torq?
entries.a: In Torq's Settings, under Content, type words or phrases into Hidden words (separate several with commas) and tap Add. Posts containing them are hidden from your feeds without leaving gaps. You can add up to 50.

entries.q: How do I see posts from someone I hid on Torq?
entries.a: Open their profile: Torq says User hidden and offers View feed anyway for this visit, or Unhide. You can also remove the name from Hidden users in Settings, or choose Unhide @name in one of their posts' menus.

entries.q: Why does Torq show Reply from someone you hid?
entries.a: That row stands in for a reply by someone you hid, so the thread and its count still add up. Tap Show to read that one reply. Replies on your own posts, from any of your names, always show in full, and a SuperLike's message always shows once its payment checks out.

entries.q: How do I change Torq's theme?
entries.a: Open Torq's Settings, Appearance, Theme, and choose Hub 3.0 Theme (the default), Quitter Theme, X Theme or White Theme. The theme applies to Torq's feed, composer, embeds and menus.

entries.q: How do I switch Torq between dark and light?
entries.a: In Settings, Appearance, Light or dark: Match Hub follows Qortal Hub (the default), or choose Dark or Light to keep one on this device. This choice stays on the device and isn't saved to QDN. The White Theme is always light.

entries.q: How do I keep my Torq settings on another device?
entries.a: In Settings, Account, tap Save Settings to QDN; on the other device tap Fetch Settings from QDN. This carries your theme, hidden words, hidden users and other Torq settings, but not Light or dark. The saved settings are a plain public document, hidden lists included. Follows and Qortal blocks already belong to your name.

entries.q: What does Expand reply threads do in Torq?
entries.a: With it on (the default), opening a post shows every reply and reply-to-reply. Turn it off in Settings, Content, to show only the first line of replies; deeper ones then wait behind Show replies.

entries.q: What do Torq's desktop Layout settings do?
entries.a: On a computer, Settings has Layout: Hide side panels on scroll (on by default) lets the side columns slide up with the feed, and Name switcher on Home puts the name switcher at the bottom of the left panel. Under Notifications, Right panel notifications shows them in the right panel instead of on the Profile button.

entries.q: What are Subscriptions in Torq?
entries.a: Subscriptions let a creator publish encrypted posts that only members of their private group can read. People subscribe and join the group in the Subscriptions Q-App, then read those posts in Torq's Subscriptions feed and on the creator's Sub Posts tab. Turn on Subscriptions in Torq's Settings, under Content, to see them.

entries.q: How do I post subscriber-only posts on Torq?
entries.a:
1. Own a private group set up as a subscription in the Subscriptions Q-App.
2. In Torq, turn on Subscriptions in Settings, then attach the group in Manage Owned Subscriptions, using your primary name.
3. In the composer, change Public to that group before posting. Only its members can decrypt the post.

entries.q: How do I subscribe to someone on Torq?
entries.a: Tap Subscribe on their profile. It opens the Subscriptions Q-App, where you subscribe and join their private group. Once you're a member, their encrypted posts show in Torq's Subscriptions feed and their Sub Posts tab, with Subscriptions turned on in Torq's Settings.

entries.q: Why does a Torq post say This post is encrypted?
entries.a: It's a subscription post, encrypted for the members of the author's private group. If you aren't a member, Torq shows a lock with This post is for subscribers only and the name to subscribe to. Subscribe in the Subscriptions Q-App, and once you're in the group the post opens.

entries.q: Does Torq have its own sign-in?
entries.a: Torq has no sign-in of its own: it uses the account you're signed into in Hub or GO. Sign out or switch accounts there. To post as a different name on the same account, use Torq's name switcher instead.

entries.q: Is Torq safe to use with my QORT?
entries.a: Torq can't move QORT or publish anything without you: each publish and payment shows an approval in Hub or GO with its amount and fee. The only payments Torq asks for are SuperLikes, including Q-Tube SuperLikes from video cards, and the approval shows who gets the QORT and how much. Torq never needs your seed phrase or password; never type them into any Q-App.

entries.q: Does Torq have direct messages?
entries.a: No. Torq is for public posts, replies and Revs, plus encrypted subscription posts. For private messages, use Q-Chat in Hub or GO.

entries.q: How do I add my own GIF to Torq's GIF picker?
entries.a: Add it in the GIFs Q-App: tap Library in Torq's GIF picker, or open qortal://APP/GIFs. GIFs added there are published under your name and appear in Torq's picker, and in the GIF picker of Q-Chat too.

entries.q: Why are some Torq options missing on a public node?
entries.a: Some features rely on your own node. On a public node, Torq leaves out Block, the Blocked Users page, Pin to profile, and Follow in a post's menu. You can still follow from a profile, and post, reply and like as usual.

entries.q: Why can't I like or repost my own post on Torq?
entries.a: Torq doesn't allow liking or reposting your own posts. On your own post, those buttons show who liked or reposted it instead.

entries.q: What are Revs on Torq?
entries.a: Revs are Torq's stories: a photo, or a video up to a minute long, with captions, stickers and drawing on top. They sit in the row at the top of Home for 7 days, then stay on QDN in the person's profile, under the Revs tab. Revs are Torq-only: Quitter and Q-Tube never show them.

entries.q: How do I post a Rev on Torq?
aliases: how do i post a story
entries.a:
1. On Home, tap the + on your avatar in the row at the top.
2. Choose a photo, or a video up to a minute long (up to 10 at once).
3. Frame it with drag and pinch, then add captions, stickers or drawing.
4. Tap Share Rev and approve it.

entries.q: Can I post a Rev from my computer?
entries.a: Yes. In Hub, click the + on your avatar at the top of Torq's Home. Besides choosing a file, you can drop or paste a photo into the editor. Captions and photos turn and resize with a corner handle instead of two fingers.

entries.q: How long can a Rev video be on Torq?
aliases: how long can a rev be
entries.a: Up to one minute and up to 100 MB, because every viewer's node downloads the whole video before the Rev shows. Torq doesn't trim videos, so a longer or bigger one is refused with a note; trim it in another app, or record a shorter clip or a lower resolution.

entries.q: Why was my photo or video refused for a Rev?
entries.a: Revs take JPEG, PNG or WebP photos, and videos up to a minute and 100 MB in a format Hub can play. HEVC, MKV, AVI and similar files are refused with the reason; save the video as MP4 with H.264. On an iPhone, set Settings, Camera, Formats to Most Compatible.

entries.q: How long do Revs stay on Torq?
entries.a: A Rev shows in the top row of Home, and gives the poster a gold ring, for 7 days; the row shows each person's newest 10. After that it stays on QDN in the person's profile, under Revs, until they delete it.

entries.q: How long does a photo Rev stay on screen?
entries.a: About 6 seconds, then the next Rev plays. Hold your finger on it to pause for longer, or tap the left side to go back. A video Rev plays for its own length, up to a minute.

entries.q: How do I watch Revs on Torq?
entries.a: Tap an avatar in the row at the top of Home, or any avatar with a gold ring. Tap the right side for the next Rev and the left for the one before, hold to pause, swipe sideways for the next person and swipe down to close. On a computer, use the arrow keys and Space.

entries.q: What does the gold ring around an avatar mean on Torq?
entries.a: That person has posted Revs in the last 7 days. A gold ring that gently shimmers means Revs you haven't watched; a quieter, still gold means you've seen them. Tap the avatar to play them. Which ones you've watched is kept on your device only.

entries.q: What is the New Rev from pop-up on Torq?
entries.a: While you scroll Home with the Rev row out of sight, a New Rev from pill appears when someone you follow posts a Rev. Tap it to watch. People you hide never show in it.

entries.q: Why are Rev videos muted on Torq?
entries.a: Videos start muted. Turn the sound on once and it stays on for the next ones. If your phone refuses sound for a video, it plays muted instead of stopping.

entries.q: How do I pause a Rev on Torq?
entries.a: Hold your finger on the Rev. In Hub, press Space or the Pause button by the menu, and click the middle of the Rev to play on. While paused, the name and buttons step aside so you see a clear picture; move the mouse to bring them back.

entries.q: How do I like a Rev on Torq?
entries.a: Double-tap the Rev, or tap the heart. Everyone sees how many likes a Rev has, and on your own Rev the heart lists who liked it. Some Revs swap the heart for an emoji the poster chose; a like is the same either way.

entries.q: Why do my Rev likes wait for approval on Torq?
entries.a: Double-tap likes and quick reactions count straight away but wait on your device, so Qortal doesn't ask one at a time. When you close the Revs, a summary lists them and one approval saves them all. If you choose Later or decline, Rev likes need your approval waits at the top of Notifications, with the bell dot on, until you approve or discard them.

entries.q: How do I reply to a Rev on Torq?
entries.a: Swipe up on the Rev, or tap Reply to, to open its replies. Type a few words or tap a quick reaction, and send. Replies are public and show newest first, and you can delete your own. On a phone, drag the sheet down to close it. The poster gets a notification.

entries.q: Can I see who viewed my Rev on Torq?
entries.a: No. Torq doesn't record views: which Revs someone has watched stays on their own device. You can see who liked your Rev (tap the heart on your own Rev) and read its replies.

entries.q: How do I add text to a Rev on Torq?
entries.a: In the Rev editor, tap Add text. Choose one of five styles (Classic, Strong, Serif, Mono, Neon), a text colour and a background colour; either colour can be picked straight off the photo. Drag the caption anywhere, and turn or resize it with two fingers or the corner handle; it snaps straight and centred.

entries.q: What stickers can I put on a Rev?
entries.a: Tap Add a sticker for Mention, Link (a qortal:// or web link shown as a card), Poll, GIF, Emoji or Photo. A Rev holds up to 40 captions and stickers. Viewers can tap them: a link opens, a mention opens the profile, and a poll takes their vote.

entries.q: Does someone get notified when I mention them in a Rev?
entries.a: Yes. Add a Mention sticker in the Rev editor and pick the name. The person sees it in Torq's Notifications under Mentions, and gets a Hub or GO alert if they allowed Torq notifications, unless they hide Revs. Viewers tap the mention to open the profile.

entries.q: How do I add a poll to a Rev?
entries.a: In the Rev editor, tap Add a sticker, then Poll, and write your question and its choices. A Rev can hold one poll. Viewers tap a choice to vote, and the Rev waits while Qortal asks them to approve the vote.

entries.q: Can I put more than one photo on a Rev?
entries.a: Yes, up to four photos on top of the main one: Add a sticker, then Photo. Drag, pinch or use the corner handle to size and turn them, and drop one on the bin to remove it. Tap a photo to send it To front, To back (under captions and stickers), or Behind main photo.

entries.q: How do I draw on a Rev?
entries.a: Tap Draw in the Rev editor and choose a pen, marker, neon or eraser and a colour. Undo takes back any step. When you edit a posted Rev, you can draw over the earlier drawing or rub it out with the eraser.

entries.q: How do I frame the photo or video in a Rev?
entries.a: Drag the photo or video to move it and pinch to zoom; the Fill the screen and Fit the whole picture button switches between the two quickly. Change background cycles what shows behind a smaller picture: a blur of it, or plain colours.

entries.q: How do I undo or remove something in the Rev editor?
entries.a: Tap Undo to take back any step, and drag a caption, sticker or photo onto the bin to remove it. In a set, removing a whole Rev shows Rev removed with Undo. Escape, or Android Back in GO, closes the tool you have open rather than the Rev.

entries.q: How do I change the like button on my Rev?
entries.a: In the Rev editor, tap the like button control and pick the heart or any one emoji. Viewers tap or double-tap it to like your Rev, and a double tap pops that emoji. It counts as an ordinary like.

entries.q: Can I post several Revs at once?
entries.a: Yes. Pick up to 10 photos or videos together; each becomes its own Rev. The strip of small pictures under the Rev switches between them, adds one with +, and removes one (with Undo); drag them, or long-press and drag on a phone, to change the order. Share them all with one approval, and everyone sees them in your order.

entries.q: What happens if posting a set of Revs stops part way?
entries.a: Nothing is lost. Share again to finish; the Revs already out keep their place and nothing is posted twice. A very large set, mostly from big videos, shows a size warning before it goes out.

entries.q: How do I edit a Rev after posting it?
entries.a: While watching one of your Revs, open its menu and choose Edit Rev, or use the menu on the Rev in your profile's Revs tab (a long press opens it too). Change captions, stickers, photos, framing, the drawing or the like button, then tap Save Rev. It keeps its link, likes, replies and day, and the photo or video isn't uploaded again.

entries.q: How do I delete a Rev on Torq?
entries.a: Open the menu while watching your Rev, or on the Rev in your profile's Revs tab, choose Delete Rev and confirm. It is removed from QDN for everyone and can't be undone. If Qortal's approval is declined, the Rev comes back.

entries.q: Where are my unfinished Revs saved on Torq?
entries.a: An unfinished Rev saves itself on this device as you work: one draft per name, never on QDN. Close the editor any way you like, and the orange DRAFT tab on your bubble at the top of Home brings it back as you left it. The bin in the editor throws the draft away, after asking.

entries.q: Why does Torq say my Rev draft can't be opened?
entries.a: The draft couldn't be read on this device, was saved by a newer Torq, or is taking too long to open. Tap Try again, or reload Torq to get the latest version. Starting a new Rev won't replace the old draft.

entries.q: How do I find someone's older Revs on Torq?
entries.a: Open their profile and the Revs tab. A month calendar shows a round picture on days with Revs; tap a day to see that day's Revs, with the day marked in blue. Each Rev there shows its likes and replies.

entries.q: How do I find Revs by hashtag?
entries.a: Add #tags to your Rev captions. Searching a #hashtag in Discover shows the Revs with that tag above the posts, each marked with who posted it, and hashtags on Revs count toward trending.

entries.q: How do I turn Revs off on Torq?
entries.a: Turn on Hide Revs in Settings, under Content. Revs leave the top bar (the Torq logo comes back), the Revs tab leaves profiles, and Torq stops all background Rev work: downloads, Rev notifications and their Hub alerts. Turn it off to bring Revs back.

entries.q: Do Revs use a lot of data on Torq?
entries.a: They can. Torq downloads each Rev in full in the background, video included, before showing that person, so a tap plays at once. On a limited data plan, turn on Hide Revs in Settings to stop all Rev downloads.

entries.q: How do I share a link to a Rev?
entries.a: While watching it, open the menu and choose Copy link. The link looks like qortal://APP/Torq/rev/... and opens the Rev for anyone in Hub or GO.

entries.q: How do I hide someone's Revs on Torq?
entries.a: While watching their Rev, open the menu and choose Hide, followed by their name. That hides them in Torq: their Revs leave the top bar, the rings and the New Rev pop-up at once, and their posts leave your feeds. Their replies and likes on Revs still show.

entries.q: Can I put a Torq post on my Rev?
aliases: share a post in a rev
entries.a: Yes. Paste a link to a Torq post or reply into a Link sticker and it becomes a card with the author, the words and the post's first picture. Tap the card in the editor to switch between Postcard, Glass, Polaroid and Quote. Viewers tap it to open the post.

entries.q: Why won't a Rev play on Torq?
entries.a: While a Rev downloads you see its blurred picture and how much has arrived; it says so if it can't be played. If no node holds its files any more, for example one posted from a public node that dropped it, it can't load. If it's yours, Delete Rev clears it away.

entries.q: How do I share a photo from my gallery to Torq?
entries.a: In your gallery or camera app, tap Share and choose Torq. Qortal GO opens with the photos (up to 10) or a video already in its Home composer; finish the post and tap Publish. GO removes location and camera details from shared photos first.

entries.q: How do I make a Rev from a photo or video in my gallery?
entries.a: In your gallery, tap Share on one photo or video and choose Torq Rev. Qortal GO opens Torq's Rev editor with it, ready to frame and decorate. Videos can be up to 100 MB. If GO says the file couldn't be opened or is too big, pick another one in Torq's editor.

entries.q: Why don't I see Torq in the Android share sheet?
aliases: torq rev not in share menu
entries.a: GO's share entries follow the app its Home composer posts to: Torq and Torq Rev show while Torq is chosen, and a Quitter entry while Quitter is. Switch the composer to Torq. Right after installing or updating GO, the entry can stay as it was until GO syncs after you sign in.

entries.q: How do Android Back and full screen work in Torq on GO?
entries.a: Torq takes the whole screen in Qortal GO while you watch or make a Rev, read a Subwire article or a document, view a photo or play an upright video; GO's bars step aside until you close it. Android Back closes the newest of those first, or a sheet or menu open over a Rev, before it goes back a page.

entries.q: How do I go back a page in Torq on a phone?
entries.a: Slide the page off to the right with your finger, or pull in from the right edge as with Android's back gesture; a quick flick is enough. The round back button and Android Back work too. On the first tab of a page, swiping right also goes back.

entries.q: How do I find my way around Torq on a phone?
entries.a: Use the round buttons in the bottom-right corner. The menu button opens the side bar with Home, your profile, Notifications, Discover, Bookmarks and Settings, and your account and name switcher at the top. Another round button posts (or goes back), and a scroll-to-top button appears once you are far down a page.

entries.q: Can I swipe between tabs in Torq?
entries.a: Yes, on a phone. Swipe left on Home for Following and right for Everything. Discover's tabs, the Notifications filters, profile tabs and bookmark folders follow your finger the same way, with the next tab's name riding in beside it. Sliders, players and text fields keep their own gestures.

entries.q: How do I open Torq's Settings?
entries.a: On a computer, click Settings in Torq's left panel. On a phone, tap the round menu button in the bottom-right corner and choose Settings. Settings has Account, Appearance, Notifications, Content, Safety (on your own node) and, on a computer, Layout; the version and changelog are at the bottom.

entries.q: How do I open my own Torq profile?
entries.a: On a computer, click Profile (your avatar) in the left panel. On a phone, open the round menu button and tap your avatar. Your posts, Revs, replies, likes, followers and following are there, and the pencil edits your bio.

entries.q: Why is there a dot on Torq's menu button?
entries.a: It means you have new notifications. Open the menu and tap Notifications to see them. The dot also stays while Rev likes are waiting for your approval.

entries.q: How do I use Torq in Qortal Hub on a computer?
entries.a: Open Torq from Hub's Q-Apps library. The left panel has Home, Profile, Notifications, Bookmarks, Settings and Discover, and the right panel shows notifications and, if turned on, trending hashtags. Hover over counts to see who liked, replied or voted. In Revs, use the arrow keys, Space to pause, or the Pause button.

entries.q: Do Revs pause when I switch tabs in Hub?
entries.a: Yes. A Rev pauses whenever Torq isn't on screen, including when Hub shows another tab, and carries on where it was when you come back. A Rev never plays or counts as watched while you can't see it.

entries.q: How do I peek at Torq notifications in Hub without leaving the feed?
entries.a: In Hub, use the Notifications card in Torq's right panel: it opens a scrollable preview, and See all opens the full Notifications page. If you turned off Right panel notifications in Settings, they show on the Profile button instead.

entries.q: How do I stop Torq alerts but still see them in Hub or GO?
entries.a: Torq's alerts come through Hub or GO. Open their notifications panel, then Notification settings, and turn on Disable OS push for Torq. Its desktop or phone alerts stop, while its notifications still show inside Hub or GO. Torq's own popups and sound are in Torq's Settings.

entries.q: Torq stays on Downloading from network in GO. What can I do?
entries.a: That page is the node fetching Torq's files from QDN. If it stays at 0 files, the node can't get them right now; your account and GO are fine. Wait a minute and open Torq again. On a busy public node this can stall for a while; a node of your own avoids it.

entries.q: Why does a picture in a Torq post not load?
entries.a: A picture published moments ago may not have reached your node yet, so Torq keeps a placeholder and shows it when it arrives. If it really can't load, tap it to try again. A whole post that couldn't be fetched has a Try again button.

entries.q: Why won't a PDF open in Torq?
entries.a: The PDF viewer, about 1.6 MB, downloads the first time you open a PDF, not with the app. If that download fails, Torq tries once more by itself, and the Retry button asks for it again.

entries.q: Why does Torq say These photos are too large to post together?
entries.a: Torq shrinks photos until the post is under 5 MB, the most Quitter shows. When even the smallest size doesn't fit, it stops with this message. Remove a photo, or use fewer very large ones, and post again.

entries.q: How big a video or file can I post on Torq?
entries.a: Each video or file can be up to 2 GB. On a public node, Hub and GO accept up to 500 MB per file, so use your own node for bigger ones. Rev videos are limited to 100 MB and one minute. Big uploads take a while to publish.

entries.q: Can I still use Quitter instead of Torq?
entries.a: Yes. Quitter still reads and writes the same posts and follows, so you can use either app. Torq is the newer one with more features; anything Quitter can't show, such as GIFs, polls, files, SuperLikes and Revs, appears there as a Torq link or not at all.

entries.q: Is Torq open source?
entries.a: Its source code is public. Torq is built from Quitter's code, and Torq's own code is on Qortal's Gitea as the Torq repository. The app itself is published on QDN under the name Torq.

entries.q: Why does a long Torq post show Show more?
entries.a: Long posts are folded in the feed. Tap Show more to read the rest and Show less to fold it again. It only appears when it really hides something; a post just a little longer shows in full.

entries.q: How do I preview replies without opening a Torq post?
entries.a: Hover over the reply count in Hub, or tap it on a phone. A panel shows the replies, and you can reply from there. Open the post for the whole thread.

entries.q: Why is the Torq logo showing instead of Revs?
entries.a: Hide Revs is turned on, which puts the Torq logo and slogan back in place of the Rev row. Open Settings, Content, and turn Hide Revs off to bring Revs back.

entries.q: Are Revs public?
entries.a: Yes. Revs, their likes and their replies are public on QDN, so anyone using Torq can watch them; there is no followers-only option. Which Revs you've watched stays on your own device.

entries.q: Why do I see Revs from people I don't follow?
entries.a: The Rev row shows everyone who posted Revs in the last 7 days, not only people you follow. Unwatched Revs come first, and the people you follow come first among them. Hide someone to take their Revs out of the row.

entries.q: How do I watch my own Revs?
entries.a: Tap your own avatar at the start of the Rev row on Home to play your Revs; the + beside it makes a new one. Your ring shows the moment you post. Your profile's Revs tab has all of them, by day.

entries.q: Can I make a Torq post only my followers can see?
entries.a: No. Public posts can be read by anyone on Qortal, followers or not. The only private posts are subscription posts, encrypted for the members of a private group you own.

entries.q: How do I see the posts I liked on Torq?
entries.a: Open your profile and choose the Likes tab. It lists the posts you liked; anyone can see this tab on any profile.

entries.q: Why does a Torq post have a gold edge?
entries.a: Someone SuperLiked it: they sent QORT to the author. The avatars under the post show who, each with the emoji they chose. Hover over one, or tap it on a phone, to see the amount and their messages.

entries.q: Can I play music in a Torq post?
aliases: put music in a torq post
entries.a: Yes. Audio attached to a post plays right in the feed with Torq's player. Tap the speaker to mute it, and again to get your volume back. Music in a quoted post plays too.

entries.q: Why does a profile say User Blocked on Torq?
entries.a: You blocked that name, so Torq hides their posts and profile. Tap Unblock on that page, or use Settings, Blocked Users. Blocking lives on your node, so these options aren't offered on a public node.

entries.q: Why is Follow missing from a Torq post's menu?
entries.a: Either you already follow that person (unfollow them from their profile), or you're on a public node, where the menu leaves it out. You can always follow from their profile page.

entries.q: What keyboard shortcuts does Torq have?
