entries.a: In the composer: Ctrl+B, Ctrl+I and Ctrl+U for bold, italic and underline, Ctrl+Shift+8 for a bullet list and Ctrl+Shift+7 for a numbered list (Cmd on a Mac). In Revs, the arrow keys move and Space pauses. Escape closes an open tool or window and keeps your draft.

entries.q: Can I delete my Torq account?
entries.a: There is no separate Torq account to delete. Your profile and posts are QDN publishes under your Qortal name; delete posts and Revs one at a time with Delete. Your name and Qortal account stay as they are.

entries.q: Can I change my Torq username?
entries.a: Your Torq name is your registered Qortal name, so Torq itself can't change it. If you own several names, switch between them with the name switcher. Posts stay under the name that published them.

entries.q: What does a Torq reply notification open?
entries.a: A reply notification opens the conversation at that reply. A reply to one of your Revs opens the Rev with its replies showing, and a SuperLike notification opens the post it was for.

entries.q: Why does Torq show Edited next to a post's date?
entries.a: The author changed the post after publishing it. You see the mark because Edited posts is on in your Settings (it's off by default). Open it to see when the post was published and edited, and to select and copy the current text.

entries.q: Why can't I post a Rev?
entries.a: Revs need a registered Qortal name, so sign in with one. Then check the file (JPEG, PNG or WebP photos, videos up to a minute and 100 MB) and approve the publish in Hub or GO. If posting fails, the Rev stays in the editor, so you can share it again.

entries.q: Why didn't my like stay on a Torq post?
entries.a: The heart fills once you approve the like in Hub or GO; if you decline or close the approval, nothing is published. A like also takes a minute or two to reach the network, so other devices show it a little later.

entries.q: Can I use Torq on GO's public node?
entries.a: Yes. You can read, post, reply, like, follow and make Revs on a public node. A few options that need your own node are hidden (Block, Blocked Users, Pin to profile, Follow in a post's menu), and files are limited to 500 MB each. What you publish lasts only while some node keeps it: a Rev posted from a public node that later dropped it can't load. A node of your own avoids that.

entries.q: How do I send QORT in Qortal Hub?
entries.a:
Click the account button in Hub's top bar and choose Send QORT, or use Send on the Wallet Activity card on Home.
Enter a Qortal address or registered name, the amount and your wallet password, then click Send.
Hub shows the recipient's name and full address, the amount and the fee before you confirm. Payments can't be reversed.

entries.q: How do I receive QORT in Qortal Hub?
entries.a: Give the sender your Qortal address (it starts with Q) or your registered name. In Hub, the Wallet Activity card on Home has Receive, which shows a QR code of your address with Copy address and Download QR, and the account card on Home has Copy address and Show receive QR. You don't have to approve anything: the QORT arrives when the payment confirms.

entries.q: Can someone pay me using my registered name instead of my address?
aliases: pay my name instead of address
entries.a: Yes. Send QORT in Hub and GO, Q-Wallets and Q-Trade's Send all accept a registered name. Before the confirmation, the app looks up which address owns the name and pays that address, showing both the name and the full address. If a name later changes owner, payments to it go to the new owner, so check the address when it matters.

entries.q: How do I pay someone I'm chatting with?
entries.a: Tap the person's name or avatar in the chat and choose Send QORT. The Send QORT window opens with their address filled in; enter the amount and your wallet password, then confirm. You can also find anyone in User search (Address book in GO's avatar menu) and tap Send QORT there.

entries.q: How do I check an account before I send it QORT?
entries.a: Open User search: in GO tap your avatar and choose Address book, in Hub use User Search in Home's Quick tools. Enter a name or address to see the account's level, balance, address, public key and recent payments, with a Send QORT button. It's a quick way to make sure you have the right person before paying.

entries.q: What does "This QR code is not a Qortal payment code" mean?
aliases: qortal go cant read payment qr
entries.a: GO's scanner read the code but found no Qortal payment in it, for example a website link or another wallet's payment code. Send QORT accepts qortal://pay and qortal://send links, qort: codes and plain Qortal addresses. Ask the payee for a Qortal payment QR, or type their address or name into To.

entries.q: How do I make a QR code so people can pay me with Qortal GO?
aliases: qr code to get paid qort
make a qr code to get paid
entries.a: Turn this text into a QR code with any QR generator: qortal://pay?recipient=YOUR_ADDRESS&amount=5. Leave out &amount=5 to let the payer type the amount, and you can use your registered name instead of the address (write a space as %20). Anyone who scans it with their phone's scanner gets GO's Send QORT screen filled in, and confirms with their own password.

entries.q: Why can't my phone's camera open my Qortal address QR code?
aliases: cant open an app for this qr code
qr code wont open qortal go
entries.a: A QR code with only an address is plain text, so Android can't tell it belongs to GO. Scan it from inside GO instead (Send QORT, then the QR icon in To), or use a qortal://pay?recipient=... code, which any scanner can hand to GO. GO's Receive QR holds your plain address, so payers should scan it from inside GO.

entries.q: What is the fee for sending QORT?
aliases: how much does it cost to send qort
entries.a: A QORT payment costs a small network fee, currently 0.01 QORT, on top of the amount you send. Hub and GO show the fee in the confirmation and never sign a higher fee than the one you saw: if the node asks for more, nothing is sent. The fee goes to the minters who run the network, not to a company.

entries.q: How long does a QORT payment take to arrive?
aliases: how long does qort take to send
entries.a: Usually about a minute. A payment confirms in the next block, and Qortal makes a block roughly every minute. Your balance and Wallet Activity update once it's confirmed; if it takes much longer, check that your node is online and synced.

entries.q: Can I cancel or reverse a QORT payment?
entries.a: No. Once a payment is sent it can't be cancelled, reversed or charged back, and nobody can do it for you. The only way to get it back is for the person who received it to send it back. Check the name, full address and amount in the confirmation before you accept.

entries.q: I sent QORT to the wrong address. What can I do?
aliases: get back qort sent by mistake
entries.a: A payment can't be undone, so the only way back is to ask the owner of that address to return it. Look the address up in User search to see whether it has a registered name you can message in Q-Chat. Hub and GO refuse a mistyped address before sending, so a wrong payment usually means a wrong but real address.

entries.q: What does "Your QORT balance is insufficient" mean when I send?
entries.a: Your balance doesn't cover the amount plus the 0.01 QORT payment fee. Send a little less so the fee fits, or wait for incoming QORT to confirm. Send QORT shows your balance at the top of the window.

entries.q: What does "the node asked for a fee ... Nothing was sent" mean?
aliases: node asked for a fee more than you approved
fee above approved nothing was sent
entries.a: Just before signing, Hub and GO fetch the fee again. If the node now asks for more than the fee you saw, or more than 1 QORT, they stop and send nothing. Try again; if the higher fee keeps appearing, the node may be misbehaving, so consider using another node.

entries.q: What does "could not confirm whether this transfer was sent" mean?
aliases: could not confirm whether this transfer was sent
did my qort payment go through
not sure if qort was sent
entries.a: Hub or GO sent the payment but couldn't check afterwards whether the network accepted it, so the message shows its signature. Don't send again straight away: look in Wallet Activity's Transaction history first, and only retry if the payment isn't there. The same goes when a Q-App says a payment timed out after you accepted it. Sending again blindly could pay twice.

entries.q: How many decimal places can a QORT amount have?
aliases: how small can a qort payment be
entries.a: Up to 8 decimals, so the smallest amount is 0.00000001 QORT. Amounts must be plain numbers like 1.5; forms like 1e3 are refused. In payment links, write the amount with a dot, like 0.25.

entries.q: Where can I see my past QORT payments?
entries.a: On Home, open the Wallet Activity card and tap Transaction history under the latest payment. It lists your payments newest first (who, sent or received, when and the amount), 20 at a time with Show more, and you can tap a name to look that account up. Q-Wallets also lists every QORT transaction, with filters.

entries.q: Can I send QORT while I'm on the public node?
aliases: can i pay on the public node
qortal go public node send qort
entries.a: Yes. QORT payments are signed in Hub or GO and only passed to the node, so they work on the public node too. What needs your own node is sending other coins (LTC, BTC and so on), using the ARRR wallet and selling on Q-Trade.

entries.q: Can I add a note or message to a QORT payment?
entries.a: Not in the payment itself: Send QORT in Hub and GO and Q-Wallets' QORT form have no note field. If the person needs to know what it's for, tell them in Q-Chat. Only ARRR sends in Q-Wallets have an optional memo, up to 40 characters.

entries.q: How do I send all my QORT?
entries.a: In Q-Wallets, tap Send max: it fills in the most you can send after reserving the fee. In Hub's and GO's Send QORT, enter your balance minus the 0.01 QORT fee. If Q-Wallets says Max allowed, the amount you typed is above what you can send.

entries.q: Can I send QORT to an address that starts with A?
aliases: send qort to an a address
entries.a: Yes, if it's a valid AT address. Addresses starting with A belong to ATs, Qortal's automated accounts such as a crowdfund, and Hub and GO accept them as payment recipients. Normal accounts start with Q.

entries.q: Why did a green name appear next to To in Send QORT?
aliases: name next to address when paying
entries.a: When the address you scan or type has a registered name, Send QORT shows that name in green next to the To field. It helps you check you're paying the right account. No name just means that address has no registered name.

entries.q: How do payment alerts work in Qortal GO?
entries.a: When QORT arrives in your account, GO shows an alert titled Payment from <name>, with the payer's avatar and the text You received <amount> QORT. If the payer has no registered name, it shows a short address and the Q-Wallets icon. Each payment alerts once, and it's also listed in the bell.

entries.q: What happens when I tap a payment alert?
aliases: why does payment alert open wallets
entries.a: It opens Q-Wallets, where you can see your balance and the payment in its transaction list. Payments listed in the bell open Q-Wallets the same way.

entries.q: Why does a payment alert show an address instead of a name?
entries.a: The payer's address has no registered name, or GO couldn't look the name up in time. Then the alert shows a shortened address and the Q-Wallets icon instead of a name and avatar. The payment itself is the same either way.

entries.q: Can I turn off payment alerts in Qortal GO?
entries.a: There's no switch for payments alone. The Disable all push notifications switch in the bell panel turns off all of GO's push alerts, payments included. Payments still appear in the bell and in Wallet Activity.

entries.q: Do I get an alert when I send QORT?
aliases: notified for my own qort payment
entries.a: No. Payment alerts are for QORT coming in to the account you're logged in to. For payments you send, check the Wallet Activity card or its Transaction history.

entries.q: Why didn't I get an alert for a payment I received?
entries.a: Alerts come from your node for the account you're logged in to, so check you're on the account that was paid and that GO is connected to its node. Also check the Disable all push notifications switch in the bell panel. Once the payment is confirmed it shows in Wallet Activity whether or not an alert appeared.

entries.q: How do I open Q-Wallets?
entries.a: In GO, tap your avatar and choose Wallets. In Hub or GO you can also tap Wallets in Home's Quick tools, or open qortal://APP/Q-Wallets. Tapping a payment alert opens it too.

entries.q: What is Q-Wallets?
entries.a: Your Qortal account is your QORT wallet, and Q-Wallets is Qortal's official app for managing it and your other coins. It shows balances and transaction history for QORT, BTC, LTC, DOGE, DGB, RVN and ARRR, and lets you send, receive with QR codes, keep an address book for each coin and choose network fees (low, medium, high or custom). It doesn't store your keys: Hub or GO handle them and ask you to approve each send.

entries.q: Which coins can I keep in my Qortal wallet?
aliases: can i hold bitcoin in qortal
entries.a: Every Qortal account in Hub and GO has wallets for QORT, Bitcoin (BTC), Litecoin (LTC), Dogecoin (DOGE), DigiByte (DGB), Ravencoin (RVN) and Pirate Chain (ARRR). Each coin has its own address. You see and use them in Q-Wallets, and they're the coins Q-Trade trades against QORT.

entries.q: Where do I find my Litecoin address?
entries.a: Open Q-Wallets (Wallets in GO's avatar menu or in Home's Quick tools), pick Litecoin and tap Receive to see the address and its QR code, with a copy button. In Q-Trade, pick LTC in the coin selector and tap Receive next to the LTC balance. Your LTC address is not the same as your QORT address.

entries.q: Is my Litecoin address the same as my QORT address?
aliases: ltc address same as qort address
send ltc to my qort address
entries.a: No. Each coin has its own address: your QORT address starts with Q, while your Litecoin address is a separate LTC address that starts with L. Always send each coin to that coin's own address, which Q-Wallets shows under the coin's name.

entries.q: How do I send Litecoin or other coins from my Qortal wallet?
entries.a: Open Q-Wallets, pick the coin (for example Litecoin) and choose Transfer LTC. Enter the receiving address for that coin and the amount (Send max keeps the network fee back), pick a fee, then approve in Hub or GO. It works the same for BTC, DOGE, DGB, RVN and ARRR. This needs your own node, because the node signs the send with that coin's key. Double-check the address: sends can't be reversed.

entries.q: Does Qortal Hub warn me about private keys when Core runs on the same computer?
aliases: hub local core private key warning
does hub send ltc key to core
entries.a: No. On the desktop, a node at 127.0.0.1 is the Core you run next to Hub, so Hub sends the key to it without the extra warning. A remote node needs an encrypted connection and a tick-box warning that names the host, and a public node is always blocked.

entries.q: Can I see my LTC or BTC balance on the public node?
entries.a: Yes. For BTC, LTC, DOGE, DGB and RVN, Hub and GO read the balance and history with your public wallet key, which can't spend anything, so it works on the public node. ARRR is different: its balance needs the ARRR seed on the node, so it needs your own node.

entries.q: Why can't I use my ARRR wallet on the public node?
aliases: cannot use pirate chain wallet through public node
entries.a: Every ARRR wallet action, even showing the address, balance or sync status, sends your ARRR seed to the node, and that seed can spend the wallet. Hub and GO never send it to a public node, and Q-Wallets says: You cannot use Pirate Chain wallet through public node. Please use your local node. Run your own node to use ARRR.

entries.q: Why does a Q-App ask to use my ARRR wallet while it is open?
aliases: allow this app to use your arrr wallet
entries.a: Reading your ARRR wallet (address, balance, transactions, sync status) needs the ARRR seed on your node. So the first time a Q-App such as Q-Wallets does it in a tab, Hub or GO asks whether to allow this app to use your ARRR wallet while it is open, with the node warning and a tick box. One yes covers that tab, app, account and node until the tab closes.

entries.q: What does "failed to synchronize after 36 attempts" mean?
entries.a: Your node's ARRR (Pirate Chain) wallet hadn't finished syncing, and Hub or GO gave up waiting after 36 tries. Wait a little and try again. Q-Wallets shows the ARRR sync status and lets you change the lightwallet server if it can't connect.

entries.q: What are Pirate Chain lightwallet servers in Q-Wallets?
aliases: no connection to pirate chain lightwallet server
entries.a: Your node's ARRR wallet reaches Pirate Chain through a lightwallet server. Q-Wallets shows the current server and a list of available Pirate Chain lightwallet servers, and you can switch if one isn't working. No Connection To Pirate Chain Lightwallet Server means the node can't reach one.

entries.q: What does a Pirate Chain (ARRR) address look like?
entries.a: Your ARRR address is a shielded address: 78 characters starting with zs. ARRR sends from Q-Wallets can carry an optional memo of up to 40 characters. Like the other coins, ARRR has its own address, separate from your QORT address.

entries.q: Which Litecoin addresses can I send to from Q-Wallets?
entries.a: Q-Wallets accepts all three common LTC formats: 34-character addresses starting with L or M, and 43-character addresses starting with ltc1. It checks the format before sending, so an exchange's deposit address in any of these forms works.

entries.q: Which Bitcoin addresses can I send to from Q-Wallets?
entries.a: Legacy addresses (starting with 1), SegWit (starting with 3) and Bech32 (starting with bc1). Q-Wallets checks the format before sending. Bitcoin's network fees are much higher than Litecoin's, so look at the fee before you send.

entries.q: How do network fees work when I send LTC, BTC or DOGE?
entries.a: Each coin's own network takes the fee, not Qortal. Q-Wallets lets you pick Low, Medium or High (recommended rates from fee publishers on QDN) or set a Custom fee, and shows the current fee. Low fees may result in slow or unconfirmed transactions. Send max holds the fee back for you.

entries.q: What are fee publishers in Q-Wallets and Q-Trade?
aliases: where do fee estimates come from
entries.a: They're Qortal names that publish fee estimates for each coin on QDN, as low, medium and high rates per kB. Q-Trade's settings let you choose Foreign-Fee-Publisher or JSON.Bridge, and Q-Wallets also fetches estimates from decentralized publishers. If no estimate loads, you can still enter a custom fee.

entries.q: How do I move Litecoin from an exchange into Qortal?
aliases: send ltc from exchange to qortal
transfer ltc from coinbase to qortal
entries.a:
1. Find your LTC address in Q-Wallets (Litecoin, Receive) or in Q-Trade (LTC, Receive) and copy it.
2. On the exchange, withdraw LTC to that address.
3. Wait for the Litecoin network to confirm it; the balance then shows in Q-Wallets and Q-Trade. Receiving works on the public node too.
Then you can buy QORT with it in Q-Trade.

entries.q: How do I send LTC from Qortal to an exchange?
aliases: send litecoin to exchange from qortal
entries.a: Use Q-Wallets with your own node: Litecoin, Transfer LTC, paste the exchange's LTC deposit address, enter the amount and a fee, then approve. Check that it's an LTC address and copied exactly, because sends can't be reversed. On the public node, GO blocks sending coins other than QORT.

entries.q: Why is my LTC balance missing or not showing a deposit?
entries.a: Balances of other coins come through your node, which asks that coin's network, and a deposit only counts once Litecoin confirms it, which can take around 10 minutes. Q-Trade shows a spinner until the balance arrives and refreshes it every 2.5 minutes. If it still doesn't show, check you used your Qortal LTC address (not your QORT address) and that your node is connected.

entries.q: How many confirmations does Q-Wallets show for a transaction?
entries.a: Q-Wallets marks a new transaction as Pending confirmation, then Pending, 1 of 3 confirmations and so on, and Confirmed once it has 3. A low fee can make another coin's transaction slow to confirm.

entries.q: How do I save addresses in Q-Wallets?
entries.a: Each coin has its own address book. Open it from the coin's page, tap Add contact, enter a name, the address and an optional note, and confirm the address before saving; for QORT you can search by registered name. Encrypted sync backs the address book up to QDN so it follows your Qortal account to other devices.

entries.q: Can Qortal add more coins to its wallets and Q-Trade?
entries.a: Each new coin needs its own native wallet built into Qortal before it can be held or traded, so additions take development work. Qortal's guidelines prefer coins with no ICO or pre-mine, a fair launch, no proof of stake and no KYC, plus technical support such as ElectrumX servers and legacy-style addresses. Listings are meant to be decided by community vote once the voting system is ready.

entries.q: How do I receive Bitcoin, Dogecoin or other coins in Qortal?
entries.a: Open Q-Wallets, pick the coin and tap Receive to show its address and QR code, then give that address to the sender. Each coin has its own address, and receiving works on the public node too, except ARRR, which needs your own node. The balance updates once that coin's network confirms the transaction.

entries.q: How do I see the details of a transaction in Q-Wallets?
entries.a: Open the coin in Q-Wallets and look at its transaction list: each row shows the time, sender and receiver, amount, fee and status, and you can copy the transaction hash (or signature for QORT). Unconfirmed transactions are marked until they confirm.

entries.q: How do I filter my QORT transactions in Q-Wallets?
entries.a: On Q-Wallets' QORT page, use the filters: Payments, Rewards (reward shares and related), Arbitrary (QDN publishes), AT, Group, Name, Asset and Poll, or All. Trade activity such as sell order contracts and their messages appears under AT, while Hub's and GO's Transaction history lists only payments.

entries.q: What does "Invalid LTC address" mean in Q-Wallets?
entries.a: The text in the address field doesn't match a Litecoin address format, so Q-Wallets won't send to it. Check you copied an LTC address (L, M or ltc1) completely and not another coin's address. Each coin shows a similar message for its own address type.

entries.q: Send QORT says "Invalid receiver address or name" or "Name does not exist". What is wrong?
aliases: name does not exist send qort
entries.a: Invalid receiver address or name means the text is neither a valid Qortal address (a mistyped address fails its built-in check) nor something that can be a name. Name does not exist means nobody has registered that name: check the spelling, or ask the person for their address.

entries.q: Why does a payment say the name contains invisible characters?
entries.a: The recipient name includes hidden characters, which can make a look-alike name pass for a real one, so Hub, GO and Q-Wallets refuse to pay it. Check where the name came from, and pay the address you know instead.

entries.q: Can I keep QORT in a cold wallet?
entries.a: Qortal's wiki describes a simple cold wallet: create an account on a device that isn't connected to the network, save its backup file to a USB stick (more than one copy is better), write down the address, then close the app. Send a small amount first to check it arrives, then send QORT to that address whenever you like.

entries.q: What's the difference between Q-Wallets and the Wallet Activity card?
entries.a: Wallet Activity is the quick QORT card on Home, with Send, Receive and Buy and your latest QORT payment. In Hub 3.0.3 it shows only that one payment, from the past 7 days, so it is not a history; in GO, a Transaction history row under it lists your payments, 20 at a time. Q-Wallets is the full multi-coin wallet app, with balances and history for every coin, sending, QR codes, address books and fee choices.

entries.q: Does Qortal Hub alert me when I receive QORT?
entries.a: Yes. When a payment arrives, Hub shows a desktop notification titled Payment from <name> (or New payment received) saying You received <amount> QORT, and the payment is listed in the bell. Clicking it opens Q-Wallets. The Disable all push notifications switch in the bell panel turns these off with all other alerts.

entries.q: Is the Trade Portal the same thing as Q-Trade?
aliases: where did the trade portal go
is q-trade the same as the trade portal
entries.a: The Trade Portal was the trading screen built into the old Qortal UI. In Qortal Hub and GO you trade in the Q-Trade Q-App, which uses the same trade system in Qortal Core underneath. The Buy button on Home's Wallet Activity card opens Q-Trade.

entries.q: Can I buy QORT with dollars, euros or a card?
entries.a: Not inside Qortal: Q-Trade only swaps QORT for other coins (LTC, BTC, DOGE, DGB, RVN and ARRR). The usual way is to buy LTC on an exchange, send it to your Qortal LTC address, then buy QORT in Q-Trade. qortal.dev also notes that the NonKYC.io exchange lists QORT against USDT.

entries.q: Do I need QORT to buy my first QORT?
entries.a: No. You can buy QORT in Q-Trade with only another coin, usually LTC. On the public node, if you hold fewer than 4 QORT, your encrypted buy request is held briefly on a database until it reaches the trade proxy, instead of going straight through Q-Chat.

entries.q: Who sets the prices on Q-Trade?
entries.a: Sellers do. Each seller lists QORT at the rate they choose, and buyers pick whichever orders they want; there are no buy or sell walls and no matching engine. Q-Trade sorts open orders by price per QORT, lowest first, and Trade History shows recent trades.

entries.q: Can I buy only part of a sell order?
aliases: buy part of an order qortal
buy less than the order q-trade
entries.a: No. Each sell order is bought whole: if an order is 100 QORT, you buy all 100. To get a different amount, tick several smaller orders that add up to what you want.

entries.q: Can I buy several sell orders at once?
aliases: buy many sell orders at once
entries.a: Yes. Tick as many orders as you like under Open Market Sell Orders and tap BUY once; Hub or GO asks you to approve them together, showing the number of orders, the QORT and the coin total. ARRR is the exception: Q-Trade buys one ARRR order at a time.

entries.q: Does Q-Trade have Auto Buy?
entries.a: No. Auto Buy was a tool in the old Qortal UI's Trade Portal. In Q-Trade you tick several sell orders yourself and buy them in one go.

entries.q: How much LTC do I need to buy a sell order?
aliases: how much ltc to buy qort
cost of a sell order in ltc
entries.a: The order's total LTC value plus one unlocking fee for each order you buy. Q-Trade adds it up in the bar at the bottom (the LTC total with unlocking fees, next to your LTC balance) and marks the total red if your balance is too low. Keep a little extra for the locking fee shown in the approval.

entries.q: What is the unlocking fee in Q-Trade?
entries.a: It's the Litecoin (or other coin) network fee needed to unlock the coins at the end of a trade so the seller can collect them. Sellers sign the fee their orders need, and Q-Trade shows it per order in the Unlocking fee column. Your node's unlocking fee is added to your total for each order you buy, and it goes to that coin's network, not to Qortal or Q-Trade.

entries.q: What is the locking fee?
entries.a: The locking fee is the network fee rate (per kB) for the transaction that locks your coins at the start of a buy. Hub and GO show the total unlocking fee and the locking fee rate in the buy approval. On your own node, Q-Trade's settings gear can set a custom locking fee; otherwise it follows your unlocking fee.

entries.q: Why can't I select some orders in Q-Trade, or why are they red?
entries.a: The seller needs a higher unlocking fee than your node's current fee, so a buy could fail; Q-Trade colours those orders red, blocks them and notes that your unlocking fee is too low to buy them. On your own node, raise your fee with the Fee button next to the coin selector. On the public node you can't change it, so pick other orders.

entries.q: Why don't I see the Fee button in Q-Trade?
aliases: where is the fee setting q-trade
entries.a: Q-Trade only shows the Fee button, the unsigned fees warning and the settings gear when you use your own node, because they change settings on that node. On the public node the node's own fee is used as it is. ARRR orders have no unlocking fee, so there's no Fee button for ARRR.

entries.q: Q-Trade says some orders have unknown unlocking fees. What should I do?
aliases: remove orders with unknown unlocking fees
entries.a: Those sellers haven't signed the fee their orders need. Q-Trade asks whether to Remove orders with unknown unlocking fees or Keep them. You may keep them, but there's a higher risk those trades won't go through; if one fails, you're refunded.

entries.q: Q-Trade suggests lowering my unlocking fee. Should I?
entries.a: The Suggestion appears when your fee is higher than any of your chosen orders needs. Lower fee sets it to the highest fee those orders require, which costs less and still meets every order; Continue without updating keeps your current fee. Either way the buy goes ahead.

entries.q: Does Q-Trade charge its own fee?
aliases: is there a fee to trade
entries.a: No. Q-Trade's terms say its maintainers don't profit and there are no extra fees for buying QORT through it. You pay only network fees: small QORT transaction fees and the other coin's network fees for locking and unlocking.

entries.q: Why are small trades with BTC expensive?
aliases: why use ltc to buy qort
entries.a: Bitcoin's network fees are high, and a trade needs several transactions on the BTC chain, so the fees can be large next to a small order. Qortal's wiki suggests using BTC for larger purchases. Litecoin's fees are very low, and the LTC market has the most activity, which is why most people trade QORT with LTC.

entries.q: What does My Pending Orders show in Q-Trade?
entries.a: It lists the buy orders you've submitted from Q-Trade on this device in the last day, for the coin selected, with their Status, amounts and Notes. It updates as the trade goes on, and an order another buyer completed drops off the list.

entries.q: What do the statuses in My Pending Orders mean?
entries.a:
Requested: your buy request was sent and is waiting for trade confirmation.
Submitted: the buy order was accepted and is under way.
Trading: the order is changing hands; this doesn't yet mean your account got it.
Completed: you bought it; wait for your QORT balance to update.
Failed: the buy didn't go through, and the Notes say why.

entries.q: Q-Trade says "Order(s) already taken". What happened?
entries.a: Another buyer got to that sell order before you, so your buy didn't go through; pick another order. Q-Trade warns that submitting an order doesn't mean yours will be the one that completes it. If any of your coins were already locked, they're refunded automatically after the trade's timeout.

entries.q: Can I close Q-Trade or GO while my buy is running?
entries.a: Wait until Q-Trade answers: while it says Attempting to submit buy order, don't leave the app. Once it says Successfully submitted order, the trade bot on the node finishes the trade. If you trade on your own node, keep that node running and synced until the trade completes.

entries.q: Why does buying on the public node take up to 3 minutes?
aliases: using gateway might take up to 3 minutes
entries.a: On the public node your buy goes to the Qortal trade proxy as an encrypted message, and Q-Trade waits for its answer, so it shows Using gateway: might take up to 3 minutes to submit the buy order, with a countdown. On your own node the order goes straight to your node's trade bot.

entries.q: What does the "Is using Gateway" switch in Q-Trade mean?
entries.a: It shows whether Q-Trade runs through a public node (a gateway). You can't flip it inside Q-Trade: change the node in Hub or GO instead (in GO: avatar menu, Node, then Private node). With your own node you also get selling, the Fee button and the settings gear.

entries.q: How long does a Q-Trade purchase take?
aliases: how long until qort arrives trade
entries.a: Usually several minutes, not seconds. A trade needs several transactions that must confirm on both chains: QORT blocks come about every minute, while Litecoin confirmations take longer, and a busy network or a low fee slows things down. Watch My Pending Orders until it says Completed.

entries.q: I bought QORT but my balance hasn't changed. What now?
aliases: where is my qort after buying
entries.a: If My Pending Orders says Completed, the QORT was redeemed to your account; give the balance a moment to update (Q-Trade refreshes balances every 2.5 minutes). If it still says Trading, the trade isn't finished yet. Your finished buys also appear under Trade History, My Buy History.

entries.q: What happens if a trade fails?
aliases: do i get my ltc back
entries.a: Both sides get their coins back automatically: the order's AT returns the seller's QORT, and the buyer's trade bot refunds the LTC (or other coin). Refunds wait for the trade's timeout and then for the coin's network, and network fees already spent aren't returned. If you trade on your own node, keep it running so it can do the refund.

entries.q: How long until a failed trade refunds my LTC?
aliases: when do i get my ltc back
entries.a: Your locked coins can be refunded once the order's trade timeout has passed: for sell orders made in Hub or GO that's 2 hours after your buy started. The trade bot then sends the refund, which still needs the coin's network to confirm. The seller's app sets the timeout, so orders made elsewhere can differ.

entries.q: My refund still hasn't arrived. What can I do?
entries.a: Give it time first: the trade timeout, then the coin's own confirmations. If you traded on your own node, keep Core running and don't delete its database; if a refund still hasn't come long after that, your node's API can retry failed refunds with POST /crosschain/htlc/refundAll (with your API key), after POST /admin/repository/importarchivedtrades if it returns false. If you traded on the public node, keep your saved trade record and ask in Qortal's community chats.

entries.q: Do I lose anything when a trade is refunded?
entries.a: A little: the other coin's network fees for locking and refunding are spent even when a trade fails, and QORT transaction fees aren't returned. The traded amount itself comes back to you. With LTC these fees are very small.

entries.q: How do cross-chain trades on Qortal work?
entries.a:
1. The seller's QORT is locked in an ACCT AT, a small contract on the Qortal chain.
2. The buyer's trade bot locks the coins (for example LTC) in a time-locked address on that coin's chain and messages the seller's trade bot.
3. The seller's trade bot locks the AT to that buyer.
4. The buyer claims the QORT with a secret, and the seller's bot uses the same secret to claim the coins.
If a step stalls, both sides are refunded.

entries.q: What is a trade bot?
entries.a: It's the part of Qortal Core that carries out a trade's steps for you: it creates the AT or locks the coins, sends the messages and claims or refunds the coins. It runs on the node where the trade started, so that node has to stay online and synced until the trade finishes.

entries.q: What does atomic cross-chain trade (ACCT) mean?
entries.a: It's a swap between two blockchains that either completes for both people or fails for both, with no third party holding the coins at any point. Qortal calls these ACCTs (atomic cross-chain trades) rather than atomic swaps. If one fails, each side gets their original coins back.

entries.q: What is trade presence?
entries.a: Sellers' nodes regularly announce that they're online and ready to trade. Q-Trade lists only sell orders whose seller has announced recently, so you don't buy from a node that's offline. Your own orders without a recent announcement show under Stuck orders.

entries.q: Why does Q-Trade keep showing Loading Trades?
entries.a: Q-Trade waits until it has both the open orders and the sellers' presence data from the node before it shows the list. If it stays on Loading Trades, the node may be slow or still syncing; give it a moment, then close and reopen Q-Trade.

entries.q: What does "You don't have enough LTC or your balance was not retrieved" mean?
entries.a: Your selected orders plus unlocking fees cost more than your LTC balance, or Q-Trade hasn't loaded your balance yet. Untick an order, or wait for the balance to appear (it refreshes every 2.5 minutes). For ARRR, the balance only loads on your own node.

entries.q: What does "Failed to submit buy order" mean?
aliases: unable to send buy order message
entries.a: The buy didn't get through, so nothing was bought; the message under it says why. Examples are declining the approval, Cannot make trade. Gateway node is synchronizing (the trade node was catching up), or Q-Trade not reaching the trade service. Check your balance and the order, then try again or pick another order.

entries.q: Why can't I press BUY in Q-Trade?
entries.a: BUY stays grey until you tick at least one order. If an order won't tick, its unlocking fee is higher than your node's fee. If BUY works but you get a balance error, your coin balance is too low or hasn't loaded yet.

entries.q: Can Q-Trade send the QORT I buy to another account?
entries.a: No. A buy always delivers the QORT to the account you're logged in to. Once it arrives, send it on with Send QORT if it's meant for someone else.

entries.q: What does "Allow this app to perform a buy order?" show?
aliases: allow this app to perform a buy order
entries.a: It's Hub or GO checking a Q-Trade buy before anything happens. It shows how many orders, the total QORT and coin amount, whether you're on a public node, the total unlocking fee and the locking fee rate, plus the private key warning for your node or the trade proxy. Tick the box and Accept only if it matches what you picked.

entries.q: What is the difference between trading on my own node and on the public node?
aliases: own node vs public node trading
entries.a:
Own node: your node's trade bot runs the trade with your coin's key, and you can buy, sell, cancel, set fees and use ARRR.
Public node (the default in GO): you can only buy, through the Qortal trade proxy, which receives your coin's private key and completes the trade for you; submitting can take up to 3 minutes.
Either way it's a cross-chain trade with automatic refunds.

entries.q: Why can't I sell QORT in GO or on the public node?
aliases: managing your sell orders is not possible using a gateway node
need my own node to sell
entries.a: A sell order is run by the trade bot on your node, which has to stay online to finish each trade, so it needs a node you run yourself. On a public node Q-Trade says: Managing your sell orders is not possible using a gateway node. Connect Hub or GO to your own node to sell.

entries.q: What is the minimum sell order on Q-Trade?
aliases: total sell amount needs to be greater than
entries.a: The order's total must be more than 0.01 LTC, 0.001 BTC, 1 DOGE, 0.01 DGB, 0.01 RVN or 0.0002 ARRR. Q-Trade shows the limit under the amounts and keeps Create sell order greyed out until the total is above it.

entries.q: Where does my QORT go when I list a sell order?
aliases: qort left my balance after sell order
where is my qort in a sell order
entries.a: Out of your balance and into the order's AT, a trade account on the Qortal chain that you still control. It stays there until a buyer completes the trade or you cancel, which returns it to you. That's why your QORT balance drops when you list.

entries.q: What do PENDING, LISTED and TRADING mean for my sell order?
entries.a:
PENDING: the order's AT is being created and isn't confirmed yet, so your QORT hasn't moved.
LISTED: the order is live and waiting for a buyer.
TRADING: a buyer's trade is under way; leave your node running.
BUYING and REFUNDING show for buys made from your own node. When a trade finishes, the order leaves this list and appears in Trade History.

entries.q: Why can't I cancel my sell order?
entries.a: Cancel sell order stays greyed out while the order is PENDING, because its AT isn't on the chain yet; wait until it's LISTED. If the order isn't in your list at all, look under Stuck orders, which can cancel it too. Cancelling needs your own node.

entries.q: Do I get the fee back when I cancel a sell order?
entries.a: No. Cancelling sends a small QORT transaction, shown in the approval, and neither that fee nor the fee for creating the order comes back. The QORT you listed returns to your balance.

entries.q: What are stuck orders in Q-Trade?
entries.a: They're your sell orders that are still open on the chain but haven't been announced by a node recently, so buyers can't see them in the market. Open Sell QORT, tap Stuck orders and use Cancel sell on any you want back; No stuck trades means there are none. It happens when the node that made the order hasn't been online.

entries.q: Why doesn't my sell order show in Open Market Sell Orders?
entries.a: Q-Trade only lists orders whose seller's node has announced it's online recently, and a new order needs a couple of minutes to reach the network. If your node was off, your order is hidden until it announces again. Keep your node running, and check Stuck orders if it doesn't come back.

entries.q: Does my node need to stay online while my QORT is for sale?
aliases: turn off node with sell order
node must be online to sell
entries.a: Yes. Your node's trade bot answers buyers and finishes the trade, and buyers only see your order while your node announces it's online. If your node is off when a buyer comes, the trade can't finish and the buyer is refunded. Don't delete or reset the node's database while you have trades.

entries.q: What does "Action required! You have unsigned fees" mean?
entries.a: Your node has fee data for your sell orders that you haven't signed yet. Tap the button and approve the request to sign the required fees for all your trade offers. Signing tells buyers' nodes the right unlocking fee to use, so their buys of your orders go through; it doesn't move any coins.

entries.q: What happens when someone buys my sell order?
aliases: where is my ltc after selling
where does my ltc go when i sell
entries.a: Your order moves to TRADING while the trade bots finish. When it's done, the LTC (or other coin) is in your own wallet for that coin in the same account, and the sale shows under Trade History, My Sell History. Keep your node running until then.

entries.q: My QORT was bought but my LTC hasn't arrived. What now?
aliases: where is my ltc from trade
entries.a: Your node's trade bot claims the LTC after the buyer claims the QORT, so keep your node running; then the Litecoin network has to confirm it, which Q-Wallets shows as pending. If the buyer never finished, the trade times out and the AT returns your QORT instead.

entries.q: Does selling QORT send my LTC private key to the node?
aliases: does selling qort need my ltc key
entries.a: No. For LTC, BTC, DOGE, DGB and RVN, a sell order only needs your receiving address, which Hub or GO work out on your device. ARRR is the exception: getting your ARRR receiving address needs the ARRR seed on your node, so the sell approval shows the private key warning.

entries.q: Can I sell QORT for BTC, ARRR or other coins?
entries.a: Yes, on your own node: pick the coin (LTC, DOGE, BTC, DGB, RVN or ARRR) in Q-Trade's coin selector before you tap New Sell Order, and set your price in that coin. Each coin has its own minimum order total, for example 0.001 BTC or 1 DOGE. For ARRR, your receiving address comes from the node, so the approval warns that your ARRR seed goes to that node.

entries.q: Can I post a buy order for QORT at my own price?
entries.a: No. Q-Trade only has sell orders: sellers list QORT and buyers pick from them. A buy order would need the buyer's LTC held on its own chain without knowing the seller in advance, which hasn't been built. To buy, choose from Open Market Sell Orders.

entries.q: Can I trade LTC for BTC directly on Q-Trade?
entries.a: No. Every Q-Trade pair has QORT on one side (QORT-LTC, QORT-BTC and so on). To go from LTC to BTC you'd buy QORT with LTC, then sell that QORT for BTC.

entries.q: What is the trade timeout?
aliases: how long before a trade refunds
entries.a: It's how long a trade may take before refunds can start. Sell orders made in Hub and GO use 2 hours, set when the order is created. If a buyer's trade hasn't finished in time, the buyer's locked coins can be refunded and the AT's QORT goes back to the seller.

entries.q: What does "Unable to create sell order. Please try again." mean?
entries.a: Your node couldn't create or confirm the order's AT, so no order was made. Check that your node is synced and that you have enough QORT for the amount plus fees, then try again. Q-Trade marks the failed attempt so it doesn't show as an order.

entries.q: Can I restart or bootstrap my node while a trade is running?
entries.a: Avoid it. Qortal's trade guide says that for a trade to succeed your Core must keep running and you must not delete or change its database, because the node's trade bot does the trade. Wait until your buy or sell order shows the trade finished.

entries.q: Do sell orders expire?
aliases: how long does a sell order last
entries.a: No. A sell order stays open until someone buys it or you cancel it. It's only hidden from buyers while your node isn't online to announce it, and then it shows under Stuck orders.

entries.q: Can I change the price of my sell order?
entries.a: Not directly: Q-Trade has no edit for sell orders. Cancel the order (your QORT comes back after a couple of minutes), then create a new one at the new price. Each step costs a small QORT fee.

entries.q: Why did my balance drop by more than my sell order amount?
entries.a: A sell order puts the order amount plus 0.01 QORT into its AT, to cover the AT's own running costs, and the approval shows the transaction fee on top. So listing 10 QORT takes a little more than 10 from your balance.

entries.q: My Q-Trade buy has been Trading for hours. What should I do?
entries.a: Trading means the order is changing hands, not that it's finished or that your account got it. Leave it running: either it completes, or once the trade timeout passes (2 hours for orders made in Hub or GO) the refund can start and your coins come back. If you use your own node, keep it running and synced meanwhile.

entries.q: Why are there few or no sell orders for some coins?
entries.a: Orders only appear when people list QORT for that coin, and Q-Trade only shows sellers whose node is online. Litecoin usually has the most orders; other coins can be quiet. Pick another coin in the selector or check again later.

entries.q: Is it safe to buy QORT directly from a person instead of Q-Trade?
aliases: send ltc to someone for qort
someone offers to sell me qort
entries.a: A direct deal means trusting the other person to send QORT after you pay, and a payment can't be reversed. In Q-Trade, a trade either completes for both sides or both are refunded, with no one to trust. Qortal's wiki also warns about scammers who approach people in private messages.

entries.q: Where can I get help with a trade problem?
entries.a: Ask in Q-Chat, for example in the Qortal Project group, Qortal's official community group for news and support, or report it with the Q-Support Q-App. Say which coin, roughly when, and what My Pending Orders or your sell list shows. Never share your seed phrase, private key or backup password with anyone helping you.

entries.q: What does Q-Trade's settings gear do?
entries.a: On your own node, the gear next to Terms and conditions opens Q-Trade's settings. Locking fees: tick Enable custom locking fee to set the locking fee rate (sats per kB) separately, then Update locking fee. Fee publisher: choose where recommended fees come from, Foreign-Fee-Publisher or JSON.Bridge.

entries.q: What are sats in Q-Trade's fees?
entries.a: A sat is a coin's smallest unit: 100,000,000 sats make 1 LTC (and likewise 1 BTC or 1 DOGE). So an unlocking fee shown as 30000 sats is 0.0003 LTC per order.

entries.q: How do I switch coins in Q-Trade?
entries.a: Use the coin selector under the balance card: LTC, DOGE, BTC, DGB, RVN or ARRR. The order list, your pending orders, balances and history all follow the coin you pick. Q-Trade starts on LTC.

entries.q: How do I send QORT from Q-Trade?
entries.a: On Q-Trade's Total Balance card, tap Send under your QORT balance, enter a Recipient Address or Name and the Amount, then tap Send and approve the payment in Hub or GO. Receive under the QORT balance shows your QORT address and its QR code.

entries.q: What do the LTC/QORT and Total LTC Value columns mean in Q-Trade?
entries.a: LTC/QORT is the price per QORT in LTC (the order's total divided by its QORT amount), and Q-Trade sorts by it, lowest first. Total LTC Value is what the whole order costs before your unlocking fee. QORT AMOUNT is how much QORT the order sells, and Seller shows the seller's name or address.

entries.q: How do I see a sell order's details before buying?
aliases: see the seller of an order
entries.a: Tap the info icon at the start of the order's row. Q-Trade shows the seller, the amount, the total, the price per QORT, the unlocking fee in sats and the order's AT address, with copy buttons. A red box warns you if your node's unlocking fee is too low for that order.

entries.q: Where can I see recent QORT trades?
entries.a: Qortino has no live prices, but Q-Trade does: Trade History, Historic Trades lists the latest completed trades for the coin selected, with the price per QORT, and QORT for sale shows the current sell orders sorted by price. For charts, open the Q-Charts Q-App.

entries.q: Should I buy or sell QORT right now?
entries.a: Qortino can't tell you when to buy or sell: it gives no investment advice and sees no live prices offline. For the current market, look at the sell orders and Historic Trades in Q-Trade, or the charts in Q-Charts, and decide for yourself.

entries.q: Why does QORT's dollar value change when its LTC rate doesn't?
entries.a: QORT has no direct dollar price: it trades against coins like LTC, so any dollar value is indirect. If LTC's dollar price falls while trades stay at the same LTC rate, QORT's dollar value falls with it. It can also look different against BTC than against LTC.

entries.q: Is QORT listed on any exchange?
entries.a: qortal.dev says QORT is listed on NonKYC.io, a centralized exchange that trades QORT against USDT without KYC. It also recommends Q-Trade for the most security, since there you trade straight from your own wallet and no exchange holds your coins.

entries.q: How do I choose a price for my sell order?
aliases: how much to sell qort for
entries.a: You can set any price: there are no walls, and buyers pick whichever orders suit them. Qortino can't advise on prices and has no live data, but Q-Trade's open sell orders and Historic Trades show what others ask and recently traded at. For BTC, Qortal's wiki reminds sellers that buyers also pay high network fees, which matters for small orders.

entries.q: Who can see my trades?
aliases: can others see my q-trade trades
entries.a: Anyone: trades happen on public blockchains, and Q-Trade's Historic Trades lists recent trades with the buyer's and seller's names or addresses. The other coin's side is visible on its own chain too.

entries.q: Can I trade while my node is still syncing?
entries.a: Wait until it's fully synced. Qortal's trade guide says your node must be synced the whole time you trade, because its trade bot sends and checks each step. An unsynced node can make a trade stall until refunds start.

entries.q: What does "Allow this app to perform a sell order?" show?
aliases: allow this app to perform a sell order
entries.a: It shows the order as the QORT amount for the coin amount, with the QORT fee and a tick box to confirm you've read it. For ARRR it also warns that your ARRR seed goes to your node. Accepting creates the order's AT on the chain.

entries.q: What does "Allow this app to cancel a sell order?" mean?
aliases: allow this app to cancel a sell order
entries.a: Q-Trade is asking to cancel one of your sell orders, shown by its QORT and coin amounts, for a small QORT fee. Accepting sends a message to the order's AT that cancels it and returns your QORT. Decline if you didn't ask to cancel.

entries.q: What does "Allow this app to update foreign fees on your node?" mean?
aliases: update foreign fees on your node
entries.a: Q-Trade wants to change your node's fee setting for a coin, such as the unlocking fee you picked with the Fee button or a custom locking fee. It only works on your own node and changes what your future trades use. Decline if you didn't ask for it.

entries.q: Is Q-Trade a decentralized exchange (DEX)?
entries.a: Yes: trades happen directly between the two people's nodes, and nobody takes control of the coins at any point. A trade either succeeds or fails, in which case each side gets their coins back. Qortal prefers the name Trade Portal because DEX is used loosely elsewhere.

entries.q: What do I need before I can trade on Qortal?
aliases: what do i need to trade qort
entries.a: A Qortal account in Hub or GO, and something to trade: LTC (or another supported coin) in your Qortal wallet to buy QORT, or QORT to sell. You can buy on the public node; selling needs your own node, kept online and synced. Open Q-Trade with Buy on Home's Wallet Activity card.

entries.q: How do I buy QORT with ARRR?
entries.a: You need your own node, because the ARRR wallet and its balance need your ARRR seed on the node. Pick ARRR in Q-Trade's coin selector, tick one sell order (ARRR orders are bought one at a time and have no unlocking fee) and tap BUY, then accept the approval with its ARRR seed warning.

entries.q: What if the seller cancels while I'm buying their order?
entries.a: Your buy can't complete, so your trade bot refunds your locked coins once the trade's timeout has passed. The order then ends as failed or refunded rather than completed, and you lose only the other coin's network fees.

entries.q: Where are my coins while a trade is running?
aliases: where are my ltc during a trade
where is my qort during a trade
entries.a: The seller's QORT sits in the order's AT on the Qortal chain. The buyer's coins (for example LTC) sit in a time-locked address on that coin's chain, which only the seller can claim with the trade's secret, or which the buyer can take back after the timeout. That's what makes the trade atomic.

entries.q: Why was my buy refunded?
entries.a: Common reasons: another buyer took the order first, the seller's node didn't respond in time (for example it went offline), or the seller cancelled. In each case the trade can't finish, so the coins go back after the timeout. Q-Trade hides sellers whose nodes aren't online to make this rarer.

entries.q: Can a seller on Q-Trade cheat me?
aliases: can a seller scam me q-trade
entries.a: Not with the trade itself: the seller can only claim your coins with the secret that you reveal when you claim the QORT, and if they never deliver, your coins come back after the timeout. On the public node, though, you do trust the trade proxy with your coin's private key.

entries.q: What are Q-Trade's terms and conditions?
entries.a: In short: Q-Trade aims to make trading LTC and other coins for QORT easy, its maintainers don't profit and there are no extra fees, and it's a hobby project whose developers aren't responsible for lost coins. It explains that the gateway (public node) means trusting that node with your coin's private key, and offers your local node instead. Read them with Terms and conditions at the top of Q-Trade.

entries.q: What's the difference between the QORT for sale and Sell QORT tabs?
entries.a: QORT for sale is where you buy: it shows My Pending Orders and other people's Open Market Sell Orders. Sell QORT is for your own sell orders: New Sell Order, Stuck orders and your listed orders with Cancel sell order. Trade History is the third tab.

entries.q: Why don't my pending Q-Trade orders show on my other device?
entries.a: Q-Trade keeps My Pending Orders on the device you bought from, and only for the last day. On another device the list starts empty, but finished trades show under Trade History, My Buy History on any device.

entries.q: How can a shop or market stall take QORT payments?
entries.a: Show the customer a QR code made from qortal://pay?recipient=YOUR_ADDRESS&amount=<price>: scanning it opens GO's Send QORT with your address and the amount filled in, and the customer confirms. You see the payment arrive as an alert (Payment from <name>) and in Wallet Activity, about a minute later. GO's Qortal Card test feature can also take payments by tap.

entries.q: Can POS+ take QORT or card payments itself?
entries.a: No. POS+ is the register: it records how each sale was paid (Card, Cash or a split of both) and makes the receipt, but it doesn't charge cards or move any QORT itself. To take QORT, a customer with GO can pay you with Send QORT, for example by scanning a qortal://pay QR code you show.

entries.q: Does POS+ cost anything to use?
entries.a: POS+ needs no separate server, subscription or cloud account. What you do pay is the small QORT fee for each QDN publish you approve, such as closing the day, saving products or settings, or sharing a clock-in. Turning off live clock-in sharing means fewer publishes to approve.

entries.q: POS+ didn't open my store automatically. What should I check?
aliases: pos+ asks to sign in again
entries.a: Make sure Keep me signed in on this device is ticked, and approve Hub's or GO's request to share your account, accepting if it offers to remember the choice. If Hub or GO is signed in to a different account, POS+ asks you to choose the store.

entries.q: Q-Wallets says my ARRR wallet is "Not initialized yet". What does that mean?
entries.a: Your node is still setting up and syncing your Pirate Chain wallet, so Q-Wallets can't show the address or balance yet. Keep your own node running and check again later; if it can't reach a server, try another Pirate Chain lightwallet server in Q-Wallets.

entries.q: Which address formats do DOGE, DGB and RVN use in Q-Wallets?
entries.a: Dogecoin: 34 characters starting with D. DigiByte: 34 characters starting with D or S, or 43 starting with dgb1. Ravencoin: 34 characters starting with R. Q-Wallets checks these formats before it sends.

entries.q: What does "invalid amount" mean when I send QORT?
aliases: please enter an amount greater than 0
entries.a: Send QORT only accepts a plain number above zero with at most 8 decimals, such as 2.5. It refuses zero, negative numbers, more than 8 decimals and forms like 1e3. If it says please enter an amount greater than 0 or please enter a recipient, fill in that field first.

entries.q: Can I send LTC to someone's Qortal name?
entries.a: No. Qortal names point to QORT addresses only, so Q-Wallets resolves names for QORT but needs a real address for LTC and the other coins. Ask the person for their LTC address (in their Q-Wallets, Litecoin, Receive).

entries.q: What does "Allow this app to set the current server?" mean?
aliases: allow this app to set the current server
this action cannot be done through a public node
entries.a: A Q-App such as Q-Wallets wants to change which server your node uses for a coin, for example a Pirate Chain lightwallet server; the window shows the coin, the server type and its host. It only works on your own node: on the public node you get This action cannot be done through a public node.

entries.q: Can I speed up a slow trade?
entries.a: Not once it's running: the trade bots have to wait for each confirmation, or for the timeout if something stalls. For later trades, a higher fee (Medium or High with the Fee button on your own node) helps the other coin's transactions confirm sooner, since confirmation speed depends on the fee.

entries.q: Does my trade keep going if I close Hub or GO?
entries.a: Yes, once Q-Trade has answered, because the trade bot runs inside Qortal Core on the node, not in the app. What matters is that the node keeps running: your own Core for orders made there, or the trade proxy's node for buys on the public node. Closing Hub or GO doesn't stop it.

entries.q: Can I cancel a buy order in Q-Trade?
entries.a: No. Once a buy is submitted, Q-Trade has no cancel for it: it either completes or, if it can't, refunds your coins after the trade's timeout. Only sell orders can be cancelled. Check the orders and the approval before you tap BUY.

entries.q: How do I find the cheapest QORT on Q-Trade?
entries.a: Q-Trade sorts Open Market Sell Orders by LTC/QORT (price per QORT), lowest first, so the cheapest orders are at the top; tap the column header to sort the other way. Remember each order you buy adds an unlocking fee, so many tiny orders can cost more in total than one bigger one.

entries.q: Why does buying many small orders cost more?
aliases: buy one big order or many small
entries.a: Q-Trade adds your unlocking fee once for every order you tick, so ten small orders pay ten unlocking fees while one big order pays one. The bottom bar shows the total with unlocking fees, so compare it before you tap BUY.

entries.q: How do I send QORT with Q-Wallets?
entries.a: Open Q-Wallets, pick Qortal and choose Transfer QORT. Enter a QORT address or name, or pick a contact from your address book, then the amount (Send max holds back the 0.01 QORT network fee). Hub or GO then asks you to approve the payment. Always double-check the address: payments can't be reversed.

entries.q: Why doesn't my QORT balance update right away in Q-Wallets?
entries.a: Q-Wallets refreshes the QORT balance on its own about every 2.5 minutes, and a payment only counts once it's confirmed in a block. Use the refresh button to update it sooner.

entries.q: Where do I get Litecoin to buy QORT?
entries.a: Litecoin is sold on most crypto exchanges; qortal.dev mentions Coinbase and Binance as examples. Buy LTC there, withdraw it to your Qortal LTC address (Q-Wallets, Litecoin, Receive), then buy QORT with it in Q-Trade.

entries.q: What is QORT's market cap or trading volume?
aliases: how big is the qort market
entries.a: Qortino runs offline, so it has no live market figures and won't guess them. Q-Charts charts QORT's past trades and shows each day's volume when you hover a candle, and Q-Trade's Historic Trades lists the latest trades.

entries.q: What is the smallest amount of QORT I can buy on Q-Trade?
entries.a: There's no fixed minimum for buyers: you buy whole sell orders, so the smallest buy is the smallest order on offer. Sellers' orders must be worth more than 0.01 LTC (or the matching minimum for other coins), so you won't find orders smaller than that. Tick a few small orders to reach the amount you need.

entries.q: What is ARRR (Pirate Chain) in Qortal?
entries.a: ARRR is the coin of Pirate Chain, a privacy-focused blockchain whose shielded addresses start with zs. Every Qortal account has an ARRR wallet next to its QORT, and ARRR can be traded for QORT in Q-Trade. Its wallet only works with your own node, because the node needs your ARRR seed to read or send it.

entries.q: Can Qortal Hub scan payment QR codes?
entries.a: No. The QR scanner in Send QORT is part of Qortal GO on phones only. In Hub, paste or type the address or registered name into Send QORT. qortal://pay links and payment QR codes are GO features; Hub 3.0.3 doesn't open them.

entries.q: Why do my other coin wallets take a moment after I log in to GO?
entries.a: GO unlocks your QORT keys first so Home and chat are ready quickly, then works out your BTC, LTC, DOGE, DGB, RVN and ARRR wallets in the background. Coin addresses, balances and trades become ready a moment later; if Q-Wallets or Q-Trade is still loading right after login, give it a few seconds.
